notes: THRU on the profile and on the face together: no rise at the fit end (the profile FALLS to ~0.5e4 there) and the stop is 3.1 cm from the anode. Neither fit-failure mode is applicable - there is no peak to overshoot and nothing forward of the fit end to undershoot into. Worth flagging separately that this object's charge scale is not usable: it is a near-anode, near-U-wire-parallel track whose whole plateau sits at half MIP, so any finer statement than 'not a stopping muon' would be over-reading the reconstruction.
evidence: A 43.6 cm stub in the far bottom corner of the volume, running from (335,-331,88) to (337,-308,53) - the drift coordinate changes by 1.4 cm over the whole 43 cm, so the track lies essentially in the anode plane, 3-5 cm inside it, and the fit's last point is 3.1 cm from the anode face. f_meas makes the geometry explicit: the whole object sits at time slice 15-25, i.e. at the anode, and its U projection collapses onto about five channels while V and W see a flat horizontal streak, so the track is close to parallel to the U wires and the charge attribution here is not to be trusted. The profile shows it. At 4x the entire track is far below MIP - the chain's own mean is 2.9e4 against a 5.4e4 plateau reference, which is why the chain flags plateau_off_mip - and its shape is a broad hump: 0.5-1.3e4 over s=0-2, rising to 2-3e4 by s=5, a maximum of 4.4e4 near s=11 and a 3.7e4 shoulder at s=21, then falling back through 2e4 at s=33 to 0.2-1.5e4 over s=38-44. Both ends fade to nothing and the fit end is the lower of the two. There is no Bragg rise anywhere, let alone at the fit end, and the profile finishes at about a tenth of its own maximum - a stopping muon cannot do that - so this is a through-goer, and it has a face 3.1 cm away to go through. The chain agrees on all three counts (no_bragg, shape_flat, plateau_off_mip, is_stm 0), and range KE 130 MeV against MCS 340 MeV and a dQ/dx-based 45 MeV shows the three estimators do not even agree with each other on this object. Nothing else is drawn: one object row, the chain itself, no arms, no dots, no capture gamma, and all three azimuths show a single isolated spine with empty space at both ends.

notes: Flat-profile THRU on a contained end. Unlike the other two THRUs in my chunk there IS a plausible exit here: a dead U band 0-2 channels beyond the fit's last point in the direction of travel. Neither fit-failure mode: no overshoot (no peak anywhere before the end - the 1.17-1.40e5 burst is 20 cm back up the body), and no undershoot (the one forward object, 193004, is a 2-point 0.9 cm speck at cos_fwd 0.02 and 6e4, nowhere near the straight-ahead 0.9-1.2e5 tip signature). The rubric's THRU convention forced 193004 to delta / other; if this were judged a stop it would be an attached-Michel candidate, which is the one way this record could be wrong.
evidence: 126 cm chain entering 1.1 cm from the z face at (177,55,2) and ending at (76,1,42), 41.4 cm from the nearest (z) wall - a contained end, so the profile has to decide it, and the profile is flat. At 4x and 9x the chain sits on a 4.5-6.0e4 band from s=100 the whole way in to s=0, with no trend: the values in the last 10 cm are 5.0-5.5e4 and the very last fit point is 4.1e4, below the band, while the muon reference curve at those arc lengths wants 7.5e4 to 1.6e5. The only elevated chain points anywhere near the end are a single 7.4e4 at s=9 and a tight burst of four points at 1.17-1.40e5 at s=19-21, twenty centimetres BACK up the muon - a delta ray, not a Bragg peak, and its position rules out reading it as one. Range KE 306 MeV against MCS 1380 MeV (amb 0.94) points the same way. The chain agrees: reject no_bragg and shape_flat, is_stm 0. f_meas shows a dead U band at channels 2860-2880 with the fit's last point sitting at about 2878 and the track heading straight into it, so the cluster very plausibly ends because the imaging loses U coverage there, not because a muon stopped. On a through-goer there is no stop, so every non-chain row is delta / other by convention: 193004 is a 2-point 0.9 cm speck 2.6-2.9 cm out that the chain bridges across empty space and calls a 4.1 MeV Michel, but at cos_fwd 0.02 and 2.8 cm off-axis it is just a fragment beside a fit end that is not a stop; 206009 is a 3-point speck 25.5 cm out; 195005, 197006 and 198007 are 2-point survey specks at 51-56 cm sharing roughly one direction, and 202008 is another at 38 cm pointing the opposite way (cos -0.78 against them). None of them can be a capture gamma or a Michel dot when there is no stop to be past.

notes: Undershoot check run: no short high-charge forward tip - the only forward objects are 2-point specks 46-52 cm out at 2.5-4.7e4, far below the several-times-MIP the undershoot signature needs. Overshoot considered and rejected on the d_min=0.0 attachment of 95021 (no gap to bridge) plus the terminal dip being only 0.8 of plateau. Hardest sub-call was 95007, whose charge is almost all zero-charge fit points.
evidence: 155 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the z face at (292,22,1) and stops deep at (169,7,76), 75.7 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not in question. The profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau out beyond 25 cm, climbs through 7e4 near 20 cm and 9e4 near 8 cm, and peaks at about 1.05e5 in the 2-6 cm before the fit end, following the shape of the muon curve without ever crossing it - a clear ragged Bragg rise. The last 1.33 cm (segment 95022, 4 points, median 4.4e4) sits below the plateau, but that is 0.8 of the track own MIP level, well outside the 0.15-0.5 band a real bridged collapse shows, and the Michel object 95021 has d_min 0.0, i.e. it attaches at the stop, so there is no gap for the fit to have bridged; pin left alone. Past the stop, 95021 is a 10.8 cm 19-point arm at about 5.3e4 - MIP level, which a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot produce - leaving the stop at a 38 deg kink that the d azimuth shows as a wide-angle arm clearly separated from the green muon body; that is the Michel. A 2-point 0.2 cm speck 237020 sits 21 cm out, 20.5 cm perpendicular off the muon body line and within 0.996 cosine of the Michel arm direction, detached across a clean gap: gamma, and the chain gamma body exclusion label is outranked by that off-axis distance. The three 2-point survey specks 234017/235018/236019 at 46-52 cm all have cos_fwd +0.95 and lie on the muon own forward continuation, perpendicular to the Michel arm and spread over 9 cm - read as a different object, delta / other. 95007 is 12 points 2.3-5.6 cm back, only 2.8 cm perpendicular off the body line and almost entirely zero-charge fit points (median 2536): hugging the body, so delta / other despite the chain pdg 11 shower type. 95013 is 74 cm back at cos_fwd -0.98, body activity. No dead channel band touches the stop in U, V or W and measured matches predicted there.

notes: No Bragg rise at the fit end, charge is flat-to-falling to the last point, and the cluster simply ends where the imaging runs out - a wide U dead band abuts the track and about 40 percent of its U extent is inside it. Competing readings I weighed: (a) overshoot, i.e. the four 5.4-8.2e4 points at s = 7-9 are the real Bragg peak and the last 6 cm is bridged fit - rejected because there is no Michel or other blob for the fit to bridge to, the 3-D shows the terminal segment collinear with the body, and the 24 cm 0.2-MIP trough at s = 14-38 shows the profile is untrustworthy rather than physically peaked; (b) UNCLEAR on that same corruption - rejected because the operative test is whether a rise is present, and none is. Chain rejects with no_bragg + plateau_off_mip.
evidence: 62.3 cm chain entering 0.7 cm from the y wall at (258,-336,238) and ending at (260,-296,205), 40.7 cm from the nearest face, so the end is nowhere near a wall. The profile has a real 4.5-6e4 MIP plateau over the far 20 cm (s = 40-62), then collapses through a ~24 cm mid-track stretch (s = 14-38) where most points sit at 0.7-2e4, recovers to a four-point scatter of 5.4-8.2e4 around s = 7-9, and falls again to 0.4-3e4 over the last 5 cm, with six points under 2e4 in the last 2 cm. There is no rise off the plateau anywhere near the fit end - the terminal charge is the lowest on the track, which is the opposite of a Bragg. The three stop azimuths show the last 6 cm as a smooth collinear continuation of the body with a terminal vertex square and nothing whatsoever past it: no arm, no dot, no blob, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). The U projection is the reason for the medium confidence: the track lies along the right edge of a wide hatched dead-channel band with roughly 40 percent of its U extent inside it, and it spans only about 35 U channels over 62 cm, so U is nearly prolonged; that is a charge-loss story that explains the unphysical 0.2-MIP mid-track trough and could in principle hide a Bragg. 114008 is a 15-point pdg-11-shower piece whose centroid lies exactly on the muon body line (perpendicular offset under 0.1 cm at 9.1 cm back), so body activity. 295010, 299011 and C297 are 1-2 point specks 17-60 cm out at cos_fwd -0.6 to -0.9; on a through-goer there is no stop to define gamma against, so all are delta / other.

notes: Undershoot check run: nothing short, forward and several-times-MIP sits past the fit end - the only forward object is a 0.7 cm speck 21 cm out at 4.7e4, i.e. MIP-level and far too distant for the undershoot signature. Overshoot considered and rejected because the post-peak stretch stays at 1.2-2x MIP. The chain reject is no_bragg and I disagree with it; the bimodal sawtooth in the profile is what most likely defeated the chain plateau test. Competing reading: if the 1.0-1.5e5 points at s = 9-12 are charge misassigned around the adjacent V dead band rather than a real peak, this would be THRU.
evidence: 265 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the y wall at (197,336,11) and stops at (19,263,162), 73.4 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained. The profile is bimodal along its whole length - a sawtooth that repeatedly drops from the 5-5.5e4 upper envelope down to 2.3-3.5e4 all the way out to s = 100 - so I read the upper envelope. That envelope is flat at 5-5.5e4 beyond 40 cm, lifts to 7-8e4 over s = 25-35, to 8-9.2e4 at s = 13-15, and to 1.0-1.5e5 at s = 9-12, then eases back to 6-9.7e4 over the last 8 cm with the single point nearest the fit end at 9.7e4. That is a ragged rise of a factor 2-3 off the track own plateau spread over the last 25 cm, following the muon curve shape, so I read a Bragg despite the chain no_bragg reject. I did not move the pin: the post-peak stretch sits at 1.2-2 times MIP, not the 0.15-0.5 of MIP a bridged gap shows, and the very last point is one of the highest in that stretch, so there is no collapse for a fit to have bridged. Nothing is attached at the stop in any of the three azimuths - no arm, no kink, the chain agrees with n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0 - so this is STM_ONLY, not STM_MICHEL. 386016 is a 2-point 0.7 cm speck 21.1 cm past the stop, 11 cm off the body line, forward at cos_fwd +0.88, detached across a clean gap: gamma, and the chain independently offers it as a 2.62 MeV capture gamma. 385015 is a second 2-point speck at 21.4 cm but backward at cos_fwd -0.75 and only 9.8 cm off the chord, i.e. on the muon side rather than past the stop, and in an unrelated direction from 386016 (about 111 deg apart), so delta / other. 383014 is 4 points 50 cm back at cos_fwd -0.89, body activity. Confidence is medium because the V projection shows a hatched dead-channel band immediately beyond the track end, so the terminal charge scale is not above suspicion, and because the peak sits about 10 cm before the fit end rather than at it.

notes: Unambiguous through-goer: flat 3e4 plateau to the last point plus a fit end 3.1 cm from the x face. Undershoot check run - nothing short, forward and several-times-MIP past the fit end. C430 is a 21-point 7.2 cm streak 44.5 cm off the muon line and is almost certainly a different object entirely.
evidence: 719 cm of chain spanning essentially the whole detector in drift: enters 11.4 cm from the x face at (-329,203,17) and the fit end is at (337,172,56), only 3.1 cm from the far x face, so this crosses from one anode side to the other. The profile is dead flat over the last 25 cm at 2.6-4.0e4 with no hint of a lift off that level, no approach to the muon reference curve, and the single elevated point at s = 7 (5.7e4) is isolated scatter; the last two points before the fit end are near zero and are fit points with no measured charge, which the rubric says to ignore. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot be at 3e4 in its last 25 cm, so this is a through-goer, and the 3.1 cm face distance says exactly where it went. The three stop azimuths show the track running straight into the star with nothing attached and nothing past it - the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma), and it rejects the object three ways (no_bragg, shape_flat, plateau_off_mip). f_meas shows a clean nearly-vertical trace in all three planes with the dead-channel bands well away from the track and measured matching predicted. Because there is no stop, gamma and michel are undefined here: 130034 (a 12-point pdg-11 shower piece 190 cm back on the body line) and the two far pieces 429055 (2 points, 46 cm out, 33 cm off-axis) and C430 (21 points, 49 cm out, 44 cm off-axis, visible as a faint separate streak in the d and e azimuths) are all delta / other, and the fourteen fitted chain segments are muon.

notes: MESSY convention applied: all 21 rows delta / other, kind none. Chain reject is profile_sparse and only 420 image points cover a claimed 170 cm. Competing reading: a very sparse THRU (the profile is flat, but at 0.1 of MIP rather than on the MIP plateau, and the fit path is not one-dimensional), which is why confidence is medium. No pin move - there is no stop to move.
evidence: This is not one track. The chain claims 170.3 cm but the entry-to-stop chord is only 84.9 cm, a factor two, and the chain segments revisit the same distance shell repeatedly - 66037 spans 45.8-63.7 cm from the stop while 66011 (57.4-61.6), 66012 (57.4-59.2) and 66009 (58.1-75.1) all sit inside or across that same band, so the fit doubles back on itself rather than running out along a spine. Twenty-one drawn objects, thirteen of them unassigned and typed pdg 11 or pdg 11 shower, sit 14-48 cm off the entry-stop chord. The dQ/dx panel is decisive: the fitted chain from the stop out to 25 cm sits flat at 5-9e3 e/cm, roughly a tenth of MIP, and most other segments are 3-15e3; only 66009 (52388) and 66010 (25387) carry anything muon-like. f_meas shows the whole stop region as bottom-of-scale navy in all three planes, so that is real absence of charge, not a projection effect. a_proj_full shows the entire object as a compact blob about 50 cm across at Z 60-115, Y -180 to -130, X 280-340, hard against the x wall (entry d_face 0.1 cm), packed with vertex squares; b and d show it decomposing into at least three disconnected structures - the purple/orange line running to the star, a separate L-shaped 60 cm green piece 30-60 cm below it, and an isolated amber stub. The chain range KE of 402 MeV disagrees with dQ/dx (151 MeV) and with MCS (34.5 MeV at ambiguity 1.00), which is what a wandering fit through a fragmented blob looks like. With no identified stop, the rubric convention applies and every row is tagged delta / other. Medium rather than high because near the stop the c and e azimuths do show a fairly linear purple spine, so a reading in which one sparse through-going track is buried in the junk is not fully excluded.

notes: Flat-to-zero profile at the fit end with no rise; no visible continuation and no face nearby, which the rubric says still gives THRU. Confidence is medium because the charge on this object is close to unusable - 0.27 image points per cm and a prolonged W projection - so the absence of a Bragg rests on the SHAPE (a two-sided symmetric hump 30 cm back) rather than on absolute charge. Competing reading: a huge overshoot in which the real stop is near s = 15-20 and the last 15 cm is bridged fit; rejected because the hump falls to zero on its far side too, which a Bragg cannot do. Undershoot check run on 74003 and rejected on charge.
evidence: A 202 cm chain running almost purely in Y, from (103,-34,280) 18.4 cm inside the z face to (112,-227,261), 37.8 cm from the z face - so the fit end is well away from any wall. The object is starved of charge: 107 chain points but only 54 image points at full density over 202 cm, about 0.27 points per cm against 2.5-7 per cm on the other items in this chunk, and the track lies nearly parallel to the collection wires (the W panel of f_meas compresses the whole 200 cm into roughly 20 channels), so W is prolonged and dQ/dx is barely measurable. What the profile shows is a single smooth, near-symmetric hump peaking at 4.7e4 around s = 30 and falling to zero on BOTH sides - to about 0.2e4 by s = 12 and to zero by s = 47 - with nothing but 0-1.7e4 over the last 15 cm before the fit end and nothing again from 47 to 100 cm. A Bragg peak is one-sided: it rises into the stop and ends there. A symmetric hump 30 cm back is a localised deposit that the fit line happens to pass through, not a Bragg, so there is no rise at the fit end and the operative test gives THRU; the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. The three azimuths show a sparse straight amber line with a faint pale point cloud a few cm past the fit end and nothing else - no arm, no kink, no dots, and the chain agrees (no daughter, n_dots 0, no capture gamma). 74003 is the 7.3 cm chain segment lying straight ahead of the fit end at cos_fwd +0.98; I checked it against the undershoot signature and it fails on the load-bearing clause - it carries 3.9e3 e/cm, a fifteenth of MIP, not the several-times-MIP a mis-cut muon tip shows, so it is chain body, not a hidden stop. 257001 is a 2-point 0.1 cm speck 34.9 cm out and 34.8 cm off the chord; with no stop it cannot be a gamma, so delta / other.

notes: Unambiguous exiting through-goer: fit end 1.0 cm from the x face, in_fv 0, flat 1-5e4 profile to the last point. Undershoot check run - nothing short, forward and several-times-MIP past the fit end; the two far objects are 2-5 point specks 40-54 cm out at 0.7-1.8e4.
evidence: 738 cm of chain crossing the detector in drift: it enters 17.2 cm inside the x face at (-323,86,144) and the fit end is at (339,5,248), 1.0 cm from the far x face and outside the fiducial volume (in_fv 0). The profile over the last 30 cm is flat and scattered between 1e4 and 5e4 with no lift at all toward the fit end, nowhere near the muon reference curve which is at 6e4 by 30 cm and climbing; a single 7.6e4 point at s = 9 is isolated scatter in a band whose bulk sits at 2-3e4. There is no rise, the last points are among the lowest on the track, and the fit end is 1 cm from a wall, so this is an exiting through-goer and the chain rejects it four ways (no_bragg, shape_flat, stop_near_boundary, plateau_off_mip). The three azimuths show a straight uninterrupted line running into the star with a couple of faint specks beyond it and nothing attached; the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. f_meas shows the trace running down into a dead-channel band in U at the very end, which is consistent with an exit and is another reason the terminal charge is low. Because there is no stop, gamma and michel are undefined: 337034 (5 points, 53.7 cm out, 45 cm off the chord), 338035 (2 points, 41.7 cm out, 40.6 cm off) and 91024 (a 9-point pdg-11 piece 142 cm back sitting 3.5 cm off the body line) are all delta / other, and the ten fitted chain segments are muon.

notes: Undershoot check run: the forward pieces past the fit end carry 1.2-1.8e4 e/cm, a fifth to a third of MIP, so they fail the load-bearing several-times-MIP clause and are a real Michel, not a mis-cut muon tip; the chain peak is at the fit end, not past it. One 1.37e5 point sits at 3 cm on the non-chain side - a single point, not a piece, so it does not change the reading. The chain accepts this as STM. Hardest sub-call was 131011/134013 gamma versus delta, which flips the kind between attached and both; I went gamma because both sit within 3 deg of the Michel arm direction while the other three specks are scattered elsewhere.
evidence: 100.6 cm visibly curved chain entering 0.4 cm from the y face at (-167,336,78) and stopping at (-249,312,123), 24.5 cm from the nearest face. The profile is textbook: it sits at 6e4 out at 25 cm, climbs to 8e4 by 8-15 cm, 9.4e4 by 4-6 cm, and 1.11-1.24e5 in the last 2 cm, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve the whole way without crossing it, with the peak at the fit end itself - so the pin stays where it is and there is nothing bridged. Past the stop, two pieces sit together at 3-7 cm carrying 1.2e4 and 1.8e4 e/cm, a fifth to a third of MIP: 129009 (13 points, 7.5 cm, the chain 10.8 MeV Michel core, bridged across 3.34 cm of empty space because the 3-D clustering split it off) and 37007 (16 points, 9.3 cm, chain-typed pdg 11 shower, unassigned). Both point the same way (cos to the arm 1.00 and 0.99) and the d and e azimuths show them as one short cyan arm leaving the stop at a clear angle away from the amber muon body, which is curving the other way - a muon at 1.24e5 cannot continue at a fifth of MIP, so both are the electron and both are tagged michel. Two faint specks lie along that arm direction and detached from it: 131011 (4 points, 1.6 cm, 5.1e4) at 31.4 cm with cos 0.96 to the arm, and 134013 (2 points, 0.1 cm, 1.8e4) at 40.5 cm with cos 0.97 - a clean charge-free gap separates both from the 7.5 cm core, so by the attachment tie-break they are detached dots, gamma. The remaining three are in unrelated directions and go to delta / other: 130010 and 132012 sit together 20.7 cm out at cos -0.3 to the arm and cos_fwd -0.6/-0.72, hugging the body side in the c azimuth, and 135014 is 49 cm out on the opposite side at cos -0.67. cos_fwd is only advisory here because the track is visibly curved, so I judged all of these off the three azimuths and the arm-relative angles. No dead-channel band touches the stop in any plane and measured matches predicted.

notes: No rise above the track own plateau at the fit end - the terminal 2.2e4 equals the 2e4 far plateau and the only structure is a dip 4-10 cm back. Confidence is medium because the U plane is entirely dead across this track and the absolute charge scale is therefore meaningless; the call rests on the scale-free shape. Competing reading: a genuine stopper whose Bragg is invisible because U is dead - a 54 cm range would want about 130 MeV and the chain range KE is 154 MeV - but V and W alone should still show a terminal lift and they show a dip instead. Undershoot check run: nothing at all is drawn past the fit end, so there is no forward tip to test.
evidence: A single drawn object: 54.5 cm of chain entering 0.1 cm from the y face at (102,-336,198) and ending at (102,-307,157), 29.4 cm from the nearest face, with x essentially constant (102.4 to 102.0), so the track lies in a plane of fixed drift depth. The whole profile sits between 0.5e4 and 2.4e4, a tenth to a half of MIP, and it is flat in the sense that matters: the far stretch from 17 to 30 cm sits at about 2e4 and the last point before the fit end is 2.2e4, so there is no rise above the track own plateau. What there is instead is a DIP - the profile falls to 0.5e4 around s = 4-5 and recovers to 1e4 by s = 10 - which is the opposite shape from a Bragg and matches the imaging rather than the physics. f_meas explains the suppressed scale: the entire track sits inside a wide hatched dead-channel band in U (the U blob spans only about 15 channels, all of it inside the band), so charge is coming from V and W alone, and the object has only 84 image points over 54.5 cm. The three azimuths show a single clean track with a scattering kink about 8 cm before the end, running into the star with nothing attached and nothing past it; the chain agrees (no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma) and rejects the object as no_bragg, shape_flat and plateau_off_mip. With no rise at the fit end the operative test gives THRU and the cluster ended where the imaging ran out; the sole row, the fitted chain segment 62000, is muon and the kind is none.

notes: THRU on the operative test: the last 10 cm into the fit end is flat at 0.7-1.9e4, below the track own 2-2.7e4 plateau. Confidence is medium because the drawn object is a three-prong vertex and the fit end is the tip of the SHORTEST prong, so THRU here means the underlying track passes through this region rather than that a single clean cosmic was traced end to end; which pair of prongs is the real track (blue-amber, which are roughly collinear, or purple-amber, which is what the chain chose) is not resolvable from these frames. Competing reading rejected: a large overshoot with the true stop at the vertex 18 cm back and the amber prong as the Michel - rejected because the elevated points at s = 13-17 coincide with five overlapping chain segments at the vertex, so they are prong pile-up rather than a Bragg peak. Undershoot check run: nothing is drawn past the fit end.
evidence: The topology decides this one. b, c and d all show a clean three-prong vertex: a purple/magenta prong about 50 cm long running down to the entry marker 0.7 cm from the z face, a blue prong about 45 cm long leaving the same vertex, and a short amber prong about 17 cm long running the other way to the star, which is the fit end, 46.2 cm from the nearest face. The chain threaded purple then amber and left the blue prong unassigned as 64001 (77 points, 45.8 cm, 2.7e4 e/cm, 28.6 cm off the chord), which is the most substantial piece in the picture. Along the amber prong the profile falls rather than rises: 64004 (10.0-17.9 cm from the fit end) sits at 3.3e4 and 64005 (0-10.0 cm, the last stretch into the star) at 1.2e4, and the panel shows the last 10 cm flat between 0.7e4 and 1.9e4 with no lift at all. The elevated points at s = 13-17 (2.1, 3.4, 4.1, 4.9, 5.5e4 stacked at almost the same arc length) are not a Bragg peak - they sit exactly where five chain segments (64011, 64013, 64015, 64017, 64032) pile up in the 13-24 cm band at 13-18 cm off the chord, i.e. at the vertex where the prongs overlap and the charge per unit length is naturally doubled. Against the track own depressed plateau of about 2-2.7e4 the terminal 1.2e4 is below, not above, so there is no rise at the fit end and the operative test gives THRU. The object is also poorly imaged - 99 image points over a 96 cm claimed chain, about 1 per cm - and the chain rejects it as no_bragg, shape_flat and plateau_off_mip with MCS at 34.5 MeV against a range KE of 243 MeV at ambiguity 1.00, which is what a fit threading a branch point looks like. Nothing is attached past the star in any azimuth. With no stop, the eight fitted chain segments are muon and the two unassigned pieces (64001 and the 7-point 64006 at 10-13 cm) are delta / other.

notes: Undershoot check run and rejected on the load-bearing clause: 81011 has exactly the undershoot geometry (2.3 cm, dead ahead, cos_fwd +0.91, perp 0.4 cm from the muon line) but carries 4.6e4 e/cm, at MIP rather than the several-times-MIP a mis-cut muon tip shows, and the muon own Bragg points at 1.24-1.30e5 are already on the chain side of the pin. So the pin stays and the arm is a real Michel. Confidence is medium only because of 400009: verdict STM_MICHEL is not in doubt, but the michel_kind hinges on whether that 3-point speck across a 5 cm gap is a detached dot (gamma, kind both) or the electron own shower continuing (michel, kind attached). I applied the rubric attachment tie-break and called it gamma; a scanner who read the gap as part of the arm would file this as attached.
evidence: 105.6 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the x face at (340,-270,114) and stopping at (243,-290,125), 46.8 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained. The profile is a clean Bragg: about 5e4 out beyond 15 cm, 6-7e4 at 6-10 cm, 8.3-9.0e4 at 1-5 cm, with two points at 1.24e5 and 1.30e5 in the last 5 cm, the higher of them sitting on the fit end itself - so the peak is AT the pin and there is nothing to move. f_meas confirms it independently: the trace runs dark blue up the whole track and terminates in a bright orange-red blob at the top, i.e. the highest charge on the object is its last centimetres, with no dead-channel band anywhere near. Past that stop, three pieces make an arm of about 8.4 cm - 81011 (5 points, 2.3 cm, 4.6e4, dead ahead at cos_fwd +0.91), 81003 (11 points, 6.0 cm, 5.1e4, cos_fwd +0.35) and 81001 (6 points, 3.3 cm, 6.3e4, chain-typed pdg 11 shower, cos_fwd +0.29) - all sitting at 4.6-6.3e4, i.e. at MIP. A muon that has just peaked at 1.24e5 cannot continue at MIP, so the arm is a second particle, and 8.4 cm is the right range for a low-tens-of-MeV electron; the c and d azimuths show it leaving the star at a sharp bend away from the green muon body, while e projects it back onto the body line, which is exactly the one-view-fakes-it trap, so I took the bend from the other two. All three are tagged michel even though the chain types the first two pdg 13, because within 10 cm of the stop direction does not discriminate and the charge does. 400009 is a 3-point 1.4 cm speck at 13.5-14.1 cm carrying 2.0e4, separated from the far end of the arm by about 5 cm of charge-free space (the chain itself calls it bridged across 13.51 cm of empty space): by the attachment tie-break a detached compact dot is a gamma however close it sits, so gamma. 399008 is a 3-point speck 42.5 cm back at cos_fwd -0.88 on the muon body line, delta / other.

notes: THRU with a fit end 64.9 cm from every face and no visible continuation - the rubric explicit case. The profile is not merely flat, it declines to about 0.6 of the plateau over the last 12 cm, which is the opposite of a Bragg, so I did not reach for UNCLEAR. Overshoot considered: the peak-then-fall shape is superficially the signature, but the fall is gentle, ends at 0.6 of the plateau rather than the 0.15-0.5 band, and there is no Michel or blob anywhere past the end for a fit to have bridged to. Undershoot check run: nothing is drawn past the fit end.
evidence: 160.9 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the z face at (135,-174,298) and ending at (263,-127,234), 64.9 cm from the nearest face - so this one really does end deep inside the volume, and the containment number is not what decides it. The profile does: it sits at 4.5-5.3e4 from 13 to 30 cm, then FALLS toward the fit end, 3.2-4.2e4 over 8-12 cm and 3.0-3.7e4 over the last 8 cm, with two low points at 2.3e4 and 1.5e4 around s = 2 and a single isolated 7.9e4 point at s = 1. The last 12 cm therefore sits at about 0.6 of the track own plateau while the muon reference curve at that range is climbing through 6e4 towards 1.6e5 - the profile is going the wrong way, and a muon at its Bragg peak cannot be at 3e4. Imaging quality is good here (787 image points over 161 cm, about 5 per cm), so this is a trustworthy profile, not a charge-loss artefact; f_meas shows a clean straight trace in all three planes with no dead-channel band at the terminating end and measured matching predicted along its whole length. All three azimuths show one straight uninterrupted track running into the star with nothing attached and nothing past it - a single drawn object, and the chain reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma while rejecting the object as no_bragg and shape_flat. MCS puts the momentum at 644 MeV against 382 from range, which is what a truncated through-goer looks like. The cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out; the sole row, chain segment 84001, is muon and the kind is none.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face contact at the stop end (18.9 cm) and no dead region at the stop in U/V/W - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out, which the rubric says is still THRU. Elevated but falling charge 21-32 cm back is body/delta activity, not a Bragg rise. Neighbouring cluster 31's arc lies 40 cm off and is not collinear, so this is not called FRAG.
evidence: A short 33.8 cm chain in the far z corner: the fit's first point sits 0.6 cm from the z face and the pinned stop is 18.9 cm from it (x 45.1, y 180.8), so the interior end is well clear of every wall. The dQ/dx panel, upscaled 4x, shows the chain flat over the whole last 15 cm out of the stop, scattering between 3.3e4 and 6e4 e/cm, i.e. sitting on or just under the solid muon reference curve's 5.4e4 asymptote while that curve climbs through 8e4 and on to 1.6e5 inside s = 12 cm. There is no rise of any shape at s = 0; a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot do that, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. The only elevated charge is a scattered band 21-32 cm back up the chain, topping at 1.24e5 at s = 22 and falling back to 6.5-8.8e4 by s = 31-33, which is delta-like activity in the middle of the body and not a terminal rise into either end (and that end is at the face anyway). Nothing in the object table has a positive cos_fwd, so there is no forward tip and the undershoot case is excluded outright. Past/behind the stop: S32005 is an 11-point 6.3 cm shower piece at 14-18 cm, cos_fwd -1.0, lying straight on the muon body line at only 1.4e4 e/cm - body activity, delta / other; the 22.4 cm arc S31006 at 40-43 cm and the three 2-3 point specks at 30-34 cm all sit at cos_fwd -0.81 to -0.97 and, in the three azimuths, belong to a visibly separate curved track from the neighbouring cluster 31, so they are a different object entirely. The chain's own verdict agrees independently (is_stm 0, reject shape_flat). What made it hard is the mid-body charge excursion, which on a small plot could be mistaken for a peak at the far end.

notes: OVERSHOOT: fit runs about 2.2 cm past the muon's real stop. The Bragg peak is at s = 3.1 (1.57e5) and the last five chain points collapse to 1.3-4.3e4; pin moved to rr 2.2. The collapse falls inside the single chain row 81004, which cannot be split - the row is tagged muon for the 204 cm that is muon, and its last 2.2 cm is the bridge into the Michel. This overshoot is why the chain reports no_bragg + shape_flat and is_stm 0.
evidence: A 206.4 cm cosmic that enters 0.8 cm from the z face at y 177 and curves down to a fit end 37.1 cm from the x wall (y 308, z 108 clear), so the stop is genuinely interior. Upscaled, the profile is textbook: a 5.5e4 plateau from s = 100 in, lifting off the solid muon curve's asymptote at about s = 25, 6.5e4 by s = 15-20, 8-9e4 at s = 6-8, 1.0-1.2e5 at s = 5-11 and a 1.57e5 peak at s = 3.1 - three times MIP and the highest point on the plot. Then it collapses: the five chain points inside s = 2.3 read 8.4e4, 1.3e4, 2.0e4, 3.3e4, 3.9e4, 4.3e4 at s = 2.3, 2.0, 1.3, 0.7, 0.5, 0.0, i.e. a sustained fall to a quarter of MIP over the fit's last 2.2 cm. That is the owner's overshoot signature - the fit bridging a small gap between the muon's real stop and the electron - not one low endpoint, so I move the pin to the junction at 2.2 cm and the last 2.2 cm of the chain row is bridge, not muon. Past the stop an arm leaves the shared vertex 81003 at an 82 deg kink: 81006, 14 points over 9.4 cm at 2.6e4 mean and visibly rising outward from 3e3 near the vertex, then 81005, 9 points over 4.9 cm at 5.5e4, 10.9 cm out and 10.9 cm off the muon body line. A muon at a 1.57e5 Bragg peak cannot continue at or below MIP, and 14 cm is the right range for the quoted 22 MeV electron, so both pieces are the Michel. S280007, 5 points over 2.4 cm at 25.3 cm out, sits only 9-10 deg from the arm's own direction and 25.1 cm off the body line - detached, compact, on the Michel's side: gamma. S281008, a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 22.7 cm out, is 41 deg away from the arm and 12.3 cm behind the stop along the muon axis, an unrelated direction, so delta / other. Measured panels show real charge for the arm and both specks in U, V and W with no dead band anywhere near the stop. The chain's own no_bragg / shape_flat rejection is exactly what the overshoot predicts: it tested the collapsed last points instead of the peak.

notes: Both far specks are off the Michel's side, so michel_kind stays attached rather than both; 283007's 2.1e5 e/cm is a 0.2 cm dx artefact and not evidence of anything. Stop is only 7.9 cm from the x wall, which would be the reading for a THRU, but the last 15 cm follow the muon curve to a 1.22e5 last point, which a through-goer cannot do.
evidence: A short 34.7 cm chain in the low-z, high-x corner: it enters 0.6 cm from the z face and the fit end sits 7.9 cm from the x wall (z 18.4, y 293 clear), so the stop is close to one wall but not on it. Upscaled, the profile is a clean Bragg rise and does not collapse: the chain scatters 1e4-6.7e4 out at s = 20-35, climbs through 7.0e4 at s = 14 and 8.0-8.4e4 at s = 8-11, and the last five centimetres read 8.9e4, 9.3e4, 9.9e4, 1.14e5, 1.16e5 and 1.22e5, the maximum being the fit's own last point at s = 0.5. That is the muon curve's shape over the last 15 cm with no terminal dip, so the pin stays where the fit put it and this is not the overshoot case. Attached at the shared stop vertex 82002 is S82004, 9 points over 4.9 cm at a 126 deg kink, mean 4.3e4 e/cm with its charge falling monotonically outward from 9.4e4 at the vertex to 3.0e4 by 4 cm - at or below MIP where a muon at a 1.22e5 Bragg peak would be far above it, and the chain prices it at 13.1 MeV, which a ~10 MeV muon at its own Bragg peak cannot deliver as a delta ray. Its cos_fwd is -0.62, so the close-and-backward delta rule was the competing reading, but it is neither on the body line (the rule wants -0.85 or below) nor body-excluded by the chain, and the 3-D azimuths show a distinct teal arm leaving the star rather than charge lying along the body: Michel. S283007 is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 9.2 cm out at cos_fwd -0.90, 4.0 cm off the body line and 23 deg from the body direction; b_3d_wide shows its vertex square sitting directly on the muon body inside the image-point halo, and its 2.1e5 e/cm is a dx artefact of a 0.2 cm segment, so it is body activity: delta / other. S284008 is a 2-point 0.4 cm speck 45.7 cm out, 33.5 cm off the body line but 168 deg away from the Michel arm - the far side of the ring in an unrelated direction - so delta / other and not a capture gamma. A V-plane dead band crosses the track mid-way but charge continues past it on both sides, and U and W are clean at the stop, so nothing exits through a dead region.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs 3.3 cm past the muon's real stop; peak 1.16e5 at s = 4.0, terminal segment 32007 at 0.15 MIP. Pin moved to rr 3.3 and 32007 retagged michel per the rubric, though physically it looks more like the fit over-extending through sparse points than electron charge - the real Michel is the 6.8 cm arm 32009 off the same vertex. Not called FRAG: the upstream end is cut 2.2 cm from the cathode, which is where this drift volume ends, but no continuation is drawn in any frame so it is not visibly a fragment.
evidence: A 133.4 cm chain running almost purely along the drift at y about -80, z about 200: the fit's first point is 104.7 cm from the nearest outer face but only 2.2 cm from the cathode plane at x -3, and the fit end is deeply contained, 89.2 cm from the z wall and 212.7 cm from the anode face. Upscaled, the profile climbs off a 2-4e4 plateau at s = 70-133 through 5-6e4 at s = 20-40 and 7-9e4 at s = 5-15 to 1.0e5 at s = 4-8 and a 1.16e5 peak at s = 4.0, then collapses: the last five or six chain points inside s = 2.7 read 3.7e4 falling to 0.5-1.0e4, about 0.15 of MIP, which is exactly the mean 8157 e/cm the table gives for the terminal segment S32007 over its 3.4 cm. That is the owner's overshoot signature and here it has its own row, so the pin goes to the junction at 3.3 cm and S32007 is tagged michel rather than muon. The zoomed azimuths make the same picture directly: the yellow high-dQ/dx body ends at a vertex square, a dark near-charge-free stub carries on 3.3 cm to the star, and an orange arm S32009 - 12 points over 6.8 cm at 4.2e4 mean, below MIP, chain-typed pdg 11 shower - branches from that same vertex at about 50 deg with its own halo of image points. Measured from the corrected stop the arm sits about 3.2 cm out and 3.5 cm off the muon body line; its cos_fwd -0.62 is neither on the body line nor body-excluded by the chain, and a muon at a 1.16e5 Bragg peak has only some tens of MeV left and cannot throw a 6.8 cm delta, so the arm is the Michel. S236010 is a 2-point 0.6 cm speck 51.8 cm out at cos_fwd +0.20, 50.7 cm off the body line and 90 deg from the Michel arm on the forward side while the decay went backward - an unrelated direction, so delta / other, and michel_kind stays attached. U, V and W are all clear of dead bands at the stop, so nothing exits through one; the chain's profile_sparse rejection and its no daughter / n_stop_arms 0 answer are what the overshoot produces, since it tested the collapsed stub instead of the peak.

notes: Exits the active volume: stop 1.5 cm from the y face, 2.5 cm from the z face, in_fv 0, and a dead U band sits at the same channels as the fit end. Profile flat/saw-tooth to the last point with no rise of any shape.
evidence: A 144.3 cm chain that runs down the far corner of the detector: it enters 0.3 cm from the z face at y -213 and the fit end sits 1.5 cm from the y floor and 2.5 cm from the z wall, with in_fv 0 - the projections show it hugging the z 295 wall and terminating on the y -340 floor. Upscaled, the profile never rises: over the whole 100 cm shown it oscillates between 1.8e4 and 6e4 with a saw-tooth that dips to near zero around s = 24-28, and the last 10 cm out of the stop run 6e4 at s = 6-9 down to 3.0e4, 2.6e4 and 1.8e4 at s = 0-2, i.e. flat on and below the solid muon curve's 5.4e4 asymptote while that curve is climbing to 1.6e5. A stopping muon cannot leave its last centimetres at a third of MIP. One isolated 9.4e4 point sits on the origin line among neighbours at 1.8-3.0e4, which is scatter, not a peak with the muon curve's shape. Nothing at all sits past the fit end: the three zoomed azimuths show the amber selection band running straight into the star with no arm, no dot and no kink, and the chain reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The five non-chain rows are all body activity - S33009, S33012 and S33016 are pdg 11 shower pieces 47-73 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00, exactly on the muon line, and the two gamma-body-exclusion specks S238028 (5 points, 19.7 cm, 12.1 cm off the line) and S241029 (3 points, 35.6 cm, 27.9 cm off the line) are both behind the stop with no stop to be past. Since the verdict is THRU I tag every chain segment muon and everything else delta / other, and michel_kind is none. In U the amber end coincides with a wide dead band and in V with a narrower one, so the exit may be through dead channels as well as through the floor; either way the flat profile settles it. The chain agrees: no_bragg + stop_near_boundary.

notes: The two dots the chain calls the Michel are 11.2 cm away across empty space and worth 3.8 MeV, so they are detached dots (gamma) and do not promote this to STM_MICHEL. Tagging the further specks was the soft part: the 20-23 cm forward trio sits 44-61 deg from the closer dot and could be argued onto the decay side, but with specks in four unrelated directions the rubric's scattered case applies, and michel_kind is detached dots either way. Upstream end is cut 0.3 cm from the cathode, i.e. this is the half of the muon in one drift volume, but no continuation is drawn so I did not call it FRAG.
evidence: A 72.5 cm chain in the low-z corner: the fit's first point sits 0.3 cm from the cathode plane at x -3 and the fit end is comfortably interior, 41.3 cm from the z wall and 257-276 cm from the y and x faces. Upscaled, the Bragg rise is unambiguous and does not collapse - a 5.4e4 plateau at s = 50-72 lifting off the muon curve at about s = 40, 6.5-7e4 at s = 25-40, 8-9e4 through s = 3-20, then 1.13e5, 1.19e5 and a 1.63e5 point at s = 0.2, the maximum being the fit's own last point. So the pin stays put and this is neither the overshoot nor the undershoot case. Nothing is attached at the star: the three azimuths show the amber band running into it with no arm, no kink and no charge bridging out. What the chain offers as the Michel is two 2-point specks across 11.20 cm of empty space - S278006, 0.7 cm at 2.0e4 and 11.2 cm out with cos_fwd -0.08, and S275003, 0.1 cm at 8.0e4 and 11.8 cm out with cos_fwd +0.39 - together priced at 3.8 MeV. A 0.1 cm and a 0.7 cm speck across a clean charge-free 11 cm gap is not a 35 MeV electron; by the attachment tie-break they are detached dots, so I tag them gamma, the item stays STM_ONLY and michel_kind is detached dots. The remaining specks are scattered around the ring in at least four unrelated directions with no common axis: a forward trio S274002 / S276004 / S277005 at 20-23 cm and cos_fwd +0.60 to +0.64, S279007 at 27.4 cm backward at cos_fwd -0.62, S280008 and S281009 at 35.9 and 42.4 cm sitting on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.90 and -0.93, and S493010 at 122 cm which the chain itself calls too far from the stop - all delta / other. b_3d_wide shows exactly that: brown vertex squares sprayed on both sides of the track and beyond it, not a directional arm. The stop is clear of dead bands in W and V; the nearest U band sits just beyond the last channels, but the 1.63e5 peak settles the stop regardless.

notes: Competing readings weighed. THRU is live: the profile is flat to the last point at 0.15-0.27 MIP with no rise. I rejected it because the fit's last 22 cm crosses empty space rather than being a track that ran out of imaging, so there is no through-goer to describe. STM_MICHEL with the pin at about 22 cm was the third reading - the 1.55e5 spike as a Bragg peak and the shower pieces as the decay - and I rejected it because a 22 cm pin move is far outside the rubric's several-cm overshoot signature and the spike has no MIP approach in front of it (s = 33-98 scatters 0.2e4-5.5e4). Medium confidence for that reason. No pin recorded.
evidence: Twenty drawn objects in a compact 80 x 90 cm complex at high x, z 220-300, y -150 to -240; the fit's first point is 3.2 cm from the z face and its last point is 22.5 cm from the anode face. Eleven of the twenty rows are pdg 11 shower fragments and only 141 of 973 image points are on the chain, which is stitched from 8 segments whose mean dQ/dx runs 6219, 8570, 114822, 46556, 23100, 25927, 39917, 14623 - no monotone ordering of any kind. Upscaled, the profile confirms it: near zero (2e3-1.8e4) from s = 60 to 98, scattered 0.5-5.5e4 from s = 35 to 60, a 1.0-1.55e5 spike around s = 22-33, then 0.15-0.27 of MIP over the whole last 22 cm into the fit's last point. The big single-azimuth zoom shows what that means - the chain follows a haze of image points down from the upper right, bends at a vertex square and then runs to the star across empty space with essentially no image points under it, so the fit's tail is not a track at all. Three of the shower rows, S91018, S91019 and S91020, hold 79 points over 45.8 cm and sit 20-27 cm off the muon body line within 18 deg of each other, i.e. a second EM structure in its own direction rather than an arm off a stop, while S91013, S91016, S91023 and S91010 lie exactly on the body line at cos_fwd -0.98 to -1.00. MCS gives 33.7 MeV against 288.6 MeV from range with ambiguity 0.93 - the scattering says this is not a muon by a factor of eight and a half - and f_meas shows sparse blobs rather than continuous measured charge in all three planes. That is an EM blob broken into many pieces with a fit drawn across it, so there is no identified stop, every row is tagged delta / other by the MESSY convention and michel_kind is none. The chain's own shape_flat + profile_sparse rejection agrees that it found nothing muon-like at the end.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit's last 3.4 cm carry 0 to 1.7e4 e/cm after 9.2e4-1.0e5 just before, so the pin moves to rr 3.4; the collapse is inside the single chain row 98011 and cannot be split, which is stated in the evidence. Here the low-charge tail is probably the fit running into the Michel blob where the charge is attributed to the shower clusters rather than a true empty gap - either way the muon's own charge stops 3.4 cm short of the fit end. The michel-vs-gamma line was drawn at the 5 cm gap in front of 486013; 485012's 2.7 cm gap is ordinary shower patchiness.
evidence: A short 16.2 cm chain that enters 0.2 cm from the anode face at x 339.7 and ends 13.8 cm inside it, 64.8 cm from the y wall and 44.1 cm from the z wall. Sixteen centimetres is entirely inside the Bragg region for a 65 MeV muon and the profile behaves like it: upscaled, every chain point from s = 16 down to s = 3.8 sits above the solid muon curve at 1.5-2 times MIP - 1.03e5 at s = 16, 8.7e4 at s = 11, 8.0-8.6e4 at s = 6-9, 9.2e4 to 1.0e5 at s = 3-5 - which is a rise off the plateau in the curve's own shape, not a flat MIP track. Then the fit's last 3.4 cm collapse: six points at s = 3.0, 2.3, 2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.1 read 1.7e4, 1.0e4, 0.6e4, 0.2e4 and two at zero, so I move the pin to the junction at 3.4 cm; the collapse falls inside the single chain row S98011, which is tagged muon for the 12.8 cm that is muon while its last 3.4 cm is the bridge. What sits past the stop is unmistakable in the zoomed azimuths: a fan of dotted segments and vertex squares leaves the star and spreads over about 20 cm, and the object table matches it - S98007 (8 points, 4.5 cm, 2.0e4) attached at d_min 0, then S98008, S98006, S98009 and S98010 out to 11.8 cm, 64 points and 36 cm of segments in all, every one of them at 0.6e4 to 2.2e4 e/cm, i.e. well below MIP where a muon at its own Bragg peak would be far above it. All five sit 60-80 deg off the muon body direction and within 25 deg of each other, so this is one electron shower, not scattered body activity: michel. S485012, 6 points over 3.0 cm at 14.5-15.7 cm and 13.9 cm off the body line, lies 3-10 deg from that same shower axis across only a 2.7 cm gap and the chain excludes it as Michel body, so I keep it in the shower. S486013 is different: 3 points over 1.4 cm at 20.6-21.6 cm, 20.0 cm off the body line, separated from the nearest shower piece by a clean 5 cm gap - a detached compact dot on the Michel's side, so gamma, and michel_kind is both. Measured charge for the muon and the whole fan is real in U, V and W; V and W are clear of dead bands at the stop. The chain's shape_flat + profile_sparse rejection is what the terminal collapse produces.

notes: STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL because there is genuinely nothing past the stop - the nearest object of any kind is 28 cm back along the body. The body outside 15 cm is fragmented and sits well below MIP (plateau_off_mip, MCS/range factor 4.4), which is a data-quality oddity of the outer track and not a reason to doubt an 11 cm rise to 1.45e5 at the end. Not called MESSY: only one EM piece in the table and the fragments are collinear.
evidence: An 80.8 cm chain of seven segments entering 8.8 cm from the z face and ending deep inside - 49.8 cm from the z wall, 64.4 cm from the anode face, 264 cm from the y wall. Upscaled, the last 11 cm are a clean Bragg rise that tracks the solid muon curve: 6.3e4 at s = 11, 7.9e4 at s = 7, 9.4-9.9e4 at s = 3-4, 1.05-1.12e5 at s = 1-5 and 1.45e5 at the fit's own last point, with a 1.50e5 point at s = 6 - the maximum is at the end and there is no terminal dip, so the pin stays where the fit put it. Beyond s = 15 the chain saw-tooths between 0.4e4 and 5.7e4, well under MIP, which is why the chain rejects it as plateau_off_mip and why MCS (48.1 MeV) disagrees with range (210.5 MeV, amb 0.90); b_3d_wide shows the body broken into three roughly collinear pieces with gaps, so that outer stretch is poorly imaged rather than muon-like, but it does not touch the reading at the stop. Nothing at all sits past the fit end: the zoomed azimuths show the yellow-orange terminal segment running into the star with a thin halo of image points and clear white space beyond it in all three views, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. The nearest non-chain object S108023 is a pdg 11 piece 28-32 cm back at cos_fwd -0.97, only 7.3 cm off the body line - body activity. The five remaining specks are all behind the stop when projected on the muon axis (along -35 to -42 cm for S530031, S829032, S526029 and S528030, -6.5 cm for S523028) and S530031 and S829032 sit on the body line at cos_fwd -0.94 and -0.90; the two at 58-59 cm lie 21 deg from each other but 92-111 deg from S523028, i.e. scattered in unrelated directions around the ring with no decay to be on the side of. So every one of them is delta / other and michel_kind is none. A V-plane dead band runs through the stop channels, but U and W both show the charge simply ending there with nothing above it in time, so the stop is not a dead-region exit.

notes: OVERSHOOT: peak 1.11e5 at s = 4.1, then six points at 0.5e4-4.7e4 over the last 3.6 cm; pin moved to rr 3.6. The collapse is a little mixed - four points at about 0.15 MIP with two at 0.8 MIP among them - rather than monotone, but every one of them is far below the 1.1e5 immediately before, so the signature holds either way. The collapse is inside the single row 110001 and the split is stated in the evidence. Moving the stop back makes both dots farther away, not closer, so it does not promote them.
evidence: A clean 155.6 cm single track: it enters 0.5 cm from the z face at x 244 and runs mostly across the drift to a fit end at y 269, 67.3 cm from the y wall, 72.4 cm from z and 111 cm from the cathode, so the stop is deeply interior. The three azimuths show one continuous dQ/dx-coloured spine with a tight image-point halo and no branch anywhere - nothing is attached at the star. Upscaled, the profile is the best Bragg rise in my twelve: a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s = 100 in, lifting off the muon curve at about s = 25, 6-7e4 at s = 15-25, 6.7-8.1e4 at s = 6.5-13, 8.9-9.2e4 at s = 5.6-6.1, 9.9e4 at s = 4.9 and 1.08-1.11e5 at s = 4.1-4.5. Then it collapses over the fit's last 3.6 cm: six points at s = 0.1 to 3.1 read 4.2e4, four at 0.5-1.0e4, and 4.7e4, all far under the muon curve's 9.5-1.35e5 there, so this is the owner's overshoot and I move the pin to 3.6 cm. The collapse falls inside the single terminal row S110001 (0-6.87 cm, mean 74627), which cannot be split: it is tagged muon because its charge is dominated by the 1.1e5 peak half, and its last 3.6 cm is the bridge. Past the stop there are only two dots, and both are detached across empty space: S536004, 2 points over 0.1 cm at 10.9 cm from the fit end (12.6 cm from the corrected stop), cos_fwd +0.45, 9.7 cm off the body line, which the chain offers as the Michel at 0.2 MeV; and S535003, 2 points over 0.1 cm at 17.9 cm, cos_fwd +0.62, 14.1 cm off the line, which the chain calls a capture gamma at 0.52 MeV. A 0.1 cm two-point dot across an 11 cm charge-free gap is not a 35 MeV electron, so by the attachment tie-break both are detached dots - gamma - the item stays STM_ONLY and michel_kind is detached dots. The two dots are 108 deg apart as seen from the stop, so they are not one arm. Measured charge for the muon and both dots is real in U, V and W and there is no dead band at the stop in U or W. The chain's no_bragg / shape_flat rejection is what the terminal collapse produces - it tested the bridged points rather than the peak 4 cm earlier.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation and no face contact (94.7 cm), which the rubric says is still THRU - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Confidence medium rather than high because the track runs at constant drift x for its whole length, which makes every dQ/dx point a long-path estimate and produces the 20-25 cm saw-tooth; the terminal 6 cm at 0.5-1.7e4 is one trough among five, so the load-bearing statement is the absence of any rise over the last 25 cm, not the depth of the last dip. I did not move the pin: the 9.3e4 at s = 20-22 is 1.7x MIP among 4-7e4 neighbours, not a Bragg peak, and 20 cm is far outside the several-cm overshoot signature.
evidence: A 152.6 cm track that enters 3.5 cm from the z face at y -216 and ends 94.7 cm from the z wall, 132.6 cm from the anode and 214 cm from the y wall, so the fit end is as deeply contained as anything in this chunk. The projections show why the charge is odd: it runs at essentially constant drift coordinate x 207 through the whole 152 cm, moving only in y and z, and f_meas confirms it lies in a 25-slice band of time across a few hundred channels. Upscaled, the profile is a saw-tooth between 0.5e4 and 7e4 with troughs recurring every 20-25 cm (at s = 0-6, 26, 34-42, 62-68, 84, 92) and no monotone structure anywhere; the two highest points, 8.8e4 and 9.3e4 at s = 20-22, sit among neighbours at 4-7e4 and are not a peak with the muon curve's shape. Over the last 25 cm the level is 4-7e4, i.e. at or below the solid curve's MIP asymptote while that curve climbs through 8e4 and on to 1.6e5, and the fit's final 6 cm land in one of the troughs at 0.5-1.7e4. There is no rise of any kind at the fit end, which is the operative THRU test, and a stopping muon cannot leave its last 25 cm on the plateau. Independent support: MCS gives 726.9 MeV against 363.6 MeV from range (amb 0.78), i.e. the track is straighter than a muon of that residual range would be, so it did not stop. Nothing sits past the fit end - the zoomed azimuths show the amber band running into the star with the image-point halo thinning out and clear space beyond, and the chain reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. All five non-chain rows lie exactly on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.99 to -1.00, between 48 and 133 cm back (S80007, S80010, S80015, S80020, S80021, several at 500-2700 e/cm), so they are body activity along the track; on a THRU item they are all delta / other and michel_kind is none. No dead band coincides with the fit end in U or V; W has a channel gap 100 channels away from it. The chain's own no_bragg + shape_flat rejection agrees.

notes: Pin left at the fit's last point: the maximum of the profile IS the last point (1.32e5) with a monotone 15 cm approach, which is the opposite of the overshoot signature. The judgement call was the five far specks - two of them are forward and clear of the body, which the bare gamma rule would take, but both are more than 110 deg from the Michel arm and the set as a whole is sprayed around the 45 cm ring, so I applied the scattered-directions case and kept michel_kind at attached.
evidence: A downgoing 68.5 cm cosmic: it enters 0.9 cm from the top y face at y 335 and the fit end sits 45.1 cm below it, 138 cm from the anode and 137 cm from the z wall, so the stop is interior. Upscaled, the last 15 cm are a textbook rise that follows the solid muon curve and peaks at the fit's own last point: 5.4-6.3e4 at s = 13-15, 7.1-7.6e4 at s = 12, 8.1-9.2e4 at s = 7-11, 9.5-1.02e5 at s = 5-8, 1.05-1.10e5 at s = 3-5, 1.25e5 at s = 1.5 and 1.32e5 at s = 0.7 - the maximum is the final point, there is no terminal dip and no forward high-charge tip, so neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies and the pin stays put. (The chain does have a low trough of 0.5-2e4 around s = 18-32, which is the same periodic dQ/dx pathology that earns the plateau_off_mip rejection; it is 20 cm back and does not touch the stop.) Attached at the shared stop vertex 88004 is S88008, 18 points over 10.4 cm at an 88 deg kink, mean 5.6e4 e/cm, which the chain prices at 24.5 MeV over a 32.6 cm range. A muon sitting at a 1.32e5 Bragg peak has a few tens of MeV left and cannot continue at MIP, so that arm is a second particle, and 10 cm at MIP is exactly a ~25 MeV electron: Michel. The three azimuths show it directly - a blue arm leaving the star at right angles to the amber body and running to its own vertex square, with the muon's image-point halo ending at the star. The five remaining rows are 2-3 point specks at 42-47 cm scattered around the ring in unrelated directions: S379010, S380011 and S381012 sit on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.89, -0.87 and -0.89, while S378009 and S382013 are forward (cos_fwd +0.57 and +0.94) but lie 114 and 150 deg away from the Michel arm, i.e. on the opposite side of the stop from the decay. None is on the Michel's side, so all five are delta / other and michel_kind is attached rather than both. Charge for the muon, the arm and the specks is real in U, V and W, and U and W are clear of dead bands at the stop.

notes: THRU taken on the profile alone - no visible continuation, no face, no dead-region exit at the stop; the cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out. Near-miss undershoot checked and rejected: 421013 has dqdx 95227 and cos_fwd 0.93, both inside the undershoot window, but dstop 35.8 cm fails the "a couple of cm" clause by an order of magnitude, so it is not an undershoot tip. Confidence medium because the s=8-25 excursion does look like a rise until it is compared with the s=72-95 band.
evidence: 193.7 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the y face at (315,336,74) and the fit ends at (310,215,179), 29.6 cm from the anode face, so containment is not the question here. The outward segment ladder is 90005 38.9e3 (50-160 cm back), 90009 8.4e3, 90010 17.0e3, 90007 46.3e3, 90001 37.3e3 over the last 6 cm - non-monotonic and the terminal segment is LOWER than the one before it, which is the opposite of a Bragg ladder. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the plateau sits at 4-5e4; points reach 7-9e4 between s=8 and s=25, but the same excursion band (1.21e5, 9.4e4, 8.5e4, 8.2e4, 7.7e4) recurs at s=72-95, so the terminal bump is not localized to the last 10-20 cm and is not a Bragg rise. Over the last 6 cm the profile falls to 1.2-5.2e4, a ~20 percent step down from the preceding segment mean, which the rubric calls ordinary scatter and not the sustained collapse that would move the pin (a collapse would be 0.15-0.5 of MIP; 37.3e3 against a 4-5e4 plateau is 0.75-0.9). The single ringed 1.02e5 marker sitting exactly on s=0 is one point and cannot make a rise either way. In all three 3-D azimuths nothing is attached past the star - the amber band there is the particle-flow selection overlay on segment 90001, not charge, and the same amber blob reappears unchanged in the f_meas difference panels, confirming it is an overlay. f_meas shows no dead region at the stop in any plane: nearest dead channels are ~40 (U), ~20 (V) and ~60 (W) away. The 896-point 230 cm C93 crossing the frame at a large angle in c/d/e is a different object, 19 cm off at closest. Verdict is THRU on the flat/falling profile alone; I cannot say where the muon went, which the rubric permits.

notes: THRU taken on the falling profile alone; no visible continuation past the fit end in any frame, no face reached, and only a marginal dead V wire nearby, so the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. LOW confidence, and the honest reason is that this row matches NEITHER named signature cleanly: the THRU signature the rubric describes is flat on the MIP plateau to the last point, whereas this profile FALLS (0.69 of the preceding segment); the falling terminus belongs to the pin-move section, which I tested and found too shallow for the 0.15-0.5 collapse band. So it sits between the two, and the near-drift-parallel geometry (the track spans only ~6 U and ~5 W channels over its whole length) is why the dQ/dx cannot settle it. The competing verdict is STM_ONLY / detached dots, because the two detached specks 12.1 and 17.6 cm out lie on the same side of the stop and would read as capture gammas past a real stop - the rubric warns that wanting gamma on a THRU means questioning the verdict. I stayed with THRU because the terminal segment mean is 0.69 of the preceding one and the charge maximum is mid-track; a stopping muon cannot do that. No undershoot: nothing forward within a couple of cm at several times MIP.
evidence: Short object: 21.5 cm of chain, 38 points, entering 0.2 cm from the x (anode) wall at (340,327,51) and running almost straight along drift to the fit end at (320,322,51), 14.6 cm from the y face. Outward ladder is 91008 60.3e3 over 2.9-17.9 cm back and 91003 41.6e3 over the last 4.3 cm, i.e. the terminal segment is 0.69 of the one before it - the profile FALLS into the fit end instead of rising. On the 4x g_dqdx the whole track occupies s=0-21: points sit at 1.3-6.3e4 over the last 6 cm and at 6.0-9.8e4 between s=7 and s=17, so the highest charge is in the middle of the track and there is no rise localized to the last 10-20 cm against the muon curve. I checked the overshoot reading (peak then collapse, move the pin) and rejected it: 41.6e3 against a 5-5.5e4 plateau is 0.76 of MIP, well above the 0.15-0.5 band the rubric gives for a fit-bridged collapse, and the high points are scattered over s=7-17 rather than forming one peak a few cm back. Past the fit end the chain offers 411009 as its Michel, but the three azimuths show it as a 4-point 1.8 cm dot sitting 12.1 cm out across a completely charge-free gap, well off the muon line and above it, with 412010 a 2-point 0.3 cm speck a further 5 cm out in the same direction (cos_fwd 0.13); 6.2 MeV would carry an electron ~3 cm, so nothing bridges that gap and there is no attached arm in any view. With no Bragg rise the operative test gives THRU, and the THRU convention then makes both dots delta / other. f_meas shows the track spanning only ~6 U, ~20 V and ~5 W channels over 60 time slices, and a dead V wire sits within a few channels of the stop region, so the dQ/dx here is measured on a poorly-conditioned near-drift-parallel geometry.

notes: No undershoot: the only forward object is 21.6 cm out at 27586 e/cm, i.e. below MIP and far outside the "couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5" window. No overshoot either; the terminal dip is one partial point. Chain rejects on shape_flat alone (no no_bragg), which is consistent with what the profile shows.
evidence: 194.6 cm chain, enters 4.0 cm from the y face at (70,-332,107) and stops deep at (-62,-220,177), 116 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not in doubt. The dQ/dx profile is the cleanest kind of Bragg evidence on this set: the plateau over s=60-100 sits at 5.5-7e4, the band lifts to 7-9e4 over s=20-40, to a coherent group of ten points at 1.0-1.1e5 over s=3-13, and to 1.17e5 and 1.44e5 in the last 3 cm, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve without crossing it. There are isolated 1.1-1.29e5 spikes at s=27 and s=55-58, but those are two or three lone points against a continuous rising band in the last 30 cm, so the rise is localized and real rather than a repeat of a mid-track excursion. The very last 1-2 cm hold one 6.9e4 point and one 1.8e4 point; that is a single partial-charge point at the end and ordinary scatter, not a sustained several-cm collapse, so the pin stays on the fit end. Past the stop the only thing there is 466013: four points, 1.9 cm, 3.88 MeV, 21.6 cm out at cos_fwd 0.68, and c/d/e show it as a lone brown vertex square with a completely charge-free gap back to the star and no arm of any kind attached at the stop. That is a detached dot, so gamma, and it does not promote the item to STM_MICHEL. C469 and C570 are single-point 2 cm clusters 58-60 cm BACKWARD (cos_fwd -0.80, -0.81), on the wrong side of the stop for the gamma rule and scattered rather than lying on any decay side, and 104012 is a 6-point pdg-11 delta 132 cm back on the body at cos_fwd -0.93; all three are delta / other. f_meas shows a well-predicted track (difference panels near white) with no dead channel at the stop in any plane - nearest dead wires are ~20 U, ~35 V and ~50 W channels away.

notes: OVERSHOOT: fit overshoots by 11.1 cm; the real stop is at the vertex where segment 39004 ends, and 39005 plus 39001/39003 are the Michel. Pin set to rr 11.1 (cross-checked three ways: segment size, where the collapse string ends on the plot, and the 19-point count). Attribution re-derived from the corrected stop, not the fit end - 39001 6.5 cm, 39003 3.1 cm, 134006 30.0 cm - and no tag changes as a result. One thing I cannot explain: a clump at 1.40-1.46e5 sits at s=28-30, i.e. ~18 cm back from the moved pin where the muon curve wants ~6e4; I read it as a delta ray on the body rather than evidence for a stop there, because the collapse and the branch vertex both fix the stop at s=11.
evidence: 43.2 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the y face at (-158,-336,100) and running shallow along the bottom to a fit end at (-192,-322,108), 14.1 cm from that same face. This is the overshoot case and the pin moves. The outward ladder is 39004 67370 over 7.2-37.9 cm back and 39005 12857 over the last 11.1 cm of path, i.e. the terminal segment is 0.19 of the one before it and about 0.2 of MIP - squarely inside the 0.15-0.5 band the rubric gives for a fit-bridged collapse, not the 20-30 percent terminal dip that is ordinary scatter. On the 4x g_dqdx the shape is unmistakable: a broad high band of 1.0-1.46e5 over s=12-30, then a tight dark string of about fifteen points at 0.7-1.4e4 filling s=4 to s=11, then a handful of 2.2-5.6e4 points in the last 3 cm. Three things fix the junction at arc length 11.1 cm: 39005 size is 11.1 cm, the collapse string ends and high charge resumes at s=11-12 on the plot, and the string point count matches 39005 19 points. 39005 is also by far the most curved terminal segment on this set (arc 11.1 against chord 7.15, ratio 1.55, where every other d_min=0 segment I scanned runs 1.02-1.06), which is why 11.1 and not 7.15 is the right pin coordinate. The 3-D zoom on azimuth e settles it geometrically: the amber muon body ends at a brown vertex square and TWO low-charge prongs leave that vertex - one beaded chain that dips and then runs 11 cm up-left to the fit star (39005), and a second cyan prong running down-left to the two vertex squares of 39001 and 39003, which sit 5.3-7.2 cm from the star at about 4e4 e/cm. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at a fifth of MIP, let alone fork, so all three pieces past the moved pin are the Michel. I re-derived every attribution from the CORRECTED stop rather than the fit end, because moving the stop moves the attribution: taking the junction 7.15 cm along the chord toward 39004, 39001 sits 6.5 cm and 39003 3.1 cm from it, both inside the 10 cm radius where direction does not discriminate, which confirms michel for both and disposes of 39003 cos_fwd -0.91 (that number is taken against the tangent at the fit end, 11 cm inside the electron). 134006 moves from 28.5 cm to 30.0 cm from the corrected stop - still a 0.4 cm two-point speck far outside the Michel radius, isolated and clear of the body line - so it stays a detached gamma and the kind stays both. f_meas rules out the dead-channel explanation for the collapse: the U dead bands are at channels 5-15 and 20-28 while the track occupies 31-44, and V and W are clear at the stop.

notes: No undershoot and no overshoot. The arm is 33.8 MeV over 10.7 cm of core with a 72 deg kink, which is the right range for a Michel. The only judgement call was 173009 attached-vs-scattered: it is 21.6 cm out and nearly perpendicular to the muon tangent, but it lines up with the arm direction in two of three azimuths, so I called it gamma and the item both rather than attached.
evidence: 30.6 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the z face at (-251,48,298) and stopping at (-274,52,281), 17.8 cm from that face - short, so the whole track is inside the Bragg region and the mean over the single muon segment is already 80478. On the 4x g_dqdx the chain occupies s=0-30: the far end at s=20-30 sits at 5.5-8e4 and the band climbs steadily to 8-1.0e5 over s=5-15 and to 1.05e5, 1.11e5 and 1.13e5 in the last 3 cm, tracking the muon curve without crossing it. No terminal collapse - the highest points are the last ones - so the pin stays on the fit end. The negative axis carries the arm: nineteen 55008 points and six 55007 points spread from magnitude 1 to 12 cm at 1.3-7.7e4, i.e. at and below MIP and falling as they go out, which is the ordinary Michel case rather than the undershoot (the undershoot needs a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 and there is nothing like that). Frames c and d show why this is easy: a clean teal arm leaves the very star at about 72 degrees to the amber muon body and runs ~11 cm with its own vertex squares, so it is attached at the stop, not bridged across a gap. 173009 is a 3-point 1.1 cm speck 21.6 cm out at 15549 e/cm and cos_fwd 0.03; in frame c it sits directly along the extended line of the arm and in frame d it sits up-range of the arm on the same side, so by the faint-far-speck rule it is on the Michel side and detached - gamma, giving kind both. f_meas confirms the arm is measured charge, not fit: blue points continue past the amber band in all three planes with near-white difference panels. The one soft spot is U, where hatched dead bands sit at channels 1500-1525 next to the track end, but V and W are clear there.

notes: THRU on the profile alone: no face reached, no dead-region exit and no visible continuation, the cluster just ends where the imaging ran out. No undershoot (there is no other object at all to be a mis-typed tip) and no overshoot (the terminal trough is one of four identical periodic troughs, so there is no localized peak-then-collapse). Caveat worth recording: this is a near-U-wire-parallel, near-drift-perpendicular track, so every dQ/dx number on it is poorly conditioned - but the absence of any rise anywhere, and the absence of any object past the end, both point the same way.
evidence: 149.7 cm single-segment chain running along the bottom of the detector at essentially constant drift x=130, entering 2.3 cm from the y face at (130,-334,146) and ending at (131,-268,38), 36.9 cm from the z face. It is the only object drawn - no michel, no gamma, no unfitted cluster anywhere near the end. The 4x g_dqdx shows a strongly oscillating profile: four near-identical troughs at 1.8-2.6e4 separated by crests at 4.5-5.6e4, with a period of roughly 15-20 cm, and the highest points anywhere on the track are 7.4-8.2e4 at s=20-22. The last 12 cm of the track (s=0 to 12) is simply one of those troughs, a flat band at 1.9-2.6e4; it is not a Bragg rise and it is not a fit-bridged collapse either, because the identical dip recurs at s=35, s=55 and s=87-92 where nothing special is happening. Nowhere does the profile approach the muon reference curve near s=0, and the segment mean over all 250 points is 34754, below MIP. f_meas explains the oscillation and rules out a dead-region exit: the track occupies only ~5 U channels over its whole 150 cm (nearly parallel to the U wires) while spanning 152 W and 150 V channels at a constant time slice ~1508, which is the degenerate near-wire-parallel geometry that modulates dQ/dx wire by wire; the W dead channels are at 10028, 10086-10092 and 10125 while the fit end sits at W 10018, clear of all of them. All three 3-D azimuths show the track simply stopping, with a mild bend in the last ~15 cm and nothing whatever past the star. Flat to the last point with no rise is the operative THRU test, so THRU.

notes: No undershoot: nothing forward of the stop at several times MIP - the arm starts at ~3e4, i.e. below MIP, and falls, which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel case. No overshoot: the last two points are the highest on the whole track. The chain also accepts this one (is_stm 1), and I agree with it independently.
evidence: 65.7 cm chain entering 0.9 cm from the x face at (339,-253,93) and stopping at (282,-232,103), 57.6 cm from the nearest face - comfortably contained. The dQ/dx is as clean as it gets on this set: the plateau over s=20-65 sits at 4.5-6.5e4 and the band climbs without a break to 8.3e4 at s=11, 9.1-9.8e4 over s=3-6 and 1.00-1.09e5 in the last 2 cm, following the shape of the muon reference curve and topping out just under it. The last points are the highest ones, so there is no terminal collapse and the pin stays on the fit end. Past the stop the negative axis carries forty big points from magnitude 1 to 17 cm at 1.0-5.2e4, i.e. at and below MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at a third of MIP, so this is a second particle, and 15 cm at 35 MeV is the right range for a Michel. All three azimuths show it as one continuous arm leaving the very star at about 83 degrees to the muon body and running ~15 cm with its own two vertex squares, attached rather than bridged, so 86001 and 86003 are both michel. 357004 is a 4-point 1.5 cm speck at 29008 e/cm, 23.6 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.34; in c, d and e it sits just beyond the far end of the Michel arm and on the same side, detached by a clear charge gap, which is the faint-speck-on-the-Michel-side case, so gamma and kind both rather than attached. f_meas shows the arm as real measured charge in all three planes with near-white difference panels, and the nearest dead channels (U 2115, V 5960, W 10220) are all far from the stop at U 2085 / V 5860 / W 10155.

notes: THRU is over-determined here: flat-and-near-zero to the last point AND a face 4.4 cm away AND the chain rejecting on no_bragg, shape_flat, stop_near_boundary and plateau_off_mip. No undershoot and no overshoot. One rubric tension to flag: the THRU convention says "fitted chain segments muon, everything else delta / other", but the muon tag row separately claims "a stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop", which is exactly 87017. I followed the muon-row clause because the THRU paragraph justifies itself only on gamma/michel forcing michel_kind, which muon does not; either way michel_kind is none.
evidence: 162.9 cm chain entering 2.6 cm from the z face at (203,-247,3) and running down to a fit end at (192,-332,95) that is 4.4 cm from the y face, with in_fv 0 - the side view in a_proj_full shows the track walking straight into the bottom boundary. The profile never gets near a Bragg anywhere: on the 4x g_dqdx it is a train of humps peaking at 4-5.6e4 separated by troughs that touch zero, with the segment means running 10625 over the 114 cm of 87003, 21802 over 87013 and 28277 over the last 18.6 cm of 87016 - the whole track sits at a fifth to a half of MIP, which is what the chain flags as plateau_off_mip. The last few centimetres are in one of the zero troughs at 0.3-0.8e4, and the hump at s=5-17 that reaches 5.6e4 is indistinguishable from the humps at s=33 and s=86, so there is nothing localized about the end. No rise at the fit end plus a face 4.4 cm away is THRU on both counts. Nothing sits past the end: the three azimuths show the fit terminating in open space with its brown vertex square and no arm. 87017 is a 3-point 1.2 cm stub attached at the fit end (d_min 0) at cos_fwd 0.98, i.e. carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop, so I tagged it muon under that clause rather than delta / other; it carries only 2958 e/cm, which is consistent with the rest of this very low track. 87011 is a 12-point 6.3 cm pdg-11 piece 18-21 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, dead on the body line, and 359015 is a 2-point speck 34 cm back at cos_fwd -0.77 - both delta / other. f_meas shows the same story: the measured charge along the whole track is dark, near the bottom of the colour scale, in all three planes.

notes: MEDIUM, and the reason is worth recording: the stop is 0.6 cm from the anode plane, so this item stretches the STM_MICHEL clause "ends inside the volume".
