The competing reading is THRU with the terminal rise being an anode-proximity artefact - dQ/dx here is perfectly correlated with distance-to-anode (0.6 cm at s=0, ~4 cm at s=20), so the profile alone cannot separate a Bragg peak from a near-anode response effect. What breaks the tie for me is the arm: an attached three-piece 28.9 MeV electron at a 107 degree kink leaving the exact endpoint at or below MIP is not something an anode artefact produces, and the rubric makes the profile, not the distance to a face, the operative test. No undershoot (nothing forward at all - the anode is forward) and no overshoot.
evidence: 91.5 cm chain entering 1.2 cm from the z face at (324,153,2) and running at a shallow ~10 degree incidence toward the anode, ending at (339,88,50) just 0.6 cm from the x/anode plane, so in_fv is 0 and the chain rejects on stop_near_boundary ALONE - it does not fire no_bragg or shape_flat. The profile agrees: on the 4x g_dqdx the plateau at s=50-95 sits at 3.5-6e4 and the band rises monotonically through 5-8e4 at s=10-30 to 8.8e4 at s=5, 1.03-1.05e5 at s=2-3 and 1.16e5 and 1.35e5 in the last centimetre, hugging the shape of the muon curve; the last points are the highest, so there is no collapse and the pin stays. Past the stop the zoom on frame c shows an unambiguous attached arm: a bead chain of three fitted pieces leaves the very star at about 107 degrees to the amber muon body, arcs up and back over the muon for ~9 cm carrying 25.7-49.0e3 e/cm and ends at its own two vertex squares - at and below MIP, which a muon at 1.35e5 cannot do, so 103007/103006/103008 are the Michel. Five centimetres beyond the arm end, 401009 is a compact 5-point 2.6 cm piece at 14-17 cm from the stop, separated from the arm by a clean charge gap and lying along the arm direction in frames b, c and e: a detached dot, so gamma. The three 2-point survey specks at 41.5, 46.1 and 50.0 cm (cos_fwd -0.59, -0.34, -0.69, perpendicular offsets 34-44 cm from the muon body line) all sit in the same backward-and-above hemisphere as the arm in b, c and e rather than being scattered around the 60 cm ring, so I called them gamma on the Michel side too. notes: No undershoot: the only forward-ish object is 16.2 cm out at 47474 e/cm, below MIP, nowhere near the "couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5" window. No overshoot. evidence: 152 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x face at (340,141,196) and stopping deep at (219,197,254), 44.2 cm from the nearest face. notes: LOW confidence - this was the hardest item of my twelve and two readings are live. Competing reading: STM_MICHEL / attached, taking 45003 as the muon and 45004 as the chain-offered 24.8 MeV Michel, which the rubric licenses because "a Michel topology is sufficient on its own" even when the Bragg peak is unclear. I went THRU because the fact that survives every reading is that 45003 never rises into any candidate stop - it peaks 5-7 cm early at only 1.5x its own plateau and then falls to a fifth of MIP - and because 45004 continues at only 22 degrees, which reads as continuation rather than decay, and charge continuing past the fit end is itself a THRU condition. A third reading I rejected: overshoot with pin-rr ~2.5, which fails for the same reason. No undershoot recorded (tested and rejected on the charge clause; see evidence). Not tagged FRAG because nothing else is drawn nearby, though a 21 cm shallow track dying next to a dead U band is plausibly a fragment.
evidence: A short shallow object skimming under the top of the detector: the 13.2 cm chain 45003 runs from 0.8 cm off the y face at (-254,336,234) to a fit end at (-247,329,227) only 7.6 cm from that same face, and 45004 (8.1 cm, cos_fwd 0.93) carries straight on past the fit end with only a 22 degree kink, so b, c, d and e all show ONE nearly straight ~21 cm line, not a track plus an arm at an angle. On the 4x g_dqdx, read along the whole 21 cm, there is no Bragg terminus anywhere. Coming down 45003 the profile goes 3.2e4 at s=13, 5.0-5.5e4 at s=8-10, up to a modest 8.1e4 at s=5-7, then DOWN through 6.3e4, 5.4e4, 5.2e4 to three points at 1.5-1.8e4 in the last ~2 cm - it falls into the fit end instead of rising, which is what the chain flags as no_bragg plus shape_flat. On the 45004 side the charge is 3.8-4.5e4 in the first centimetre, bumps to 7.9e4, 9.2e4 and 1.07e5 at 2.5-3.5 cm out, and then falls back through 6.2-6.8e4 and 5.2-5.5e4 to 4.7-4.9e4 at 7-9 cm. So the object has two interior local maxima with charge falling on BOTH sides of each - delta rays or a shower fluctuation - and no rise to any candidate terminus. I explicitly tested the undershoot: the peak does sit 3 cm past the fit point in a forward piece the chain types pdg 11, but the load-bearing clause fails - a muon tip would be highest right at the fit end and stay high for its couple of centimetres, whereas here the charge at the fit end is 1.6e4 on the chain side and 3.8-4.5e4 (below MIP) on the 45004 side, rising only later. I also tested the overshoot with the pin at rr about 2.5-3, but the muon then still has to fall from 8.1e4 to 5.2e4 into its own corrected stop, which a muon cannot do either. f_meas shows the far end of 45003 running into a wide dead U band at channels 1850-1855 (the track occupies 1840-1852), so part of the reason this object is short and ragged is U-plane loss; V and W are clear. 156001 is a 2-point speck 15.7 cm back at cos_fwd -0.88, on the muon body line, and 157002 is a 3-point 1.4 cm piece 6.8 cm back at cos_fwd -0.69 sitting alongside the body - both delta / other under the THRU convention.

notes: No undershoot: the forward-side arm starts at about 6.9e4, i.e. near MIP rather than several times it, and the piece is 11.5 cm not a couple of cm. No overshoot: the last point is the maximum. evidence: 222.2 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face at (261,-112,298) and stopping deep at (155,-92,117), 116.5 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not in question. Past the stop, 68021 is a 20-point 11.5 cm arm leaving the very star: the c-frame zoom shows it as a blue bead chain attached at the stop vertex and separated from the green muon body by a clean charge-free lane, running off at 82 degrees with its own end vertex, carrying 48891 e/cm mean and 2.0-6.9e4 point by point - at and below MIP, which a muon that has just reached 1.35e5 cannot do, and 11.5 cm at 27.4 MeV is the right range for a Michel. So the item is STM_MICHEL and the kind is attached. notes: Hard call two ways. (1) The terminal dip: four points below plateau spanning 2.3 cm looks like the overshoot signature until you notice three of them are at essentially zero charge and there is nothing at dstop 0 for the fit to have bridged to. Pin left at the fit end; if the owner counts near-zero terminal points as a real bridge this item becomes an overshoot with the pin near rr 3.0. (2) The 229006/229007 blob is ~13 MeV of electron-like charge over 6 cm, which is Michel-scale, and if its first centimetres simply were not imaged this becomes STM_MICHEL / attached; I went with gamma because the 11.6 cm gap to the stop is clean and an electron cannot start 11 cm from the muon it came from. The chain body-excluded it, but at 10 cm off the body line that exclusion is not what decided me.
evidence: 33 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the y face and the fit ends 24.9 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. The dQ/dx profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau from s=33 back to s~12, climbs through 7e4 at s~12, 8-8.5e4 at s=5-9 and reaches 0.98-1.17e5 at s=3.4-4.3, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve, so this is a real Bragg rise and the chain's no_bragg/shape_flat rejection is wrong. The last four points then fall away: 3.2e4 at s=2.3 and three points at 0.4-1.2e4 over the last 1.2 cm. I considered moving the pin for a peak-then-collapse but did not, on two grounds. Those three lowest points are at 7-22 percent of the plateau, essentially no measured charge, which is the class the rubric says to ignore as fit points rather than read as a bridge; once they are dropped the only survivor below the plateau is a single 3.2e4 point at 0.58 of MIP, i.e. one partial-charge point at the very end, which is the explicit leave-the-pin-alone case. And there is no destination: the fit bridges a gap to something, and here no object row sits at dstop near zero, with the chain reporting n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0. So the stop stays at the fit's last point. Past/near it the substantial object is the 229006+229007 pair, one blob of 21 points over ~6 cm at 4.9e4 and 1.6e4, centroid 12.6 cm from the fit end, 7.7 cm back along the body but 10.0 cm off the muon body line by direct 3-D projection of the centroid onto the entry-to-stop axis, confirmed by the d and e azimuths where it stands clearly off the amber band. It is detached: d_min 11.6 cm with a clean charge-free gap to the stop, so by the attachment tie-break it is a detached compact piece, gamma, not the Michel. 230008 sits at cos_fwd -1.0, d 15-20 cm, right on the body line: delta / other. The two 3-point survey specks 227004/228005 at 38 and 42 cm are 4.8 cm from each other in the same forward direction at z~62-66, reading as two pieces of one unrelated distant object rather than isolated capture gammas, so delta / other. No dead channel band touches the track at the stop in U, V or W.

notes: Flat profile to the last point, no visible continuation and no face contact, which the rubric says is still THRU. Confidence is medium not high only because the absolute charge scale is anomalous: the whole track sits near a tenth of MIP, so this may be a badly imaged or mis-flashed cluster rather than a clean MIP through-goer. That anomaly does not change the verdict, since a Bragg rise would still show as a relative rise on the track's own plateau and there is none.
evidence: 116.6 cm four-segment chain running almost entirely at constant drift (x 241.9 to 244.1), entering 4.0 cm from a face at z=4.8 and ending 13.2 cm from the nearest wall. The dQ/dx profile is the whole story: every chain point from s=100 to s=0 sits between 0.2e4 and 1.35e4 e/cm, an order of magnitude below the 5-6e4 MIP plateau these tracks normally show, and it is flat to the last point. The final point is 1.2e4 against a local 0.5-1.0e4, a 1.5x wobble no bigger than the bump at s=70, so there is no rise off the track's own plateau and nothing that follows the shape of the muon reference curve, which asymptotes at 1.6e5 far above every point on this plot. By the operative test that is a through-goer even though the fit end is 13 cm inside the wall: the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. The 3-D azimuths show a long winding low-charge spine with the amber selection band on the stop half and the rest continuing away in blue; nothing sits at the fit end, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The only unassigned object, 298005, is 18 points over 10.2 cm at cos_fwd -0.94, 38-46 cm back and lying on the muon body line, so delta / other. In f_meas the object is a single narrow time-slice band around 1540 with dead channel bands well away from it in U and V; nothing about the fit end is a dead-region exit.

notes: Not the ordinary flat-to-the-end THRU: the profile actively collapses over the last 15 cm to a fifth of the plateau. That is not the rubric's overshoot signature either, because there is no peak before the collapse -- the charge just fades from MIP into nothing, which reads as the track leaving through a poorly imaged or dead region rather than stopping. Either way there is no Bragg rise, so THRU.
evidence: 150.8 cm six-segment chain entering in the far corner 1.2 cm from a face and running diagonally to a fit end 19.9 cm from the z wall and 106 cm from the cathode. The dQ/dx profile holds a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in to s~15, then does the opposite of a Bragg: it declines monotonically over the last 15 cm, 3.8e4 at s=13, 3.2e4 at s=10, 2.6e4 at s=7, 2.0e4 at s=5, 1.4e4 at s=3, 0.95e4 at s=2, with only a small 2.85e4 tick on the very last point. Nothing ever climbs above the track's own plateau, let alone follows the muon curve, so there is no Bragg rise at the fit end and by the operative test this is a through-goer. The colour of the 3-D point cloud says the same thing independently of the panel: the spine is green over most of its length and turns cyan then blue over the last 20 cm into the star, in all three azimuths. The c and e frames show a single clean smoothly curving spine with nothing attached at the star and nothing detached anywhere near it, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). In f_meas the last stretch to the stop is nearly all dark in U, V and W, and there is a dead U channel band immediately alongside the track's final channels, which is a plausible reason the charge faded out where it did. The only unassigned row, 55010, is a 3-point 1.5 cm speck 132 cm back at cos_fwd -0.96, sitting on the muon body far from any stop, so delta / other.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: the fit stops about 3.9 cm short; the real stop is at the far end of 73013 (cos_fwd +0.99, d_max 3.9 cm, 1.31e5 e/cm), which the chain offered as the pdg 11 daughter. --pin-rr cannot express this so the tip is tagged muon instead. Confidence is medium because the verdict's michel_kind hangs on one call: 281011 at 13.4 cm and 8.9 cm off the body line is a detached dot (gamma) on my reading, but if it is instead counted as body activity the item is STM_ONLY / none. The undershoot itself is not in doubt.
evidence: 62.3 cm chain entering 0.7 cm from the z face at z=1.5 and running to a fit end 26.3 cm from the nearest wall, comfortably contained. The chain's own profile has a wide per-point scatter but a clear upper envelope: 5.0-5.5e4 from s=60 in to s=5, then 6.3e4, 7.0e4 and 8.05e4 over the last 3 cm, a ragged but real rise off its own plateau in the shape of the muon curve. The decisive object is 73013: 8 points over 4.2 cm sitting at d_min 0.0 to d_max 3.9 cm straight ahead of the fit end at cos_fwd +0.99, carrying 1.31e5 e/cm. That is two and a half times this track's own plateau and four to six times MIP, which is what a muon's last centimetres look like and not what an electron's first centimetres look like, so despite the chain typing it pdg 11 and offering it as the daughter it is the muon tip and the true stop is 3.9 cm beyond the fit's last point. Note that 73013 is absent from the dQ/dx panel entirely -- the panel is not a census -- so the object table is what carries this. Past that corrected stop there is no forward charge at all. 281011 is 4 points over 2.0 cm at 5.5e4, 13.4 cm from the fit end, and projecting its centroid onto the entry-to-stop axis puts it 8.9 cm off the muon line; the e azimuth shows it plainly below and clear of the spine, with a clean charge-free gap, so it is a detached compact conversion blob, gamma, not a Michel and not body activity, and the chain's Michel-body-exclusion label is outranked by that 8.9 cm. 73003 is a 7.4 cm fitted piece typed pdg 11 shower but it carries only 3219 e/cm and projects to 1.4 cm off the muon line at cos_fwd -0.85, i.e. it hugs the body just short of the stop: delta / other. 73006 is on the body at cos_fwd -1.0, 32-35 cm back. The three remaining specks 280010, 282012 and 279009 sit 31, 25 and 38 cm out with transverse offsets of 24, 25 and 38 cm in three unrelated directions (+z, +x, and -x/+z), which is the scattered-ring case, so delta / other. No dead channel band touches the fit end in U, V or W.

notes: Flat to the last point with no face contact -- THRU on the profile alone. The dead U and W channel bands at the fit end give an independent reason the cluster ended where it did.
evidence: 246.6 cm two-segment chain, straight as a ruler in all three azimuths, entering 0.2 cm from a face in the far corner at z=296, x=-340 and ending in open liquid 147.9 cm from the nearest wall and 150.6 cm from the cathode. This is the rubric's textbook case: containment says nothing, the profile decides. The dQ/dx holds a flat 5.5-6.5e4 plateau over its whole visible length and is still on that plateau at s=2-5; the only departure is a single 3.2e4 point at s=0, one low last point which is ordinary scatter and not a rise. Nothing anywhere climbs off the plateau toward the muon curve, which sits at 1.6e5 at the origin. The scattered 0.8-1.1e5 points at s=30, 74 and 87 are mid-track delta activity, not an end effect. A stopping muon cannot deposit at MIP to its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. f_meas supports that mechanically: the fit end sits at U channel 900 hard against broad dead U bands at 890-900 and 920-930, and the W end coincides with a dead W channel near 8490, so the imaging is exactly where the track disappears. The 3-D frames show a bare spine with no arm, no dot and no blob anywhere near the star, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The single unassigned row 26005 is 9 points over 4.8 cm sitting 192-194 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the muon body far from any stop, so delta / other.

notes: Confidence medium, not high. The geometry is degenerate -- constant x and constant z, so the collection plane sees the whole 68 cm in about two channels -- and the absolute dQ/dx is a tenth of MIP everywhere, so the Bragg test is weak on this item. The verdict rests mainly on the forward stub being collinear at cos_fwd +0.94 in all three azimuths and carrying the same charge as the muon body rather than falling away like an electron. The competing reading is STM_MICHEL on the grounds that a Michel topology is sufficient without a Bragg peak and the chain calls 88009 pdg 11; I rejected it because a 20 degree, same-charge continuation is a continuation, not a decay. Process note: I first judged this item on five frames, having read the rubric when it said six PNGs and mis-set the c zoom against d and e; I went back and read d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop before finalising, and they confirmed rather than changed the call.
evidence: 68.3 cm chain running almost purely along y, from (272.6,-259.1,286.4) to (273.2,-190.2,285.8): x and z change by less than a centimetre over the whole length, so both listed d_face numbers, 12.1 at entry and 12.6 at the stop, are the sideways distance to the z wall that the track keeps all the way along, not a face it approached at either end. The dQ/dx profile is flat at 0.5-1.5e4 e/cm from s=68 in to the last point at s=0, an order of magnitude under MIP, with two smooth isolated humps at s=27-35 (3e4) and s=40-50 (6e4) in the middle and nothing at all at the end. There is no rise off its own plateau anywhere near the fit end and nothing that follows the muon curve. What sits past the fit end is 88009: 11 points over 6.0 cm at cos_fwd +0.94, d_min 0.0, carrying 6361 e/cm, which is the same charge as the adjacent muon segment 88010 at 7785. All three stop azimuths agree on its geometry: in the c frame, zoomed 5.5x, it is a short yellow stub carrying straight on from the purple last muon segment with a few more faint image points beyond it, and the d and e frames from their own angles show the same stub collinear with the spine and the same faint points continuing past it, so the collinearity is not a one-view projection effect. That is the rubric's stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop, and charge continuing past the fit end is itself a THRU, so it is tagged muon and the item is a through-goer despite the chain typing the stub pdg 11 and counting it as a stop arm. 464008 is a 2-point 0.5 cm speck 33 cm away at cos_fwd -0.35, isolated in an unrelated direction with no stop to be past, so delta / other. In f_meas the object collapses into two W channels around 10805 at an essentially constant time slice near 1520, which is the degenerate vertical-track geometry and is why the absolute charge scale here should not be trusted.

notes: Unambiguous: stop 0.1 cm from the y wall, out of the fiducial volume, MIP charge to the last measured point. No object other than the chain is drawn, so michel_kind is none by construction as well as by the THRU rule.
evidence: 64.4 cm single-segment chain entering 5.8 cm from a face and running straight to a fit end 0.1 cm from the y wall, with in_fv 0 and the chain's own stop_near_boundary flag set. The dQ/dx sits on a 4.5-6e4 plateau over the whole length with the usual wobble; the last few centimetres reach 6.4e4 at s=4 and 7.1e4 at s=5-6, but the same track already shows 6.5e4 at s=18 and 6.6e4 at s=51, so that is the top of its own scatter band and not a rise off the plateau, and it does not follow the muon curve, which is at 1.3e5 by s=2. From s=2 in the profile falls, 5.8e4 then 4.85e4 then 2.7-3.0e4 on the last two points, i.e. the charge is still at MIP when the track reaches the wall and then simply stops being measured. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot be at 3e4 on its last point. All three 3-D azimuths show a single bare spine with nothing attached at the star, nothing detached anywhere near it, and the object table has exactly one row, the chain itself, so there is no candidate Michel or gamma to weigh. In f_meas the track runs off the bottom of the drift window and its U channels sit inside a broad dead band around 2400-2440, both consistent with a track leaving the imaged volume rather than stopping. This is a through-goer that exits the y wall.

notes: The chain itself asserts a capture gamma 35 cm past the stop (1.74 MeV, 508014), which would be detached dots if this were a stopper. I am calling THRU on the profile, so by the rubric's THRU rule that row is delta / other and the kind is none. If the verdict were wrong this is the row that would flip the kind, but the profile leaves no room: MIP to the last point with the only high-charge points a third of the way back up the track.
evidence: 74.3 cm four-segment chain entering 1.2 cm from a face and running dead straight in all three azimuths to a fit end 15.4 cm from the y wall. The dQ/dx sits on a broad 4.0-5.5e4 band with an upper envelope around 6-7e4 for its whole length and is still there at the end: the last few centimetres read 5.1e4, 5.3e4, 4.5e4, 3.3e4 and 2.55e4, i.e. flat then slightly falling, with nothing climbing off the plateau and nothing following the muon curve, which is at 1.3e5 by s=2. The genuinely high points on this track, 1.05e5 to 1.25e5, are all at s=34-42, a third of the way back, so they are mid-track delta activity and not an end effect. A stopping muon cannot be at MIP on its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out 15 cm short of the wall. Nothing is attached at the star in any of the three stop azimuths. What the display draws around it is a scatter of ten two-point specks 33-53 cm out at cos_fwd from -0.45 to +0.94, sitting in every direction around the ring in the b and d frames, which is the scattered-in-unrelated-directions case, plus the chain's own capture-gamma candidate 508014 (5 points, 2.6 cm, 8277 e/cm, 35 cm out at cos_fwd +0.34) and 98011, a 5.2 cm pdg-11 shower piece lying on the muon body at cos_fwd -1.0, 26-29 cm back. On a through-goer there is no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so all of these are delta / other and the kind is none. f_meas shows no dead band at the fit end in U or V; the nearest W dead band is about 20 channels away.

notes: This is the most flip-prone call in my twelve. The rubric collides with itself here. The attribution tie-break says a piece with a clean charge-free gap to the stop is a detached dot, gamma, however close it sits, and its worked example is a piece 9.4 cm out -- exactly this d_min. The undershoot section says a short forward piece at or below MIP whose charge falls as it goes out is a real Michel and the ordinary STM_MICHEL case, which also describes this object, though that passage is written about a piece attached at dstop of a couple of cm. I went with the tie-break because the gap is measured, clean, and not a dead region, and because an electron cannot cross 9.4 cm without depositing. If the owner reads it the other way this item is STM_MICHEL / attached with 527006 tagged michel; nothing else in the record changes.
evidence: 103.6 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from a face and ending 15.8 cm from the z wall, contained. The Bragg is real and easily the clearest in my chunk: a 5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to s~15, 7-8e4 at s=10-18, 9.2-9.6e4 at s=6.5-7.5, and a peak of 1.06e5, 1.10e5, 1.20e5 and 1.31e5 at s=4-6, following the shape of the muon curve, with the last point back at 9.4e4. Between s=1 and s=3.5 the points scatter hard (2.35e4, 3.4e4, 3.6e4, 5.2e4, 7.8e4), but that is scatter of a factor of three in both directions, not a sustained collapse, and the very last point is the second-highest of the tail at 9.4e4, so a muon still at 1.7x its own plateau reaches the fit end and the pin stays where it is. Past the stop the display draws exactly one thing: 527006, 5 points over 2.5 cm, mean 2.66e4 e/cm with its own points falling 6.4e4, 2.65e4, 1.25e4, 0.75e4 as they go out, sitting 9.4-11.4 cm from the stop, 8.6 cm forward along the muon direction and 5.6 cm off its axis by direct projection. Charge at half MIP and falling outward is electron-like and this is the chain's own Michel object, but it is separated from the stop by 9.4 cm of empty space, which the chain itself calls a bridge rather than a graph edge. f_meas shows that gap is real and not an imaging hole: in all three planes the blob sits about 30 time slices past the end of the track at the same channels, and no dead band lies between them, so charge would have been recorded if a charged particle had crossed it. A 4.8 MeV electron has a range of about 2.4 cm, which matches the 2.5 cm core exactly and rules out its having travelled 9.4 cm invisibly, so what crossed the gap was neutral. Detached, compact, past the stop and clear of the body line: gamma, and by the rubric an isolated compact capture gamma does not promote the item to STM_MICHEL.

notes: Unambiguous stopper, but with nothing at all past the end, so the interesting content is the chain's rejection rather than the verdict: plateau_off_mip fires because the whole visible track is Bragg, which is a rejection reason that will misfire on every short low-energy entering stopper.
evidence: Short 23.7 cm single-segment track that enters 0.1 cm from the y wall and stops 7.5 cm inside it, moving inward in y the whole way. The dQ/dx is the cleanest Bragg in my twelve: it rides along the muon reference curve for its entire visible length, 8.2-8.3e4 at s=20-23, 9.3-9.5e4 at s=17-19, 1.00-1.05e5 at s=13-16, 1.10-1.15e5 at s=10-12, 1.20-1.28e5 at s=5-8, 1.44e5 at s=2.5 and 1.57-1.66e5 at s=0.5-1.5. The very last point falls back to 1.25e5, about 25 percent below the peak, which is exactly the ordinary-scatter case the rubric says to leave alone rather than a sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit end. This also explains the chain's plateau_off_mip rejection: there is no MIP plateau on this object because the entire 24 cm is inside the Bragg region, which is what a muon entering the wall with 84 MeV of kinetic energy looks like, and the chain's own range estimate of 83.9 MeV agrees with 23.7 cm of argon. The scattered low points at s=19-23 (1.25e4 up to 5.15e4) are at the entry end where the track crosses the wall, not at the stop. Nothing else is drawn: the object table has a single row, the three stop azimuths show a bare spine with nothing attached at the star and nothing detached anywhere around it, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. f_meas confirms the isolation -- one short high-charge streak per plane with no companion blob and no dead band within 45 channels of the stop. Stops inside with a Bragg rise and nothing past the end: STM_ONLY, kind none.

notes: Medium, not high, and this is the row in my twelve I would most like a second opinion on. For THRU: no rise that stands out from this track's own scatter, a pronounced dip 10-20 cm before the end, a last point at a fifth of MIP, dead V and W channels one or two channels from the fit end, and the last 20 cm showing two interleaved strands that made the terminal shape harder to read than on any other item I scanned. Against THRU, and stronger than I first credited: the chain's range momentum (1146 MeV/c) and MCS momentum (1166 MeV/c) agree to 2 percent, and that agreement is corroborated by the lowest MCS ambiguity in my chunk, amb 0.05. I originally set this aside as the chain's own number rather than display evidence. Then on 039252_7/34, an item I judged THRU on independent and much harder grounds (exits 8 cm from the anode face, flat profile, no dead band), the same two momenta disagreed by a factor of 1.9 at amb 0.87. So in the two places I can check it in this chunk, the range-vs-MCS ratio behaves exactly as a stopping discriminator should, and here it points at a stopper. I kept THRU because the rubric makes the profile the operative test and the profile has no Bragg, but the owner should treat this as the flip candidate.
evidence: 453.5 cm six-segment chain, dead straight in every azimuth, entering 0.5 cm from a face in the far corner and ending 145.2 cm from the nearest wall. Its dQ/dx band is 5.0-6.0e4 with a wide scatter that reaches 1.0-1.2e5 repeatedly at s=22, 51 and 57 from delta rays. Reading the last 20 cm on a 4x crop: the profile does not build toward a peak, it dips, falling from 4.65e4 at s=20 along a smooth coherent strand to 1.95e4 at s=10, recovering to 4.6-5.8e4 at s=2.4-6.9, touching 7.9-8.6e4 at s=1.4-2.7 and then dropping to 1.2e4 on the last point. The 8.6e4 high is only 1.55x the local band and is well inside the scatter this track shows all along its length, so it is not a rise off the plateau in the shape of the muon curve, which is at 1.35e5 by s=1.5. There is no Bragg. f_meas, zoomed tight on the stop, shows why the charge disappears where it does: the last centimetres are dark blue in all three planes, and the fit end sits immediately against a dead V channel near 5440 and a dead W channel near 9390, one or two channels away in both. A track fading into dead channels in two of three planes is a through-goer that stopped being imaged, not a stopper. Nothing is attached at the star in any azimuth. 32022 is the only thing at the stop: 5 points over 2.4 cm at cos_fwd +0.85 carrying 1.17e4 e/cm, a fifth of MIP, and the chain itself types it pdg 13 and counts it inside the muon, so it is the last low-charge scrap of the fit rather than a decay product: muon. 32009 is 10 points over 5.4 cm sitting 423-426 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the body at the far entry end: delta / other.

notes: Clean THRU: flat to the last point, exiting 8 cm from the anode face, and the range-vs-MCS momentum disagreement (430 vs 806 MeV/c) independently says this muon did not stop. Worth noting as a cross-check the round could use: on my one deeply contained THRU with a strong stopping case against it (039252_7/32) those two momenta agreed to 2 percent, and here they disagree by a factor of 1.9. The MCS-vs-range ratio looks like a usable discriminator, but it is the chain's own number, not display evidence, so I did not let it decide either item.
evidence: 140.2 cm single-segment chain entering exactly at a face (d_face 0.0) at z=298 and running straight, with a gentle curve, to a fit end 8.0 cm from the anode face at x=-331.9. The end view puts the star hard against the x boundary of the drawn volume and f_meas puts the last measured point at time slice 1418, the short-drift end, so the track is heading into the anode plane rather than stopping in open liquid. The dQ/dx holds a 5.5-6.5e4 band along its whole 140 cm and does nothing special at the end: the last few centimetres read 5.35e4, 4.75e4, 4.05e4, 3.85e4 and 2.45e4, at or below the plateau. There is a mild lift at s=4-8 (8.55e4 and one point at 1.02e5) but that point has an exact twin at s=33 (1.015e5) and the track carries 8-9e4 points repeatedly out at s=73-95, so it is delta-ray scatter and not a rise off the plateau following the muon curve, which is at 1.1e5 by s=3. No Bragg rise at the fit end means through-goer. The chain's own kinematics agree with that even though its verdict does not: range gives 337 MeV of kinetic energy and 430 MeV/c, while MCS on the same track gives 707 MeV and 806 MeV/c, a factor of 2.4 in energy, which is what you get when a muon that has not stopped is assigned a range-based energy. All three stop azimuths show one bare spine, nothing attached at the star and nothing detached near it; the object table has a single row, the chain itself, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. No dead channel band lies at the fit end in U, V or W, so the track is simply leaving through the anode.

notes: RUBRIC GAP: the rubric only discusses the flat case for THRU ("flat on the MIP plateau to its last point") and the peak-then-collapse case for the pin move. This profile is neither - it declines by about 3x into the fit end with no peak before it. I read the no-Bragg-rise test as operative and called THRU. Confidence medium, not high, because the U dead band at 538-550 covers the stop end, so I cannot exclude that a real Bragg rise there was simply not measured; if it did stop in the dead band the verdict would be STM_ONLY. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 96 cm chain, enters 0.6 cm from the bottom y face and runs along the floor of the detector to a fit end 15.8 cm from the same y wall; the 3-D azimuths show one smooth, strongly curved spine with the pin star sitting on the last cloud point and nothing attached beyond it. On the 4x/6x dQ/dx crop the profile plateaus at 3.0-4.5e4 (matching 37008 mean 33152 and 37013 mean 37599 from the table) all the way from s=95 down to s=20, with only ordinary green scatter to 5-7e4 and no localised excursion anywhere; from s=15 it then falls monotonically 4.5e4 -> 3.4e4 -> 2.3e4 -> 1.3e4 and ends at 2.6e4/3.6e4 in the last centimetre. That is a decline into the fit end, not a rise: it never climbs above its own plateau, let alone follows the muon reference curve, which asymptotes near 5.4e4 so the whole track already sits well off MIP (the chain agrees: no_bragg, shape_flat, plateau_off_mip, is_stm 0). The decline is at least partly instrumental - in f_meas the U plane has a wide dead band at channels 538-550 and the stop end of the track (high time slice ~1505, U~545) sits inside it, while V is live there at 4348 and only goes dead mid-track at 4360-4372 - so the last ~15 cm are measured on a degraded plane set. There is nothing to bridge to in any case: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no object with small d_min, so a pin move would buy no Michel. The only forward object is the 4-point 1.9 cm capture-gamma candidate 142017 at 31 cm, cos_fwd 0.27, and on a through-goer gamma is undefined, so it is delta / other; 37015 (11 pts, cos_fwd -1.0, d 26-31) and 37012 (9 pts, cos_fwd -0.95, d 81-83, up at the entry end) hug the muon body and are body activity; the 2-point survey speck 144018 at 50 cm is unrelated.

notes: Undershoot checked and rejected (the tip charge profile rises outward from below MIP, and the kink is 97 deg). No pin move: the terminal easing from 7.5e4 to 4.3e4 lands at 0.9 of the plateau, not far below it, so it is not the sustained collapse the pin rule asks for. Confidence medium because the Bragg rise is within this track own scatter and because the 423008 gamma-vs-delta call is a genuine two-reading case decided on the 8.7 cm off-body separation. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 113 cm single-segment chain entering 1.1 cm below the top y face and running down to a fit end that is deeply contained - 46.4 cm from the anode x face, 86 cm from the y wall, 84 cm from the z wall - so containment is not in doubt and the projections agree. The dQ/dx plateau is 4-6e4 (segment mean 47062) with heavy scatter, and over the last 10 cm the chain climbs onto the muon reference curve, 6.4-7.6e4 at s=5-8, before easing back to 4.1-4.9e4 in the final 3 cm with two low points at 2.3 and 2.9e4; the rise is real but only about 1.6x its own plateau and the track shows comparable green excursions to 7.2-9.7e4 at s=30, 46 and 60, so I do not treat the Bragg alone as decisive - the chain rejects it as no_bragg / shape_flat. The topology does decide it: an 8-point, 4.1 cm arm (98005) leaves the shared stop vertex at a 97 degree kink, and on the zoomed panel its points run 2.8-4.2e4 in the first two centimetres and only reach 1.03e5 at its far tip, i.e. it starts at or below MIP and rises as it ends, which is an electron ending and not a muon tip - the reported mean 45740 is 0.97 of the muon plateau. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, and 4 cm at 14 MeV is the right range for a Michel. I checked the undershoot case explicitly and it does not apply: the piece is not straight ahead (cos_fwd -0.1, 97 deg) and it is not several times MIP through its length. 423008 (3 points, 1.2 cm, 5.6e4) sits 9.4 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.37, which puts it only 3.5 cm behind the stop axially and 8.7 cm off the muon body line, i.e. well clear of the body, and it lies within 25 degrees of the Michel arm direction with a clean 5 cm charge-free gap between the arm tip and it - detached, compact, on the Michel side, so gamma, notwithstanding the chain labelling it Michel body exclusion. The two 2-point survey specks at 40.1 and 44.9 cm point 89 and 135 degrees away from the Michel arm, scattered in unrelated directions, so delta / other. f_meas shows measured and predicted matching along the whole track with no dead band anywhere near the stop in any plane.

notes: Closest call was the pin: peak 8.9e4 at s=3.5 then a fall over 3 cm to near zero. Left alone because the two terminal points carry essentially no charge (2-4e3, the zero-charge fit points the rubric says to ignore), because a dead V channel sits at the stop, and because the intermediate 24-37e3 points are inside the local scatter - not because of how deep the fall is, which the rubric explicitly says is not a threshold. If the owner reads it as the bridged gap, the pin belongs at rr = 3.0. Dots 425011/426012 tagged gamma on the detached-and-compact rule; the chain counts them inside its Michel object, so an attached reading would make the kind attached instead of both. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 329 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and running the length of the drift to a fit end that is deeply contained - 45.1 cm from the y wall, 60 cm from the z wall, 275 cm from the anode - and the projections confirm it stops in open liquid. The dQ/dx plateau is 4.5-5.5e4 out at s=40-100 and the last 10 cm climb clearly onto the muon reference curve: 62-70e3 at s=10-13, 77-83e3 at s=7.5-10, and 76-89e3 at s=3-4, where the curve itself is 8-9e4. That is a genuine, ragged Bragg rise even though the chain rejects the item as no_bragg / shape_flat. Attached at the shared stop vertex is a two-piece arm - 99006, 10 points over 5.4 cm at 5.7e4, then 99007, 8 points over 4.3 cm at 4.6e4 - leaving at a 96 degree kink and carrying 29.4 MeV; both pieces sit at or just above MIP, and a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue for 8.4 cm at MIP, so this is a second particle and 8.4 cm is right for a ~30 MeV electron. Beyond the arm there are two 2-point specks, 425011 at 12.7 cm and 426012 at 15.7 cm, both strung out along the same direction as the arm (within 10-20 degrees of it) with a clean 4.2 cm charge-free gap between the arm tip and the first of them - detached and compact on the Michel side, so gamma rather than michel by the attachment rule, which makes the kind both. 424010 is a 2-point, zero-size, no-charge speck 6.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.68, i.e. 4.1 cm behind the stop and only 4.5 cm off the body line, body-excluded by the chain, so delta / other. I considered moving the pin: the profile does fall from 89e3 at s=3.5 to 37e3, 24e3 and then two points at 2-4e3 in the last 3 cm. I left it for three reasons, none of which is the depth of the fall, which the rubric says is not a threshold. First, the two terminal points carry essentially no charge at all - 2-4e3 is the zero-charge fit point the rubric tells me to ignore rather than a real low-charge segment. Second, f_meas shows a narrow dead V line at channel 7045 right where the track turns over, which accounts for them. Third, the intermediate 24-37e3 points are inside this track own point-to-point scatter near the stop, which also has a 29e3 point at s=6.0 sitting between 44e3 and 39e3 neighbours, so there is no clean junction to pin.

notes: Neither undershoot nor overshoot; the Bragg peak is the fit last point. The only judgement calls were 117015 (michel, on a 0.35 cm gap that is inside the point spacing) and the three forward specks (gamma on the along-the-arm direction rather than delta on the random-ring reading); both are stated in the evidence.
evidence: 177 cm chain entering 9.7 cm inside the z face and stopping in the middle of the liquid - 120.4 cm from the anode, 194 cm from the y wall, 132 cm from the z wall - so containment is not in question and the three projections put the stop nowhere near an edge. The Bragg is textbook: the plateau runs 5.5-7e4 from s=100 in to s=20, lifts to 8-9e4 over s=5-10, reaches 1.09-1.14e5 at s=2-4 and the fit last point itself is a 1.36e5 red point sitting exactly on the muon reference curve, which is why the final chain segment 32009 carries a mean of 109348 over its 4.7 cm against 59557 for the 172.8 cm behind it. The pin needs no move in either direction: the peak is inside the fit, not past it, so the undershoot case does not arise, and there is no terminal collapse. Leaving the stop vertex at a 54 degree kink is a 20-point, 11.6 cm arm (32007) at a mean 41870, i.e. below MIP, with a 5-point 2.3 cm piece (117015) picking up 0.35 cm beyond its tip - contiguous within the point spacing, so michel rather than a detached dot - and the chain measures 30.4 MeV over it, exactly the right length and charge for a Michel; a muon on a 1.36e5 Bragg tip cannot then run 11.6 cm below MIP. Three further specks lie strung out along the same direction as that arm, within about 15 degrees of it: 114013 (4 points, 1.5 cm) at 29.7 cm, 115014 (2 points, 0.3 cm) at 32.2 cm and 113012 (2 points, 0.5 cm) at 58.0 cm, all detached and compact, all forward at cos_fwd 0.57-0.69, so they are gammas on the Michel side rather than randomly scattered ring specks, and the kind is both. 32010 is 6 points over 3.1 cm at only 11370 sitting at cos_fwd -0.96 across the 32009/32011 junction, i.e. squarely on the muon body line, so delta / other whatever the chain pdg 11 label says. f_meas has measured matching predicted along the whole track and no dead band within tens of channels of the stop in any plane.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU with no visible continuation, which the rubric explicitly allows: the cluster simply ran out where the imaging did, and the stop is 0.7 cm from the z face in any case. Charge and 3-D fit are both degraded because the track runs nearly along a wire direction (240 cm into ~40 W channels), which is why the profile oscillates rather than being smoothly flat; this does not change the verdict since there is no rise anywhere. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 242 cm chain that enters 0.6 cm inside the z face and ends 0.7 cm from the same z face, running the whole way down in y at x about 230 and z about 1.5, i.e. skimming the boundary along its entire length; in_fv is 0 and the chain itself rejects it with stop_near_boundary. The dQ/dx profile is the clearest THRU in my chunk: it never approaches the muon reference curve anywhere, oscillating in a regular sinusoid between about 3e3 and 3e4 with a roughly 17 cm period from s=100 all the way in to the fit end, mean 18647, which is about a third of the 5.4e4 MIP asymptote - the chain agrees with plateau_off_mip and shape_flat. The last point sits at 1.7e4, mid-oscillation, with no rise of any kind in the last 10-20 cm. The oscillation and the 3-D frames explain each other: c/d/e show the fitted path itself wobbling in a regular zig-zag rather than following a straight spine, and f_meas shows the whole 242 cm collapsing into only about 40 W channels and 150 U/V channels, so the track runs nearly along a wire direction and its 3-D position and charge per unit length are both poorly constrained. Past the fit end there is nothing but 199005, a 2-point 0.1 cm speck carrying 0.3 MeV that the chain itself says it bridged across 12.65 cm of empty space on proximity rather than a graph edge - far too little to be a Michel, and on a through-goer gamma is undefined, so it is delta / other. 77001 (57 points, 33.4 cm) and 77004 (23 points, 13.1 cm) both sit at cos_fwd -1.0 and -0.99 at 164-200 cm back, squarely on the muon body up at the entry end, so they are body activity. No dead band bears on the call; the problem here is geometry, not dead channels.

notes: Confidence medium because the entire STM_MICHEL rests on a 4-point, 1.8 cm, 6 MeV arm - a Michel at the very low end of the spectrum - and because the last two chain points fall a little under the diverging Bragg curve. STM_ONLY is the competing reading if that arm is judged too small to be decay activity. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 166 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and stopping deep in the liquid - 116.2 cm from the y wall, 120 cm from the z wall, 189 cm from the anode - and the three projections and the wide 3-D view all put the star in open volume. The profile sits on the muon reference curve rather than below it: 5-6e4 from s=100 in to s=20, exactly the 5.4e4 asymptote, then it lifts to 6.6-7.9e4 at s=6-8 and 8.3-8.8e4 at s=4-5, where the curve itself is about 8.5e4, so the last points before the end track the Bragg shape properly. The final 1-2 cm come back to 6.5-7.7e4, short of where the diverging curve would put them, but that is two points a little low at the very tip rather than the sustained collapse the pin rule asks for, and there is no separate low segment for the fit to have bridged, so I left the pin at the fit last point. Attached at the shared stop vertex is 82003, a 4-point 1.8 cm arm leaving at a 75 degree kink with a mean 53853, i.e. exactly MIP, carrying 6.0 MeV. That is the whole basis for the michel call and it is a thin one - four points is the smallest arm I judged - but a muon whose last centimetres are climbing an 8.8e4 Bragg rise cannot then continue 1.8 cm at MIP, and the piece is attached at the vertex rather than detached, which rules out the capture-gamma reading since a gamma has no track back to the stop. I checked the undershoot explicitly: the arm would have to be several times MIP for the tip to be the muon own last centimetres, and at 5.4e4 it is not - the rubric partial-match warning applies and this is the ordinary Michel case. Nothing else is drawn near this stop at all: the object table has only these two rows, so the kind is attached with no gamma. f_meas shows measured matching predicted the whole way with only a thin V dead line adjacent to the stop channel, not a band across it.

notes: Same rubric gap as 039252_7/37: the profile declines by 3-4x into the fit end rather than staying flat on the plateau, which is neither of the two cases the rubric spells out. I read no-Bragg-rise as the operative test and called THRU. Confidence medium because the V dead band at 6885-6895 covers the stop, so a real rise there could have gone unmeasured; if it did stop in that band the verdict would be STM_ONLY. This item is deeply contained (65 cm from the nearest face), so the THRU rests entirely on the profile, exactly the case the rubric says is still THRU. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 357 cm chain crossing most of the detector, entering 14.9 cm inside the z face and ending at a point that is genuinely deep - 65.3 cm from the nearest z wall, 181 cm from the y wall, 209 cm from the anode - so this is not a face exit and the containment numbers would allow a stopper. The profile refuses it. From s=100 in to about s=15 the chain sits on the muon reference curve at 4.5-6e4, exactly the 5.4e4 MIP asymptote (segment means 51283, 50817, 52874 across the three chain segments), and then over the last 12-15 cm it declines monotonically instead of rising: 5-6.5e4 at s=10-14, 4-5e4 at s=6-9, 3.2-3.5e4 at s=4-5, 2.4e4 at s=2-3 and 1.5-1.7e4 in the last centimetre, about 0.3 of its own plateau. There is no peak anywhere before that fall - the single 7.9e4 green point at s=9 is one point inside the general scatter, which elsewhere reaches 8-13e4 at s=30, 40 and 73 - so this is not the peak-then-collapse the pin rule describes, and there would be nothing to bridge to in any case: the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the nearest drawn object is 14.8 cm away. The 3-D azimuths confirm it: a straight spine ending at the star with no arm, no dots and no continuation. In f_meas the stop is the low-time end at U 3070 / V 6890 / W 11250, and the V plane carries a hatched dead band at 6885-6895 exactly there, so the terminal decline is at least partly a degraded-plane artefact rather than physics. Of the drawn objects, 220014 (cos_fwd -0.98, 19 cm) and 83005 (cos_fwd -1.0, 139-142 cm) and 83018 (cos_fwd -1.0, at the far entry end) lie on the muon body line, 221015 sits 14.8 cm back at cos_fwd -0.41 and is body-excluded by the chain, and 219013, 222016 and 223017 are 2-3 point survey specks at 36-58 cm; on a through-goer none of these can be a gamma or a michel, which are defined relative to a stop, so all are delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: I am overruling the chain here: it flags is_stm 1, but the point-level profile is flat at about 5e4 to the last point with the local maximum 5-8 cm back, and there are three aligned clusters 47-57 cm straight ahead. Confidence medium, not high, because this is an isochronous track (constant drift, 45 cm into ~20 time slices) where the charge scale is unreliable and the 47 cm gap before the forward clusters is large enough that they could in principle be an unrelated faint object. I considered FRAG_THRU - the forward clusters make the fitted chain look like part of a longer track - but the chain runs from a detector face to its fit end as a complete object, so it is not visibly a fragment on its entry side. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: Short 45 cm chain that enters 0.6 cm inside the z face and ends 6.4 cm from the anode, running the whole way at x about 332-334, i.e. nearly parallel to the anode plane; f_meas shows the consequence, the entire 45 cm collapsing into about 20 time slices and 50-90 channels in each view, which is the isochronous geometry where dQ/dx is least trustworthy. The profile never approaches the muon reference curve: point by point it is 4.7-5.1e4 in the last centimetre, 3.0-4.8e4 at s=2-4, 5.4-6.3e4 at s=5-8 and 4.4-6.1e4 at s=10-13, so the last 13 cm are flat around 5e4 with the local maximum at s=5-8 rather than at the end, while the curve wants 8.5e4 at s=5 and 1.4e5 at s=1. The chain segment means do climb, 24377 then 35861 then 43177 into the stop, and that is why the chain accepts this as is_stm 1, but the climb is an artefact of a dip to 1.4-2.0e4 at s=15-22 pulling the middle segment mean down - the point cloud shows no rise off the plateau at the end and no muon-curve shape. Nothing is attached at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0) and no arm appears in any of the three azimuths. What does appear, and is the second reason for the verdict, is charge continuing straight on: 319007 (9 points, 5.0 cm), 319008 (17 points, 9.5 cm) and 465009 (3 points, 1.3 cm) all sit 47-57 cm past the fit end at cos_fwd 0.98-0.99, i.e. within about 10 degrees of straight ahead, and the wide 3-D view shows them strung along the extension of the track line with a faint dotted trail. Charge that continues past the fit end is THRU by the rubric own clause. 93005 (cos_fwd -0.99, 17-20 cm) and 93006 (cos_fwd -1.0, 28-31 cm) lie on the muon body line and are body activity; on a through-goer none of these can be gamma or michel, so every non-chain row is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: The hardest item in my chunk. The competing reading is UNCLEAR: this is an isochronous track (4 cm of drift over 138 cm) whose last 45-50 cm the fit interpolated through near-empty space, so one could argue nothing about the end is measurable. I called THRU because the one thing that IS measurable - the profile - shows no rise off the plateau anywhere near the fit end, and because the objects strung along that stretch all lie on the body line, which says the fit is threading a broken track rather than approaching a stop. I did NOT move the pin despite the huge collapse: the rule wants a peak several cm before the end and there is none, and moving it would not produce a Michel since everything past any candidate stop is body-line fragments. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 138 cm chain entering 0.6 cm below the top y face and ending 28.5 cm from the anode, running at x 311-316 the whole way - only 4 cm of drift over 138 cm of track, so this is an isochronous object and f_meas around the stop is essentially empty, two small blobs and nothing else in any of the three planes. The profile says the same thing far more strongly than any containment number: real charge only exists for the first 60 cm from the entry (segment 97013 mean 40695, points 2-5e4 out at s=60-100), and from about s=55 inward it collapses to a near-zero band, 0.3-1.7e4 in a smooth low sinusoid all the way from s=50 to s=15, which is why the terminal chain segment 97015 has a mean of 7830, about 0.15 of MIP over 59 cm. The final points at s=0 climb back to 5.0 and 6.7e4, but two points at MIP after 45 cm at a seventh of MIP is not a Bragg rise, and there is no peak anywhere before the collapse for the pin rule to key on - the highest point near the junction, 5.4e4 at s=61, is exactly the MIP asymptote, not a peak above it - so I left the pin at the fit last point. The 3-D azimuths show what happened: a dense amber section at the far end, then a long dark-purple, near-zero fit path threading a string of small detached fragments, then the star. Those fragments are the object: 325024, 326025, 466032, 467034, 467036, 467037 at 18-35 cm and 324023 at 49-52 cm all sit at cos_fwd -0.88 to -0.99, i.e. on the muon body line, each 2-9 points at 11-35e3, and they are the broken-up remains of the track rather than anything past a stop. 323022, which the chain offers as the Michel, is one more of the same - 11 points, 6.2 cm, 11784, at 9.2-10.4 cm and cos_fwd -0.83, which puts it 8.1 cm behind the stop and 5.4 cm off the body line, and the chain itself says it was bridged across 9.14 cm of empty space on proximity rather than a graph edge, with kink -1 deg, i.e. no kink measured at all. On a through-goer gamma and michel are undefined anyway, so every non-chain row is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: The competing reading, and the reason for medium: 102009 is the chain terminal segment but its centroid is only 1.2 cm from the pin, and its direction (cos_fwd -0.44) is within 18 degrees of 102005, so it can equally be read as the first 2.4 cm of the Michel arm that the fit swallowed - in which case the pin belongs at rr about 2.4 and 102009 should be tagged michel. I left the pin and tagged it muon because the rubric overshoot signature requires the peak several cm BEFORE the last point followed by a collapse, and here the largest charge on the whole plot, 1.36e5, is the last point itself. cos_fwd on a 1.2 cm centroid is not trustworthy (rubric trap 5), which is exactly why I did not let it drive the call. Neither undershoot nor overshoot as the rubric defines them.
evidence: 107 cm chain entering 0.1 cm inside the y face and ending 27.0 cm from the same y wall, 59 cm from the z wall and 270 cm from the anode, in FV. The muon body 102011 sits on a 2-5e4 plateau (median 42547) from s=100 in to s=20 and then climbs onto the muon reference curve: 70-79e3 at s=8-13, 88-95e3 at s=6.5-7.6 where the curve is about 8.5e4, and the fit last point itself is a 1.36e5 red point against a curve value of 1.6e5. That is a real Bragg rise even though the chain calls it no_bragg; the interleaved low points at 3-35e3 at s=1-5 are, I think, charge shared between the muon tip blob and the arm blob crossing the same wires near the vertex, which is also why the terminal segment median 36494 sits below the body plateau despite containing the largest point on the plot. All three azimuths show the same thing: a green MIP spine arriving at the star, and an amber arm of about 8 cm leaving it at a large angle. That arm is 102009 (5 points, 2.4 cm, in the chain) running seamlessly into 102005 (14 points, 7.9 cm, median 50019, typed pdg 11 shower by the chain), whose centroid is 5.9 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.55, i.e. 4.9 cm off the muon body line - a muon on a 1.36e5 Bragg tip cannot then run 8 cm at MIP, so 102005 is the electron and the item is STM_MICHEL. 357013 (2 points, 0.6 cm) at 23.1 cm and 355012 (2 points, 0.3 cm) at 42.8 cm are both detached and compact, 19 and 32 cm clear of the body line, and both point within 12-16 degrees of the arm direction, i.e. on the Michel side rather than scattered around the ring, so both are gamma and the kind is both. f_meas shows a wide V dead band at 7535-7555 just beside the stop channels, which is worth noting but does not undercut the measured 1.36e5 tip.

notes: STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL purely on absence: the item draws one object and nothing else. Worth noting the stop is 14.2 cm from the y face, the nearest of my chunk apart from the two boundary-skimming through-goers, so a Michel emitted towards that face could have left the volume - but that is speculation, not evidence, and the rubric asks for what is drawn. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: Short 21.2 cm chain that enters 0.1 cm inside the y face and stops 14.2 cm from that same y wall, 29 cm from the anode and 86 cm from the z wall, in FV; the projections show a small stub near the top corner and the three azimuths show a clean single spine with the star at one end and the entry triangle at the other, nothing else drawn anywhere. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk and needs no interpretation: the points lie on the muon reference curve over the whole visible length rather than crossing it or falling off it - 5-8.5e4 at s=10-21 where the curve is 5.5-6e4, 6.5-8.9e4 at s=3-8, 1.07-1.10e5 at s=2-3, 1.19-1.25e5 at s=0.5-1.5 and a 1.345e5 red point as the fit last point, against a curve value of 1.6e5 there. The segment median 76368 over 21 cm is what a track that is entirely inside its own Bragg region looks like, and the KE of 77.8 MeV from range agrees with 86.2 MeV from dQ/dx, so the stop is where the fit puts it and no pin move is called for in either direction - there is no collapse at the end and no high-charge piece past it, indeed no piece past it at all. The object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself: nothing at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted clusters), no arm in any azimuth and no speck in the 60 cm ring, so there is nothing that could read as an electron or as a capture gamma and the kind is none. f_meas shows measured matching predicted along the whole stub with the stop end at U 1355 sitting clear of the hatched dead bands at 1305-1330 and 1395-1500, so the absence of decay charge is not a dead-region effect.

notes: Confidence medium: the Bragg rise is the weakest I accepted in this chunk - only about 2 cm of clearly elevated charge, topping at 9.7e4 rather than the 1.2e5 a clean stopper reaches, with a dip to 3-5e4 four to seven cm before the end - and the chain calls it no_bragg. THRU is the competing reading and would take the two specks with it to delta / other and the kind to none. I went with the rise because it is a factor 1.8 over this track own plateau, follows the curve shape, and the item is 66.6 cm from the nearest face with a clean single spine. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 145 cm chain entering 0.8 cm inside the z face and ending deep - 66.6 cm from the z wall, 135 cm from the anode, 168 cm from the y wall - and all three azimuths show a single straight spine with the star at its end and no arm, no dots attached and no continuation. The plateau sits on the muon reference curve at 5-6e4 from s=100 in to s=15 (segment medians 54696 and 58715). Over the last 15 cm it climbs, raggedly: 6.7-8.5e4 at s=8-14 where the curve is 7-7.5e4, then a dip to 2.8-4.9e4 at s=4-7, back to 5.9-6.1e4 at s=2-3, and 8.0, 8.0, 9.0 and 9.7e4 in the last two centimetres. That tops out well under the 1.2-1.35e5 that a clean stopper reaches here and the chain rejects it as no_bragg and shape_flat, but it is a factor 1.8 above the track own plateau and it follows the curve shape, and the rubric is explicit that a ragged rise with point-to-point scatter of a factor of two still counts. The pin needs no move: the maximum is the fit last point, there is no sustained terminal collapse, and there is no high-charge forward tip past the end for the undershoot case. Nothing at the stop reads as an electron - the chain finds no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - so the verdict is STM_ONLY. Two isolated specks do sit past the stop, though: 158024 (2 points, zero size, no charge measured) at 15.3 cm and cos_fwd -0.77, i.e. 9.7 cm off the muon body line, and 159025 (2 points, 0.3 cm, 34059) at 39.4 cm and cos_fwd -0.52, 33.7 cm off the body line. They point within 18 degrees of each other and 41 and 59 degrees away from the body direction, so they are not scattered in unrelated directions around the ring but sit together on one side, clear of the body, detached and compact - capture gammas, which makes the kind detached dots rather than none while leaving the verdict STM_ONLY. The four remaining rows, 49013, 49018, 49019 and 49022, all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 between 41 and 135 cm back, on the body line up at the entry end, so delta / other. f_meas puts the stop at the high-time end at U 1195, clear of the U dead bands, though a V dead line at 4980 runs right beside it.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence (clean Bragg, contained, no forward piece); the medium is entirely about michel_kind, which is a counted field here resting on whether one 2-point 0.1 cm speck 21 cm off-axis is a capture gamma (detached dots) or unrelated body activity (none).
evidence: 91.9 cm chain, enters right on the z face (d_face 0.1 cm) and stops 20.5 cm from the nearest z wall, deeply inside in x and y. The dQ/dx profile sits on a 4-5e4 MIP plateau from s=90 down to about s=15 and then climbs steadily along the solid muon reference curve to 1.15-1.22e5 in the last two points at the origin - a clean, essentially monotone Bragg rise that peaks exactly at the fit last point, so there is no pre-peak collapse and the pin stays where the fit put it. Nothing sits forward of the stop at all (no row with positive cos_fwd), so the undershoot signature is absent too. The only other drawn object is a 2-point, 0.1 cm speck (236004) at 20.9 cm: taking the entry-to-stop axis, its along-axis component is only 2.3 cm behind the stop plane and its transverse offset is 20.9 cm, so it is well clear of the muon body line and separated from the stop by a charge-free gap in all three 3-D azimuths - detached and compact, which the tie-break paragraph resolves to gamma rather than delta, and it is a single speck rather than several scattered round the ring. The chain calls it gamma body exclusion, but off-axis separation outranks the chain label. f_meas shows the track ending cleanly in all three planes with the dead-channel lines well away from the stop, and the measured-minus-predicted panels show no leftover charge past the end, so this is a real stop and not a dead-region exit. A 0.1 cm two-point speck is not a 35 MeV electron, so the item stays STM_ONLY.

notes: Bragg rise is weak and only 3 cm long (chain says shape_flat); the STM_MICHEL rests on the attached forward falling-charge arm, which the rubric says is sufficient on its own - hence medium. 299016 is tagged gamma on on-the-Michel-side plus 17.8 cm clear of the body; the competing reading is delta / other because it sits 29 cm back along the muon rather than past the stop. michel_kind is both either way, since 297014/298015 are unambiguous gammas.
evidence: 118 cm chain entering flush on the x/anode face (d_face 0.2 cm) and ending 56.6 cm from the nearest z wall, deeply contained. The profile sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau for the whole 100 cm and only lifts in the last ~3 cm, to 6.2e4 / 6.9e4 / 7.8e4 - a real but weak and short rise, well under the muon reference curve which is at 9e4-1.2e5 there; the chain itself rejected the item shape_flat on exactly this. What settles it is the topology: a two-piece 9 cm arm (94013 then 94012) attached at the very stop vertex, running forward at cos_fwd +0.76/+0.78, along +1.4 and +3.4 cm past the stop with 1.6 and 3.8 cm transverse offset, carrying 6.2e4 falling to 4.9e4 as it goes out - at or just above MIP and falling, which is the ordinary Michel signature and explicitly not the undershoot case (that needs several times MIP, 0.9-1.2e5, in the forward tip). A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP for 9 cm, so the arm is a second particle, and 9 cm with a 39 deg kink is right for a ~25 MeV electron. The three near specks are past the stop and clear of the body - 297014 and 298015 at +12.8 cm along and 22-24 cm transverse, 300017 at +28 along and 48 transverse - and all four unassigned specks sit within 27 deg of the Michel arm own transverse azimuth, i.e. on the decay side rather than scattered round the ring, so they are gammas. 299016 is the hard one: 29 cm BACK along the body, but 17.8 cm clear of the body line and on the same azimuth as the rest. f_meas shows the muon ending cleanly at time slice 1100 in all three planes with dead-channel lines well away, and the arm rendering dark blue/near-black in the measured panels, i.e. genuinely low charge - a real stop, not a dead-region exit.

notes: OVERSHOOT: peak at s=5.5-5.7 (9.0e4, on the muon curve) then a sustained collapse to 0.25-0.6 MIP over the last 5 cm; pin moved to rr=5.0 and the tail past it read as the Michel. Two hard calls: (a) 101005 is a split row - muon for 108 cm, Michel for the last 5; (b) the far pair 325004/C327 at 57-60 cm is right at the edge of the gamma ring and perpendicular to the muon rather than along any arm direction, and tagging them gamma is what makes michel_kind both rather than attached. I went gamma because they are isolated, compact, clear of the body and grouped in one direction (the rubric delta half wants specks scattered in unrelated directions), but belongs to a different object entirely is a live competing reading for an 11 cm-separated pair 60 cm out.
evidence: 113 cm chain entering 1.6 cm inside the x/anode face and ending 88.6 cm from the nearest wall (y), with no seam nearer than 58.8 cm - deeply contained by the numbers, and the three projections agree. This is the overshoot case. The profile runs on a low 3.5-4.5e4 MIP plateau from s=100 back to s=20, then climbs cleanly along the muon reference curve to 7.5e4 at s=7 and 8.7-9.0e4 at s=5.5-5.7, where the data actually sits on the curve - an unmistakable Bragg peak about 5.5 cm before the fit last point. Over the last 5 cm it then collapses and stays collapsed: 4.6e4 at s=4.4, 2.5e4 at s=4.0, 1.0-1.2e4 at s=2-3.5, 2.3-3.1e4 at s=0.5-1.5, 4.6e4 at the last point, i.e. roughly 0.25-0.6 of this track own MIP over several centimetres, which is a sustained collapse and not the one-low-point scatter the rubric tells you to ignore. f_meas rules out the cheap explanation: the track is nearly parallel to the channel axis in all three planes and the dead-channel bands (V at 7540-7560, W at 12200-12230, U at 3712) are well away from the stop, so the missing charge is real. So the pin goes back to the junction at s = 5.0 cm and the low tail past it is the Michel; 101006, the 2-point 0.6 cm piece the chain types pdg 13 at the very fit end, sits inside that tail and is tagged michel, while 101005 is tagged muon because 108 of its 113 cm are muon - the row is split by the pin and its last ~5 cm belongs with the Michel, which the per-object alphabet cannot express. Nothing in the 3-D azimuths shows a kink or a detached blob at the stop; the tail is collinear, which is what makes this a fit bridge rather than a visible arm. The two far objects, 325004 (0.4 cm, 2 pts) and C327 (2.6 cm, 5 pts, no PR segment), sit 56.7 and 59.3 cm transverse at essentially the stop plane (along +0.7 and +6.9), 11 cm from each other and in one common direction rather than scattered round the ring.

notes: Clean THRU on the operative test (no rise at the fit end; charge actually falls into it), and unusually it also has a visible exit mechanism: coincident dead-channel bands in U, V and W right at the last point. Not called FRAG because no larger spine is drawn or visible in any frame - the cluster is the whole of what the imaging produced.
evidence: A short, lonely 43 cm segment low in the detector: it enters flush on the bottom y face (d_face 0.4 cm) and the fit ends 11.0 cm from that same y wall, 45.7 cm from the anode and 130 cm from the z wall, so containment by the numbers is unimpressive but it is the profile that decides. There is no Bragg rise of any kind at the fit end - the last points are at 2.2-2.5e4 with one zero-charge point, which is BELOW the 4-7e4 the same track carries at s = 5-20 cm, so the charge is falling into the fit end, the exact opposite of a stopper. The only high charge on the panel is a vertical column at s = 16-20 reaching 1.58e5 / 1.13e5 / 9.2e4, a delta ray or crossing mid-track, not a terminal rise, and the far end at s = 25-42 also sags to 1-3e4, which is why the chain flagged plateau_off_mip alongside no_bragg and shape_flat. f_meas then supplies the mechanism, and this is the frame that settles the item: the fit last point sits at time slice ~205 in all three planes and in all three the track is running into a dead region at exactly that channel - U reaches ch 573 against a wide dead band covering 545-578, V reaches 4287 against a dead band at 4250-4287, and W reaches 8200 against a dead line at 8195-8200 - with the track moving toward decreasing channel in each. So the object leaves through dead channels rather than stopping, and the depressed last few centimetres of dQ/dx are the edge of that same loss. Nothing else is drawn near this object at all - one row, no arm, no dots, no specks - so there is nothing past the end to attribute, and the single fitted chain row is tagged muon with kind none as the THRU convention requires.

notes: The one thing that gave pause is the pale-blue unfitted halo around the last 10-20 cm in c/d/e; it is not in the object census, carries no visible measured charge, and the complete 1.3e5 Bragg peak at the fit last point says the muon really stopped there, so it does not promote the item to STM_MICHEL.
evidence: 81 cm chain entering 8.4 cm inside the bottom y face and stopping 38.3 cm from the nearest wall (y), 138.8 cm from the anode and 83.5 cm from the z wall - comfortably contained. The Bragg evidence is as clean as it gets in this set: the track sits on its own 7e4 plateau out to s = 12, then climbs 9.5e4, 1.01e5, 1.12e5, 1.21e5 and tops out at 1.27-1.31e5 in the last two points, tracking the solid muon reference curve point for point from s = 10 inward and peaking exactly at the fit last point, so there is neither a pre-peak collapse (no pin move) nor a high-charge forward tip beyond the fit (no undershoot). The chain rejected the item shape_flat, which is simply wrong here. Nothing is attached at the stop: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and f_meas shows the track terminating at time slice 1548 in U, V and W with no measured charge continuing past it. The three azimuths do show a diffuse pale-blue halo of unfitted image points spread over the last 10-20 cm, mostly to one side of the spine and partly around the stop; it carries little charge (it is not visible as extra charge in any measured panel), it is not a coherent arm, and it does not appear in the object census, so I read it as the raw cloud width plus context rather than a Michel. The only other object is 148001, a 2-point 0.8 cm speck at 43.7 cm, 16 cm past the stop along the muon direction and 40.6 cm transverse, i.e. isolated, compact, clearly past the stop and well clear of the body line - a single dot on one bearing rather than several scattered round the ring, which the rubric resolves to gamma. That makes the item a stopper with a detached dot and no Michel.

notes: The only wobble is the single 6.5e4 last point after a 1.38e5 peak two centimetres earlier; I read it as one partial-charge point (the rubric explicitly excludes that from the pin-move signature) rather than a collapse, and the Michel arm attaching at d_min 0.0 corroborates that the stop is where the fit put it. 287009 is listed with dstop 52.4 but d_min/d_max 159.0/159.8 and a centroid 159 cm away; I used the geometry, not dstop.
evidence: 100 cm chain entering 11.9 cm inside the z face and stopping 55.0 cm from the nearest wall, deep in x and y - contained on the numbers. The profile leaves a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau at about s = 15 and climbs along the muon reference curve through 8.8-9.8e4 at s = 5-9, 1.10-1.16e5 at s = 2-9 and a 1.24e5 / 1.38e5 pair at s = 3-4, an unmistakable Bragg peak. The very last chain point at s = 1.4 drops back to 6.5e4; that is a single partial-charge point at the end rather than a sustained collapse over several centimetres, so the pin stays where the fit put it - this is not the overshoot case. It is not the undershoot case either: the forward piece at the stop carries 43e3, below the plateau, and the undershoot needs a tip at several times MIP. Past the stop a two-piece arm leaves the stop vertex itself - 87001, 3.4 cm attached at d_min 0.0, then 284007, 1.7 cm at 5-7 cm - running forward at cos_fwd +0.78 / +0.74 with a 40 deg kink and charge falling outward, 43e3 then 27e3, i.e. at or below MIP and dropping, which is the ordinary Michel signature; f_meas shows exactly that as a small dark-blue (low charge) tip on the end of the bright muon in all three planes, with no dead channels anywhere near the stop. Of the four unassigned pieces, 3004 (4 pts, 1.9 cm, 29 cm out, 24 cm past the stop and 17.8 cm clear of the body, on the same transverse bearing as the Michel arm) and 283006 (2.9 cm, 56 cm out, 10 cm past the stop, 55.8 cm transverse, same bearing) are isolated, compact, past the stop and clear of the body line: gammas. 286008 sits 17.7 cm BACK along the muon, 29.7 cm off the body and on the diametrically opposite bearing to the Michel, so it is unrelated activity, and 287009 is 159 cm from the stop and 130 cm off the body line, plainly a different object - both delta / other.

notes: Three-way call between MESSY, THRU and STM_MICHEL. Decided on the absence of any single MIP level: without one, THRU is unmeasurable, and with the profile falling into the fit end there is no Bragg peak to support STM_MICHEL. The 9.3 cm arm past the fit end (cos_fwd 0.36 against a local tangent on a track this curved) is the piece I went back and forth on; under the MESSY convention its tag is delta / other either way, so it does not change the record.
evidence: This is not one adjudicable track. The chain is 46.7 cm long but the entry-to-stop chord is only 26.7 cm, so it is bent almost double, and it is split into six fitted muon segments whose mean dQ/dx runs 48700, 12592, 3340, 27522, 31382 and 35808 going back from the fit end - a fifteen-fold spread with a roughly 5 cm stretch carrying essentially no charge 14-16 cm before the stop, which shows on g_dqdx as a dense floor of near-zero points at s = 14-22. Thirteen objects are drawn inside a compact tangle barely 35 cm across, with of order ten brown vertex squares, and two of the rows (99025, 16 pts, and 99026, 8 pts) are typed pdg 11, shower by the chain and lie directly ON the body line, cos_fwd -1.00 at 2.3 and 5.0 cm transverse, 26-29 cm back. The chain could not even compute MCS (0 segments) and rejects the item no_bragg and shape_flat. I considered THRU and rejected it: THRU asserts a flat profile on the MIP plateau to the last point, and this object has no single MIP level to be flat on - the segment means span 3340 to 48700, and f_meas shows bright-orange and near-navy stretches inside the same small blob. I considered STM_MICHEL, on the strength of a 9.3 cm arm (99020, 46343 e/cm, 55 deg kink) attached at the stop vertex, and rejected that too: the profile falls INTO the fit end, from about 8.2e4 at s = 2.5 to 3.8-4.5e4 over the last 2.5 cm, so there is no Bragg peak for the arm-at-MIP-must-be-a-second-particle argument to rest on, and the arm reads in the d azimuth as a continuation of the same bent object. With no identified stop the tag alphabet does not apply, so every row is delta / other per the MESSY convention and the kind is none.

notes: medium because the Bragg rise rests on the last two points of a 14 cm chain with no established plateau, and because the stop is only ~12 cm from both the x and z walls; the object moves inward and the attached sub-MIP fan is what makes it a decay rather than an exit. 102014 could equally be read delta / other under the on-the-body-line clause - it does not affect michel_kind either way.
evidence: A short one: 14.4 cm of chain entering 0.7 cm inside the anode/x face and running AWAY from it to stop 11.8 cm from that wall and 11.9 cm from the z wall - shallow containment but on the correct side, and the object travels inward, so it did not leave. Despite the chain no_bragg / shape_flat flags the profile does rise: the chain sits at 5.3-7.4e4 from s = 14 in to s = 2 and the last two points at the origin are 9.5e4 and 1.03e5, a factor 1.6 lift in the final centimetre or two along the muon reference curve. It is only two points on a 14 cm track with no long plateau to measure against, which is why I am at medium rather than high. What carries the item is the topology past the stop: four unassigned pieces the chain types pdg 11 / shower (102009 attached at d_min 0.0, then 102005, 102007 and 102011) fan out forward at cos_fwd 0.74-0.81, spanning 5.2 to 8.3 cm each and reaching 9.5 cm from the stop with transverse offsets of only 1.9-4.6 cm, and they carry 4.8e3 to 3.0e4 e/cm, i.e. a tenth to half of MIP. That is a low-energy electron fan leaving the stop, not muon charge - and it is emphatically not the undershoot case, which needs a short forward tip at several times MIP. b, c, d and e all show the same picture: a clean straight amber stub, a star, and a spray of thin dotted arms opening past it; f_meas shows the muon bright orange to time slice 728 and the fan as near-navy (very low charge) immediately after, with the dead-channel bands in all three planes well away from the stop. 102014 is a 2-point 0.6 cm stub at 81e3 e/cm sitting dead on the body line (0.1 cm transverse) just beyond the fit first point at the entry end, i.e. a stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop, so muon. 340012 is a 2-point speck 39 cm out, 31.8 cm past the stop plane and 23.7 cm clear of the body, on the same forward bearing as the fan: gamma.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: the real stop is about 3 cm past the fit last point, at the far end of 110007 (3.0 cm at 1e5 e/cm, cos_fwd 0.95); --pin-rr cannot record it, so the tip is tagged muon.
