Competing reading, and the reason for medium: the chain sells a coherent muon-CAPTURE story (a pdg 2212 stub plus 13.7 MeV of capture gammas), and capture excludes a Michel - on that reading 110001 is part of the stop/capture smear rather than an electron and the item is STM_ONLY / detached dots. I went the other way because the charge falls from 1e5 to 42705 across 110007 into 110001, and a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP. 110001 is small for a Michel (1.8 cm, 4 pts, about 3-4 MeV).
evidence: 88 cm chain entering 0.9 cm inside the anode/x face and running inward to end 67.3 cm from the nearest wall, so contained on d_face even though the chain rejects it stop_near_boundary - the reason for that flag is the y seam, which sits 5.4 cm from the stop, but f_meas shows no dead or missing channels anywhere near the end in U, V or W (the nearest V dead band is ~30 channels away), so no charge is being lost there. The profile is a clean stopper: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau out to s = 90, lifting from s = 15 through 6.5-7.5e4, 8.5e4 at s = 5 and 1.24e5 at s = 4, with the last chain points at 1.11e5 and 1.01e5. This is the undershoot case. Straight ahead of the fit last point sits 110007, 6 points over 3.0 cm at 99976 e/cm with cos_fwd +0.95 and d_min 0.0 - a 3 cm piece at 1e5, twice the plateau, which is not an electron and not a coincidence at 18 deg off the muon direction; the chain types it pdg 2212 and offers a muon-capture proton reading, but an isotropic capture proton landing within 18 deg of the muon line is a 1-in-40 accident, so I read it as the muon own last three centimetres and the true stop as its far end, about 3 cm beyond the pin. Immediately past that, 110001 (4 points, 1.8 cm, cos_fwd +0.85, spanning 2.9-3.4 cm from the fit end, chain-typed pdg 11 shower) carries 42705 e/cm, i.e. back down at MIP: charge cannot fall from 1e5 to MIP and still be the same muon, so that piece is a second particle sitting at the corrected stop, and inside 10 cm the michel rule says direction does not discriminate - michel. Further out, 384004 and 385006 sit 27.8-32.6 cm from the stop, 28-32 cm clear of the body line, forward of it and compact (0.6 and 4.1 cm): gammas, which is also what the chain calls them (13.7 MeV total). The 3-D azimuths show the past-the-stop structure as one compact 5 cm blob straight off the amber spine, with the two gamma dots well detached beyond it.

notes: medium because the Michel is weak and separated: 4.8 cm at only 0.23 MIP across a 2.21 cm charge-free gap. The competing reading is the rubric detached-dot clause - a clean gap makes a piece a gamma however close it sits - which would give STM_ONLY / detached dots. I went michel because a 9-point 4.8 cm object directly past the stop is not a dot, the gap is only ~2 cm (comparable to the point spacing), and the viewer own text says the clustering split the electron off the muon.
evidence: A long one: 226.7 cm of chain (525.7 MeV by range, 569.8 MCS) entering 1.3 cm inside the y face and ending 95.4 cm from the nearest wall, about as deeply contained as this set gets. The Bragg is textbook - a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau all the way out to s = 100, lifting from about s = 25 through 7-8e4 at s = 10-20, 8.5-9.5e4 at s = 5-10 and 1.00-1.08e5 at s = 1-4, with the last point at 1.10e5, riding the muon reference curve and peaking exactly at the fit last point. No pre-peak collapse, so the pin stays; and no high-charge forward tip past the fit end, so this is not the undershoot either. Past the stop sits 125015: 9 points over 4.8 cm at 12326 e/cm, centroid 1.6 cm past the stop plane and 3.2 cm transverse, spanning 2.2-4.9 cm from the pin, which the viewer describes as bridged to the same stop vertex across 2.21 cm of empty space with the 3-D clustering having split the electron off the muon. In c, d and e it reads as a short pale-blue (low dQ/dx) arc leaving the stop, mostly hidden behind the vertex squares. At 0.23 of MIP and 4.9 MeV it is a feeble electron, but it is bridged to the stop rather than a detached dot, and the tie-break rule says bridged-to-the-stop and clear of the body goes michel. The two remaining rows are body activity: 124014, 3 points at 25 cm, sits 22.7 cm BACK along the muon at cos_fwd -0.90 and on a bearing 110 deg away from the Michel, and 36006 (9 pts, 4.6 cm, 4127 e/cm, chain-typed pdg 11 shower) lies 36 cm back dead on the body line at 3.4 cm transverse, cos_fwd -1.00 - both delta / other, neither past the stop. f_meas confirms a real stop: the dead-channel lines the track crosses are all mid-track (U ~190, V ~4000) and the last points at U 220 / V 4055 / W 7805 are well clear of any of them.

notes: medium for two reasons. First, the terminal two-point dip from 9.8e4 to 4.5e4 over the last 1.3 cm is the weakest form of the overshoot pattern; if it were read as a collapse the verdict would flip to STM_MICHEL with the pin near rr = 1.5, but there is no drawn object past the stop to be the Michel and the dip is too short, so I left it. Second, michel_kind rests entirely on one 2-point speck 20 cm off-axis - same configuration as the one on 039252_9/88, and I tagged it the same way for consistency.
evidence: 62 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and stopping 37.1 cm from the nearest z wall, 125 cm from the anode and 264 cm from the y wall - contained, and the three azimuths show one clean unbroken spine with nothing attached at the end. The profile leaves a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau at about s = 20 and climbs along the muon reference curve: 6.5-7.8e4 at s = 13-19, 8.0-8.5e4 at s = 4-8, 8.4e4 at s = 1.3 and a gold pair at 9.3-9.8e4 at s = 1.8-4.5. The last two points then fall back to 6.2e4 (s = 0.4) and 4.5e4 (s = 0.1). I left the pin where the fit put it: that dip spans about 1.3 cm and two points, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse the pin-move signature requires, and - decisively - there is no object at all past the stop for the fit to have bridged to (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the census lists exactly two rows), so there is no Michel candidate at the far side of any bridge. There is no forward high-charge tip either, so the undershoot does not apply. f_meas shows the track terminating at time slice 1140 in all three planes with the dead-channel bands well clear (nearest is the V band at 6040-6060 against a track end at 6080), so this is a real stop rather than a dead-region exit; a small puff of unfitted pale image points sits at the stop in c and d but carries no measurable charge and is not in the object census. The only other object is 180003, a 2-point 0.6 cm speck: taking the entry-to-stop chord its along-axis component is 0.0 and its transverse offset 19.7 cm, so it sits essentially in the stop plane, 20 cm clear of the muon body line and separated from the stop by a clean gap in all three azimuths - isolated, compact and on one bearing rather than several scattered round the ring, which is the gamma case; the chain calls it gamma body exclusion but off-axis separation outranks that label. A 0.6 cm two-point speck is not an electron, so the item stays STM_ONLY.

notes: medium not because the verdict is in doubt - it is a contained stopper with nothing past the end and michel_kind none is certain - but because the object is almost certainly not a muon: charges of 1.35-1.60e5 over the last 10 cm and a 6-8e4 body level are proton-like, the chain says not_muon_pid, and dQ/dx-vs-range energies disagree by 60 percent. Worth an eye if the round is counting muon stoppers.
evidence: 93 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and stopping 63.8 cm from the anode, 67.2 cm from the z wall and 205 cm from the y wall - deeply contained, and b, c, d and e all show one straight unbroken spine with a star at one end, a green entry marker at the other and absolutely nothing attached past the stop. The profile rises hugely: a 6.0-8.5e4 level over s = 40-95, a sagging patch at 3-5e4 around s = 25-40, then a steep climb from s = 25 through 8.3e4 at s = 22, 1.0-1.2e5 at s = 12-22 and a run of points at 1.35-1.60e5 at s = 2-10, with the last points at 1.17-1.42e5. That is far more charge than the muon reference curve carries anywhere (it asymptotes to 1.6e5 only at s = 0), which is why the chain rejects this one not_muon_pid and why its dQ/dx energy, 377 MeV, sits 60 percent above the 236 MeV from range - the object is much more heavily ionizing than a muon and reads as a stopping proton or similar. For the rubric question that does not matter: this is unambiguously a stopping track with a large terminal rise. The peak sits a few centimetres before the fit last point and eases to 1.17e5 at the origin, but that is not the pin-move signature - the pin-move test is a collapse far BELOW the track own plateau, and 1.17e5 is still roughly twice the 6-8e4 this track carries in its body (a fall-off at the very tip is also what recombination does to a heavily ionizing particle), so the pin stays. 98010, the 3-point 1.2 cm piece at 1.23e5 sitting essentially at the stop (0.1 cm along, 0.6 cm transverse), is the muon own final centimetre and is tagged muon; it is not the undershoot tip, which has to lie clearly ahead at cos_fwd around +0.9. The only other objects are 370007 and 371008, at 45.6 and 36.8 cm from the stop but 44.6 and 33.6 cm BACK along the body at cos_fwd -0.97 and -0.91 with transverse offsets of 10.5 and 15.6 cm - body activity behind the stop, not past it, so neither can be a gamma in the ring and both are delta / other. f_meas shows the track crossing dead-channel lines mid-body (U ~3040, V ~6890) but the terminal charge peak is incompatible with a dead-region exit in any case.

notes: Flat-to-falling profile with no face reached and no visible continuation - calling THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs. Competing reading was STM_ONLY with 105023 as the muon tip; rejected because 105023 is backward and hugging the body line.
evidence: 64 cm of chain (chord only 45 cm, so visibly wiggly), enters 1.0 cm from the +y face and the fit's last point sits 38.1 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not the issue - the profile is. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 2.5-5.4e4 plateau all the way from s=64 back to s=20, bump to about 8e4 around s=11-13, and then FALL steadily to 4.2e4 at s=2 and 3.2e4 at s=0-1. There is no rise above the track's own plateau over the last 10-20 cm; the last centimetres are at plateau, which a stopping muon cannot do, so this is a through-goer that simply ran out of imaged charge (no face, no visible continuation, no dead region under the stop in U, V or W in f_meas). The call I had to weigh: 105023 is 12 points over 6.3 cm carrying 7.4e4 mean with points to 1.25e5, sitting 2.3-4.6 cm from the fit end; on the 3-D azimuths it is 1.6-2.5 cm off the muon body line and my chord calculation puts it 85 percent aligned with the backward body direction (cos_fwd -0.69), i.e. backward and hugging the body, which is the delta rule, not a muon tip - and reading it as the true tip would additionally require the fitter to have both missed the tip and fabricated 3 collinear cm of MIP-level chain past it. The turbo gradient in the c/e stop zooms looks like a rise toward the end but that is display trap 2 and I did not use it for charge. 105020 (26 cm, 44 pts, cos_fwd -0.87) and 105024 (9.4 cm, cos_fwd -0.84) lie along the body behind the stop; 410028 is a 2-point speck 39 cm back essentially on the body line (chord cos 0.98); 407027 is a 2-point speck 38 cm out in an unrelated direction; C106 is a separate 160 cm track 39-60 cm away. All delta / other, and no gamma tag is used because a through-goer has no stop to define one.

notes: Flat plateau to the last point plus a dead-channel exit in U; the fit end is 108 cm from any face but that is not the test.
evidence: A 489.5 cm cosmic that enters 0.6 cm from the +x face and whose fit end sits 108.3 cm from the nearest face, so containment says nothing here and the profile has to decide. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points run 5-9.5e4 across the whole displayed window with the usual factor-two scatter and occasional delta spikes to 1.4-1.5e5 around s=41-44; over the last 20 cm they sit at 4.8-5.2e4 with a couple at 6.5-7.7e4 at s=2-7, i.e. flat on the plateau to the very last point with no climb toward the muon reference curve at all. All seven fitted segments carry essentially the same mean charge (4.7-5.3e4), which is what a minimum-ionising through-goer looks like end to end. f_meas explains where it went: in the U plane the whole stop neighbourhood is inside hatched dead-channel bands (roughly channels 855-905 and again 915-985), and the U/V/W measured panels show the last hit separated from the body by a ~75 time-slice empty stretch that the fit bridged, so the cluster ends where the imaging ran out rather than where the muon did. The d/e stop azimuths show the same thing geometrically - the pin star stands clear of the drawn track with only a two-or-three point speck beside it. Nothing at the stop in the flow summary (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The only non-muon row, 116018, is 28 points 90-105 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -0.99 and 7 cm off the chord line - body activity, delta / other; no gamma tag is used because a through-goer has no stop to define one.

notes: Fit end is 132 cm from every face with no visible continuation and no dead region under it, but the plateau runs flat to the last point - THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs.
evidence: A 310.9 cm essentially straight cosmic - the chord from entry to fit end is 283 cm - entering 10.1 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest face, so this is a containment-vs-profile case and the profile decides it. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a broad 4-6.5e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in, and over the last 20 cm they are 6.5e4, 6.9e4, 7.4e4 at s=10-15 then 4.6e4, 5.2e4, 5.5e4 at s=3-8 and 6.4e4, 5.0e4, 4.2e4, 3.8e4 at s=0-3. That is flat-to-slightly-falling into the fit end with no climb along the muon reference curve at all; the chain's own reject list says the same (no_bragg, shape_flat) and the flow summary reports nothing at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). The three stop azimuths show a pencil-thin uniform track running to the pin star with no arm, no dot and no widening near the end, and the b frame shows it crossing most of the drift volume. f_meas has the last hits clear of the dead-channel lines in U (bands at 1055-1075, 1140 and 1305-1330 are all well away from the track end) and V, so I cannot point to a dead-region exit - by the rubric a flat profile is enough on its own, and this cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. The three unassigned rows 25015, 25018 and 25021 are all 173-212 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1.00 and only 1-5 cm off the chord line, at 0.5-1.6e4 - body activity far from the end, so delta / other; no gamma tag, since a through-goer has no stop to define one.

notes: Competing reading was overshoot with the true stop at the s=11-13 spike; rejected because the spike is ~2 cm wide with plateau charge on both sides and the profile recovers to plateau afterwards instead of staying collapsed.
evidence: 165.9 cm of chain running almost parallel to the top y wall - it enters 2.4 cm from that face and the fit end is still only 13.2 cm below it, so an exit through the wall it has been hugging the whole way is entirely available. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 5-6.5e4 plateau from s=15 back to s=60, and coming in from s=20 they go 6.2e4, 6.3e4 at s=15-20, then 4.3-4.5e4 at s=6, 4.4-4.7e4 at s=2, 5.8-6.0e4 at s=3 and 3.6e4 at s=1: at or below plateau to the last point, no climb along the muon reference curve. What made this one medium rather than high is a narrow spike at s=11-13 - four points at 8.1e4, 9.2e4, 1.2e5 and 1.37e5 - which at first reading looks like a peak several cm before the fit end. I rejected the overshoot for two reasons: it is only about 2 cm wide with plateau values at 6.3e4 immediately outside it on the far side, which is a localised delta or blob rather than the gradual last-10-to-20-cm climb the rubric asks for; and the charge after it does not stay collapsed, it recovers to 4.4-6.0e4 by s=1-3, whereas the low-dQ/dx bridge the overshoot mechanism describes stays low all the way to the fit end. The same picture appears far back at s=60-100 where the chain carries 0.9-1.65e5 in patches, and f_meas shows why to distrust those: in U the track sits among hatched dead-channel bands at 1390-1420 and the brightest orange hits are right on them. The stop azimuths show a pencil track running to the pin star with no arm and no widening. The chain itself rejects with no_bragg and shape_flat and reports nothing at the stop. 124013 is a 2-point 0.1 cm speck the chain calls a capture gamma 26 cm out and 121012 a 2-point speck 10.6 cm out, but a through-goer has no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so both are delta / other, as are 35003 and 35008, which lie 106-126 cm back essentially on the body line.

notes: Chain says no_bragg but the 4x plot shows a clean monotone climb 6.5e4 -> 9.7e4 over the last 15 cm on the reference curve. Overshoot rejected because the post-peak decline passes back through plateau, leaving no sustained sub-plateau bridge. Michel is small (1.4 cm, 4.6 MeV) and its plane image overlaps a dead-channel band in V, hence medium.
evidence: 206.6 cm of chain entering 0.5 cm from the z face and stopping 66.1 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the plateau is 5-6.5e4 from s=100 in to s=20, and then the chain climbs monotonically along the muon reference curve - 6.5e4 at s=20, 7.0e4 at s=15, 7.8e4 at s=10, 8.5e4 at s=8, 9.4e4 at s=6 and 9.7e4 at s=5 - sitting essentially on the drawn curve the whole way. That is a textbook last-15-cm rise, and I am disagreeing with the chain here, which rejects the object as no_bragg / shape_flat and sets is_stm 0. The last four chain points then come back down: 7.9e4 at s=4, 6.7e4 at s=3, 4.5e4 at s=2 and 4.0e4 at s=1. I considered moving the pin to the s=5 peak and calling 77001 the collapsed bridge, and rejected it because the decline passes back THROUGH the plateau on its way down - 7.9e4 and 6.7e4 are at or above the 5.5e4 plateau - so there is no sustained sub-plateau stretch for the fit to have bridged, only the last two points sitting about 27 percent low, which is exactly the ordinary end-of-track partial-charge scatter the rubric tells me to leave alone. The pin stays. Past the end sits 229003, three points over 1.4 cm carrying 5.4e4 mean (6.7e4, 5.4e4, 3.8e4), bridged to the stop vertex across 0.37 cm and lying essentially perpendicular to the muon body (chord cos +0.09, cos_fwd -0.26, 0.6 cm off the line at 0.6 cm out). It is attached at the stop and it leaves at MIP where the muon has just been at nearly twice MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP - so it is a second particle and I tag it michel. What keeps this medium rather than high: the piece is only 4.6 MeV and 1.4 cm, a very short Michel, and f_meas shows the whole stop neighbourhood collapsing into a single compact high-charge blob which in V sits directly on a hatched dead-channel band at 7540-7550, so I cannot separate the electron from the muon tip in the measured planes. The 3-D stop azimuths show a clean pencil track running to the pin with only that small terminal structure and no other arm or dot.

notes: Hardest part was the 1.47e5 hump 8.5 cm before the fit end; rejected as a delta because it is more than twice the muon reference curve at that residual range and the profile returns to plateau behind it.
evidence: 243.4 cm of chain, entering 14.7 cm from the z face and ending 101.1 cm from the nearest wall, so again the profile has to decide. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 4.5-6.5e4 plateau all the way in from s=100. Coming into the end there is a hump: 6.6e4 at s=12, 8.1e4 and 1.03e5 at s=10, then 9.4e4, 1.33e5 and 1.47e5 at s=8.5, then straight back down to 7.5e4 at s=7 and 5.2-6.0e4 - i.e. plateau - through s=3 to s=5, before the last two centimetres tail off through 4.3e4, 3.4e4, 2.7e4, 2.1e4 to 1.55e4 at the fit's last point. I read the hump as a delta ray, not a Bragg peak, on the rubric's own scale argument: the overlaid muon curve is only about 6.8e4 at 8.5 cm of residual range, real stoppers top out at 1.2-1.35e5 and only in their last centimetre, and these points sit at more than twice the curve where they are - a stopping muon cannot be at 1.47e5 with 8.5 cm still to run. The profile also recovers to full plateau for two centimetres after the hump, which the low-charge bridge in the overshoot mechanism does not do. So there is no rise above the plateau in the last 10-20 cm and the item is a through-goer; the final 2 cm tail is where the imaging ran out, and f_meas supports that - in W the track's terminal hit at channel ~11995 sits directly on a grey dead-channel line, while U and V show it running clean off the panel. The three stop azimuths show a straight pencil track to the pin star with no arm, no fan and no dot. The chain agrees on the reject (no_bragg, shape_flat) and reports nothing at the stop. Both unassigned rows are small specks back along the body - 342014 is 5 points 20 cm out at chord cos +0.97 and 4.9 cm off the line, 343015 is 6 points 38 cm out at chord cos +0.96 - so delta / other, and no gamma tag since a through-goer has no stop.

notes: Fit end 3.5 cm from the x face with a flat-to-falling profile - a genuine wall exit, the least ambiguous kind of THRU.
evidence: 132.3 cm of chain in the far -x/-y corner of the detector: it enters 0.6 cm from the z face and the fit end is 3.5 cm from the x face, so it leaves through the wall it is pointed at. The projections confirm it - in the top and end views the pin star sits right on the dashed detector boundary. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 4.5-6.5e4 plateau across the whole displayed range with the usual delta spikes to 1.0-1.3e5, and coming into the end they are 6.3e4 and 8.3e4 at s=15, 6.6e4 at s=12, 8.1-8.4e4 at s=8, 5.8-6.6e4 at s=5-7, 3.0-4.6e4 at s=3-4 and 1.0-2.15e4 over the last two centimetres. That is flat to falling, never a rise off the plateau along the muon reference curve; the terminal drop to a fifth of plateau in the last 2 cm is the track running out of active volume, not a Bragg peak, and a Bragg peak would have to be at 1.2e5 there, not 1e4. f_meas shows the same thing directly: in all three planes the measured hits run in an unbroken diagonal straight off the top of the panel with no terminal blob and no dead-channel band under the end (the hatched bands in U at 20-30 and 90-100 and in V at 3810-3830 are far from the track). The three stop azimuths show a single smooth pencil track with nothing at the pin - no arm, no dot, no fan. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) and reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0. There is only one drawn object, the muon chain itself, so no attribution question arises.

notes: Wall exit at 11.8 cm plus a flat profile with a 2 cm terminal die-off; the terminal hits also sit on a dead-channel band in U.
evidence: 101.5 cm of chain low in the -x/-y corner: it enters 0.5 cm from the z face and the fit end is 11.8 cm from the x face, and in the end and top projections the pin star sits essentially on the dashed boundary, so a wall exit is right there. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 5-6.5e4 plateau over the whole displayed range with delta spikes to 1.0-1.4e5 scattered along it, and coming into the end they read 7.5-8.3e4 at s=15, 6.1-6.5e4 at s=12-14, 5.6e4 at s=10, 5.7-6.5e4 at s=8, 5.4-6.3e4 at s=5-7, 5.3-5.5e4 at s=3-4 and then 3.6e4, 2.5e4, 1.3e4 and 0.4e4 over the last two centimetres. Flat all the way in and then a two-centimetre die-off - no climb along the muon reference curve, which at 5 cm of residual range would already be near 9e4 and is nowhere approached. The chain's own reject list is shape_flat plus profile_sparse and it reports nothing at the stop. f_meas is consistent with an exit rather than a stop: the measured hits run in an unbroken line off the top of all three panels, the terminal hit in U sits right against the hatched dead-channel band at channels 700-712, and there is no terminal charge blob in any plane. The three stop azimuths show a straight pencil track ending at the pin with no arm, no dot and no widening. The single unassigned row 166008 is a 2-point speck with no measured dQ/dx 49.9 cm away and 46 cm off the muon line - an unrelated object, and in any case a through-goer has no stop against which gamma or michel could be defined, so it is delta / other.

notes: Flat profile at the fit end with no face and no visible continuation; I suspect this 33 cm stub is a piece of a longer track but no parent object is drawn, so THRU rather than FRAG_THRU.
evidence: A short object: only 33.0 cm of chain in 56 points, entering 12.9 cm from the z face and ending 41.4 cm from it, so both ends are interior. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 6.5-8e4 band across the whole 33 cm with spikes to 9-1.1e5 around s=13-22 and dips to 2.2e4 and 0.75e4 at s=3-4; at the fit end itself the points are 6.8e4, 6.5e4 and 5.5e4, i.e. sitting on the same band the rest of the track sits on. There is no climb off that plateau over the last 10-20 cm and nothing approaching the muon reference curve, which would be near 9e4 at 5 cm and 1.6e5 at the stop, so by the operative test this is a through-goer even though the fit end is 41 cm from the nearest face - the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. The three stop azimuths show a uniform pencil stub running to the pin with nothing at either end - no arm, no dot, no fan and no widening - and f_meas shows a clean unbroken diagonal in all three planes with no terminal blob; the hatched dead-channel bands in U at 2480-2550 and V at 6390-6440 are beside the track but not under either end. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). What keeps this at medium: 33 cm of flat MIP-level track with both ends interior looks like a piece of something longer rather than a whole object, but no larger parent is drawn in any frame - only 27 thinned context points, none of them forming a continuation - so I cannot call it a fragment on the evidence in front of me and I have used the plain THRU. There is only one drawn object, the muon chain itself.

notes: Flat-to-falling profile on a badly imaged 97 cm chain with a near-empty stretch at s=60-75; no face, no continuation, THRU on the profile.
evidence: 96.7 cm of chain entering 1.0 cm from the z face and ending 51.8 cm from it. This is a poorly imaged object - the chain mean is only 3.4e4 and on the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the points scatter between 2e4 and 5e4 for most of their length with a long nearly charge-free stretch at s=60-75 where they drop to 0.3-2e4, which is why the chain also flags profile quality. Coming into the fit end the non-zero points read 7.3-7.9e4 at s=13-18, 5.2-5.8e4 at s=10-12, 4.4-5.2e4 at s=2-8 and then 3.7e4, 2.3e4 and 0.75e4 over the last centimetre and a half: no climb off the band, and the muon reference curve would demand roughly 9e4 at 5 cm and 1.6e5 at the stop. So there is no Bragg rise at the fit end and the item is a through-goer whose cluster ran out of imaged charge - there is no face within 50 cm and no visible continuation, and the rubric says to say so rather than reach for UNCLEAR. f_meas shows only a short orange stub of the track inside the stop window with no terminal blob and no dead-channel band under it. Everything else drawn here is a ring of 2-point specks: 252003 (32.4 cm out, 26 cm off the muon line), 251002 (32.5 cm, 32 cm off), 250001 (39 cm, 37 cm off), 257006 (40 cm, 34 cm off), 253004 (53 cm, 53 cm off), 255005 and 258007 (57 cm, 20-35 cm off), pointing in unrelated directions all round the 60 cm ring. The chain calls 252003 a capture gamma at 0.52 MeV, but a through-goer has no stop against which a gamma can be defined, so by the rubric's THRU rule every non-chain row here is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 1). Bragg climbs on the reference curve to 1.14e5 at s=1-3; nothing past the stop, so STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL.
evidence: 311.4 cm of chain entering 0.9 cm from the +y face and stopping 55.0 cm from the nearest wall, comfortably contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: on the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 4-6e4 plateau from s=100 in to about s=20, then climb steadily - 6.4-6.7e4 at s=15, 7.7-8.4e4 at s=13, 6.8e4 at s=7, 7.9-9.2e4 at s=5, and 9.2e4, 1.02e5, 1.09e5, 1.13e5 and 1.14e5 clustered at s=1-3 - sitting right on the drawn muon reference curve through the whole climb and topping out at 1.14e5, exactly the 1.2-1.35e5 band the rubric says real stoppers reach. The rise is ragged in places (two points back at 3.5-4.0e4 around s=10) but it is unmistakably a rise, and the single 3.3e4 point at the fit's very last position is one partial-charge point, the ordinary end-of-track scatter the rubric tells me to leave alone rather than a sustained collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. Past the stop there is nothing at all: the three stop azimuths show the track terminating cleanly at the pin star with no arm, no dot, no fan and no second particle in any direction, and the flow summary agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). I also checked for the undershoot - there is no short forward high-charge piece, no row here has positive cos_fwd or a small dstop. All three non-muon rows sit far back along the body: 106011 is 13 points 46-53 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 and 3.4 cm off the chord line, 378022 a 2-point speck 40 cm back and 4.1 cm off the line, and 106008 is 21 points at only 3.2e3 e/cm some 259-267 cm back, up near the entry. All body activity, so delta / other, and with no michel and no gamma the kind is none. One caveat noted but not decisive: in V the stop neighbourhood sits beside the hatched dead-channel band at 7290-7345, so some terminal charge could be missing - it does not change a peak that already reaches 1.14e5.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 1). Undershoot checked and rejected on charge: the forward arm is at MIP, not several times MIP, and the muon's own peak already reaches 1.19e5 at the fit's last point.
evidence: A short stopper: 40.0 cm of chain entering right on the x face (d_face 0.0) and ending 34.0 cm from it. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the chain points hold a 5-6e4 plateau from s=40 in to s=15 and then climb along the drawn muon reference curve - 7.9-8.5e4 at s=8-10, 6.6-7.3e4 at s=6, 8.5-8.6e4 at s=4, 8.7-9.1e4 at s=2-3, 1.10e5 at s=1 and 1.19e5 at the fit's own last point. The peak is reached AT the fit end, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach, so the muon's tip is fully accounted for inside the fit and the pin does not move. I explicitly checked the undershoot, because the shape here is the one that manufactures false Michels - a short forward piece the chain types pdg 11 - and it fails on the load-bearing clause: 116008 carries 5.77e4 mean over 13 points, essentially the muon's own MIP plateau, with its points spread 2.05e4 to 8.7e4, nowhere near the 0.9-1.2e5 (four to six times MIP) that would mark it as the muon's last centimetres. So it is the ordinary case: a 7.4 cm arm attached at the shared stop vertex, leaving at a 44 degree kink (cos_fwd +0.69, 2.3 cm off the body line at 3.2 cm out) at MIP where the muon has just been at more than twice MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP - and 7.4 cm at 20.9 MeV is a sensible Michel. The three stop azimuths show it plainly as a distinct blue low-charge arm branching off the amber muon tip. 447009 is a 2-point 0.2 cm dot 22.0 cm out, 21.7 cm clear of the muon body line and 57 degrees from the Michel arm's direction against 133 degrees for the body - isolated, past the stop, on the decay's side of the ring, so gamma; charge is not a criterion here and I did not use its 5.1e4. C448 is a separate 11-point cluster 58.9 cm out, 54.8 cm off the body line and 129 degrees round from the Michel arm - the opposite side of the ring, an unrelated object with no PR segment, so delta / other. With one michel and one gamma the kind is both.

notes: Verdict is high-confidence: contained stop, unambiguous Bragg rise, attached MIP arm. The uncertain part is only the far-speck attribution (119008 at 51 cm, 121010 at 54 cm): kind is 'both' regardless because 120009 at 15 cm is already a detached dot. No undershoot - the forward attached piece is at MIP (5.07e4 against a 5.4e4 plateau), not the several-times-MIP tip the undershoot signature requires. No overshoot - no sustained collapse before the fit end.
evidence: 205.8 cm chain, enters 14.9 cm from the z face and stops 114.0 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained, so containment is not in question. On the 4x-upscaled dQ/dx panel the chain sits on a 5.4e4 plateau all the way in and then climbs off it over the last ~15 cm: 6.8e4 near s=10, 7.6-8.4e4 at s=5-8, 9.4e4 at s=4, 1.04e5, 1.10e5 and 1.15e5 in the last two cm, following the shape of the solid muon curve (which asymptotes to 1.6e5 and is never crossed, as expected). The peak is at the fit's own last point with no collapse before it, so the pin stays. Attached at the stop is a 7.9 cm 14-point segment 35005 at 5.07e4 e/cm (d_min 0.0, cos_fwd 0.37) continued by a 2.6 cm piece 35007 out to 8.96 cm at 4.46e4 - an arm leaving the Bragg peak at MIP and falling, which a muon at its own peak cannot do, and 9 cm is the right range for a ~25 MeV electron; the three azimuths show it as a distinct blue arm breaking off the amber muon band at a large angle, well clear of the body line. A 0.4 cm 2-point speck 120009 at 15.1 cm sits along the continuation of that arm direction (12 deg from it) but across a clean ~6 cm charge-free gap, so by the attachment tie-break it is a detached dot, gamma, not part of the electron. Two faint far specks, 119008 at 51 cm (2.4e4 e/cm, 12 deg off the arm axis) and 121010 at 54 cm (4.8e4, 27 deg off), are on the Michel's side of the stop and read as gammas; 125012 at 52.8 cm has cos_fwd -0.96, i.e. sits on the muon body line, and 122011 at 13.7 cm is backward at 81 deg from the arm in an unrelated direction and body-excluded by the chain, so both are delta / other. f_meas shows no dead-channel band at the stop in U, V or W, and the measured-predicted panels leave no residual charge past the end.

notes: Medium, not high, for two reasons. (1) The highest charge on the chain is not at the stop but in a 5 cm blob 20-26 cm before it, peaking at 1.26e5 against 9.8e4 at the end; I read that as a local delta or nuclear interaction rather than the true Bragg peak, because the charge recovers to a 5.5-6.6e4 MIP band after it instead of collapsing to the 0.15-0.5-of-MIP level the overshoot signature requires, and because an electron does not then climb again at its own far end. The pin is therefore left alone, but this is the item in my chunk where an overshoot pin is most arguable. (2) MESSY is a live competing reading - 19 of 27 drawn objects are shower-typed and MCS gives 84.8 MeV against 172.4 by range with ambiguity 0.84 - and I ruled it out only on the spine visible in d_3d_stop/e_3d_stop. No undershoot: no forward high-charge tip past the fit end (the only forward speck is 44 cm out with no measured charge).
evidence: A short, heavily fragmented object: 63 cm of chain broken into 8 muon segments with 19 further pieces the chain types 'pdg 11, shower', all of them at cos_fwd -0.96 to -1.0 and 20-53 cm from the stop, i.e. lying on the muon body line. It enters 1.5 cm from the z face and the fit ends 22.0 cm from the nearest face, so the end is inside the volume but not deeply. b_3d_wide is a formless clump, but d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop resolve a genuine continuous spine from the stop star running the full 50 cm chord with the shower pieces bundled around its back half and sprayed at the entry end - so there is a coherent spine and this is not MESSY. The dQ/dx profile is bimodal and ugly: from the entry end the segment averages sit at 8e3-1.6e4 out beyond 40 cm, 3.2e4 at 35-40, 4.7e4 at 26-35, then a 5 cm blob at 20-26 cm whose points run up to 1.26e5 (segment 41044, mean 8.2e4), then back down to a 5.5-6.6e4 band over 5-20 cm, and finally a climb over the last ~5 cm through 8.0-8.4e4 to 9.4, 9.7 and 9.8e4 in the last two centimetres, tracking the shape of the solid muon curve without crossing it. That final climb off the local band is a ragged but real Bragg rise, so the verdict is not THRU. Nothing past the end reads as an electron: the chain reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0, and the only objects not on the body line are three 2-point specks at 44, 47 and 59 cm (136051 forward and up in +y+z with no measured charge, 137052 at -x+y, 135050 at -y) pointing in mutually unrelated directions around the ring, which the rubric's far-speck rule puts in delta / other rather than gamma. f_meas shows the stop well away from the dead bands in all three planes.

notes: High confidence: single object, monotone Bragg rise to 1.24e5 at the fit end, nothing drawn past the stop. No undershoot (no forward piece of any kind exists past the fit end) and no overshoot (no pre-end collapse). The one mild caveat is that the chain reports MCS not computed (0 segments), so the muon hypothesis rests on range and dQ/dx alone - but the profile shape settles it.
evidence: A short, completely isolated 38.7 cm track - the object table lists exactly one drawn object, the muon chain itself, so there is nothing else anywhere near this stop. It enters 0.2 cm from the x face, i.e. right at the boundary, and the fit ends 27.8 cm from the nearest face (z), so the end is inside the volume. The dQ/dx profile is textbook: a 5.5-6.5e4 band from the entry end in, with normal factor-of-1.5 scatter, then a monotone climb over the last 6 cm - 8.6e4 and 8.8e4 at s=5-6, 9.85e4 at s=2, and 1.17, 1.21 and 1.24e5 in the last centimetre - hugging the shape of the solid muon reference curve, which as always asymptotes higher (1.6e5) and is not crossed. The peak sits at the fit's own last point with no collapse in front of it, so the pin stays where it is. The three 3-D azimuths show a smoothly curving single filament ending in the stop star with no arm, no stub and no detached speck in the frame; b_3d_wide confirms nothing else is drawn at wide zoom. f_meas shows the track resolved in all three planes with the stop end clear of every dead-channel band, and the measured-minus-predicted panels show no residual charge continuing past the end. Nothing past the stop reads as an electron or a gamma, so this is a bare stopping muon.

notes: High confidence THRU: flat sub-MIP profile to the last point, charge continuing straight ahead past the fit end, and the end 1.3 cm from the z wall on the cathode seam - three independent reasons. Chain agrees (is_stm 0, rejects continuation / stop_near_boundary / plateau_off_mip). RUBRIC TENSION, flagged rather than resolved silently: the THRU convention says 'fitted chain segments muon, everything else delta / other', but the muon tag row explicitly covers 'a stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop', which can only ever occur on a THRU item. I tagged the continuation stub 88006 muon so that clause is not dead text; a scanner reading the THRU sentence literally would tag it delta / other. michel_kind is none either way. No undershoot and no overshoot - there is no Bragg peak anywhere on this profile to be early or late.
evidence: 42.7 cm of chain entering 11.4 cm from the z face and ending 1.3 cm from the z wall, i.e. at the boundary, with the end point also sitting exactly on the x seam (stop x 234.69 against seam_x 234.7, cathode 231.7). The dQ/dx panel decides it on its own: the profile is a flat, low band the whole way in, roughly 2e4-6.4e4 with a 4e4 centre of gravity, running well below the solid muon curve everywhere and with the last points at s = 0-3 sitting at 4.3e4, 3.8e4, 5.2e4 and 6.4e4 - no climb off the plateau at all, and if anything the band is below MIP rather than rising above it. A stopping muon cannot end at MIP, so this is a through-goer regardless of geometry. The picture agrees twice over: a 9.0 cm 16-point piece 88006 leaves the fit's last point at cos_fwd +0.98 and d_min 0.0 carrying 4.1e4 e/cm - the same charge as the chain, i.e. the track simply carrying straight on across the cathode seam into the neighbouring drift volume, which is what the chain itself flags as 'continuation' - and d_3d_stop shows that stub collinear with the incoming track past the stop star. A separate 26.6 cm 45-point object 88001 at 3.7e4 leaves at cos_fwd +0.46 in a direction 117 deg from the muon body and is a different object entirely; 88004 is a 6.7 cm 12-point piece at cos_fwd -1.0 sitting on the body line 37 cm back. Neither is decay charge and neither can be, since there is no stop here. f_meas shows the track running to the edge of the drawn region with charge still present in all three planes.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: the fit stops about 2.4 cm short. The real stop is at the far end of piece 39009 (5 points, 2.4 cm, cos_fwd +0.88, d_min 0.0, 1.19e5 e/cm), which I have tagged muon; --pin-rr cannot be pushed past the fit's last point so the corrected stop is not recorded in the label. Note the chain types this tip pdg 2212 (proton), not the pdg 11 the rubric's undershoot template describes - I invoked the undershoot on the charge and the geometry, which the rubric says are the load-bearing clauses, not on the chain's particle guess. Medium and not high for the second call: 39005 sits at cos_fwd -0.81, only just off the -0.85 body-line threshold, so the competing reading is that it is a large backward delta and the item is STM_ONLY / none. I went michel on off-axis separation (about 35 deg from the muon body chord, a visible V in d_3d_stop) plus attachment at 1.74 cm and the 15.7 cm at-MIP length; a scanner weighting cos_fwd over the azimuths would land on STM_ONLY.
evidence: 50.0 cm of chain entering 0.5 cm from the z face and ending 31.1 cm from the nearest wall (y), so the end is contained. This is the fit-stops-short case. The chain's own plateau sits high, 6.5-7.5e4 against the 6.7e4 MIP line, and its last five centimetres climb only modestly to 8.5-9.2e4, which is why the chain rejected the item as shape_flat. What the chain's fit does not include is 39009: a 2.4 cm five-point piece with d_min 0.0 and cos_fwd +0.88 - i.e. sitting straight ahead of the fit's last point - carrying 1.19e5 e/cm, and appearing on the dQ/dx panel as the single red point at 1.22e5 right on the origin line. A 2 cm piece at 1.2e5 is not an electron and is not a shower fragment; it is what the muon's own last centimetres look like, so the fit ended about 2.4 cm early and the true stop is at the far end of that tip. Read that way the profile is a proper Bragg rise - 7e4 plateau, 8.5-9.2e4 over the last five cm, 1.19e5 in the final tip - and the flat-shape rejection is an artefact of the early fit end. Past that stop there is a 15.7 cm 27-point object 39005 at 5.4e4 e/cm, slightly below the muon's own plateau, whose nearest point is 1.74 cm from the fit end; d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop show it leaving the stop as a distinct faint spray that opens away from the amber muon band into a clear V rather than hugging it, and the chain types it pdg 11 shower rather than body-excluding it. An arm leaving a Bragg peak at MIP is a second particle and 15.7 cm is the right range for a ~30 MeV Michel, so it is the electron. The three remaining objects are 2-3 point specks at 24.5-28 cm with cos_fwd -0.93 to -0.95, i.e. sitting on the muon body line, and the chain body-excludes all three, so they are delta / other; there is no isolated dot clear of the body line and hence no gamma. f_meas shows the stop clear of the dead-channel bands in U, V and W.

notes: Medium. The competing reading is THRU: the chain rejects this item as no_bragg and shape_flat, and the pre-collapse rise I am calling the Bragg peak only reaches 9.7e4 against a 5.5e4 plateau, a factor 1.6, while comparable excursions to 8.6-9.7e4 occur at s = 20-25, 45-48 and 68 where they must be delta rays. I went STM_MICHEL on the rubric's own clause that a Michel topology is sufficient even when the Bragg peak is unclear, plus three things THRU cannot explain: the end is 115 cm from every face with no dead region in any plane, the profile is not flat to the last point but collapses to a quarter of MIP, and nothing at all continues in the muon's own direction. Second soft spot: the Michel candidate carries only 1.4-1.7e4 e/cm, well below the MIP an electron's first centimetres should have, which is what a fit bridging sparse charge looks like but is also what a badly imaged region looks like. Pin moved to rr 8.2 (the 73015/73013 junction); a scanner who left the pin alone would still have to explain the 8 cm quarter-MIP tail. No undershoot here.
evidence: 141.7 cm of chain entering 0.2 cm from the x face and ending 115.2 cm from the nearest wall, so the end is as deeply contained as anything in this chunk and the track has to finish somewhere. The segment arc lengths cumulate from the fit end as 73013 0-8.2 cm, 73015 8.2-10.6, 73011 10.6-121.9, 73012 121.9-142.3, and the dQ/dx panel read against that ruler shows the overshoot signature: a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau all the way in, a rise to 7.4, 7.6, 8.4, 8.9 and 9.7e4 over s = 12-16, then a collapse through 5.2e4 at s = 11, 4.0e4 at s = 9.5 and 2.8e4 at s = 8.5 into a smooth run of 13 points at 1.2-2.2e4 filling the whole of s = 0-8 - roughly a quarter of the track's own plateau, where a muon within 8 cm of its Bragg peak would be far above it. Segment 73013 is also geometrically a bridge rather than track: 8.2 cm of arc spanning only 4.36 cm of 3-D distance, i.e. a hairpin, and its centroid direction (0.54,0.58,-0.61) sits 75 deg off the muon body direction (0.92,-0.33,-0.20). So the muon really stopped at the 73015/73013 junction and the fit ran on into the decay product; I have put the pin at 8.2 cm. Past that junction, in the same 75 deg branch, are 73005 (17 points, 9.8 cm, 1.4e4) and 73014 (9 points, 4.7 cm, 1.6e4), and then a string of detached compact pieces along the same direction at 15-18, 22-25, 26 and 33 cm from the fit end (208016, 209017, 210018, 211019, dir vectors all within about 15 deg of the arm's). The attached low-charge branch is the Michel; the four detached specks lie on the Michel's side rather than scattered around the ring, and each is separated from the arm by a clean 4-6 cm charge-free gap, so by the attachment tie-break they are dots, i.e. gamma. f_meas is decisive on the alternative: in U, V and W the track ends well clear of every dead-channel band, with the blob string visible as real measured charge off to the side, so the end is not a dead-region exit.

notes: High confidence. Textbook contained stopper with a monotone Bragg rise to 1.195e5 at the fit end, one isolated faint speck 25 cm straight ahead. The only judgement call is gamma vs delta / other on 442004, and it is not close: it is on the far side of the stop from the body (cos_fwd +0.88), not on the body line, and the rubric says charge is not a criterion for a gamma. That call is what makes michel_kind 'detached dots' rather than 'none'; nothing else in the item turns on it. No undershoot, no overshoot.
evidence: A long, clean 248 cm muon: it enters 8.0 cm from the z face and the fit ends 80.7 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained, and range, dQ/dx and MCS all agree on the energy (573, 601 and 558 MeV, MCS ambiguity 0.02). The dQ/dx profile is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk - a 5.4e4 plateau far out, lifting to about 6.5e4 by s = 20, 7.5-8.5e4 over s = 10-15, 9.0-9.3e4 at s = 6-9, 1.04-1.10e5 at s = 2-5 and 1.195e5 at the fit's own last point, tracking the shape of the solid muon curve the whole way up and, as always, staying below it. The peak is at the last point with no collapse in front of it, so the pin does not move, and there is no forward high-charge tip past the end, so this is neither the overshoot nor the undershoot case. Only one other object is drawn: 442004, three points spanning 1.3 cm at 9.1e3 e/cm, sitting 24.6-25.6 cm from the stop at cos_fwd +0.88, i.e. essentially straight ahead on the far side of the stop from the muon body (its direction from the stop, (-0.99,0.11,0.02), is very nearly the exact reverse of the body's (0.93,-0.14,-0.33)). The three azimuths show it as a single isolated speck floating clear of the track with a completely charge-free 25 cm gap between it and the stop, and f_meas confirms it as real measured charge in U, V and W with no dead band anywhere near the stop. At 0.17 of MIP, 1.3 cm long and detached across 25 cm it cannot be a 35 MeV electron; it is a detached dot, so gamma. An isolated capture-gamma candidate does not promote the item, so the verdict stays STM_ONLY while michel_kind is detached dots.

notes: High confidence THRU on the flat profile alone, per the rubric's rule that a flat MIP profile to the last point is sufficient and no visible continuation, face or dead region is needed. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). Nothing else is drawn, so there is no tag or michel_kind judgement to make and no undershoot tip to consider. Worth noting for the round: this is the second item in my chunk where both ends of a long track are tens of centimetres from any face and the cluster just stops - the imaging, not the physics, sets the end.
evidence: A 312 cm ruler-straight track, the only object drawn in the whole item. Neither end reaches a face: the entry is 47.8 cm from the z face and the fit end 61.2 cm from it (68.5 cm from the x wall, 143.9 from y), so this is exactly the case the rubric warns about - a deeply placed end that is nevertheless a through-goer. The dQ/dx profile settles it: a flat band at 5.0-7.0e4 straddling the 6.7e4 MIP line from s = 0 all the way out past s = 100, with isolated single-point spikes to 1.0-1.5e5 scattered at s = 7, 12, 41, 68 and 88 that are plainly delta rays rather than a Bragg structure, because they occur at random arc lengths and the band between them never lifts. The last chain points before the origin sit at 7.2-7.6e4, one MIP-width above the band and nowhere near the solid muon curve, which is at 1.6e5 by then - there is no climb off the plateau at all. A stopping muon cannot end at MIP, so the object is a through-goer that simply ran out of imaged charge. Three points at the very end carry 1.0-2.0e4, but that is a one-centimetre partial-charge tail with no peak in front of it, which the rubric calls ordinary scatter rather than the sustained several-centimetre collapse of the overshoot signature, so the pin stays. Supporting numbers: MCS returns 1634 MeV against 718 by range with ambiguity 0.88, i.e. the track is too straight for MCS to constrain, which is what a high-momentum through-goer looks like and not what a 700 MeV stopper looks like. The three azimuths show a single unbroken filament with nothing at either end, and f_meas shows the track ending clear of every dead-channel band in U, V and W with no residual charge past the end.

notes: Medium, and this is the weakest call in my chunk - stated so a re-scan disagreement is expected rather than surprising. THRU rests on the rubric's operative test: no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the last 11 cm sitting at MIP when a stopper's last 11 cm must be roughly twice that. The competing reading is a pattern I only saw after scanning several items: across my chunk, MCS-versus-range separates my own verdicts 9 for 9 - the six items where MCS agrees with range (12/35, 13/39, 13/73, 13/103, 15/45, 15/77) I called stopping, and the three where MCS exceeds range by 1.3x to 6x (12/88, 14/47, 15/30) I called THRU. 14/84 is the single item that breaks that split: MCS 330.9 MeV at ambiguity 0.27 against 344.1 by range and 299.6 by dQ/dx, all agreeing, and the chain itself accepts the item (is_stm 1). I still went THRU for two reasons. First, the charge contradiction is direct and large, while MCS-range agreement is coincidence-prone at this length: a 143.5 cm segment has a range-equivalent momentum of about 437 MeV/c, and an ordinary through-going cosmic in that momentum band would reproduce the agreement without stopping - the test only bites when the track is long enough for the two to separate, which is why it is convincing on 14/47 (817 by range against 1737 by MCS over 312 cm) and not here. Second, f_meas rules out a dead region at the end, so there is no mechanism to hide a Bragg peak. If a re-scan calls this STM_ONLY, the MCS split is the reason. No undershoot: nothing is drawn forward of the fit end.
evidence: 143.5 cm of chain in eight fitted segments, entering 6.7 cm from the z face and ending 53.1 cm from the z wall (142.8 from x, 239.9 from y), so the end is inside the volume. The dQ/dx panel shows no Bragg rise of any kind at that end. Reading the last 20 cm on the 4x and 8x crops: the band tops out at 7.2-7.4e4 around s = 9-11, sits at 6.1-6.5e4 at s = 3-6, and the chain's own last points at s = 0-2 are 5.4-5.6e4 with three low outliers at 1.9-3.4e4 - i.e. the profile is flat at, and over the last ten centimetres drifting slightly below, the 6.7e4 MIP line right up to the fit's last point, while the solid muon curve has climbed to 9e4 by s = 2 and 1.6e5 at the origin. Segment 84024, the 10.9 cm nearest the end, averages 5.36e4, which is MIP; a muon in its last 11 cm averages roughly twice that, and its last two centimetres should be at 1.0-1.4e5 rather than 5.5e4. That is a factor-of-two contradiction with the stopping hypothesis, not point-to-point scatter. The 7.2e4 shoulder at s = 9-11 is only 1.09 of MIP, far too small to be a Bragg peak, and the subsequent fall to 5.5e4 is only 25 per cent, nothing like the sustained fall to a quarter of the plateau that the overshoot signature needs, so the pin stays where it is. Every other drawn object sits on the muon body line - the four unassigned pieces 84026, 84029, 84033 and 84034 have cos_fwd -0.99 to -1.0 at 9, 24, 63 and 72 cm from the end, and their direction vectors are within a few degrees of the body's - so they are body activity, delta / other, and there is nothing at the fit end at all in the three azimuths. f_meas shows the stop end in V sitting between two dead-channel bands about 10-15 channels away on either side, close but not inside, and clear in U and W, so missing charge from a dead region is not available as an explanation.

notes: High confidence. Three independent reasons converge: no Bragg rise (the profile falls to a third of MIP over the last 4 cm), the end lies inside a V dead-channel band and on the edge of a U one, and MCS exceeds the range momentum by a third. Chain agrees on all three (no_bragg, shape_flat, stop_into_dead). No undershoot - nothing is drawn forward of the fit end - and no overshoot, since the terminal fall has no peak in front of it.
evidence: 314.3 cm of chain entering 7.2 cm from the z face and ending 9.2 cm from the x wall (the anode face). The dQ/dx profile has no Bragg rise anywhere near that end: a broad 4.0-6.5e4 band straddling the 6.7e4 MIP line all the way in, punctuated by isolated single-point delta spikes to 1.0-1.3e5 at s = 33-36, 55, 74 and 90 that occur at random arc lengths, and then over the last four centimetres the band FALLS - 5.6e4, 5.3e4, 4.8e4 at s = 3-6, then 3.8e4, 3.7e4, 3.3e4, 3.1e4 and two points at 1.9e4 at s = 0-2 - while the solid muon curve has climbed past 9e4. Falling to a third of MIP at the end is the opposite of a Bragg peak, and there is no peak in front of the fall to make it the overshoot signature, so the pin stays. f_meas says why the charge dies: in V the track's end at channel about 4790 sits squarely INSIDE a broad dead-channel band running from roughly 4765 to 4820, and in U the end at channel 1030 is on the edge of a second wide dead band at 1010-1030 - the track walks into dead wires and the imaging stops, which is exactly the chain's own stop_into_dead rejection. The independent momentum estimates agree: MCS gives 965 MeV against 723 by range (ambiguity 0.25), i.e. the track is stiffer than its visible length allows, which is what a through-goer looks like. Of the three non-chain objects, 30008 is a 5.5 cm 10-point piece at cos_fwd -1.0 sitting on the body line 25-30 cm back, and 112010 and 113011 are 2-point specks 44 and 48 cm out in a direction unrelated to anything; on a through-goer none of them can be decay charge, so all three are delta / other and michel_kind is none.

notes: High confidence on the verdict: contained end, monotone Bragg rise to 1.05e5 at the fit's last point, and a 15 cm sub-MIP arm attached at that point and perpendicular to the muon - about as unambiguous an STM plus Michel as this chunk contains. The judgement that could move is the speck string: I tagged four of the five gamma because they lie on a straight continuation of the Michel arm rather than being scattered around the 60 cm ring, which is the rubric's stated discriminator, and michel_kind is 'both' as a result. A scanner treating everything past 20 cm as delta / other would get 'attached' instead. No undershoot (the forward attached piece is sub-MIP, not several times MIP) and no overshoot (no pre-end collapse).
evidence: 106.8 cm of chain entering 10.3 cm from the z face and ending 21.4 cm from the x wall, inside the volume. The profile is a clean Bragg: a 5.5-6.5e4 band far out, 7.0-7.6e4 at s = 7-10, 8.7-9.4e4 at s = 3-5 and 1.00, 1.00 and 1.05e5 in the last two centimetres, following the shape of the solid muon curve; segment 45020, the 26.8 cm nearest the end, averages 6.89e4 against 5.7e4 for the segment behind it. The peak is at the fit's own last point with no collapse in front of it, so the pin stays. Attached at that point is a three-piece arm - 45024 (13 points, 7.5 cm, 4.47e4, d_min 0.0), 45022 (16 points, 8.8 cm, 4.55e4, 5.6-12.8 cm) and 45009 (6 points, 3.2 cm, 1.56e4, 12.8-15.0 cm) - leaving at cos_fwd 0.06-0.19, i.e. essentially perpendicular to the muon's local tangent, and carrying 4.5e4 e/cm, BELOW the 6.7e4 MIP line and falling to 1.6e4 as it goes out. That is the ordinary Michel case and explicitly not the undershoot: the undershoot tip would be a couple of centimetres of 0.9-1.2e5 lying straight ahead, and this is 15-19 cm of sub-MIP charge at 80 deg. e_3d_stop shows it as a distinct blue arm breaking cleanly away from the green muon band, and the chain agrees, calling it the Michel object at 39.1 MeV with a 79 deg kink. Beyond the arm, and continuing along the same line, is a string of five two-point specks at 24.2, 27.3, 32.3, 40.7 and 49.4 cm from the stop whose direction vectors all sit within about 15 deg of the arm's; each is separated from the arm and from its neighbours by clean 3-9 cm charge-free gaps, so by the attachment tie-break they are detached dots on the Michel's side rather than part of the electron - gamma. I left the outermost, 148030 at 49.4 cm, as delta / other because it carries no measured charge at all and so cannot be evidence of anything. 45028, a 3.6 cm piece at cos_fwd -0.98 sitting 79 cm back on the body line, is delta / other. f_meas shows the stop and the dot string clear of every dead band in U, V and W.

notes: High confidence. Monotone Bragg rise to 1.365e5 at the fit's last point, deeply contained end at 133.5 cm, nothing drawn past the stop, and the Bragg peak visible as bright charge in the raw f_meas planes. The one other object is a zero-charge speck on the body line 37 cm back, which cannot be a gamma, so michel_kind is none rather than detached dots. No undershoot, no overshoot.
evidence: 192.8 cm of chain entering 0.8 cm from the y face, i.e. right at the boundary, and ending 133.5 cm from the nearest face - the most deeply contained end in my chunk. The dQ/dx profile is the cleanest stopper here after 13/103: a 5.5e4 band far out, lifting to 6.5-7.5e4 over s = 5-12, then a smooth monotone climb through 8.3e4 at s = 4, 9.0e4, 9.75e4, 1.09e5, 1.19e5, 1.29e5 and finally two points at 1.36-1.365e5 at the fit's own last point, sitting right on the shape of the solid muon curve the whole way. The segment averages tell the same story - 6.09e4 over the 38 cm nearest the end against 4.28-4.90e4 for every segment behind it. The peak is at the last point with no collapse in front of it, so the pin stays, and there is no forward tip past the fit end at all, so this is neither the overshoot nor the undershoot case. Independent momentum estimates agree with the range (MCS 403.2 MeV at ambiguity 0.10 against 450.9 by range and 406.1 by dQ/dx), which is what a track whose visible length is its whole length looks like. Only one other object is drawn: 77013, five points spanning 2.2 cm at 1971 e/cm - essentially no charge - sitting 37.0-38.3 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. exactly on the muon body line, so it is body activity and delta / other. The three azimuths show a single filament ending at the star with nothing attached, nothing detached and nothing at all past the stop, so michel_kind is none. f_meas shows the end as a bright concentrated blob in U, V and W - the Bragg peak visible directly in the raw planes - and clear of the dead-channel bands.

notes: Contained end with no continuation and no face: the cluster simply ends where the imaging runs out, and the flat profile alone is what makes it THRU per the rubric. Competing reading, which is why this is medium and not high: if the 1.04e5 pair 12 cm back is taken as a real Bragg peak, this becomes an overshoot with the true stop there and the last 10 cm a bridge. I rejected it because a peak needs to be sustained into the stop and because equal-or-higher points appear 70 cm away, and with no peak there is nothing to anchor a pin to, so no --pin-rr is set. The chain's own verdict agrees (is_stm 0, shape_flat, profile_sparse), but the flat-vs-curve shape is what I judged on.
evidence: 85.8 cm chain entering 2.5 cm from the z=0 face and ending 33.8 cm from the nearest wall, so containment is not the issue -- the profile is. Over the last 20 cm the data sits on its own ~5e4 plateau and follows the solid muon curve only while that curve is still flat; from about 10 cm in, where the curve climbs steeply, the data stays at or below plateau instead of climbing with it, and the last ~3 cm drop to 0.15-0.4 of MIP in four points, which is the ordinary partial-charge fit tail, not a Bragg peak. The one apparently high cluster (a pair near 1.04e5 about 12 cm back, with 7.7-8.5e4 beside it) is not distinctive: the highest points on the whole track are 1.08-1.16e5 sitting 65-85 cm back from the fit end, so that population is delta-ray scatter, not the rise. No charge continues past the fit end in any of U, V or W in f_meas, and the track end is not in a dead band in U or V. The two compact specks the chain calls capture gammas (1.1 cm/3 pts and 2.3 cm/5 pts, 29.6-33.5 cm out, cos_fwd +0.29 and +0.44) and the two 2-point unassigned specks at 22 and 57 cm are all tagged delta / other, because gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop and this object has none.

notes: The far speck 360001 is the only judgement call here and it does not change the verdict, only michel_kind: calling it a capture gamma would make this detached dots. I did not, because the gamma rule wants a piece PAST the stop and this one is behind and beside it, near the y face the muon came in through. The chain's own ring test also found no capture gamma past the stop, and the chain accepts this object as STM (is_stm 1), which my reading agrees with.
evidence: 105 cm chain entering 0.4 cm from the y face and ending 49.6 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. The profile is the cleanest kind of Bragg in this set: it sits on a ~4.5-5e4 plateau out past 40 cm, and from about 18 cm in it lifts off the plateau and tracks the solid muon reference curve point for point -- roughly 5.5e4 at 18 cm, 6.5e4 at 12, 7.5e4 at 7, 8.5-9.5e4 in the last 3 cm and a single 1.08e5 point essentially at the fit's last point. The peak is AT the fit end, not before it, so there is no collapse and no reason to move the pin; equally there is no short high-charge tip past the end, so this is not the undershoot case either. Nothing at all sits at the stop -- the chain reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0, and f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at time slice ~2146 in all three of U, V and W with no charge beyond it and no dead band at the end. The only other drawn object is a 2-point, 0.1 cm speck 46 cm away; I resolved it delta / other rather than a capture gamma because it is not past the stop at all (it is ~28 cm back along the track direction and ~36 cm off to the side, cos_fwd -0.48) and it sits about 5 cm from the same y face the muon entered through, which reads as unrelated boundary activity belonging to a different object rather than a de-excitation gamma from this stop.

notes: The one real judgement is michel vs gamma on 146001, and it decides the verdict: tagged michel it would be STM_MICHEL / attached, which is what the chain claims (pdg 11, seed seg 146001). I went gamma on the rubric's attachment tie-break -- a clean charge-free gap makes it a detached dot however close it sits -- backed by the energy, 1.1 MeV over 1.9 cm, which is not a 35 MeV Michel. Hence medium, not high.
evidence: Short 38.6 cm chain, entering 12.4 cm from the y face and stopping 11.1 cm from it. The Bragg is unambiguous: the data lies on the solid muon curve for its whole length, ~5.8e4 at 35 cm, 6.5-7e4 at 20, 8e4 at 10, 9.6-1.06e5 at 3-5 cm and 1.14-1.19e5 in the last centimetre, with the maximum AT the fit's last point, so the pin stays where it is and this is neither the overshoot nor the undershoot case (the low 1.9-2.6e4 points near s=37 are the first points at the entry end, not the stop). The chain offers 146001 as the Michel, and I disagree: it is 4 points over 1.9 cm carrying 7500 e/cm, about 1.1 MeV total, sitting 14.3 cm from the stop and 14 cm off the muon's line, and the chain itself says it is bridged across 14.32 cm of empty space. f_meas confirms the gap is real charge-free space in all three planes, with no dead band bridging it in V or W, so nothing connects it to the stop. An electron born at the stop cannot start 14 cm away with nothing in between; a converting de-excitation gamma can, so it is a detached dot. The other two survey specks, 147002 (5 points, 44.5 cm out) and 148003 (2 points, 41.5 cm out), are also isolated, forward of the stop and 28-45 cm clear of the muon body, and 147002 lies almost exactly along the same ray out of the stop as 146001, so all three go in the ring as gammas.

notes: Flat-and-far-below-MIP to the fit end, so THRU by the operative test rather than by any exit -- the fit simply runs about 40 cm through charge at a fifth of MIP. Worth flagging separately: this object looks pathological rather than through-going, in the sense that the body carries a sixth of the charge that its own end segment carries, so the fit is bridging nearly empty space; I considered MESSY but there is a single coherent spine in all three azimuths, which is what MESSY excludes. Confidence medium because the alternative reading is that this is not one object at all, in which case the STM question does not really apply to it. The chain agrees it is not an STM (is_stm 0, shape_flat, profile_sparse).
evidence: 57.8 cm of chain in four segments, entering 0.7 cm from the z face and ending 32.9 cm from it, so containment is not what decides this. There is no Bragg rise anywhere near the fit end: the chain points form a smooth navy band that starts at 0.6-2.1e4 in the first 3 cm, sags to about 2e3 in the middle around 20-30 cm, and climbs back to 2e4 by 45-50 cm, which is a fifth of MIP for the whole 40 cm body (segment 95007 averages 8434 e/cm) and nothing like the solid muon curve, which is at 1.6e5 where these points sit at 1e4. The only MIP-level charge in the whole object is at the far, entry end -- segment 95008 at 51759 e/cm over 7.7 cm and the off-chain 24-point 14 cm piece 95009 at 56430 that the chain types pdg 11 shower -- and the three pieces at the stop end (95005 at 1.2e4, 95012 at 1.6e4 and the 6.6 cm pdg-11 piece 95011 at 5.3e3) are all far below MIP, so nothing there reads as either a muon Bragg or a Michel electron. The 3-D azimuths show the shape plainly: a long thin faint filament running from a small clump at the fit end down to a track-plus-shower at the other end, which is also why the chain's own energy estimates disagree by a factor of five (range 161 MeV, dQ/dx 46, MCS 34). f_meas shows very little measured charge over most of that filament.

notes: Straightforward. The only object past the stop is a 2-point speck 24.7 cm out; it is well clear of the muon body (14 cm off-axis) and forward, which is the gamma rule rather than the delta rule, so michel_kind is detached dots and not none.
evidence: Long 267 cm chain in two segments, entering 0.5 cm from the x face and stopping 58.3 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained, and the chain's three independent energies agree to a percent (range 616.6, dQ/dx 603.6, MCS 610.7 MeV), which is what a well-measured muon looks like. The profile sits on a ~5e4 plateau with the usual scatter for 200 cm and then lifts cleanly onto the solid muon curve over the last 10 cm: about 6.5-7.4e4 at 5-8 cm, 8.3-8.8e4 at 2-4 cm, 9.2e4 at 3 cm and 1.20e5 and 1.33e5 in the final centimetre, with the maximum at the fit's own last point. So the pin stays put -- there is no peak-then-collapse and no high-charge tip beyond the end, so neither failure mode applies here. Nothing is attached at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0) and f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at time slice ~2333 in U, V and W with no charge continuing and no dead band at the end. The single other object, 192006, is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck carrying 33148 e/cm about 1.3 MeV, sitting 24.7 cm from the stop, forward of it (cos_fwd 0.91, 20 cm along the muon direction) and 14 cm off the body line, isolated across a clean charge-free gap in all three planes -- a detached dot, i.e. a capture gamma candidate, not an electron attached to the stop, so this stays STM_ONLY with detached dots rather than becoming STM_MICHEL.

notes: Corrected after cross-checking my own tagging across the chunk: I first read 270008 with the scattered-ring paragraph and called it delta, but that paragraph is scoped to specks with cos_fwd near 0 and exists to settle attached-versus-both on items that already have a Michel, and neither applies here -- 270008 is at cos_fwd 0.93 and this item has no Michel. On the plain gamma rule it is the same configuration I tagged gamma on 039253_16/51, 039253_16/98 and 039253_17/44, and it is more clearly past the stop than any of them, so leaving it delta was inconsistent. Medium rather than high because the five sideways specks are a genuine judgement call and because the chain's own ring test found no capture gamma; the STM part itself is not in doubt.
evidence: 202.5 cm chain in two segments, entering 0.6 cm from the z face and stopping 43.6 cm from the nearest face. The profile runs on a ~4.8e4 plateau for 190 cm and then rises hard over the last 10 cm, following the solid muon curve: about 5.5e4 at 10 cm, 6e4 at 8, then 1.19e5 at 6 cm, 1.05e5 at 2.5, 9.6-9.9e4 at 2 and 1.03e5 essentially at the last point, so it tops out at 1.19e5 which is in the band real stoppers here reach. Two points at the very end sit low (6.0e4 and 3.55e4) but that is one centimetre of ordinary end scatter, not a sustained collapse over several cm, so the pin stays at the fit's last point. Nothing is attached at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0) and no short high-charge tip lies beyond it, so neither fit-failure mode applies. The seven other objects are all 2-point specks and they split two ways. 270008 sits 50.7 cm from the stop, 47.8 cm of that straight ahead along the muon's own direction (cos_fwd 0.93) and 17.1 cm off the body line, isolated and compact, and the wide 3-D frame shows it clear of the track past the star with nothing bridging it: that is the plain gamma rule -- isolated, past the stop, clear of the body, inside 60 cm -- so it is a detached dot and it alone sets the kind. Everything else is not. 109007 sits exactly on the muon body 70 cm back (cos_fwd -1.0, 1.3 cm off the line), so it is body activity whatever the chain's pdg 11 says, and 271009, 272010, 273011, 274012 and 275013 lie 25-52 cm out with cos_fwd between -0.4 and +0.11, i.e. essentially sideways, in mutually unrelated directions -- 271009 and 275013 point almost exactly opposite each other along plus and minus y -- which is the rubric's scattered-ring case, so those five are delta / other.

notes: Contained end, no continuation and no face, and I am still calling it THRU because the profile is flat on the MIP plateau all the way to the last point and a stopping muon cannot do that. The chain agrees (is_stm 0 with rejects no_bragg and shape_flat). Single object row, so no attribution question.
evidence: 307 cm single chain segment, entering 6.6 cm from the z face and ending 148.2 cm from the nearest face, i.e. right in the middle of the volume, and yet the profile says through-goer. The data sits on its own ~5.5e4 plateau for the whole 300 cm and is still on it, or a little below it, at the last point: roughly 6.0e4, 5.2e4, 4.9e4, 4.4e4 and 3.1e4 over the final two centimetres against a solid muon curve that is at 1.0e5 by 3 cm and 1.6e5 at zero. There is no climb of any kind towards the end. The scattered high points near the end (8.0e4 at 3 cm, 8.7e4 at 5, 9.55e4 at 6) are the same delta-ray population that produces 1.15-1.48e5 points 44-46 cm back and 1.03-1.30e5 points 71-92 cm back, so they are not a rise. f_meas shows the track ending flat at time slice ~272 in U, V and W with no charge beyond it and no dead band at that channel in any plane, and no other object is drawn at all, so there is nothing that could be a Michel or a gamma. This is the case the rubric names explicitly: the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out, and a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own. Note the orange entry circle sits mid-track here rather than at the far end, so it is not a guide to either end.

notes: Worth flagging as a reconstruction observation rather than a scan problem: the chain claims 600.6 cm of path over a 254 cm chord and one of its segments, 44005, is 166.8 cm carried by only 4 points and sits 40 cm off the chord, so the chain is almost certainly bridging to something else at the far end. The MCS energy (570 MeV) disagrees with the range energy (1354 MeV) by a factor of 2.4, consistent with that. None of it touches the stop end, which is where the verdict comes from, so I did not downgrade the confidence for it. The speck 226008 sits slightly behind the stop, which is the only reason a delta reading is available at all; 25 cm off the body line rules it out.
evidence: A very long chain, 600 cm of path in three segments over a 254 cm chord, entering 7.2 cm from the z face and stopping 94.9 cm from the nearest face, deep in the volume. The stop end is as clean a Bragg as this set produces: the data lies on the solid muon curve continuously from about 15 cm in -- 6.7e4 at 12 cm, 8.0-8.7e4 at 5-8, 9.8e4 at 3, 1.05e5 at 2.5, 1.17e5 at 1.5 and 1.31e5 at the last point -- with the maximum at the fit's own last point, so the pin stays and neither the peak-then-collapse nor the high-charge-tip failure mode is present. f_meas shows the track ending at time slice ~773 in all three planes with no charge continuing and no dead channel there. The only non-chain object, 226008, is a 2-point 0.5 cm speck at 70655 e/cm sitting 25.8 cm from the stop, 24.9 cm off the muon's body line and only 7 cm behind it along the track direction, isolated across a clean gap in U, V and W. It is far too far off-axis to be body activity, well outside the 10 cm radius where direction stops discriminating, and detached and compact rather than attached, so it is a detached dot and the kind is detached dots rather than none. Nothing is attached at the stop itself (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0), so this does not become STM_MICHEL.

notes: OVERSHOOT of the other kind -- the fit runs about 10 cm past the muon's stop, so --pin-rr 10.1, taken at the 77001/77005 junction, which is also where the visible kink and the colour change are. Medium and not high for two honest reasons. First, the elevated 8-9.2e4 stretch is only about 1.7x the 5.4e4 plateau and comparable single points (1.05e5 at 48 cm, 9.0e4 at 80, 8.5e4 at 84) occur far back on the same track, so the peak is not unambiguous; and between the bump and the junction the charge sits back at plateau rather than climbing, which is not the monotone approach a clean Bragg makes. Second, everything past the junction is very low: 0.54 MIP on the arm and 0.08 MIP on the 8.8 cm piece, whereas a 35 MeV Michel should be around MIP. The competing reading is THRU with the arm being some other object, and I rejected it because the profile is not flat on the plateau to the last point -- it halves and then collapses -- and because the rubric's own clause that a Michel topology suffices even with an unclear Bragg fits what the three azimuths show. The chain disagrees with me: is_stm 0 with rejects shape_flat and profile_sparse.
evidence: 83.9 cm of chain in two segments, entering right on the y face (d_face 0.0) and with the fit's last point 26.9 cm inside that face. The fit overshoots the muon's real stop. The muon segment 77001 carries 57320 e/cm and shows an elevated stretch of about eight points at 8.0-9.2e4 between 15 and 22 cm from the fit end; from there in, the profile never recovers -- 4.2-6.0e4 over 10-15 cm, a shallow 3.6-4.4e4 staircase over 6-13 cm and then 0.5-2.5e4, a tenth to under a half of MIP, over the last 6 cm. The chain's own segmentation matches: the last 10.1 cm is a separate segment, 77005, averaging 30723 e/cm, which is 0.54 of the body's charge, and a muon cannot fall below MIP as it approaches its own Bragg peak, so that segment is not muon. The three 3-D azimuths show it plainly: the high-charge body ends at a visible kink and a distinctly lower-charge arm leaves it at roughly 40-50 degrees and runs to the fit's last point, where a compact 14-point 8.8 cm piece (77007, typed pdg 11 shower) and a 4-point 1.9 cm piece (77008, pdg 11) sit attached, which is why the chain counts n_stop_arms 2. f_meas shows all of that extra charge packed within about twenty channels and fifteen time slices of the muon's end in U, V and W, with nothing continuing beyond, so it is a compact clump at the end of the track and not a through-going continuation. I therefore put the pin at the segment junction, 10.1 cm back, and call the arm plus its two attached pieces the Michel.

notes: MESSY rather than THRU. THRU was the alternative -- there is certainly no Bragg -- but THRU asks the profile to be flat on the MIP plateau to the last point, and this object has no MIP plateau anywhere (the chain's own plateau_off_mip reject says so) and is not one track: the chain doubles back inside a 40 cm clump, is cut into eleven segments whose charges vary by a factor of eight, and carries six separately typed shower pieces.
