Medium rather than high because MESSY is a rare call and the clump does have a rough overall long axis, so someone could read it as one very badly reconstructed track.
evidence: Twenty drawn objects: eleven chain segments and nine unassigned pieces, six of which the chain itself types pdg 11 shower, all packed into a clump that the full-extent projections show spanning only about 40 cm in z and 40 cm in y, even though the chain claims 122.1 cm of path over an 84.5 cm chord. The dQ/dx panel has no plateau to read: instead of a MIP band the chain points form a scalloped near-zero ribbon that repeatedly dips to a few thousand e/cm and climbs back, at s about 3, 18, 40, 73 and 92 cm, with a second scattered population at 2e4 to 1.3e5 sitting above it, which is why the chain's own rejects are no_bragg, shape_flat and plateau_off_mip together. The per-segment charges bear that out, running from 11718 to 98673 e/cm between adjacent segments of the supposed same muon, and the range and MCS energies disagree by a factor of 2.4 (298 vs 125 MeV). The three azimuths show the same thing geometrically: differently coloured segments overlapping and crossing at angles, branches leaving in several directions, and about twenty vertex squares strung through the clump, with a fan of loose points beside it, and f_meas shows a dense smear about thirty channels wide rather than a track. There is no coherent spine to hang a stop on, so by the rubric's convention every row is tagged delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Clean and, unusually for this chunk, one where I agree with the chain's Michel: it is attached at the shared stop vertex rather than bridged across empty space, it has three collinear pieces and 23 MeV, and the Bragg peak is at the fit end. The chain nevertheless rejects the object as an STM on shape_flat, which looks wrong from the picture -- the rise onto the muon curve over the last 20 cm is visible.
evidence: 85.8 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x face and stopping 19.2 cm inside it. The profile follows the solid muon curve from about 20 cm in: ~5.5e4 plateau out past 40 cm, 6.5-7e4 at 12-18, 8.0-9.0e4 at 3-8 and 1.05e5 and 1.20e5 in the last centimetre and a half, with the maximum at the fit's own last point, so the pin stays put. An arm of three pieces leaves that same point at a large angle -- the chain measures the kink at 102 degrees and puts 23.1 MeV in it -- made of 115007 (5 points, 2.3 cm, 42770 e/cm) touching the stop, then 115008 (9 points, 4.8 cm, 18740) and 115011 (17 points, 9.5 cm, 19662) continuing out to about 16 cm, with all three lying within 3 degrees of the same direction. The three azimuths show it directly: the amber muon body ends at the star and a separate teal-green arm runs off it sideways, and f_meas shows that arm as charge attached to the muon's last point in all three planes. That is a Michel: a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot carry on at three quarters of MIP and then fall to a third of it, and the arm's charge falls as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel case and not the undershoot trap -- the tip is well below MIP, not the four-to-six times MIP that would make it the muon's own last centimetres. The three far 2-point specks go the other way: 540012 at 22.7 cm and 541013 at 35.4 cm both lie back along the muon body (cos_fwd -0.75 and -0.87, and their directions from the stop are within 30 degrees of the body direction), so they are body activity, and 542014 sits 50 cm out entirely sideways in a direction opposite the Michel arm, which is an unrelated direction round the ring, so all three are delta / other and the kind stays attached rather than both.

notes: As clean an STM_ONLY as the chunk contains; the chain agrees (is_stm 1). The only object anywhere near the stop, 590032, is 50 cm back along the body, so it fails the gamma rule's past-the-stop clause and does not lift the kind to detached dots.
evidence: A detector-crossing muon: 835.6 cm of chain in nine segments over a 778 cm chord, entering 0.2 cm from the z face and stopping 18.5 cm inside the x face, with the range, dQ/dx and MCS energies agreeing to within a few percent (1847, 2019, 1782 MeV), which is what a cleanly measured muon looks like. The stop is unambiguous. The profile sits on a 5.4e4 plateau for hundreds of centimetres and then climbs onto the solid muon curve and stays on it point for point over the last 12 cm -- 6.8e4 at 12, 8.0e4 at 7-9, 8.9-9.4e4 at 5-6, 9.5-1.05e5 at 2-4, 1.11e5 at 3.5 and a final 1.53e5 at the fit's own last point, which is the highest charge anywhere on 1327 points. The maximum being at the last point rules out both fit-failure modes: there is no peak-then-collapse, and no short high-charge tip sits beyond the end. f_meas confirms it, with the track ending at time slice ~115 in U, V and W and no charge below that and no dead band at the end channel in any plane, and the chain reports nothing at the stop at all (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). Every other drawn object is body activity far up the muon: six unassigned pieces, some typed pdg 11 shower, sitting 300 to 660 cm back along the track, plus one 2-point speck 590032 which is 56 cm from the stop but 50 cm of that is straight back along the muon direction (cos_fwd -0.83), so it is behind the stop on the body side rather than past it. All of those are delta / other, and with nothing past the stop the kind is none.

notes: OVERSHOOT: profile peaks 1.38e5 at s=4.4 then collapses over the last 3.4 cm to 0.7-4e4; pin moved to 3.4. Departure from the rubric's mechanism: nothing sits past the collapse for the fit to bridge to (no row with d_min ~0 beyond it), so this is fit overrun into empty space rather than a muon-Michel gap crossing - medium confidence on the pin for that reason. No undershoot candidate: every row is at cos_fwd -0.93 or below. Chain says is_stm 0 / no daughter / n_stop_arms 0; I disagree on both counts.
evidence: A 253 cm chain that enters 0.1 cm from the y face and stops deep, 76.5 cm from the nearest (z) face, 8 cm inside the x seam - containment is not in doubt. The dQ/dx panel (gridlines calibrated at 61 px = 20 cm, so 3.05 px/cm) sits on a 5.5e4 MIP plateau from s=100 back to s=10, scattering 4-8e4 about the flat solid muon curve. Over the last centimetres it climbs to 8.0e4 at s=6.2, 1.05e5 at s=5.6 and 3.9, 1.21e5 at s=5.2 and 1.38e5 at s=4.4 - a factor 2.5 above its own plateau, following the muon curve's shape and topping out exactly in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach. That is a Bragg rise, so the chain's own no_bragg / shape_flat rejection is measuring the wrong thing: inside s=3.4 the profile collapses to 3.2e4, 4.0e4, 3.0e4, 1.2e4 and 0.7e4 at the fit's last point, and the chain reads the collapse rather than the peak. The collapse is sustained over 3.4 cm and five points, not one low end point, so I moved the pin to s=3.4. It differs from the rubric's stated mechanism in one respect worth recording: no row has d_min near 0 past the collapse, so the overrun bridges to nothing rather than across a gap to the Michel. Similar low clumps do appear mid-track at s=8 and s=22-26, but the s=22-26 clump sits exactly on the 13003/13001 junction at d=22.06 while the terminal collapse is not at any junction. Past that stop, object 13005 - 13 points, 7.0 cm, 3.5e4 e/cm, chain-typed pdg 11 shower and left unassigned - attaches at the 13004/13003 vertex 6.09 cm from the fit end, i.e. about 2.7 cm behind the corrected stop, and in the d and e azimuths it leaves the chain as a distinct branch at a large angle and runs several cm clear of the muon body line to its own vertex, so off-axis separation and attachment (which the rubric puts above cos_fwd and above the chain's exclusion) make it michel, not delta. cos_fwd -0.93 is honest here (I checked it against the d azimuth) but a 7 cm, 15 MeV-scale electron emitted at 155 deg from a muon with only a few MeV of range left cannot be a knock-on delta - the delta reading is kinematically excluded. Row 13004 is split by the pin move: s=3.4-6.09 is the muon's Bragg peak and s=0-3.4 is the low-charge overrun, and I tagged the whole row muon because that is what carries the peak and its 5.6e4 mean is MIP. f_meas shows dead U channels at global rank ~665 and ~703 and the stop end sits near the 703 band, which may be why the last centimetres read low in one plane; V and W are clear there.

notes: No undershoot candidate: the only non-chain row is at cos_fwd -1.0 and 78 cm out. No overshoot: the profile is flat to the last point, no peak-then-collapse, pin left alone. Caveat recorded for the audit: this track is nearly parallel to U and nearly isochronous, so its dQ/dx is intrinsically poorly measured (whole-track mean 2.3e4, about 0.4 MIP); the THRU call rests on the flat shape plus the 0.4 cm wall contact rather than on the absolute charge.
evidence: A 93.7 cm chain whose fit end sits 0.4 cm from the +y wall (in_fv 0), with the far end 21.8 cm from the z face - so the fit end is an exit, not a stop. The dQ/dx panel (tick labels -40/-20/0/20/40 confirm 20 cm gridlines, 3.05 px/cm) never approaches the muon curve anywhere: it starts at 3.0e4 at the fit's last point, sits at 2.5-3.2e4 over the first 5 cm behind it, and then oscillates between 0.5e4 and 4.8e4 with a ~25-30 cm period all the way back to s=94, always well under the 5.4e4 solid muon asymptote and the 6.7e4 dashed MIP line. There is no rise off any plateau over the last 10-20 cm - the last five centimetres are flat and if anything slightly below the local mean - so by the operative test this is a through-goer, and the wall contact agrees. f_meas explains the low, oscillating charge rather than undermining the call: in U the whole 94 cm track collapses into a single blob at channel ~3750 over ten time slices, i.e. the track runs essentially along the U wire direction and is nearly isochronous (V and W show it spanning ~100 channels at a near-constant time slice 2240-2250), which is exactly the geometry that makes dQ/dx unreliable and low. Both readings - unreliable-but-flat charge and a 0.4 cm wall contact - point the same way. The only other drawn object, 75001 (11 points, 6.0 cm, 3.5e4 e/cm, chain-typed pdg 211), sits 78-84 cm away at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. at the opposite, entry end of the track and squarely on the body line; on a THRU there is no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so it is delta / other. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any of the three azimuths, which show only the amber flow band terminating cleanly at the star.

notes: No undershoot (no row at cos_fwd >= 0.85 with a couple-of-cm dstop and ~1e5 charge; 77005 is 13.4 cm at 3.5e4). No pin move: the s=12-18 bump reaches only 9.1e4, short of the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper tops out at, and what follows it is a decline to 0.8-1.0 of the plateau over 14 cm, not the sustained collapse into 0.15-0.5 of MIP that the pin rule asks for. Competing reading, stated plainly: on the operative THRU test (no Bragg rise at the fit end) this is a through-goer, and only the STM_MICHEL rule's explicit 'a Michel topology is sufficient on its own' clause keeps it out of that bin. Dead U and V channels across the stop region give a mechanism for a suppressed Bragg, but I did not verify it - it is a plausibility, not a measurement.
evidence: A 324.8 cm chain entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 95.6 cm from the nearest (x) face, in_fv 1 - the end is deep, containment is not the issue. This one is decided by the arm rather than by the Bragg, and I want that on the record. The dQ/dx profile (labels -40/-20/0/20/40, 20 cm gridlines) rides the 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=20 on the solid muon curve, bumps to 7.5-9.1e4 over s=12-18, and then DECLINES: 3.6-4.6e4 at s=8-11 and 4.4-5.5e4 over the last 7 cm, so the final 15 cm sit at or below the track's own plateau where the muon reference asks for 8e4 rising to 1.6e5. There is no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the C/B azimuths agree - the turbo colour runs yellow-green far from the star and cools toward it. The chain's no_bragg / shape_flat rejection is measuring the profile correctly. What overrides it is the topology: object 77005, 23 points and 13.4 cm at cos_fwd +0.79 with a 33 deg kink, leaves the very stop vertex (d_min 0.0) and in the dQ/dx panel its large markers run from 6.4-6.7e4 at s=0 down through 3.1-4.4e4 at 1-6 cm to 0.6-1.7e4 at 10-12 cm out - at or just under MIP at the vertex and falling as it goes out, which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel case rather than the undershoot (the undershoot wants 0.9-1.2e5 over a couple of cm; this is 3.5e4 over 13.4 cm, so it is emphatically not that). A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, and this arm neither continues at MIP nor Braggs at its own end - it fades out over 13 cm, which is right for a ~20 MeV electron; the chain itself types it the Michel object at 19.8 MeV. Contained end plus an attached electron arm is sufficient on its own by the verdict rule, so STM_MICHEL, but at medium confidence because the muon's own profile actively argues the other way. f_meas is part of why I do not treat the flat profile as decisive: the stop sits at U channels 2520-2560 and V 6390-6460, both of which carry several dead-channel lines in that exact span (U ~2485-2540, V ~6385-6435), while only W is clean there. The eight unassigned pdg 11 shower pieces (77019, 77025, 77029, 77035, 77037, 77040, 77041, 77043) all sit 84-157 cm back at cos_fwd -0.78 to -0.97 and at 1.5e3-2.2e4 e/cm, i.e. on the muon body line far beyond the 60 cm gamma ring - body activity, so delta / other.

notes: No undershoot: the only non-chain row is at cos_fwd -1.0, 206 cm out, 2.4e4 - nothing forward and nothing near 1e5. No overshoot: no peak-then-collapse; the single 2.05e4 point at s=0 is one point, not a sustained several-cm fall, and the four points immediately behind it are 1.19-1.40e5.
evidence: A 391 cm chain that enters 0.4 cm from the z face and ends 105.7 cm from the nearest face, about as deep as anything in this set; in_fv 1 and the chain itself accepts it (is_stm 1, reject list just STM). The dQ/dx panel (ticks -40/-20/0/20/40, 20 cm gridlines) gives a textbook Bragg: 5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=20 scattering on the flat solid muon curve, then a clean monotone climb - 7-8.5e4 at s=10-18, 9.0-10.5e4 at s=5-7, 1.19-1.27e5 at s=2-4, 1.40e5 at s=1 - and the rising points lie right on the muon reference curve the whole way up, topping out at 1.40e5, at the upper edge of the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach. The d and e azimuths show the same thing independently: the turbo colour runs green over the body, warms to yellow then orange and red over the last few centimetres and the track terminates at the star. There is exactly one low point, 2.05e4, sitting on the origin itself - a single partial-charge point at the very end, which the rubric explicitly calls ordinary scatter, not a collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. Nothing at all is drawn past the stop: no arm, no dot, no speck in any of the three azimuths, and the chain agrees with n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. The only non-chain object, 102011 (7 points, 3.4 cm, 2.4e4 e/cm, pdg 11), sits 206-209 cm back up the track at cos_fwd -1.0, squarely on the muon body line and far outside any gamma ring, so it is delta / other and does not touch the kind, which is none. f_meas is clean at the stop in all three planes - the dead channel lines in U, V and W all lie clear of the track's channel span there, and measured minus predicted is flat white along it, so nothing about this profile is a readout artefact.

notes: OVERSHOOT: peak 1.17e5 at s=4.3 then a monotone seven-point fall to 4.0e4 at the fit end; pin moved to 3.5. Competing explanation I could not rule out and am recording rather than resolving: f_meas shows the stop end sitting at U channels ~1005-1020, which is inside a group of dead U bands at ~1000-1030, so one of three planes is dead exactly where the charge falls. V (track at 4820-4870, dead band at 4760-4790) and W are clear there. If the U loss is the cause, the fit end is the true stop and the pin should stay - hence medium confidence on the pin, though not on the verdict, which does not depend on it. No undershoot: the forward tip 29010 is 1.25 x MIP, not the several-times-MIP the undershoot requires. Physics oddity worth flagging to the owner: the chain asserts both a stop arm and a 18.81 MeV capture gamma, but mu- capture and mu decay are competing processes - one of the two labels must be wrong. I tagged geometrically as the rubric directs and did not try to resolve it.
evidence: A 118.7 cm chain entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 20.4 cm from the x (anode) face, in_fv 1 - contained, though not deeply. On a 4x crop of the last 12 cm the profile is unambiguous: 5.5e4 plateau back at s=20-100, then 7.0e4 at s=9, 7.5e4 at s=7, 7.8e4 at s=6.3, 8.9e4 at s=5.7, 1.02e5 at s=4.9 and a peak of 1.17e5 at s=4.3, tracking the muon reference curve's shape the whole way up. Then it falls, monotonically and over seven points: 1.11e5 (s=3.9), 7.7e4 (3.2), 5.9e4 (2.7), 5.0e4 (1.9), 4.2e4 (1.3), 4.1e4 (0.35), 4.0e4 (0.0). That is the peak-several-cm-before-the-fit-end-then-collapse signature, so I put the pin at s=3.5, the junction between the last real muon point and the fall. Row 29011 is split by that and I tagged it muon, which is what 103 of its 107 cm are. The collapse bottoms at 0.73 of the track's own plateau rather than in the 0.15-0.5 band, which is why this is medium and not high. Past the stop the chain of objects runs straight on: 29010, 5 points and 2.4 cm at 6.8e4 e/cm with cos_fwd +0.91, touching the fit end (d_min 0.0), then 29001, 14 points and 7.5 cm at 5.3e4 with cos_fwd +0.70, out to 8.6 cm. I checked this against the undershoot case and it is not one: the undershoot wants a couple of centimetres at 0.9-1.2e5, four to six times MIP, and 6.8e4 is 1.25 x MIP - the charge is the load-bearing clause and it fails, so the tip is not the muon's own last centimetres. What it is instead is the ordinary Michel: about 10 cm of forward charge at and just below MIP whose dQ/dx falls as it goes out, which is what a ~20 MeV electron looks like. In the d azimuth it is visible as a faint low-charge arc curving away from the stop vertex to its own vertex square. The chain's pdg 2212 type on 29010 is not something I can support - a 2.4 cm proton would be far brighter than 1.25 x MIP. Further out, 125008 (12 points, 6.8 cm, 3.8e4) and 125009 (14 points, 7.9 cm, 5.4e3) sit 17.2-22.4 cm from the stop at cos_fwd +0.69 and +0.73, drawn as a compact green two-piece V that is clearly detached from the arm across an 8.6-to-17.2 cm charge-free gap in all three azimuths, and clear of the muon body line. Detached, compact, past the stop, inside 60 cm and on the Michel's own side - gamma by the rubric, which makes the kind both. Neither of these is on the dQ/dx panel's negative axis as anything but the green hexagon cluster at s=-17 to -23, and 29010 and 29001 are not drawn on that panel at all, which is trap 6 in action - the object table is the census.

notes: OVERSHOOT: profile peaks 8.8e4 at s=3.5 and collapses to 0.5e4 at the fit end; the collapse coincides with its own 2.4 cm chain segment 61008 at 0.23 MIP, so the pin moves to 2.1 and 61008 is tagged michel. No undershoot: the forward pieces are 2.9-3.0e4, half of MIP, nowhere near the several-times-MIP the undershoot requires, and cos_fwd +0.59 is below its 0.85 bar. Medium confidence: the Bragg peak reaches only 8.8e4, well short of the 1.2-1.35e5 band, so a reader who insists on an absolute height would call this shape_flat and land on THRU; I went the other way on the shape of the climb plus the arm. The kind is robust to the 61008 call either way, since 61007 carries the michel tag independently.
evidence: A 197.6 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the z face and ending 93.9 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained. The profile does rise, gently and over a long stretch, and it follows the muon curve's shape: 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=40, 5.5-6.5e4 at s=20-40, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=10-20, 7.6-8.8e4 at s=3-10, peaking 8.8e4 at s=3.5. It falls short of the curve in absolute terms (the curve wants 9.5e4 at s=5 and 1.05e5 at s=3.5) and never reaches the 1.2-1.35e5 that the cleanest stoppers in this set reach, which is the main reason this is medium rather than high; but the climb off its own plateau is real and shaped right, so I do not read this as the flat MIP profile the chain's shape_flat flag claims. Inside s=2 it collapses: 4.85e4 at s=2, 2.15e4 at s=1, 0.5e4 at s=0.3. That is not just plot reading - the collapse has its own row. Segment 61008, chain-typed the muon chain, is 5 points over 2.4 cm at a mean of 1.29e4, i.e. 0.23 of the track's MIP, and it occupies exactly d=0 to 2.09 while 61004, the long body carrying the peak, starts at d=2.09. Peak a few centimetres before the fit end, then a sustained fall into a fifth of MIP, in a segment the fit bridges - that is the overshoot signature with a row to hang it on, so the pin goes to the 61004/61008 junction at 2.1 and 61008 is tagged michel per the rule that the segment past the peak is the Michel whatever the chain calls it. Past the fit end the decay charge continues forward: 61007, a fitted stop arm of 14 points over 7.8 cm at 2.9e4 (0.55 MIP) at cos_fwd +0.59 spanning d 0-7.45, then 61001, 13 points over 7.1 cm at 3.0e4 at cos_fwd +0.65 spanning d 7.29-9.75 - about 10 cm of forward, sub-MIP charge, which all three azimuths show as a faint arm leaving the star and running to its own vertex square. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, and this is below MIP and 10 cm long, so it is a second particle of about the right range for a 20 MeV electron. Well beyond it, 140006 (5 points, 2.4 cm, 9.6e3) at 24.6-26.1 cm and 139005 (3 points, 1.0 cm, 1.4e4) at 33.7-34.4 cm sit at cos_fwd +0.49 and +0.54, and in every azimuth they are two tiny green specks between paired vertex squares, lying up the same side as the arm rather than scattered around the ring, across a clear charge-free gap. Faint, isolated, past the stop, inside 60 cm and on the Michel's side - gamma, which makes the kind both. f_meas is clean here: the stop sits at U 2220 / V 6000 / W 10430 with the nearest dead bands 45 channels away in U and 35 in V, and measured minus predicted is flat white along the whole track, so nothing about the terminal collapse is a dead-channel artefact.

notes: No undershoot: no row anywhere near cos_fwd +0.85, and the highest non-chain charge past the stop is 4.6e4. No overshoot: the profile's two highest points are its last two, there is no peak-then-collapse, pin untouched. The only soft call is 179013 - gamma vs delta / other at 60 cm - and it does not move the kind either way, since 180014 already carries the gamma tag. Slight oddity recorded but not resolved: the arm's charge runs 0.17 then 0.76 then 0.43 of MIP going outward rather than falling monotonically; the first piece 79009 is 5.9 cm long but spans only 3.4 cm of distance from the stop, so it curls, and diffuse curling charge is the likeliest reason its dQ/dx reads low.
evidence: A 94.3 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 46.0 cm from the nearest face, in_fv 1, and the chain already accepts it (is_stm 1). The Bragg is textbook and needs no argument: 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=50 to s=100, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=15-20, 7.5-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.4-9.8e4 at s=3-7, 1.07-1.11e5 at s=2 and 1.23-1.25e5 at the last two points, sitting on the solid muon curve the whole way up and topping out squarely in the 1.2-1.35e5 band. There is no terminal dip at all - the two highest points in the whole profile are the last two - so the pin stays put and neither failure mode is in play here. Past the stop a three-piece arm leaves at roughly a right angle to the muon: 79009 (11 points, 5.9 cm, 9.1e3 e/cm, d 0.0-3.41, cos_fwd -0.35) attached at the fit end, then 79011 (10 points, 5.5 cm, 4.1e4, d 2.41-7.28, cos_fwd -0.04) and 79012 (8 points, 4.0 cm, 2.3e4, d 7.28-10.62, cos_fwd -0.02), about 10.6 cm of charge at 0.17-0.76 of MIP. All three azimuths show it as a green-then-yellow chain of segments running away from the star through its own vertex squares, at a large angle to the muon and nowhere near hugging its body - cos_fwd near zero is perpendicular, not the -0.85-and-below that the delta rule wants - and it is inside 10 cm where the rubric says direction does not discriminate anyway. Attached, well clear of the body, sub-MIP: michel. A muon that has just put 1.25e5 into its last centimetre cannot carry on at a fifth to three quarters of MIP for another 10 cm. Then 180014, a 2-point 0.6 cm speck at 4.6e4 sitting 18.7-19.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.26, which in the c and d azimuths lies beyond the far end of the arm and roughly along its direction, across a clear charge-free gap - isolated, compact, past the stop, inside 60 cm, clear of the body and on the Michel's own side, so gamma, and that gives kind both. I am overriding the chain's gamma body exclusion label on it, which the rubric explicitly permits when off-axis separation says otherwise. The last object, 179013, is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 60.1 cm out at cos_fwd +0.19, flagged survey only and never offered to either stage; it is at the very edge of the 60 cm ring, its polar angle differs from the arm's by about 0.45 in cos_fwd, and in the c azimuth it sits on the opposite side of the stop from the arm, so I read it as an unrelated speck on the ring rather than part of this decay: delta / other. f_meas is clean - the stop is at U 3600, V 7370, W 12200 with the dead lines 30-40 channels off in U and V, and measured minus predicted is flat along the track.

notes: No undershoot: no row is anywhere near cos_fwd +0.85 - the arm is at -0.73 and the speck at -0.55. No overshoot: the muon's chain points climb monotonically to their own last point (6.8e4, 1.078e5, 1.184e5, 1.258e5 at s=2.6, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0) with no peak-then-collapse, so the pin stays at the fit's last point. Marker-size note for the audit: the 1.226e5 point at s=0.3 is an 8x8 object marker (79003's first point), not a chain point - I checked this on the raw PNG after first reading it as part of the muon's profile at 3x. Medium confidence for two reasons, both about 79003 rather than the verdict skeleton: its opening centimetres read 1.1-1.2e5, twice MIP, which is not what an electron's start looks like and leaves a live alternative that it is a second stopping track whose own end is at this vertex (that reading would make the item STM_ONLY / detached dots); and the 139 deg kink puts it in the michel-versus-delta collision, which I broke on the ~10 cm off-axis separation measured from the stop zooms rather than on cos_fwd. Dead U and V channels overlap the stop region, so charges near the vertex should be treated with some caution in either direction.
evidence: A short one: 37.3 cm of chain, 115.8 MeV by range, entering 0.8 cm from the z face and ending 17.0 cm from the x (anode) face, in_fv 1 - inside, but not deeply. The muon Braggs. Its far end starts low at 1.0-2.4e4 over s=33-38 (the 79002 stub), climbs through 5.0-6.5e4 at s=20-32 and 6.5-8.2e4 at s=8-20, dips slightly to 6.8-7.0e4 at s=3-6, and then runs 6.8e4 at s=2.6, 1.078e5 at s=2.0, 1.184e5 at s=1.5 and 1.258e5 at its last point at s=1.0 - right on the muon reference curve and inside the 1.2-1.35e5 band. I separated chain points from object points by measuring marker sizes on the raw PNG rather than by eye, because they overlap here: chain markers are 4-7 px across and object markers 8-16, and the 1.226e5 point at s=0.3 that sits between the muon's last point and the origin is an 8x8 marker, i.e. the first point of the arm, not part of the muon's profile. So the muon's own climb is monotone to its own last point and there is no terminal collapse - the pin stays where the fit put it. The whole object is a hairpin: all three azimuths show the amber muon rising to the star and a teal arm coming back down beside it to its own vertex square. That arm is 79003, 26 points over 14.8 cm at a mean 5.2e4, attached at the shared stop vertex (d_min 0.0) with a 139 deg kink and cos_fwd -0.73 - squarely in the michel-versus-delta collision the rubric describes, close to the stop and backward. I resolved it on off-axis separation as instructed: measuring on the 5x stop zooms, its far end sits about 9.5-10 cm off the muon's body line in both the c and d azimuths (and on the far side in e), which is nothing like hugging the body, and cos_fwd -0.73 is well short of the -0.85 the delta rule wants. It is attached and well clear, so michel. The second-particle argument agrees: a muon that has just deposited 1.26e5 in its last centimetre has no range left to run another 14.8 cm at MIP, and the arm's own charge falls as it goes out - 1.226e5 at the shared vertex, about 1.1e5 through its first 6 cm, 8.6-9.0e4 at 9-10 cm, 5-6.5e4 at 11-12 and 2.4-4.6e4 at 12-13.6. That opening value is the thing I am least comfortable with and it is why this is medium: a Michel's first centimetres should be at or below MIP, not twice it, and the honest alternative reading is charge sharing with the muon's own dense Bragg blob at a vertex the two objects share. Beyond the arm, 304004 is a 2-point 0.9 cm speck at 5.3e4 sitting 19.2-19.8 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.55, drawn as an isolated pair of vertex squares roughly out past the arm's far end in all three views, across a clear 5.6 cm charge-free gap from where the arm ends. Detached, compact, past the stop, inside 60 cm, off the body line and on the Michel's side: gamma, which makes the kind both, and I am overriding the chain's gamma body exclusion label as the rubric permits. f_meas puts the stop at U 2170-2190, V 6050-6075 and W 10240-10310, and there are dead bands at U 2165-2180 and V 6045-6055 that the stop end overlaps - worth noting, though here they clearly did not suppress the Bragg.

notes: No undershoot and no overshoot, both ruled out cheaply: there is no non-chain row in the table at all, so nothing forward at high charge to mistake for a Michel, and the profile's last two points are its highest, so there is no peak-then-collapse. High confidence - the profile, the geometry and the chain's own verdict all agree, and there is no competing reading to record.
evidence: A 214.6 cm chain, 498.8 MeV by range with MCS agreeing at 467.7 (amb 0.09), entering 1.0 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 47.7 cm from the nearest (y) wall, in_fv 1; the chain accepts it as an STM. The dQ/dx panel is as clean as the best in this chunk: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=15 scattering about the flat solid muon curve, then a monotone climb that follows the curve all the way in - 6.5-7.2e4 at s=6-13, 8.9-9.3e4 at s=4-6, 1.03-1.09e5 at s=1.5-3, and 1.26e5 and 1.345e5 at the last two points, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band and hugging the reference. There is no terminal dip whatever: the highest two points in the entire profile are the two nearest the origin, so neither failure mode applies and the pin stays exactly where the fit put it. This is the only item in my chunk with no non-chain object at all - the table has two rows and both are the muon's own fitted segments, 80002 spanning d 0-127.65 and 80005 spanning 127.65-201.16, both at cos_fwd about -1.0 as body segments must be. All three stop azimuths show the amber flow band running to the star and stopping there with nothing drawn beyond it: no arm, no dot, no speck, and no image-point halo past the end. The chain reports the same - n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring, 0 unfitted clusters - so there is nothing to weigh and the kind is none. f_meas is clean at the stop: it sits at U 2010, V 5805 and W 10120 with the nearest dead bands 40 to 90 channels away in every plane, and measured minus predicted is flat white along the whole track, so the Bragg is measured, not inferred.

notes: No undershoot: 341003 does reach cos_fwd +0.88 but it is 59 cm out with no dqdx at all, not a couple of centimetres at 1e5, and 347009's 8.3e4 is at 37 cm and cos_fwd -0.32. No overshoot: the last point is the highest, no peak-then-collapse. Medium because this is a genuine two-way call. The competing reading is that the 4.33 cm gap is a 3-D clustering artefact - the chain itself says the clustering split the electron off the muon - in which case 345007+346008 are an attached Michel and the item is STM_MICHEL / attached. I went the other way on the rubric's explicit attachment tie-break plus the 4.1 MeV total, which is far more gamma-like than Michel-like, and having satisfied myself that U and W are live across the gap so the hole is not instrumental. If the owner's key says Michel, this is the item and this is why.
evidence: A 328.6 cm chain, 756.7 MeV by range with MCS at 729.8 (amb 0.03), entering 2.6 cm from the x face and ending 88.4 cm from the nearest (z) face - deep, and the chain accepts it. The Bragg is clean and needs no interpretation: 4.8-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=20, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=12-18, 7.7-9.5e4 at s=5-11, 1.01-1.12e5 at s=1.5-4 and 1.36e5 at the last point, sitting on the muon reference curve the whole climb and topping in the 1.2-1.35e5 band. No terminal dip, so the pin stays. The whole item turns on two small pieces past the stop, and I came down against calling them the Michel. 345007 (2 points, 0.4 cm, 2.9e4) and 346008 (6 points, 3.2 cm, 1.5e4) sit at d 4.32-6.69 cm at cos_fwd +0.30, drawn in the c and d azimuths as a short blue trail below the star between two vertex squares, and on the dQ/dx panel as eight large markers at s=-4.3 to -6.7 running 4.3e4 down to 1.4e4. They are separated from the stop by a charge-free gap - d_min is 4.32 cm and the chain's own flow text says it bridged them to the stop vertex across 4.33 cm of empty space, by proximity rather than a graph edge. The rubric's tie-break for exactly this collision is attachment, and it says a piece across a clean charge-free gap is a detached dot however close it sits. Two independent things back that here. First the energy: the chain totals the object at 4.1 MeV, and a 4 MeV Michel is a fraction of a percent of the decay spectrum while 1-6 MeV is precisely the de-excitation gamma range from mu- capture on argon, which is the majority outcome for a negative cosmic muon. Second, the gap is not a readout hole - I checked f_meas for that specifically, and while V does have a dead band at 6770-6785 immediately past the stop at 6760, both U (gap region 2965-2990, nearest dead bands at 2905 and 3030) and W (track at 11300, dead lines at 11400) are live right across it, so imaging had two good planes there and still produced nothing. So: gamma, the verdict stays STM_ONLY because isolated compact capture-gamma pieces do not promote it, and the kind is detached dots rather than none. The five survey-only specks - 347009 at 37.1 cm, 344006 at 37.4, 343005 at 39.9, 342004 at 40.7 and 341003 at 59-60.5 - are each two points, 0.1-2.0 cm, and their cos_fwd runs from -0.32 through -0.15, +0.21 and +0.63 to +0.88. All three azimuths show them scattered around the stop in a broad arc at quite different directions rather than lined up on the dots' side, which is the rubric's own criterion for calling ring specks delta / other, so that is what they get; charge did not enter it. 91001 (4 points, 1.6 cm) is 314 cm away at cos_fwd -0.99, on the body line at the far entry end: delta / other.

notes: No undershoot: the closest row to the bar is 407023 at cos_fwd +0.82, but it is 45 cm out and 2 points, not a couple of centimetres at several times MIP. No overshoot and no pin move: there is no peak anywhere to collapse from. Medium confidence and the reason is worth the owner's attention: this track is nearly isochronous, all three planes show its charge at a near-constant time slice across ~150 channels, so its dQ/dx is intrinsically ill-measured (whole-track plateau at 0.04-0.74 of MIP with a regular 15-20 cm oscillation, and the chain's own range and dQ/dx energies differ by 42 percent). The THRU call therefore rests on the absence of any rise relative to the track's own plateau, which is scale-free and does survive the bad calibration, but it is not backed by a wall contact or a visible continuation the way item 039253_2/75 was - the fit end is 105.2 cm from everything. If any item in my chunk deserves a second look on the question of whether a suppressed Bragg is hiding under a broken dQ/dx, it is this one.
evidence: A 377.6 cm chain entering 0.7 cm from the y face and ending 105.2 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained, which is exactly why I want the reasoning on the record rather than the geometry. The dQ/dx profile never touches MIP anywhere along the track: it oscillates between about 0.2e4 and 4.0e4 with a regular period of roughly 15-20 cm, from s=100 all the way in, and the solid muon curve (5.4e4 asymptote) and the 6.7e4 dashed MIP line both sit far above every single point. The chain flags this itself with plateau_off_mip alongside no_bragg and shape_flat, and its two energy estimates disagree by 42 percent (871 MeV by range against 503 MeV by dQ/dx, MCS 608). At the fit end the value is 1.3e4, rising slightly to 1.7e4 at s=2 and then dropping to 0.3e4 at s=7-9 - so relative to the track's own oscillating plateau of about 2e4, the last point sits below, not above. That is the scale-free version of the test and it fails: there is no rise off its own plateau over the last 10-20 cm, in either absolute or relative terms, so by the operative test this is a through-goer. Nothing is drawn past the star in any of the three azimuths - the amber flow band covers only the last 5.7 cm (segment 95001, which turns sharply, hence its cos_fwd -0.77) and terminates, with the rest of the object running away as a low-charge blue trace. There is no visible continuation, no face within 105 cm, and no dead region at the end, and the rubric is explicit that a flat profile is enough on its own in exactly that situation and that UNCLEAR is not the way out of saying so. f_meas explains the profile and supports treating the object as badly measured rather than genuinely low-ionising: in all three planes the whole track's charge lies at a nearly constant time slice, about 1910-1920, spread across 150 channels - the track is very close to isochronous, lying almost in a plane of constant drift, which is the geometry that makes dQ/dx unreliable and periodic. Per the THRU convention every fitted chain segment (95001, 95003, 95004, 95018, 95019) is tagged muon and everything else delta / other, including 408024, which the chain groups as a capture gamma at 18.9 cm - gamma and michel are defined against a stop and a through-goer has none. The twelve remaining unassigned pieces are 12-49 cm long at 0.3e4-2.9e4 and sit 115-265 cm back at cos_fwd -0.84 to -0.96, i.e. strung along the muon body far outside any ring: body activity in every case.

notes: No undershoot - and this is the item where I checked hardest, because 32003 is a short forward piece the chain types pdg 11 and offers as the Michel, with a mean above MIP. It fails on both discriminators: cos_fwd +0.25 is 76 deg off straight ahead, and 6.9e4 is 1.27 x MIP rather than the several times MIP the rule requires. The decisive structural point is that the muon's own Bragg peak, 1.442e5, is at its own last point, verified by marker size (5x5 chain marker at s=0.8) rather than by eye, so there is nothing left over for a tip to be. No overshoot either: no peak-then-collapse, the last chain point is the highest, pin untouched. The only soft call is 126011's gamma tag at 50 cm and cos_fwd +0.94, which does not move the kind since 124009 already carries a gamma tag.
evidence: A 134.0 cm chain entering 4.9 cm from the z face and ending 19.4 cm from the x (anode) face, in_fv 1 and accepted by the chain. The Bragg is as clean as any in my chunk and, crucially, it peaks AT the fit's last point rather than before it: 5.4e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=40, 6.5-8.5e4 at s=15-35, 8.5-9.0e4 at s=8-12, 9.9-1.05e5 at s=3-8, 1.077e5 at s=3.3 and 1.135e5 at s=2.6, and 1.442e5 at the last chain point at s=0.8, hugging the solid muon curve the entire climb. That single fact does most of the work, because it rules out the undershoot: the fit did not stop short, so the high-charge piece past the end cannot be the muon's own last centimetres. Because the two objects overlap at the vertex I did not trust my eye on which marker is which - I measured marker sizes on the raw PNG. Chain markers here are 5-7 px across, object markers 8-16. The 1.442e5 dark red point at s=0.8 is 5x5, so it is the muon's own last point; the 1.364e5 blue point sitting essentially on the origin is 8x8, so it is 32003's first point. Both readings I relied on are therefore confirmed rather than assumed. Past the stop, 32003 (8 points, 3.8 cm, mean 6.9e4, d 0.0-3.68, cos_fwd +0.25) leaves the shared stop vertex with a 72 deg kink and 32001 (4 points, 1.6 cm, mean 6.3e4, d 3.68-4.78, cos_fwd +0.37) continues it, together 5.4 cm and 21.4 MeV by the chain's reckoning. Their twelve large markers run down the negative axis from 1.364e5 at the vertex through 8.0-8.6e4 at s=-2.3 to -2.8, 6.9e4 at -0.2, 4.1e4 at -2.0 and 3.5e4 at -0.5, down to 2.6e4 near -4.8: falling as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature. I tested this against the undershoot case properly rather than by eye, because the mean is above MIP: the undershoot wants a piece lying straight ahead at cos_fwd 0.85 or better, a couple of centimetres long, at 0.9-1.2e5, i.e. four to six times MIP. This piece is 76 deg off the muon's forward direction, and 6.9e4 is 1.27 x MIP - the charge is the load-bearing clause and it is nowhere near, so this is the ordinary case, not that one. The 1.364e5 opening point sits on the vertex the two objects share and is charge the muon's own Bragg blob contributes to; from 2 cm out the arm is at or below 8.6e4 and falling. Three faint specks lie past the stop in the forward hemisphere: 124009 (2 points, 1.5 cm, 5.0e3) at 26.1-26.7 cm and cos_fwd +0.12, 125010 (3 points, 1.1 cm, 6.1e3) at 37.9-38.5 cm and cos_fwd +0.05, and 126011 (2 points, 0.1 cm, 1.4e4) at 50.1 cm and cos_fwd +0.94. All three are isolated, compact, clear of the muon body line, inside the 60 cm ring and on the decay's side of the stop, and charge is explicitly not a criterion for them, so all three are gamma and the kind is both. In the c and e azimuths 124009 and 125010 line up along the arm's own direction; 126011 is the least secure of the three because it sits nearly straight ahead of the muon while the arm is about 80 deg off, but it is still past the stop, off the body and faint. The last row, 32007 (14 points, 7.6 cm, 7.5e3), sits 106-110 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the body line at the far end: delta / other. f_meas is clean, with measured minus predicted flat along the track and the nearest dead lines 15 channels off in U and 45 in W.

notes: Hard call, competing reading recorded: the two highest points in the panel sit at s=12-13 (8.8e4 and 9.6e4) and the last 8-12 cm collapse to 0.1-0.3 of plateau, which is the shape of the overshoot signature, and under that reading the pin would move to rr about 12 and the tail of 53002 would be the Michel. I did not take it because (a) equally high points sit at s=24-27, so the maximum is not localised near the stop as a real Bragg peak would be, (b) the collapse runs 8-12 cm which is long for the 'small gap' mechanism, and (c) there is nothing on the far side for the fit to bridge to - the fit's last point is the end of all charge in the event. Read instead as the rubric's sanctioned case: no continuation, no face, no dead-region exit, charge simply fading to zero where the imaging ran out on a drift-parallel track. No undershoot signature (no high-charge forward tip past the fit end).
evidence: 150 cm chain, 140 cm of it drawn in two chain segments; enters 0.4 cm from the z face at (-56, 46.8, 298) and the fit ends at (-193.4, 46.4, 279.6), 18.9 cm from the nearest (z) wall, so containment does not decide this one. The track is almost entirely along drift (dx 137 cm, dz 18 cm, dy 0.4 cm), which is why f_meas shows it as a narrow channel stripe over 140 time slices in all three planes. On the 5x crop of g_dqdx the profile has a wide two-population scatter at every arc length, but both envelopes do the same thing: they climb slowly from about 1-4e4 at s=50-58 to 5-7e4 (with 9.5e4 excursions at s=24 and s=27) around s=15-25, and then FALL over the last 8 cm - 4.6e4 at s=4, 3.5e4 at s=3.4, 1.2-1.5e4 at s=0-2, with two literal zero-charge points at s=0 and s=7.8. There is no rise above the track's own 4.3e4 plateau anywhere in the last 10-20 cm and nothing that follows the shape of the muon reference curve into s=0, so the operative test fails. Nothing is drawn past the fit end: all three 3-D azimuths show the point cloud stopping at the star with no arm, no dots and no kink, and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, 0 unfitted dot clusters. f_meas shows measured and predicted agreeing with a thin residual and the charge simply ending mid-time-range rather than running into a dead band, though W sits between dead channel groups at 9605-9615 and 9625-9635. Both drawn rows are fitted chain segments so both are muon and the kind is none.

notes: Competing reading: fully contained at both ends (17.8 and 47.5 cm) with a last point at 2x plateau, which would make it STM_ONLY. I took THRU because the elevation is two points over 0.4 cm on an otherwise dead-flat 20 cm profile, and because the object's own imaging gaps at s=32-46 show the cluster ends where imaging ran out rather than where the particle stopped. No continuation and no face at either end - stated explicitly as the rubric requires. Neither the overshoot (no peak-then-collapse before the last point) nor the undershoot (no high-charge piece past the fit end) signature is present.
evidence: One drawn object, the 95 cm muon chain segment 121003 (143 points, mean dQ/dx 51875, d 0 to 90 cm, cos_fwd -1.0). The fit runs from (-31.8, 102.6, 280.7), 17.8 cm from the z face, to (22.6, 169.0, 251.0), 47.5 cm from the nearest face, so both ends sit well inside the volume and containment cannot decide it. The 6x crop of the last 20 cm shows a flat plateau: reading in from s=20 the points are 0.60, 0.64, 0.50, 0.53, 0.50, 0.56, 0.62, 0.585, 0.515, 0.45, 0.515, 0.52, 0.54e5 down to s=0.7, all below the muon reference curve (0.62e5 at s=16, 0.71e5 at s=6, 0.82e5 at s=4, 1.03e5 at s=2.3) and with no trend toward it. Only the final two fit points lift: 0.672e5 at s=0.4 and 1.036e5 at s=0.0. With 0.66 cm between fit points that is a rise confined to the last half-centimetre, not the 10-20 cm climb the test asks for; a real stopper would have its last seven points all elevated and here the seventh-from-last is 0.515e5, dead on the MIP plateau. The single high terminal point reads as the fit's last point sweeping up the leftover cluster-end charge. The three 3-D azimuths show a straight track ending at the star with no arm, no dots and no kink past it, f_meas shows the charge in all three planes stopping at the pin time slice with nothing beyond and no dead band at the stop, and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. The drawn cloud is in two pieces with a clear mid-track gap, matching the dQ/dx dropouts to 0-2e4 at s=32-35 and s=44-46, so imaging on this object is demonstrably patchy - which is exactly the rubric's sanctioned THRU reading of a flat MIP fragment that simply ends where the imaging ran out. Only chain segment drawn, so it is tagged muon and the kind is none.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation and no face at the stop end - stated explicitly as the rubric requires; the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. No overshoot (nothing is elevated before the low last point) and no undershoot (nothing past the fit end at all, let alone a high-charge forward tip). Note for the round: the 3-D azimuths put the orange entry circle at the mid-track kink, not at the far end, which is display trap 3.
evidence: 62.3 cm chain in three fitted segments plus one survey speck. It enters at (-267.7, -53.9, 2.2), 1.4 cm from the z face, and the fit ends at (-308.8, -24.6, 28.8), 28.0 cm from the nearest z wall and 31.1 cm from the anode face, so the far end is genuinely inside. On the 6x crop the last 20 cm are dead flat: 0.35e5 at s=0.3 (two overlapping points), 0.48-0.60e5 from s=1.2 to s=8 with one 0.75e5 excursion at s=6.2, 0.45-0.56e5 from s=10 to s=17, and 0.69-0.75e5 at s=19-21. There is no climb toward the muon reference curve anywhere in the last 10-20 cm and the final point is the LOWEST of the run, 30 per cent under the segment's own 53693 mean - ordinary end scatter, not a peak-then-collapse, because nothing before it is elevated. A 62 cm range implies 171 MeV of muon kinetic energy, and a muon that really burned that off in the last stretch could not sit on the MIP plateau to its final point. The low-charge tail in the panel at s=44-62, including the V-shaped dip to 1.0e4 at s=48-52, belongs to segments 31003 (mean 27694) and 31005 (21281) on the ENTRY side of the chain, past the kink the 3-D azimuths show at about 44 cm from the stop, so it says nothing about the stop. All three azimuths show the orange chain ending at the star with no arm, no dot and no kink beyond it, and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. f_meas shows several dead channel bands in U and a wide one in V but none at the pin, and measured matches predicted along the track. Object 173008 is a 4-point, 0.0 cm survey speck 50.8 cm out at cos_fwd 0.32 that neither stage was offered; on a THRU there is no stop for gamma to be defined against, so per the rubric it is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Clean flat-profile THRU, and here the continuation is even accounted for: U and W both have dead channel groups at the stop channel, so the likely exit is through a dead region rather than the imaging simply running out. No overshoot and no undershoot signature.
evidence: A long straight 256.5 cm chain in six fitted segments, entering at (-3.2, -14.4, 23.4) 22.6 cm from the z face and ending at (-208.3, 28.9, 149.5), 131.7 cm from the nearest face - about as deeply contained as a fit end gets in this detector, so if anything ought to show a Bragg peak it is this one. It does not. The profile sits on a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in to s=2, tracking the black muon curve where that curve is flat (5.4e4 beyond s=40) and then staying flat while the curve climbs away from it: at s=2-8 the points are 5.0-7.4e4, with two delta-like excursions of 8.85e4 at s=9 and 9.7e4 at s=10 that are isolated single points, not a rise. The only structure at the very end is a four-point descending ladder over roughly the last 1.5 cm - 4.1e4, 2.9e4, 2.0e4, 1.5e4 - with nothing elevated before it, so it is terminal partial-charge scatter and not a peak-then-collapse. f_meas is the other half of the story: at the stop the track sits at U channel about 975, immediately against a dead band spanning 950-975, and at W channel about 9075, against a dead band at 9070-9080, so two of the three planes lose the track exactly where the fit ends while V (clear there, its dead band is far off at 4760-4790) also shows the charge stopping. The three 3-D azimuths show a perfectly straight spine with the star at the end and no arm, no dot and no kink past it; the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. The four unassigned pieces 34007, 34010, 34013 and 34016 that the chain types pdg 11 shower all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 at 17.8, 26.0, 37.2 and 157.2 cm along the body - they are the orange points on the negative axis at magnitudes 18 to 38 - so they hug the muon line and are delta / other by the on-the-body rule, which on a THRU is where everything non-chain goes anyway.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence - the Bragg climb over 20 cm is unambiguous. The medium is entirely for michel_kind: it rests on calling the two forward survey specks gamma rather than delta / other, which is what moves the kind from none to detached dots. I went gamma because they are detached, compact, inside 60 cm, off the body line and on one side of the stop rather than scattered, which is the rubric's stated test; the competing reading is that two 3-4 point survey specks that neither stage was offered are just unrelated activity in a busy region that also contains a 120 cm crossing track. Note 173008 is the same object id that appears in item 039253_6/31, seen from a different stop. No overshoot and no undershoot signature.
evidence: 83.9 cm chain in four fitted segments, entering at (-195.4, -4.6, 1.9) just 1.1 cm from the z face and ending at (-256.1, 25.4, 27.4), 26.6 cm from the nearest z wall, so the far end is inside the volume. The Bragg is the cleanest thing in this item: reading in from the plateau the points go 5.5-6.5e4 beyond s=25, 6.9-7.1e4 at s=14-16, 7.1-7.8e4 at s=12-14, 9.3-9.5e4 at s=8-12, 8.6-9.2e4 at s=6-8, 1.03-1.09e5 at s=3-6, 1.25e5 at s=1.5, 1.45e5 at s=0.7 and 1.19e5 at the last point - a monotone climb over the last 20 cm hugging the shape of the black muon curve, and segment 41001's own mean of 88180 against 60030 for the segment behind it says the same thing in one number. The final point being 18 per cent under the peak just before it is ordinary end scatter, well inside the rubric's leave-the-pin-alone band, and there is no sustained collapse, so the pin stays. Nothing is attached at the stop: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the nearest drawn object is 175019 at 18.6 cm with cos_fwd -0.95, a 15-point 8.2 cm piece lying back along the muon body that the chain itself body-excluded - delta / other on the on-the-body rule, and past the 10 cm radius where direction stops discriminating. Two survey-only specks sit past the stop on its forward side: 174009 (3 points, 1.2 cm, 18743 e/cm) at 36.5 cm with cos_fwd 0.57, and 173008 (4 points, 0.0 cm, 24104 e/cm) at 40.0 cm with cos_fwd 0.89. On the e azimuth they are the two isolated brown squares beyond the star, and scaling off the 18.6 cm orange segment (5.6 px/cm) puts the nearer one about 37 cm out - they are detached across a charge-free gap, compact, well clear of the body line and inside 60 cm, and they lie on the same side of the stop rather than scattered around the ring, so both are gamma and the kind is detached dots. Charge is not a criterion for that call. C42 is a 574-point 120 cm cluster with no PR segment crossing the field diagonally in every 3-D frame - a different object entirely - and 41007 is a 3.3 cm 5184 e/cm shower speck 59 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99; both are delta / other. f_meas: V is unusable at the stop, the track sitting inside the wide dead band at 4760-4820, but U and W both show measured matching predicted and the charge ending at the pin, with the two specks appearing as separate markers at time slices 2113 and 2177 against the track's 2250-2400.

notes: Cleanest THRU in the chunk: face to face, anode-parallel geometry, and a profile that collapses rather than rises. The MCS estimate is pegged at 4000 MeV with ambiguity 1.00, which is what a straight non-stopping track does to that fit. No overshoot and no undershoot signature.
evidence: 79.6 cm chain, one drawn object, and the geometry decides it before the charge does: it enters at (335.1, -230.9, 297.4), 1.0 cm from the z face, and the fit ends at (337.4, -178.5, 253.3), 2.6 cm from the anode face - a face at each end. x runs 335.1 to 337.4 over the whole 80 cm, so the track lies essentially parallel to and 2-3 cm off the anode, which is exactly why the 3-D frames show a broad diffuse smear of image points either side of the orange chain rather than a clean spine, and why f_meas has the track compressed into time slices 2450-2470 in all three planes (isochronous). The profile does the opposite of a Bragg: taking the upper envelope it runs 6.0-7.6e4 at s=17-25, 5.2e4 at s=15, 4.6e4 at s=8, and then over the last 8 cm the points collapse into a dense band at 0.3-0.8e4 from s=0 to s=7 with a few at 1.2-2.4e4 at s=7-12 - fading to nothing, with no peak anywhere before the collapse to make it the overshoot signature and the segment's own mean only 36167 to begin with. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any azimuth, the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma, and measured matches predicted with no dead band at the fit end in any plane (U's nearest are at 2490-2540, V's at 6390-6430, W's at 10800-10820). Charge fading to zero as the track runs into the anode 2.6 cm away is an exit, not a stop. Single chain segment, so muon, and the kind is none.

notes: Cleanest STM_MICHEL in the chunk. Pin left alone: no peak-then-collapse, the profile is still climbing at the last fit point. Explicitly checked the undershoot and it does not apply - the forward piece is at 0.58 MIP, not the four-to-six times MIP that would make it the muon's own tip.
evidence: 77.2 cm chain entering at (339.6, -233.4, 150.3) 0.3 cm from the anode face and ending at (307.2, -287.0, 189.7), 32.7 cm from the nearest face, so the stop is comfortably inside. The Bragg is textbook: a 5.2-5.5e4 plateau from s=80 in to s=15, then 6.0-6.6e4 at s=10-18, 7.3-7.8e4 at s=5-8, 8.0-8.4e4 at s=2-5, 1.06e5 at s=0.8, 1.12e5 at s=0.3 and a 1.285e5 point at s=1.5 - a smooth monotone climb over the last 15 cm that tracks the black muon curve's shape and tops out where the rubric says real stoppers do. Attached at that stop, at the shared vertex 79002, is 79001: 6 points over 3.0 cm carrying 31160 e/cm, which is 0.58 of this track's own MIP plateau, leaving at a 97 degree kink (cos_fwd -0.14). It is the ordinary Michel case and explicitly NOT the undershoot - the undershoot needs a 2 cm tip at several times MIP, and this piece is below MIP, so the tip is not the muon's own last centimetres. A muon sitting at its Bragg peak has no energy left to throw a 5.7 MeV delta, and at 97 degrees the piece is well clear of the body line and attached at the vertex, so both halves of the tie-break rule give michel. Its points are the blue circles on the negative axis at magnitudes 1 to 3 carrying 3.0-3.6e4, which is minus their 3-D distance from the origin and not a claim about which side they are on; the 3-D azimuths put the small blue blob right at the star, transverse to the spine. The only other object, 79004, is a 2-point 0.4 cm piece the chain types pdg 2212, sitting 74 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 hard on the muon body at the far end of the track - delta / other. f_meas shows measured matching predicted in all three planes with the charge and the low-charge Michel points both ending at the pin near time slice 1220, and the dead bands in U at 2380-2450 and in V at 6180-6200 are nowhere near the stop. One michel piece and no gamma, so the kind is attached.

notes: Medium, not high, because the object is nearly isochronous and the per-segment means run from 2230 to 45650 e/cm - charge reconstruction is visibly unreliable over much of it, so the flat profile is weaker evidence here than it would be on a normal-angle track. Two things pull the other way and are worth recording: the chain rejected on shape_flat ALONE, not no_bragg, so its own Bragg metric keyed on that single last point; and range KE 967.9 MeV against MCS 802.6 MeV at ambiguity 0.08 are closer than one usually sees on a through-goer. I still read it THRU because the human test is a rise over the last 10-20 cm and there is none. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: A 418.6 cm chain in twelve fitted segments with ten more unassigned pieces hung along it, entering at (267.7, -295.0, 290.1) 8.3 cm from the z face and ending at (276.6, -0.8, 93.2), 63.3 cm from the anode face and 92.4 cm from the z face, so the fit end is deeply inside. Geometry first, because it colours everything else: the end view puts the whole object at x between 267 and 277 over its full 418 cm, i.e. essentially isochronous, and f_meas confirms it - the entire object occupies time slices 20 to 50 across U channels 2280-2490. On the 6x crop the last 20 cm are flat and low: 0.44-0.49e5 at s=0.6-3.9, 0.53e5 and 0.63e5 at s=2.7-3.5, 0.38-0.42e5 at s=4.5-5.1, 0.28-0.35e5 at s=6-8, 0.47-0.49e5 at s=9-10, with one zero-charge point at s=1.2 to ignore, against a muon reference curve that is at 1.3e5 by s=0.6 and 0.78e5 at s=6. The only elevated point in the whole terminal region is the single last one at 1.044e5, 2.3x the near-stop segment's own 40427 mean - one point, no climb behind it, the same fit-end charge-sweep artefact as in 039253_5/121 rather than a Bragg. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any azimuth and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. Every unassigned piece sits on the muon body: 217044 is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 33.7 cm out at cos_fwd -0.95 that the chain body-excluded, and 82001, 82013, 82017, 82020, 82023, 82027, 82029, 82035 and 82036 are all at cos_fwd -0.98 to -1.0 between 55 and 342 cm back - body activity, delta / other, which is also where a THRU sends everything non-chain. It is not MESSY: all three azimuths show one continuous coherent spine with the side activity as a halo around it, not an EM blob with no spine.

notes: Hardest call in the chunk so far and the one to re-audit. Competing reading: the profile peaks at s=2.4-3.1 and the last 2 cm sit back at MIP, and 'a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP' would make that terminal stretch a second particle - i.e. an overshoot with the collapse falling inside segment 85005, pin-rr about 2.2, and the verdict STM_MICHEL. I did not take it because the rubric's overshoot needs the charge to fall FAR BELOW the muon's own plateau and here it falls only to 0.75-0.93 of it, and because there is nothing past the fit end to be the far side of the bridge. Also note the chain's own segment means run 41052, 41906, 28266, 45103 going in toward the stop, so the terminal segment is only marginally above the ones behind it - the elevation lives in individual points, not in the segment average. No undershoot signature.
evidence: A short object: 27.1 cm of chain in four fitted segments, entering at (188.6, -82.5, 1.4) just 0.6 cm from the z face and ending at (203.0, -67.2, 14.4), 13.6 cm from that same face - the whole thing lives in the first 15 cm of z, and 27 cm of range is only 92 MeV, so a genuine low-energy stopper is entirely plausible here. On the 7x crop the last 5 cm are clearly elevated over what comes before: reading in, s=9.1 is 0.20e5, s=7.0 is 0.17e5, s=6.2 is 0.21e5, s=5.2 is 0.29e5, then s=4.9 0.50e5, s=4.3 0.79e5, s=3.7 0.44e5, s=3.1 0.95e5, s=2.4 0.87e5, s=2.0 0.57e5. The 0.79-0.95e5 points at s=2.4-4.3 sit essentially ON the black muon curve, which is at 0.83-1.0e5 there - none of the through-goers in this chunk get within a factor of three of that curve near the stop, and that is what makes me read this as a stop rather than a fragment. The last three points then fall back: 0.39e5 at s=1.4, 0.34e5 at s=0.7, 0.42e5 at s=0.0. I looked hard at moving the pin and decided against it, and say so explicitly: the fall lands at 0.75-0.93 of this track's own 4.5e4 plateau, not far below it, whereas the overshoot signature needs the charge to collapse far under the plateau where a muon at its peak would be far above it, and there is nothing at all past the fit end for the fit to have bridged to - the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. Against this item's own scatter, which runs 0.02e5 to 0.95e5 within twelve centimetres, three terminal points at plateau level are end scatter. Nothing reads as decay charge past the stop, so the kind is none. All four unassigned pieces hug the muon body and are delta / other: 85007 at 4.3-6.3 cm with cos_fwd -0.98 (about 1 cm off the muon line, so the on-the-body rule beats the inside-10-cm rule on the off-axis tie-break), 85019 at 6.3-15.0 cm at cos_fwd -1.0, 85013 at 12.4-14.3 cm at -0.99, and 345020, a 6-point 3.2 cm piece 18.2 cm out at -0.96 that the chain body-excluded. Their points are the orange clusters on the negative axis at magnitudes 4-6 and 13-15 and the grey crosses at 19-21, plotted as minus their 3-D distance, which says nothing about which side of the stop they are on. f_meas shows the object confined to time slices 2455-2505 with measured matching predicted and the nearest dead bands well off the track in all three planes.

notes: Medium because the object is sparse enough that the chain rejected it on profile_sparse alone - its Bragg and shape tests passed - and I share the unease: the near-stop rise starts from 1.65e4, which is 0.3 of MIP, so the 'plateau' it rises from may just be badly reconstructed charge. The one number that would flip this to STM_ONLY via the undershoot is the Michel piece's outermost point at 1.16e5, the highest charge anywhere in the item, sitting about 1.5 cm out rather than at the vertex - i.e. the piece's charge rises as it goes out, which is the wrong sense for an electron. I did not flip it because the piece fails the undershoot's charge clause (1.5x MIP, not several times) and its 82 degree kink and attachment at the vertex both read as a decay, but this is the item in my chunk most worth a second opinion.
evidence: 159.7 cm of chain but only 116 chain points, and the sparseness is the defining feature: segment 90005 carries 8 points over 72.1 cm and 90007 carries 6 over 7.9 cm, so most of the fit is bridging empty space, and the dQ/dx panel is correspondingly bare - a group of about twenty points between s=0 and s=9, a handful at s=77-90, and nothing at all in between. The projections show the same thing as three separated clumps strung along a 148 cm line with the star at one end. The fit enters at (35.9, -330.6, 133.5), 5.8 cm from the y face, and ends at (161.8, -277.9, 190.1), 58.4 cm from the nearest face, so the stop is well inside. Over the last 9 cm the chain points do climb: 1.65e4 at s=9, 2.15e4 at s=8, 2.7e4 at s=7, 3.2e4 at s=6, then 5.45e4, 5.55e4, 6.35e4, 5.8e4 across s=2.5-5 and 6.95e4 at s=0.5 - a factor of four, steeper than the reference curve's own slope there, though the whole run sits at only a quarter to a half of that curve and the base it climbs from is 0.3 of MIP, which on this object is as likely to be poor reconstruction as a plateau. What settles it is the topology: 90001 is attached at the shared stop vertex 90002, five points over 2.3 cm leaving at an 82 degree kink (cos_fwd 0.35), and the rubric is explicit that a Michel topology is sufficient on its own even when the Bragg is unclear. Its five points are the oversized circles on the negative axis at magnitudes 0 to 2.2 carrying 8.4e4, 7.25e4, 4.3e4, 4.25e4 and 1.16e5, mean 72624. I checked the undershoot carefully because it is exactly the trap that manufactures a false STM_MICHEL, and it does not apply: the piece is attached at the vertex rather than sitting a couple of centimetres past the fit end, its cos_fwd is 0.35 rather than the near-axial 0.85 or better, and its mean is 1.5x this track's 48387 near-stop segment mean, not the several times MIP the rubric requires before invoking it. At 82 degrees it is well clear of the muon body line and it is attached, so both halves of the tie-break give michel. One michel piece, no gamma, no dots, no capture gamma in the ring - kind attached. f_meas shows the charge as one tight clump at time slice 1230-1250 in all three planes with the fit line running off to the upper left through nothing, which is the sparseness again; measured matches predicted and no dead band touches the clump.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with a deeply contained end and no visible continuation - the rubric's sanctioned case, stated explicitly. Medium rather than high because 84.9 cm of clearance plus a 2.3x last point is the configuration a real stopper would also produce, and because a drift-parallel track's dQ/dx is the least trustworthy kind. What decided it is that the four points before the last one are the lowest in the whole 250 cm, so there is no climb for the last point to be the top of. No overshoot (nothing elevated before the terminal dip) and no undershoot (nothing past the fit end).
evidence: 251.9 cm chain in six fitted segments, entering at (339.5, -73.4, 63.5) just 0.4 cm off the anode face and ending at (107.5, -101.4, 85.7), 84.9 cm from the nearest z face and 232.4 cm back from the anode, so the fit end is deeply inside. The track is essentially drift-parallel - dx -232 cm against dy -28 and dz +22 - which f_meas confirms: in all three planes it is a narrow vertical stripe, U pinned at channel 2225 across time slices 2330-2480, and the same in V at 6020 and W at 10405. The profile is flat over its whole length at 4.0-5.0e4, and the last 15 cm show no climb at all: 5.5-6.5e4 in a bump at s=15-18, 3.4-4.6e4 from s=5 to s=15, 3.9-4.2e4 at s=3-5, then 2.6e4 at s=2, 3.0e4 at s=1.5, 4.7e4 at s=1 and 5.0e4 at s=0.3 - the points nearest the end are among the LOWEST of the run, while the muon reference curve is at 1.03e5 by s=2.3. The sole elevated point is the very last one at 1.16e5, one point with nothing rising behind it, which is the same fit-end charge-sweep artefact seen in 039253_5/121 and 039253_6/82 and not a Bragg. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any of the three azimuths - the cyan spine simply stops at the star - and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. The two unassigned objects are body activity: 64019, five points over 2.4 cm at cos_fwd -1.0, 28-29.6 cm back (the five orange points on the negative axis at magnitude 29 carrying 1.85e4 to 8.3e4), and 228026, a 2-point 0.4 cm survey speck 51.4 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 - both hard on the muon line, so delta / other, which is where a THRU sends everything non-chain anyway. Dead bands in U at 2160-2175 and in V at 5960-6060 flank the track but the charge ends mid-time-range, not against one.

notes: OVERSHOOT: real stop is about 9.2 cm back up the fit from its last point, at the 0.83-1.02e5 group at s=9.4-13.4; pin-rr 9.2 recorded. Medium, not high, and here is the competing reading: the track is drift-dominated (dx -130 against dy 34, dz 42) so it crosses only about 15 U channels over its whole length, and U carries a thin dead band at channel 3040 which is exactly where the last stretch of the track sits, while V (6820, dead bands at 6770 and 6890) and W (11310, dead band at 11400) are clear. A dead U channel eating charge along the last stretch would depress the same nine centimetres without any Michel. What kept me on the overshoot is that charge loss cannot manufacture the RISE from 0.5e5 at s=20 to 1.02e5 at s=10 that precedes the collapse. Note also the two points at 0.78-0.81e5 at s=1.8-2.0, which sit inside the region I am calling Michel; I read them as a brem or shower point on the electron. Verdict and kind are robust to the pin question - leaving the pin alone gives STM_MICHEL / attached as well, with 80009 tagged muon instead - so only the pin and that one tag are at stake.
evidence: 152.1 cm chain in two fitted segments, entering at (339.9, 72.9, 56.5) right on the anode face (d_face 0.0) and ending at (209.6, 106.8, 98.3), 97.5 cm from the nearest z face - deeply contained. On the 7x crop the profile does something none of the through-goers in this chunk do: it climbs off its own plateau and then collapses well before the fit's last point. Reading in, s=20-100 sits at 0.45-0.55e5, s=18.4 is 0.578e5, s=17.2 is 0.60-0.70e5, s=16-17 is 0.70-0.75e5, s=13.7 is 0.79e5, then a coherent group of about eight points at 0.83-0.90e5 across s=9.4-13.4 topped by 1.021e5 at s=10.1 - a climb to twice plateau that is far steeper than the muon curve's own slope over that span (0.60e5 to 0.66e5). Immediately inside it the charge falls away and stays down for nine centimetres: 0.558e5 at s=9.1, 0.31e5 at s=8.2, 0.549e5 at s=8.0, 0.466e5 at s=6.8, 0.53e5 at s=6.3, 0.545e5 at s=5.6, 0.57e5 at s=4.8, 0.47e5 at s=3.9, 0.372e5 at s=3.2, 0.418e5 at s=2.9, and 0.437e5 at s=1.3, with two points at 0.78-0.81e5 at s=1.8-2.0. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot then continue at MIP for nine centimetres, so I moved the pin to rr 9.2, the junction between the 0.83e5 point at s=9.4 and the 0.558e5 point at s=9.1. That makes the last 9.2 cm of fit plus the attached piece the Michel: about 11 cm of electron, which is the right range for a 25-35 MeV Michel and far more plausible than the 1.8 cm / 3.1 MeV object the chain offers. The tag alphabet cannot split a row, so segment 80009 (d 0 to 6.8 cm) lies wholly past the moved pin and is tagged michel, and 80006 (d 6.8 to 140.9 cm) is tagged muon for what most of it is - its first 2.4 cm, from 6.8 to 9.2, are Michel and the row is therefore split. 80001, the four oversized circles on the negative axis at magnitudes 0.4 to 1.9 carrying 0.41e5, 0.345e5, 0.256e5 and 0.204e5, is attached at the shared stop vertex 80002 at a 63 degree kink and is michel too - well below MIP and falling as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature and explicitly not the undershoot. One michel, no gamma, so kind attached. f_meas shows measured matching predicted, with the markers turning dark blue near the pin exactly as the collapse says they should.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test, corroborated by the 3.5 cm wall proximity. Containment ambiguity worth flagging: the rubric gives no d_face threshold for ends inside the volume, and this stop at 3.5 cm sits in that hole - but the verdict does not turn on it, since the profile is flat either way. Terminal 4 cm of near-zero points judged zero-charge fit points, not an overshoot collapse, because the same sprays recur mid-track and nothing lies past the fit end.
evidence: 84 cm of chain, entering 23.9 cm from the nearest y face and ending 3.5 cm from the top y wall (in_fv 0). The dQ/dx profile is flat: the bulk sits on a 4.3-5.0e4 plateau continuously from s=85 all the way in to the last measured point at s~0.5, which is itself at 4.8e4, i.e. plateau level. A handful of green/yellow points at 7.1-9.0e4 appear at s=5-25 and look at first like a ragged Bragg rise, but the identical excursion recurs at s=72-74 (7.6, 6.9, 6.8e4) far from the stop, so it is scatter in the upper envelope, not a terminal rise; the median never leaves the plateau and never approaches the muon reference curve, which climbs from 5.5e4 at s=30 to 1.6e5 at s=0. A cluster of near-zero points (0.6-2.2e4) occupies the last 4 cm, but the same near-zero sprays recur at s=34-36 and s=67-80, straddling the 92001/92002 junction at 68 cm, so they are fit points with no measured charge rather than the Michel-gap collapse - and there is nothing on the far side for the fit to have bridged to (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted clusters). f_meas shows the charge terminating cleanly in all three planes with the only dead V band crossed 15 cm upstream, not at the end. The 3-D azimuths d and e show a single straight amber band with a shallow jog and no arm; the apparent downward spur at the stop in frame c is the near-end-on projection. The only other object is a 2-point 0.6 cm survey speck 48 cm away, unrelated: delta / other. Flat to the last point plus a stop 3.5 cm from the wall reads as an exiting muon.

notes: The michel-vs-delta call on 122002 is the item: tagged delta / other because it is backward at cos_fwd -0.87, chain body-excluded, and only ~2 cm off-axis with no arm visible clear of the body in any azimuth. If it were read as michel the item would become STM_MICHEL / both. No undershoot signature - nothing forward of the stop at high charge.
evidence: 29.5 cm of chain in the bottom corner of the detector, entering 0.3 cm from the lower y face and ending 17.1 cm from the nearest wall (in_fv 1), so the stop is genuinely inside. The profile sits on a 4.5-5.2e4 plateau from s=25 in to s=5 and then lifts over the last 3 cm: 5.5e4 and 5.2e4 at s=2-3, a 6.05e4/6.25e4 pair at s=1-2, and the last point at s=0.3 at 8.2e4, about 1.75x the local plateau and following the shape of the muon curve even though it stays well under it. The rise is short-ranged and I weighed it against a larger local excursion 20 cm back (an orange 1.09e5 point with 8.1/7.2/6.6e4 neighbours at s=18-21) which reads as a delta-ray blob on the body rather than the terminal rise; that competing excess is why this is medium and not high. Past the stop the only thing present is 121001, a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 17.1 cm out at cos_fwd 0.09, drawn in all three azimuths as a lone brown square well off the muon body line and joined to the stop only by the display capture-gamma link, with a clean charge-free gap between - detached and compact, so gamma, not michel. 122002 is the real fork: 10 points, 5.2 cm, 1.9e4 e/cm (0.4 of MIP) sitting 3.9-5.0 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.87, chain-labelled Michel body exclusion. Its d_min/d_max span only 1.1 cm over a 5.2 cm object, so it lies tangentially about 2 cm off the axis at 4 cm behind the stop, and no azimuth shows any arm standing clear of the amber band there - it hugs the body, so delta / other under the off-axis tie-break, which leaves no Michel. f_meas shows charge terminating with no dead band at the stop end in V or W, although U is broadly dead across this track.

notes: Undershoot explicitly considered and rejected: 28005 mean 1.35x this items plateau and a 51 deg kink. Medium rather than high because the arms peak points reach 2.5x MIP, which is higher than a typical electron start, and because the detached-dot call on 126014 is what sets kind=both rather than attached.
evidence: 197.8 cm over two chain segments, entering 0.9 cm from the z face and stopping 13.0 cm from the anode face, comfortably inside. The profile is a textbook rise: a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s=90 in to s=20, lifting to 7-8e4 by s=12, 8.4-9.5e4 at s=5-10, and peaking at 1.145e5 at s=3.5 with 9.9e4 at s=2 and 8.2e4 at s=1 - about 1.9x its own plateau and following the muon curve shape, so the Bragg rise is complete inside the fit. A single 5.2e4 point sits at s=0.3; that is one partial-charge point at the very end, not a sustained collapse, so the pin stays. I checked this hard against the undershoot case because 28005 is a short forward piece the chain calls the Michel with individual points at 1.49e5 and 1.135e5. It fails the undershoot test on the load-bearing clause: its mean is 80580 against this items own 5.5-6.5e4 plateau, i.e. 1.35x MIP, not the four-to-six times the rubric requires, and it leaves at a 51 deg kink (cos_fwd 0.66), not straight ahead. It is a 6-point 3.2 cm arm carrying 18.3 MeV that the display draws in all three azimuths as a distinct blue limb standing clear of the muon body from the stop vertex - that is the ordinary Michel case. 126014 is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 12.3-12.5 cm out at cos_fwd 0.58, essentially along the extension of the Michel arms direction; frames c and e both show ~9 cm of clean white between the end of the arm and it, and f_meas confirms it as an isolated brown dot separated from the track end in all three planes. A 0.2 cm two-point speck across a 9 cm gap is a detached dot, so gamma rather than a piece of the electron, which makes the kind both. No dead channels at the stop in any plane.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test, independently corroborated by the dead U and V bands at the fit end in f_meas.
