notes: LOW confidence and the competing reading matters. Read A (taken): local plateau near the end is 1.5e4 and the last 4 cm rise 3x off it, monotone, to the inner-track maximum - a Bragg rise, so STM_ONLY on a deeply contained end. Read B (rejected, but close): the terminal maximum 4.8e4 is exactly where this same track sits over its far 35 cm where the wire geometry is sane, so the rise may be nothing but the suppression lifting - charge returning to MIP, which would make it THRU. What keeps me from THRU is that the profile is not flat at MIP to the last point, it climbs; what keeps me from high confidence is that this item shows 3x swings from geometry all along the track, so a 3x terminal swing is inside its own noise envelope. I did NOT move the pin (no peak-then-collapse) and this is not the undershoot case (nothing sits past the fit end at all). Record rewritten once before moving on: my first version justified the 189004 tag by its foreign 189xxx key prefix, which is not a discriminator - a genuine capture gamma is a detached cluster and carries a foreign prefix too - so the tag now rests on the faint-far-speck rule instead. Verdict, kind, confidence and every tag are unchanged.
evidence: 147.3 cm chain in two fitted segments (70001 123.3 cm, 70002 24.0 cm at the end). It enters 17.3 cm from the z face and its last point sits 120.6 cm from the nearest face, 239 cm from y and 252 cm from the anode - about as deeply contained as anything in this set - and all three azimuths show the track simply ending at the star with nothing carrying on. The profile is the problem: this track runs at constant x, nearly parallel to the U wires (f_meas squeezes all 147 cm into U channels 3440-3470, right beside the wide hatched dead band at 3420-3440), and its dQ/dx is correspondingly broken - 4-5.3e4 over the far 35 cm nearest the entry, then sagging to a wavy 0.3-2.4e4 with roughly 10 cm periodicity over the whole inner 65 cm (segment means 18922 and 11957, a third of MIP). Against that background the last four centimetres climb monotonically 2.2 -> 2.8 -> 4.0 -> 4.8e4, a factor of about three above the local level and the largest value anywhere in the inner 65 cm, ending exactly at the fit last point. The rubric says to read shape and the rise off the plateau and never an absolute number, and by that test this is a Bragg rise; the chain agrees to the extent that its only reject is plateau_off_mip, not no_bragg and not shape_flat. Nothing past the stop reads as an electron: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters, no arm in any azimuth. Of the two extra rows, 70003 (15 pts, 8.4 cm, 3910 e/cm, 19-24 cm out at cos_fwd -1.0) lies flat ON the muon body line and is drawn as the little green dotted spur off the vertex, so delta / other by the body rule whatever the chain pdg 11 label says. 189004 (4 pts, 2.0 cm, 37135 e/cm, 28.7-30.5 cm out at cos_fwd -0.14) is the faint-far-speck case the rubric legislates separately: 20-60 cm out with cos_fwd near zero, decided by whether it lies on the Michel side. This item has no michel and no arm at all, so there is no decay direction for it to be on, which leaves it an isolated speck in an unrelated direction - delta / other, not a capture gamma. It is roughly perpendicular to the muon direction rather than hugging the body, so I am not calling it a delta on the body line either; it is simply unattributable here.

notes: Flat at MIP to the last point; the fit end coincides with a U dead band, which is the leave-through-a-dead-region case f_meas is there to catch. Neither failure mode: no peak-then-collapse, and nothing sits past the fit end to be an undershoot tip.
evidence: 130.3 cm chain in seven fitted segments, entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 35.9 cm from that same wall and 40.0 cm from the anode face - not at a wall, but not deep either. The dQ/dx is noisy (this track carries a lot of associated activity: four unassigned pdg 11 shower pieces strung along its body, all at cos_fwd -1.0) yet its centre of mass is a 4-5e4 band from s = 130 all the way in, and the last points are 4.9e4 and 4.8e4 - dead on that same band, with the terminal segment 51001 (3 pts, 1.5 cm) averaging 48428 against 46867 for the 46.6 cm segment behind it. There is no rise off the plateau in the last 10-20 cm; the only elevated points near the end are single 8.0e4 and 7.2e4 spikes at s = 4-6 that sit inside the general scatter and are gone by s = 8, and the plotted muon reference curve climbs away above the data untouched. The chain rejects with no_bragg and shape_flat and I agree. f_meas explains where the track went: the fit last point lands exactly on the wide hatched U dead band at channels ~2160-2175 (the amber tip is drawn on top of it), while V and W still have it - so the cluster ends where the U imaging ran out, heading on toward the anode and the z wall. Nothing at the stop reads as decay: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters, and all three azimuths show the track just ending at the star. The five non-chain rows are all delta / other - 51007, 51010, 51013 and 51016 lie flat ON the muon body line (cos_fwd -1.0, 41-84 cm back), and 92017 is a 2-point 0.2 cm survey speck 60.8 cm away whose 92xxx key marks it as belonging to a different cluster entirely (its lone brown vertex square is the isolated marker sitting off the track in b, c and e).

notes: Textbook case: contained stop, full Bragg rise following the muon curve, two capture-gamma dots and no Michel. For 94005 I let off-axis separation outrank the chain Michel body exclusion label as the rubric directs - at 11 cm out and cos_fwd -0.21 it is roughly perpendicular, so about 11 cm clear of the body line rather than hugging it, and it is detached, which makes it a dot rather than delta / other. Neither failure mode present.
evidence: 85.8 cm chain in one fitted segment (52003, 145 pts, mean 56941). It enters exactly at the anode x face (d_face 0.0) and stops 37.0 cm from the z wall, 68 cm from the anode, in_fv 1. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the profile sits on a 4.5-6.5e4 band out beyond s = 20 and then tracks the muon reference curve point for point over the last 15 cm - 6.5e4 at s = 13, 8.0e4 at s = 8, 9.0e4 at s = 5, 1.00e5, 1.12e5, 1.18e5 and 1.23e5 at the last point - a factor of two above its own plateau, the right shape, and topping out just where the rubric says real stoppers top out. This is the one item where the chain agrees: is_stm 1. Two objects sit past the stop, and both are compact detached dots, each two points and 0.3 cm across, each drawn as an isolated marker clear of the amber body in c, d and e and each visible as a genuine isolated blob in all three f_meas planes (times 812 and 848 against the track end at 805), so they are measured charge and not fit artefacts. 93004 sits 17.6 cm out at cos_fwd +0.5 carrying 78784 e/cm and the chain independently calls it a capture gamma of 2.06 MeV; 94005 sits 11.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.21, i.e. essentially sideways, so about 11 cm clear of the muon body line, carrying 15551 e/cm. Neither is an electron: the rubric is explicit that a 0.3 cm two-point speck across a gap of this size is not a 35 MeV electron, and there is no arm of any kind leaving the stop (n_stop_arms 0, no unfitted clusters). So both are gamma, the verdict stays STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL - isolated capture gammas do not promote it - and michel_kind is detached dots.

notes: THRU on the operative test: no rise at the fit end, flat at its own plateau to the last measured point, and the end is 14.8 cm from the anode face it is heading for. Confidence medium rather than high because this track plateau is only about 0.6 of MIP, so its charge scale is suspect, and because the chain does offer two capture gammas forward of the end - the rubric says that if I want to tag gamma on a THRU I should question the verdict, and I did: what settles it is that the last 10-15 cm show no rise at all, not even a suppressed one, and that the largest object past the end is a 96 cm trail that cannot be decay charge. Neither named failure mode: no peak precedes the terminal zero-charge run, so this is not the overshoot, and there is no high-charge tip past the fit end, so it is not the undershoot.
evidence: 86.8 cm chain in one fitted segment (62009, 146 pts, mean 34704 - about 0.6 of MIP). It enters 0.6 cm from the z face and the fit last point sits 14.8 cm from the anode x face, heading that way, so this end is close to a wall. The profile never rises: it sits in a 2.5-5e4 band the whole way, is 4-6e4 around s = 15-25, and comes IN to 2.5-3.7e4 over s = 6-15 before a run of near-zero points at s = 2-5 and a last point back at 2.4-3.0e4. Ignoring the zero-charge fit points as the rubric directs, the end of this track is flat at or slightly below its own plateau, with the muon reference curve climbing away far above it - no Bragg rise of any kind, which is what the chain says too (no_bragg, shape_flat). f_meas shows the stop end clear of the hatched bands in all three planes, so the flat tail is measured rather than lost. What sits past the end argues the same way: C64 is an unfitted 50-point cluster 96.4 cm across with no PR segment, whose nearest point is 16.2 cm from the star at cos_fwd 0.71 and which the c, d and e frames draw as a long sparse trail of faint points running off at a wide angle - far too long and too detached to be a 35 MeV Michel, and at 45 degrees it is not the muon carrying straight on either, so it reads as a separate poorly-imaged track passing nearby. notes: THRU on the operative test: the last measured points are at the same charge as the plateau 40 cm earlier, so the track is running at MIP into its last point. Confidence medium rather than high because this item scatter is wide (1.6e4 to 6e4 at almost every arc length) and there is a sagging, vertex-heavy stretch 10-25 cm back, so the profile is not clean - but nothing in it rises. Neither failure mode: no peak precedes the sag, and nothing sits past the fit end at all.
evidence: 49.2 cm chain in four fitted segments, sitting in the far corner of the detector (y about -300 to -327, z about 30). notes: THRU on the operative test: flat at MIP to the last point. Confidence medium rather than high only because of the 3-6 cm spike discussed above, which is the one reading that could make this a stopper with a short overshoot; I rejected it because the post-spike charge does not collapse and because identical spikes occur mid-track. notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU with no visible continuation, no face within 32 cm and no dead-region exit at the stop - the cluster ends where the imaging runs out, which the rubric says to call THRU rather than escape to UNCLEAR. Competing reading was an overshoot pin move to s~8 with 10001 as the michel; rejected because the s=8-13 bump falls again well before the fit end and never reaches the stopper band. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0).
evidence: 109 cm chain, enters 1.2 cm below the +y wall and the fit ends 32.2 cm from the nearest (y) face, deep inside in x and z. Upscaled ~5x, the profile sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau all the way in from s=100 cm; over the last 20 cm it makes a bump to 7.7-9.2e4 between s=8 and s=13 (one point 1.1e5) and then comes back DOWN to 3.85-6.4e4 over the final 8 cm, hugging the flat electron reference rather than the muon curve, which by s=1-3 is already at 1.0-1.2e5. A bump that rises and falls mid-window is a delta ray, not a Bragg peak: re-origining the pin at s=8 would demand a monotone climb into the 1.2-1.35e5 stopper band over the last centimetres and there is none. The single 1.45e5 point at s=0.7 has four points at 3.85-4.3e4 immediately before it, so it is not a rise; it is also on the chain, and there is no forward high-charge tip, so the undershoot case is out too. The only thing near the end is the 14-point 8.1 cm unassigned cluster 10001 at 1.1e4 e/cm (0.2 MIP), 2.1-5.9 cm out at cos_fwd -0.73, drawn as a faint blue dotted trail leaving the end sideways in all three azimuths; a THRU has no stop to hang michel or gamma on, so it is delta / other. f_meas puts the U and V dead bands 10-30 channels away from the end with W clean there, so a dead-region deficit is not what flattens the last 8 cm. What made it hard: the end is visibly curved and MCS 223 vs range 270 MeV agree, both stopper-like, but the profile is the operative test and it is flat to the last point.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU. The end is 37 cm from the nearest face with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit, so per the rubric the cluster simply ends where the imaging runs out; that is THRU, not UNCLEAR. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0).
evidence: 344 cm dead-straight single-segment track, enters 0.1 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 36.9 cm from the nearest (z) wall, 64 cm from the cathode. The dQ/dx panel upscaled is flat on a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau over its whole length and stays there right through the last 10 cm: the final ten points sit at 4.8-5.5e4 with one 6.3e4 at s=0.5, while the muon reference curve has already climbed to 1.0e5 by s=2 and 1.6e5 at s=0. There is no rise of any kind off the plateau, ragged or otherwise, and the high points at s=18-40 (1.0-1.45e5) are ordinary delta activity far up the body, not a terminal feature. All three 3-D azimuths show a straight untapered track that simply ends, with nothing past the end - no arm, no dot, no widening - and the only other charge in the event is a blob belonging to a different flash which the display keeps hidden. f_meas shows the end at time slice 1487 in mid-range in all three planes with the measured and predicted panels matching and no dead band swallowing the end, so this is not a dead-region exit. Range 791 MeV against MCS 1479 MeV (amb 0.65) is the mismatch expected when a fitted range is only part of the muon.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: the fit stops about 1 cm short - the real stop is at the far end of the 1.3 cm forward tip 33010, whose 1.0-1.54e5 points carry the Bragg peak. pin-rr cannot record a stop past the fit last point, so no pin is set; 33010 is tagged muon rather than michel per the rubric charge clause. Chain reject is shape_flat only, is_stm 0, but the chain excluded the very piece that carries the peak.
evidence: 58 cm track, enters right on the anode x face (d_face 0.0) and the fit ends 24.6 cm from the nearest (z) wall, 252 cm from the y wall and 289 cm from the cathode, so the end is well inside. Range 161.2, dQ/dx 162.5 and MCS 159.3 MeV all agree, which is what a genuine stopper looks like. The profile sits near 5.5e4 out at s=40-58 and climbs modestly to 6.5-7.2e4 over the last 5 cm on the chain itself; the real terminal charge is in the unassigned 3-point 1.3 cm piece 33010 sitting 0.0-0.85 cm straight ahead of the fit end (cos_fwd +0.96), whose two plotted points are at 1.0e5 and 1.54e5 with a row mean of 1.18e5. That is the undershoot pattern exactly: the chain types the piece pdg 11 and offers it as the Michel, but an electron leaves the vertex at or below MIP and 1.0-1.5e5 is two to three times MIP here, which is what a muon looks like in its own last centimetre. So the tip is muon and the true stop is about 1 cm beyond the fit end. All three azimuths show the green flow tip hard against the track end with a clean charge-free field beyond it - no arm, no dot, no speck anywhere in the 60 cm ring - so there is nothing left past the tip to promote this to STM_MICHEL. f_meas has the end at time slice 900 with measured matching predicted and the nearest dead channels in U and V more than 100 channels away, so the end is not a dead-region exit.

notes: The three 43 cm survey clusters are the only real question here; they are clumped in ONE direction on the Michel side rather than scattered around the ring, which is the rubric test for gamma, so kind is both. If they are instead a separate object the record becomes STM_MICHEL / attached with 130007, 130008, 131009 as delta / other. The STM_MICHEL verdict itself is not in doubt. Chain agrees (is_stm 1, Michel 39005, 22.5 MeV).
evidence: 88 cm chain, enters 0.1 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 56.1 cm from that face, 282 cm from the y wall and 122 cm from the z wall, so the stop is deep inside. Upscaled, the profile sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=85 in to s=20, lifts to 6-7e4 by s=12, and runs 8.0-9.5e4 over s=2-8 with a 1.0e5 point at s=1, tracking the shape of the muon curve into the stop; the last chain points are the highest, so there is no terminal collapse and the pin stays put. Leaving that stop is the 16-point 8.9 cm object 39005 at 5.0e4 mean, plotted as a cloud at s=-1 to -10 running 3.5-6.5e4, i.e. at or just below MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle, and 8.9 cm with a 90 deg kink is the right range and topology for a ~22 MeV Michel. The e azimuth shows it as a clean blue arm off the stop vertex at right angles to the muon. Three survey-only clusters (2.9, 7.1 and 0.2 cm at 1.8-2.5e4) sit as one tight clump 43 cm out; from the 3-D centroids that clump is 33 deg off the Michel arm direction and 65-70 deg off the muon body, so it is on the decay side and well clear of the body line: gamma by the far-speck rule. What made it hard is exactly that clump - it carries its own survey vertex squares and could equally be read as a different small object entirely, which would make the kind attached rather than both.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU; U and W both have dead channels right at the stop end, consistent with the muon leaving through a dead region, and the profile shows no Bragg rise anywhere in the last 20 cm. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0).
evidence: 290 cm chain, enters 0.3 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 42.8 cm from the nearest (z) wall. The dQ/dx panel upscaled is flat on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in, and the final 10 cm are 4.0-6.3e4 with several points down at 2-4e4 and one near zero - no lift at all off the plateau while the muon reference has already reached 1.0e5 by s=2. The high 1.0-1.35e5 points at s=20-60 are delta activity well up the body, not a terminal rise. All three azimuths show a dead-straight, untapered track that simply ends at the stop star with an empty field beyond it; the only non-chain object in the whole display is the 4.3 cm 8.7e3 e/cm shower speck 40004 sitting 245 cm away at the entry end, which has nothing to do with this end, so it is delta / other. Range 668 MeV against MCS 1518 MeV (amb 0.77) is the mismatch of a fit that covers only part of the muon. f_meas puts the end at time slice 1590 with the U stop end hard against a hatched dead band at channel 2170-2180 and the W end on the dead line at 10310-10320, so a dead-region exit is the likely destination, but the flat profile settles the verdict on its own.

notes: THRU on two independent grounds: no Bragg rise anywhere in the last 20 cm, and charge that continues collinearly past the fit end. Competing reading is the chain STM_MICHEL with 70007 as the electron; rejected because the stop is 0.8 cm from the y face (in_fv 0, chain reject stop_near_boundary) and the forward pieces are collinear rather than at a kink. Per the THRU tag rule 70007 and 24009 are delta / other, not michel, so the kind is none.
evidence: 90 cm track, enters 0.5 cm from the z face at z=1.3 and runs almost parallel to the y wall while sinking toward it, so the fit ends 0.8 cm from the nearest y face with in_fv 0. The profile upscaled is flat on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau over the whole 90 cm and the last 8 cm of chain sit at 3-5e4, i.e. below their own plateau, with no lift of any kind while the muon reference is already at 1.0e5 by s=2; the only high points (1.3-1.4e5 at s=22-24 and the yellow run at s=25-33) are body deltas 25-30 cm back. Charge does continue past the fit end - the unassigned 7.6 cm piece 24009 at cos_fwd +1.0 spanning 0.0-7.0 cm and the chain 2.5 cm Michel candidate 70007 at cos_fwd +0.99 spanning 5.8-7.3 cm - and all three azimuths show it as a straight dotted trail carrying on in the same direction past the stop star to two survey vertices, not an arm at an angle. Those pieces sit at 2.8e4 and 3.6e4, below the 5e4 plateau; f_meas explains that, with the whole end region at U global rank 95-110 sitting on a hatched dead band and the V end on dead lines at 3815-3830, so charge collection at this edge is degraded. Flat profile, an end 0.8 cm from a face and collinear charge beyond it all say through-goer. The hard part is that the chain offers a 4.6 MeV Michel here and the forward charge really is sub-MIP rather than MIP; but a Michel needs a stop inside the volume and there is none, and a decay electron would not lie dead straight along the muon direction. The 10.8 cm shower 24006 is 2.2 cm off the body line 8-16 cm back, so it is body activity.

notes: OVERSHOOT: pin moved back 7.0 cm from the fit last point. Row 52015 is split - the first 22 cm from the far end are muon, the last 7 cm are the collapsed bridge into the electron - and is tagged muon for the majority per the rubric single-segment rule. Competing reading is THRU with the whole 8-30 cm band written off as overlapping charge, but the last points sit BELOW the plateau rather than on it, so the profile is not flat to the last point. Chain rejects with no_bragg and shape_flat, which is what its shape test does when the terminal charge collapses.
evidence: 187 cm chain, enters right on the anode x face and the fit ends 134.8 cm from that face, 249 cm from the y wall and 148 cm from the z wall - as deeply contained as a stop gets. Blown up around the origin the profile does the overshoot thing: from the 5.0e4 plateau out beyond s=40 it climbs into a band of 1.0-1.65e5 points between s=8 and s=30, and then falls monotonically and without a break from 1.42e5 at s=13.9 through 1.21e5 at s=7.8, 9.7e4 and 7.8e4 around s=7, 6.25e4 at s=4, 5.0e4 at s=2.6, 4.1e4 at s=0.9 and 1.5-3.4e4 at the last two points. That is a sustained collapse over the final 7 cm ending at 0.3 of the plateau, not one low last point, and it is exactly the low-charge bridge the owner describes: a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot fall back through MIP for seven centimetres. f_meas backs the geometry, putting the dense dark deposit at time slice 990-1005 in all three planes several cm before the fit end while the last stretch of fitted track carries almost nothing. So the pin goes to 7.0 cm, the collapse falls inside the single chain segment 52015 which is therefore tagged muon for the 22 of its 30 cm that are muon with the last 7 cm being electron, and the 4.2 cm 2.6e4 object 52011 sitting at 0-3.7 cm from the fit end is the visible piece of that Michel. 52007 and 52010 are shower fragments 27-52 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. on the body line: delta / other. What makes it hard is the width of the high-charge band - 20 cm above 1.0e5 is far too long for a real Bragg peak, and there are two coexisting point populations there (7-9e4 greens as well as the 1.0-1.65e5 reds), so some of that charge is an overlapping spray rather than the muon itself; the pin position is therefore uncertain by several cm even though the collapse is not.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU on a 20 cm stub; per the rubric the six chain gamma rows and the five survey rows are all delta / other because a through-goer has no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so the kind is none. Competing reading is FRAG_THRU - the bundle holds 23-62 cm of disconnected charge forward of the end - but nothing there is collinear with this track, so I did not call it a visible fragment. Chain agrees on the verdict direction (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) while still claiming 19.2 MeV of capture gammas past a stop it does not believe in.
evidence: Only 20 cm of chain, 34 points: it enters 0.6 cm from the z face at z=1.4 and the fit ends 13.8 cm from that same face, heading into the detector at about 42 deg to z. The profile upscaled is flat on 4.0-5.5e4 for the whole 20 cm and then droops rather than rises, the last two or three points landing at 1.5-3.0e4, while the muon reference is at 1.0e5 by s=2 and 6.5e4 even at s=20. A muon with the 74.8 MeV that the range fit assigns would have to climb hard over these last 20 cm and it does nothing of the kind, so this end is not a stop. All the other charge in the display is disconnected and off-axis: six chain-claimed capture gammas of 0.2-5.9 cm at 23-28 cm out (74 deg off the muon direction for the nearest) and five survey-only clusters at 42-62 cm, two of them substantial 16-20 cm arms that form their own kinked pair 42-44 deg off this direction. Nothing lines up with the muon and there is a 23 cm charge-free gap between the fit end and the nearest of them. f_meas shows the amber stub at time slice 1105-1152 sitting on a dashed dead U column near channel 3037 with all the blob charge at time 990-1040, well separated. Flat to the last point with no continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the end: THRU, with the object ending where the imaging ran out. Hard part: the bundle is visibly broken into many pieces, so this 20 cm stub may well be a fragment of something longer.

notes: Falling-into-the-last-point THRU, most likely leaving through the dead-channel confluence at the end (U band edge, V band, W dead line all at the stop). Competing reading is a shallow overshoot with the pin at s=6 giving STM_ONLY; rejected because the collapse is only to about 1.1x the plateau rather than the far-below-plateau bridge the rubric describes, and because the 6.75e4 peak is not a Bragg peak. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0); dQ/dx KE 84 vs range KE 143 MeV also flags the depressed charge.
evidence: 49 cm track living in the far corner of the detector: it enters 0.4 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 18.2 cm from the y wall, 29.5 cm from the x face and 36.2 cm from the z wall. Its own plateau is unusually low, 3.5-5.0e4 out at s=15-50, and f_meas explains why - the track sits on a hatched dead V band at channel 4355-4375 along its whole length, runs between two dead U bands at 478-500 and 522-545, and its stop end lands on a W dead line at 8420, so all three planes are compromised. Upscaled the profile lifts modestly from that 4.2e4 plateau to 6.5-6.75e4 around s=6-7, tracking about 1e4 under the muon curve, and then falls back monotonically through 5.8, 5.5, 5.35, 5.05 to 4.7e4 at the last point, exactly where the reference curve climbs to 1.0e5 and above. So there is no rise at the fit end - the charge is falling into it - and the peak that does exist is only 6.75e4, nowhere near the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches here. All four 3-D frames show a clean, slightly kinked track with a star and a vertex square at the end and absolutely nothing else drawn in the whole display: no arm, no dot, no speck, the object table holding only the two muon chain rows. Hard part: the end is at a dead-channel confluence in all three planes, so a Bragg peak could in principle have been eaten; but the last 6 cm decline rather than merely flatten, and the pre-decline peak is far too low, so the through-goer reading is the one the evidence supports.

notes: Flat-and-falling to the last point: THRU even though the end is 51 cm from the nearest face, which is exactly the case the rubric says to call THRU rather than UNCLEAR. No visible continuation and no clear dead-region exit; the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0).
evidence: 89 cm nearly straight track, enters 2.0 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 51.5 cm from the nearest (z) wall, 90 cm from the x face and 139 cm from the y wall, so this is a deeply contained end - and it is still a through-goer. Upscaled, the profile runs 5.0-5.5e4 from s=90 in to about s=20 and then, over the last 20 cm, steps DOWN to a tight 3.5-4.2e4 band and stays there flat to the very last point, at the exact place the muon reference climbs from 6e4 through 1.0e5 to 1.6e5. Falling into the end is the opposite of a Bragg rise, ragged or otherwise; the only high points, 1.28e5 and 1.43e5 at s=72-75 and the 8.5-9.5e4 greens at s=25-85, are body deltas far up the track. Every 3-D azimuth shows a clean untapered track ending at the stop star with a completely empty field beyond - the object table holds just the muon chain row and one 2-point 0.6 cm speck 20.6 cm back at cos_fwd -0.93, which is on the muon body line and is flagged gamma body exclusion by the chain, so delta / other. f_meas has the end at time slice 1597 with measured matching predicted and the dead lines in U at 700, V at 4465 and W at 8375-8410 near but not swallowing it. MCS 3674 MeV at ambiguity 1.00 against a 229 MeV range is the signature of a fit that only sees part of a much longer track.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU with the end 76 cm from the nearest face and no visible continuation; the cluster ends where the imaging ran out, possibly across the W dead line at 10315. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0).
evidence: 162 cm chain, enters 1.1 cm from the z face at z=1.9 and the fit ends 75.8 cm from the x face, 105 cm from the z wall and 200 cm from the y wall - a deeply contained end that is still a through-goer. Blown up around the origin the profile is flat on 4.5-5.5e4 from s=100 all the way in, the last ten points sit at 4.2-5.2e4 and the final two at 3.2-4.5e4, so it is flat and if anything sagging at the fit end while the muon reference has already passed 1.0e5 by s=2 and heads for 1.6e5. The 1.0-1.15e5 orange points at s=18 and s=33-37 and the 8-9e4 greens from s=25 out are body deltas, nowhere near the end. All four 3-D azimuths show a long clean track terminating at the stop star with a completely empty field past it: no arm, no dot, no speck. Everything else drawn - the two extra chain segments 39004 and 39011 and the four pdg 11 shower clusters 39005, 39006, 39007 and 39012, all at 5.8e3-1.2e4 e/cm - sits 118-148 cm away at the ENTRY end at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. on the body line as far from this stop as it is possible to be, so they are delta / other and say nothing about it. f_meas has the end at time slice about 1495 with measured matching predicted and a W dead line at 10315 close to that end. Range 384 MeV against MCS 824 MeV (amb 0.78) is the usual mismatch of a fit that only covers part of the muon.

notes: MESSY: EM blob broken into many pieces, no coherent spine, so all 43 rows are delta / other and the kind is none. There is a small amber stub beside the stop star but it connects to nothing, and the nearest structure is a dense knot of shower fragments 60-75 cm away at cos_fwd -0.95. No pin move - there is no profile to move it on.
evidence: This is not one track. The display draws 43 objects in a roughly 80 cm ball - 12 so-called muon chain segments of 4.7 to 23.7 cm, two michel rows, and 29 unassigned rows of which a dozen are pdg 11 shower fragments and a dozen more are two-point survey specks - and every 3-D azimuth is a field of thirty-odd brown vertex squares over a blue speckle cloud with a dense EM knot at one end and no spine anywhere. The chain segments themselves give it away: they carry 7.9e3, 8.2e3, 9.4e3, 9.7e3, 1.1e4, 1.3e4, 1.4e4, 1.6e4 e/cm, a fifth to a third of MIP, which is shower charge and not a minimum-ionizing muon, and the only two rows above 4e4 are 41032 and 41066, isolated 5-7 cm pieces 50-59 cm out. The dQ/dx panel matches: no plateau at all, just a band of points between zero and 2e4 from s=0 to s=90 with an unrelated 6.5e4-1.0e5 column at s=-15 and orange specks at s=-28, so there is no profile to test for a Bragg rise and nothing that could be called a stop. The chain itself rejects on profile_sparse as well as shape_flat, its dQ/dx energy is 126 MeV against 310 by range, and MCS returns 39.9 MeV at ambiguity 1.00 - three independent signs that the fit has no coherent object underneath it. Per the convention every row is tagged delta / other, because a MESSY item has no identified stop for michel or gamma to mean anything against.

notes: Called STM_MICHEL against the chain own verdict is_stm=0 with reject_names no_bragg / shape_flat: the chain shape test is presumably spoiled by the near-zero stretch 2-12 cm back from the stop, but the last points are high and there is real attached decay charge. Pin left at the fit end. Range KE 329.1 MeV and MCS 320.3 MeV agree, which is independent support for a stopper. Medium confidence because the terminal profile is not a clean monotone rise and I had to weigh a dead-channel/reco-damage reading of the dip against an overshoot reading.
evidence: 136.5 cm chain, enters 1.6 cm from the z face at (267,154,297) and stops deep at (201,78,226), 72.5 cm from the nearest wall, so containment is not in doubt. The profile sits on a 5.3e4 plateau from s=100 down to s=40, shows a high-charge patch of chain points at 1.0-1.36e5 around s=22-30 (with ordinary 5-8e4 points at the same s, so a local delta patch on the body rather than a Bragg), falls back to plateau at s=13-20, then a near-zero stretch over s=2-12 and finally two points at 1.04e5 and 1.4e5 at s=0-1, the highest of the terminal region and right on the muon reference curve. I read the near-zero stretch as the fitted segment 56015 (9 points, 4.6 cm, segment-average dqdx 6406) and as reconstruction damage rather than a bridged gap, because the piece distal to it carries 1.0-1.4e5 e/cm, which is muon-like and far above anything an electron start can do; a W-plane dead band near channel 11890 crosses the track back from the stop and is a candidate explanation for the dip, but I cannot establish the track angle in W from these frames. Past the stop the d and e azimuths show a short amber arm leaving sideways: 56008 (13 pts, 7.4 cm, 27518 e/cm, d 2.2-4.4), 56017 (5 pts, 2.5 cm, 12603, d 3.6-4.4, cos_fwd 0.85) and 216020 (12 pts, 6.5 cm, 38179, d 4.0-5.2, cos_fwd 0.11), all at or below MIP and effectively attached at d_min 2.2 cm, which is the ordinary Michel case and not the undershoot (that needs several times MIP in the forward tip). The measured-minus-predicted panels leave a bright residual blob exactly at the track end in all three planes, so the terminal charge is real and under-predicted. One 0.4 cm two-point speck 215019 at 19.3 cm, 89247 e/cm, matched to the grey cross at s=-19 on the panel: it is displaced almost purely in -y from the stop, the same side as the Michel arm, so gamma by the faint-far-speck rule, and that single call is what makes the kind both rather than attached. 56011 sits 122 cm back at cos_fwd -0.96, on the body line at the entry end: delta / other.

notes: Agrees with the chain own is_stm=0 / no_bragg. Hardest call of the item was overshoot-STM versus THRU; the tiebreak was that the high patch at s=10-17 coexists with normal-charge points at the same s, plus the MCS/range disagreement. Medium confidence for that reason. No pin move (a pin cannot be moved on a THRU anyway).
evidence: 105.4 cm of chain entering 0.1 cm from the x face at (-340,-265,3) and ending at (-254,-238,45), 44.2 cm from the nearest z face, so the fit end is nominally deep in the volume. The profile is a clean 5.3-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 down to s=30, and then it goes the wrong way: from s=13 in to the origin it falls monotonically through 6e4, 5.5e4, 4.5e4, 4.2e4, 2.9e4, 2.3e4 to 1.9e4 and 0.6e4 at the last two points. There is no rise off the plateau anywhere in the last 20 cm, and a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot decline like that, so by the operative test this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. I weighed the overshoot reading, because five chain points at s=10-17 sit at 0.97-1.18e5, well above the reference curve, which superficially looks like a peak several cm before the fit end followed by a collapse. I rejected it because ordinary 5.5-8e4 chain points sit at exactly the same arc lengths, so that patch is a localised delta blob riding on the muon rather than the whole track lifting, and because MCS gives 454.4 MeV against 262.8 MeV from range (amb 0.89) - a muon that much stiffer than 105 cm of range cannot have stopped here. A further near-zero stretch of about twenty points at s=18-27, visible as the dark navy patch about 20 cm back from the star in the d and e azimuths, is reconstruction damage on a track that runs nearly parallel to the U wires (the U measured panel spans only ten channels over 120 time slices). Past the fit end 91026 sits 19.3 cm away at cos_fwd 0.96 carrying 54739 e/cm, i.e. a MIP-level two-point fragment straight along the continuing direction, which is charge continuing past the fit end and independently means THRU. 92027 (34.2 cm, 70 deg off) and 93028 (36.5 cm, 75 deg off, and in a different direction from 92027) are scattered specks. Per the rubric the four fitted chain segments are tagged muon and everything else, including the chain two claimed capture gammas, is delta / other with kind none, because gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop this track does not have. Nothing is attached at the fit end in any of the three azimuths.

notes: Chain says is_stm=0 with reject shape_flat, which I disagree with: the rise is textbook. The flat verdict is probably driven by the same sub-centimetre low-charge tip that made me consider a pin move. Range KE 795.1 MeV versus MCS 526.0 MeV (amb 0.07) is a 34 percent disagreement that argues mildly the other way, and it plus the terminal dip is why this is medium and not high. Pin left at the fit end.
evidence: 345.2 cm of chain, entering 10.8 cm from the y face at (-32,-326,232) and ending at (-329,-197,207), 11.0 cm from the x face - close to that wall but inside it, and the Bragg settles the question anyway. This is the cleanest rise in my chunk: the plateau sits at 5.5-6.5e4 out to s=100, and from about s=25 the chain climbs monotonically along the muon reference curve through 6.5e4 at s=15, 8.8-9.8e4 at s=8-10, 1.02-1.05e5 at s=5-6, 1.18e5 at s=3 and 1.48e5 at s=3.5, which is the top of the panel region and exactly the shape the reference curve has. The only blemish is three points in the last 1.2 cm at 4.3e4, 2.15e4 and 1.0e4, and the U, V and W measured panels do show a genuinely dark low-charge spot at the very tip. I considered moving the pin back to the peak, and decided against it: the rubric signature is a sustained collapse over several cm into a piece the fit then bridges, and here the drop covers about one centimetre and there is nothing on the far side of it - the whole object table has five rows and no piece anywhere beyond 3 cm from the stop. Past the stop there is no arm and no dot: the c, d and e azimuths show the amber band simply terminating at the vertex square with only a few faint image specks around it. All four are well clear of the muon body line (the 26.6 cm one is 25 cm off the fit axis, so I overrode the chain gamma body exclusion label). C58 is a 205-point, 108.8 cm object 47-60 cm out, the big diffuse cloud in the upper right of the 3-D frames - a different object entirely, so delta / other. Note 161014 carries 9.4e4 e/cm and cos_fwd 0.85, which looks like the undershoot tip until you see it is 14.7 cm out across an empty gap and only 2 points, not a couple of cm of muon.

notes: Chain reject shape_flat and no-daughter overruled: n_stop_arms 1 and the arm is attached at d_min 0.0 with MIP-level charge.
evidence: 439 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 119.1 cm from the nearest wall, about as deeply contained as this set gets. On the 6x stop crop the profile holds a 5.4-6.0e4 plateau from s=100 in to s=20, then climbs: 6.5-7.5e4 at s=8-12, 7.8-9.0e4 at s=5-6 and 8.0-8.6e4 at s=1-3, sitting on or just above the muon reference curve the whole way in, with the last point at 7.5e4. The peak only reaches 8.6e4 rather than the 1.2e5 the best stoppers here show, and there is scatter down to 4.7e4 at s=12, but the shape is a rise off its own plateau over the last 10-15 cm and the last point does not collapse, so the pin stays at the fit end and this is not the overshoot case. Leaving the star in all three azimuths there is one attached arm: three unassigned pieces the chain types pdg 11 shower, 63005 (13 pts, 7.5 cm, d_min 0.0), 63003 (14 pts, 7.9 cm, d_min 1.75) and 63001 (20 pts, 11.2 cm, d_min 3.26 to d_max 10.58), running out to about 11 cm at cos_fwd 0.35-0.59, i.e. roughly 55 deg off the muon direction, and drawn as a fuzzy shower-like spray rather than a straight stub. Its real charge is 5.99e4 e/cm on 63001, i.e. at MIP, and a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle and 11 cm is the right range for a ~25 MeV electron; the two low-dqdx pieces (6.1e3 and 7.2e3) are the fit-point stretch with little measured charge and I discounted them rather than reading them as a collapse. Nothing here matches the undershoot tip: no piece has cos_fwd above 0.85 and none carries anywhere near 1e5. f_meas puts the U, V and W dead channels 20 or more channels off the stop, so the arm charge is real and not a dead-region artefact. No other drawn object.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit at the stop - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. THRU on the profile alone per the rubric, not UNCLEAR.
evidence: 289.5 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 44.2 cm from the nearest y wall, so it is nominally contained, but the profile settles it the other way. On the 6x stop crop the chain sits at 5.5-6.5e4 continuously from s=100 all the way in to the last point at s=0.3, which is 5.5e4 - identical to the plateau 90 cm back. There is no climb off the plateau at all in the last 10-20 cm: the muon reference curve is at 8e4 by s=3 and 1.6e5 at the origin while the data never leaves MIP. The only structure anywhere is a burst to 1.0-1.4e5 at s=32-40 (delta activity mid-track, matched by the orange and blue pieces the 3-D frames draw sitting on the body there) and a dip to 2.1-4.0e4 at s=20-22, both far from the stop. A stopping muon cannot end at its own MIP plateau, so this is a through-goer; the chain agrees, rejecting it with no_bragg and shape_flat, and the range-vs-MCS KE disagreement is extreme (667 vs 1732 MeV, amb 0.67). All three azimuths show the amber/green band running straight into the star with completely empty space beyond it - no arm, no dots, no continuation - and f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at time slice 1590 with the nearest U/V/W dead bands 25 or more channels to the side, so it did not leave through a dead region either. Every non-chain object drawn (a 2-point pdg 211 speck at 273 cm, a 10-point shower piece at 41 cm, and the two survey pieces at 45-46 cm) has cos_fwd -0.99 or -1.0 and lies on the muon body line well back from the end, so all are delta / other.

notes: Flat (indeed sub-MIP) to the last point with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit at the stop end. THRU on the profile alone. Considered MESSY and rejected it: the spine is coherent and linear, it is just heavily fragmented and charge-starved.
evidence: 155.9 cm chain entering 12.2 cm from the z face and ending 103.7 cm from the nearest wall, so containment is not what decides it. The whole object is low-charge: the 4x panel shows the chain sitting at 1.4-4.7e4 for its entire length with long runs of near-zero fit points (s=7-12, 18-21, 56-73, 78-85), a handful of real points at 6.6e4-1.24e5 in one burst at s=30-40, and nothing else above the 5.4e4 reference plateau. In the last 5 cm the points are 1.4e4, 3.0e4, 3.8e4 and 4.2-4.7e4 - flat, and below MIP rather than above it, against a muon curve that is at 8e4 by s=3 and 1.6e5 at the origin. There is no climb of any kind at the fit end, so this is a through-goer by the operative test; the chain rejects it three ways (no_bragg, shape_flat, vertex_hadron) and its range KE (371 MeV) disagrees badly with dQ/dx (196) and MCS (162). The three azimuths show a thin, wiggly but genuinely coherent spine - not an EM blob, so not MESSY - broken into many short segments with a brown vertex square every few cm, running into the star with completely empty space past it. All fifteen drawn objects, including the eight unassigned pdg 11 shower pieces, have cos_fwd between -0.96 and -1.0 and unit vectors from the stop within a few degrees of the body direction, i.e. they lie strung out along the muon body from 8 to 128 cm back, so all the non-chain rows are delta / other. f_meas explains part of the low charge: in V the track crosses dead wires at 6770, 6820 and 6890, and the measured panels are correspondingly dark, but a real Bragg peak would still show as a rise and none is there.

notes: The only genuinely arguable row is 54008: michel (past the charge maximum, at MIP) vs muon (chain-typed pdg 13, forward at cos_fwd 0.89). The verdict and michel_kind are the same under either reading.
evidence: 160 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 83.2 cm from the nearest wall. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: on the 6x stop crop the profile lies on the muon reference curve for its whole approach - 4.5e4 plateau at s=60-100, 5.5e4 at s=20-30, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=8-15, 8.5-9.3e4 at s=3-6, 9.9e4 at s=2 - and tops out at 1.31e5 (s=1.3) and 1.42e5 (s=0.7), i.e. the maximum charge sits at the fit last point with no collapse behind it, so the pin stays put. Past the stop the three azimuths show a diffuse light-blue spray, not an amber band, running forward about 11 cm at a visible kink: 54008 (7 pts, 3.6 cm, d_min 0.0 to 3.46, cos_fwd 0.89, 6.5e4 e/cm) then 54004 (15 pts, 8.5 cm, 3.46 to 10.92 cm, cos_fwd 0.79, 5.2e4 e/cm). Both sit at 1.0-1.2 times the local MIP plateau, and a muon that has just delivered 1.42e5 at its Bragg peak cannot carry on at MIP for another 11 cm, so the spray is a second particle: 11 cm at MIP is the right range for a ~25 MeV Michel, and inside 10 cm of the stop the rubric says direction does not discriminate anyway. I tagged 54008 michel even though the chain groups it with the muon and types it pdg 13, on the grounds that it lies past the charge maximum; I explicitly weighed the undershoot reading (that 54008 is the muon last 3.5 cm and the fit stopped short) and rejected it because the undershoot requires the tip to carry 0.9-1.2e5, several times MIP, and 6.5e4 is not that, while the 1.42e5 peak is behind the pin, not in the tip. 146006 is a 5-point, 2.4 cm, 8.8e3 e/cm speck 30.1 cm out at cos_fwd 0.65, isolated, on the same forward side as the Michel arm and well clear of the muon body line: a detached capture gamma, so kind is both. f_meas shows real measured charge in the arm in U and V with the nearest dead bands 15-20 channels off the stop.

notes: The medium is entirely about the two specks: they are 2 points each and the chain excluded both (one as survey-only, one as gamma body exclusion). Reading them as delta / other instead would make the kind none; I went gamma because both are far off the body line, detached, and mutually aligned to 27 deg.
evidence: 299.5 cm chain entering 16.9 cm from the z face and stopping 87.4 cm from the nearest (x) wall. The Bragg is unambiguous: on the 6x stop crop the profile holds 5.4e4 from s=40 to s=100, lifts to 6.5e4 by s=15 and 7.8e4 by s=8, then 9.8e4 at s=3-5, 1.12-1.18e5 at s=4-8, 1.24e5 at s=3 and 1.32e5 at the last point, hugging the muon reference curve the whole way in with the maximum at the fit end and no collapse behind it, so the pin stays. The three range/dQ-dx/MCS energies agree to within 20 percent (690/818/653 MeV, amb 0.01), which is what a real stopper looks like. Nothing is attached at the stop: all three azimuths show the amber band running into the star with clean empty space beyond, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The only other drawn objects are two 2-point, 0.3 cm specks at 33.4 cm (92012, 3.3e4 e/cm, cos_fwd -0.20) and 42.8 cm (91011, 6.1e4 e/cm, cos_fwd 0.27). Neither is anywhere near the muon body line - their unit vectors from the stop are (-0.14,0.92,-0.37) and (-0.44,0.90,0.00), roughly perpendicular to the body, and 92012 sits only 6.7 cm behind the stop plane against 32.7 cm of transverse offset - and they are only 27 degrees apart from each other, i.e. on the same side rather than scattered around the ring, which is the rubric criterion for calling faint far specks gamma rather than delta. So detached dots, and the verdict stays STM_ONLY because isolated capture-gamma-like pieces do not promote it. f_meas shows single dead wires close to the stop in U (ch 285-295) and W (ch 8175), but V is clean there and shows nothing past time slice 262, and a track leaving through a dead region would not have produced this Bragg peak.

notes: Genuinely cannot tell. Competing readings: (a) STM_ONLY - the three-point terminal climb to 3.8x the local plateau follows the muon-curve shape when read as a ratio; (b) THRU or plain junk - the plateau is at 0.37 MIP because U and V are both dead across the object, and a 62 cm track with a 25 cm charge void in the middle is not a trustworthy dQ/dx measurement. I did not pick because the deciding evidence (the charge) is the thing that is broken. Not UNCLEAR to dodge THRU: the profile is not flat to the last point.
evidence: Short 61.5 cm chain, only 55 chain points and 99 image points, entering 0.4 cm from the cathode and ending 31.7 cm from the nearest z wall. Two things make this object unreadable rather than merely hard. First, f_meas shows the track sitting inside wide hatched dead bands in BOTH induction planes - U ch 1025-1035 is inside the 970-1035 block and V ch 4775-4790 is inside the 4765-4790 block - so only W carries real charge, and the chain plateau is correspondingly at 1-2.7e4, about 0.37 of MIP, which is exactly what the chain flags with plateau_off_mip (range KE 169 MeV against dQ/dx KE 49 MeV). Second, the object is not continuous: the 3-D azimuths show two disconnected amber pieces about 18 cm each separated by roughly 25 cm of nothing, with only the two body-line vertex squares of 98001 in between, and the dQ/dx panel shows the same hole - chain points at s=0-24 and again at s=50-62 with nothing between. On the last few centimetres there is a real, monotonic three-point climb, 3.1e4 at s=2 then 5.0e4, 6.9e4 and 7.6e4 at s=1, 0.5 and 0, i.e. 3.8 times the local plateau, and those three points sit visibly detached from the dense band. Taken as a ratio to its own plateau that shape is not far off the muon curve (1.55 vs 1.8 at s=2, 2.5 vs 2.2 at s=1), which is the STM_ONLY reading; but with two of three planes dead across the whole object, a 25 cm void in the middle of a 62 cm track and a three-point rise, I do not think the charge is trustworthy enough to call a Bragg peak, and calling it flat would be equally false since it plainly is not. Nothing is drawn past the stop in any azimuth (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0), so there is no decay evidence either way; 98001 is a 7-point, 3.8 cm piece 24-28 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, i.e. on the muon body, so delta / other.

notes: Flat to within 2.5 cm of the last point, then a terminal decline with no preceding peak. No visible continuation past the stop and no dead-region exit - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. THRU on the profile per the rubric.
evidence: 90.5 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 24.2 cm from the nearest z wall. The profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau from s=90 all the way in to s=3, with normal scatter (4.4-6.5e4) and one delta burst to 8.4e4-1.36e5 around s=11-22 well away from the end. Over the last 2.5 cm it does not rise, it declines monotonically: 4.8e4 at s=2.5, 4.4e4, 3.9e4, then 2.6e4 and 2.55e4 at the last two points, i.e. down to 0.46 of its own MIP plateau, against a muon curve that is at 1.0e5 by s=2. I checked this against the overshoot signature and it does not fit: that pattern needs a peak several cm before the fit end followed by the collapse, and here there is no peak at all - the highest point inside 10 cm is 7.9e4 at s=6.5, only 1.4 times plateau - so moving the pin back would only put the stop on a plain MIP point, which is not a stop. That leaves no Bragg rise anywhere at the fit end, so this is a through-goer; the terminal decline reads as the fit running a couple of centimetres past the end of the real charge. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) and its MCS momentum is wildly higher than range (2539 vs 231 MeV KE, amb 0.97), which is what a straight high-momentum through-goer does. All three azimuths show the amber selection band ending at the star with completely empty space beyond, while the green chain continues in the opposite (entry) direction to the frame edge; f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at time slice 1590 with V and W clear of dead wires there. The only non-chain object is 100006, a 3-point 1.5 cm survey speck 54 cm back at cos_fwd -0.98, on the muon body: delta / other.

notes: Hardest item in my chunk. Three readings weighed: (a) STM_ONLY with the pin unmoved - recorded, the profile does rise off plateau over the last 10-15 cm and the last point is 1.4x plateau; (b) overshoot with the pin at rr 3.5 - rejected because the post-peak points carry MORE charge than the plateau, whereas the bridge mechanism requires charge-poor interpolated points, and because there is no Michel past any moved pin; (c) THRU with the s=3.5-7.1 band read as a delta blob on the body - not excluded, and the reason for the low confidence.
evidence: Straight 60.8 cm chain (KE 168 MeV by range, matching dQ/dx exactly) entering 0.5 cm from the z face and ending 35.6 cm from the nearest z wall; the three azimuths show a clean single amber spine with no arm, no dots and only a one-centimetre wisp of image points just past the star. The dQ/dx is the whole story and it is awkward. Off a 4.4-7.3e4 plateau the profile climbs through 6.7e4 at s=12 and 8.9e4 at s=8, then runs a high band over s=3.5-7.1 - 1.14e5 (7.1), 1.28e5 (6.6), 1.03e5 (5.8), 1.24e5 (4.6), 1.37e5 (4.2), 9.7e4 (3.5) - and then falls back over the last 3 cm to 6.8e4 (2.8), 5.8e4 (2.0), 6.3e4 (1.5), 7.05e4 (1.2), 7.4e4 (0). So there is a real rise off its own plateau in the last 10-15 cm, peaking in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach, and the last point is still 1.4 times plateau - not flat to the last point, so not a through-goer - but the peak sits 4 cm short of the fit end instead of at it. I tested that against the overshoot signature and rejected it: the mechanism there is the fit bridging a charge-free gap between the muon stop and the Michel, so the bridged points must be charge-POOR, and these five points are at 1.2-1.4 times the plateau, i.e. more charge than the muon body carries, not less; there is also no Michel on the far side of any moved pin - no kink, no separate cluster, no dots at the stop - so the pin move would be an attribution with nothing to attribute. The pin therefore stays at the fit end and I read the s=3.5-7.1 excursion as a late, ragged Bragg rise with a localized deposit on top (it sits 1.4-1.8 times ABOVE the muon reference curve there, which a clean Bragg does not do - it tracks the curve in), and the low last 3 cm as end-of-track scatter. Low confidence because the alternative that the excursion is simply a delta blob on the body, leaving no Bragg at all and making this THRU, is not excluded by anything I can see. 124001 is a 4-point, 2.0 cm, 5.9e4 e/cm speck 29.6 cm out at cos_fwd -0.02, essentially perpendicular to the muon axis, isolated and far clear of the body line: a detached gamma, hence detached dots. f_meas shows no dead wire within about ten channels of the stop in any plane, so neither the excursion nor the terminal fall is a dead-region artefact.

notes: Flat to the last point. It does end 14 cm from the z wall, which is the likely exit, but the verdict rests on the flat profile, not on the face distance.
evidence: 69.8 cm chain entering 0.8 cm from the z face and ending 14.0 cm from the same z wall, so it is close to a face, but the profile decides it without needing that. On the 6x stop crop the chain sits on a 4.3-5.5e4 band from s=70 all the way in, and the last two centimetres are 3.1e4, 4.25e4, 5.9e4, 6.25e4 and 6.3e4 - the same band, no lift at all, against a muon reference curve that is at 1.0e5 by s=2 and 1.6e5 at the origin. The largest values anywhere inside 20 cm are 6.9e4 at s=7-8 and 7.4e4 at s=14, i.e. 1.3-1.4 times plateau and no closer to the end than 7 cm, so there is no rise off the plateau in the last 10-20 cm and nothing resembling the muon curve shape. A stopping muon cannot finish at MIP, so this is a through-goer; the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) and its MCS momentum runs well above range (KE 273 vs 187 MeV, amb 0.81). All three azimuths show a straight amber spine ending at the star with empty space beyond it and the entry markers at the far end; the deep dips to 0.5-2.5e4 at s=15-18 and s=58-70 are runs of near-zero fit points on the body, not structure at the end. f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at time slice 1595 with V (ch 5915) and W (ch 9975) both clear of their nearest dead wires, though in U it runs between dead wires at 2010 and 2050. Only two objects are drawn and both are fitted chain segments, so both are muon and there is nothing to attribute past the stop.

notes: Flat-to-the-end call under the rubric's flat-profile clause: no face, no visible continuation, no dead-region exit - the cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out. What made it medium rather than high is the terminal decline: the last 3 cm are ~0.5 of the plateau, which is more than the 20-30 percent scatter the rubric calls ordinary, but a fall with no preceding rise is not the overshoot signature and does not make it a stopper.
evidence: 103.5 cm chain in two segments, enters 0.1 cm from the z face and the fit ends 39.3 cm from the nearest wall (279 cm from the cathode, 57.6 cm from the anode face), so containment is not the issue. The dQ/dx panel, upscaled 8x over the last 30 cm, shows a broad scatter band from 2.5e4 to 8e4 sitting on a ~5.2e4 plateau all the way along the 100 cm of positive s; the muon reference curve rises through 5.8e4 at s=20, 6.5e4 at s=10 and 7.5e4 at s=5, and the data never climb above it near the end. There is a mild cluster of 7.0-8.6e4 points at s=5-8, but comparable and larger excursions sit at s=15 (7.6e4), s=28-31 (0.9-1.04e5) and s=57 (1.07e5), so the s=5-8 group is ordinary delta-ray scatter, not a localised Bragg peak. The last 3 cm carry only low points, 2.3-4.6e4, i.e. below the plateau and far below the muon curve, so this is not a peak-then-collapse overshoot either: there is no peak to collapse from. Nothing is drawn past the stop at all (chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0); 58007 is a pdg-11-typed 4.4 cm speck 33 cm back sitting 0.6 cm off the muon line, i.e. body activity, and 141010/143011 are 3-4 cm survey specks 47-48 cm back and 17-19 cm off the line, a different object. f_meas shows measured and predicted agreeing along the whole track with no dead-channel bundle crossing the stop end in U or W (the V dead lines run the full time range and touch both ends equally). Range KE 258.9 MeV against MCS 695.9 MeV (amb 0.78) is the further inconsistency expected of a straight through-goer rather than a 259 MeV stopper.

notes: Flat-profile THRU: a 487 MeV range-KE muon cannot end at MIP. There is no visible continuation past the fit end, but the stop is 5.1 cm from a y seam and sits on the drawn region's own time boundary, so the cluster ending there is unsurprising.
evidence: 209.3 cm of chain in three fitted segments, entering 0.3 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 86 cm from the nearest wall but only 5.1 cm from the y seam at the stop. The dQ/dx panel upscaled 4x is a textbook flat MIP plateau: 4.0-5.5e4 from s=100 all the way in to s=0, with the usual delta-ray spikes (9.5e4 at s=21, 1.0e5 at s=52, 8.5-9.0e4 at s=46 and 86-92) scattered along the body and no gradient at all. Over the last 20 cm the points sit at 3.5-5.2e4, i.e. on and slightly below the plateau, while the muon reference curve there climbs from 5.8e4 through 6.5e4 to 1.6e5; the data go the other way. The one structure near the end is a run of 1.5-2.5e4 points at s=14-22, which the three 3-D azimuths show to be a genuine charge gap in the cluster about 15 cm back from the fit end, not a Bragg feature. Nothing whatever is drawn past the stop - the dQ/dx negative axis is empty and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The two unassigned rows are both pdg-11-typed body specks on the muon line (37003, 5.4 cm, 77 cm back, 2.0 cm off the line; 37006, 1.1 cm, 160 cm back, 3.7 cm off), so delta / other. f_meas shows measured and predicted matching with the residual panels blank along the track; the stop end coincides with a horizontal boundary line that runs across all three planes at time slice ~1543, which is where the drawn region ends.

notes: Flat-profile THRU and the fit end is only 9.5 cm from the z wall, so the exit is also geometrically available. Charge scale caveat: the whole track is at ~0.5 MIP, so absolute charge here is not trustworthy; the call rests on the shape being flat-to-falling, not on the level. The three azimuths also show a lavender-coloured continuation past the last vertex at the far (entry) end, outside the fitted chain, which is another sign this is a longer object than the fit.
evidence: 126.3 cm chain in five fitted segments running almost along the drift, entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 9.5 cm from the z wall - so the fit end is a hair from a face and the projections show the track pointing at it. The dQ/dx panel upscaled 4x has the whole track sitting well below MIP, a 2-3e4 band with excursions to 4-5e4, which is what the chain's own plateau_off_mip flag is reacting to; the segment means in the table (2.0-3.4e4) say the same. Over the last 20 cm the points run 0.9e4, 1.9e4, 2.4-3.1e4 with a few at 4.0-4.8e4, i.e. flat-to-falling on the track's own depressed plateau, while the muon reference curve climbs from 6.0e4 at s=15 to 1.6e5 at s=0; the only points near 6-7e4 are at s=16-18, 16 cm back from the end, and the big 0.8-1.15e5 spikes are all at s=55-90, deltas far up the body. There is no rise of any kind approaching the fit end. Nothing is drawn past the stop: the dQ/dx negative axis is empty and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The single unassigned row 43013 is a 6.2 cm pdg-11-typed piece 62 cm back and 0.8 cm off the muon line, i.e. hugging the body, so delta / other by the off-axis rule regardless of the chain's shower label. f_meas shows the track as a near-vertical trace in all three planes, sitting immediately beside dead-channel bands in U and V, with measured and predicted agreeing.

notes: THRU on the shape: flat to the last point with no terminal rise. Marked medium, not high, because the absolute charge on this object is not usable - the whole chain is at 0.2 MIP and f_meas shows wide dead-channel bands crossing the stop region in all three planes. The relative test still applies (dead channels suppress the stretch uniformly and a Bragg peak would still appear as a local rise) and there is none, but a reader should know the level is broken. Range KE 299.7 MeV against dQ/dx KE 75.6 MeV and MCS 100.9 MeV is the same story.
evidence: 122.7 cm chain entering 4.7 cm from the anode face and ending 59.9 cm from the nearest face, so the fit end is deeply contained and containment is not what decides this. The dQ/dx panel at 4x is unlike any of the others in the chunk: the entire chain sits at 0.3-1.3e4 e/cm, roughly a fifth of the 5.4e4 MIP asymptote, oscillating with no trend, with a single broad bump to 2.8e4 at s=48-58 and a return to 0.6e4 by s=62; the segment means agree (48007 7095, 48006 7743, 48003 19981). Over the last 15 cm the points run 0.4-1.3e4, i.e. flat on the track's own floor, while the muon curve climbs to 1.6e5 - there is no rise of any kind, ragged or otherwise. The one thing at the stop is 48006, a fitted 4.2 cm pdg-13 stub straight ahead (cos_fwd +0.99, d_max 4.1 cm), visible in all three azimuths as a short green tick just past the star; its 7.7e3 e/cm is at the track's own plateau, about a seventh of MIP, so it is emphatically not the high-charge forward tip of the undershoot case - it is more chain. f_meas explains the depressed charge: the last stretch of the track runs at nearly constant time slice across W and crosses a wide hatched dead-channel band at W 10080-10100 and a second at 10120, with further wide dead bands at V 5950-5970 and U 2160-2175 right where the stop sits, so a large part of this object's charge is simply not collected. The two unassigned rows are far off the muon line - 166005 is a 0.4 cm two-point speck 34 cm out at 32 cm perpendicular (the grey + at s=-33 on the panel), and 48004 is a 41 cm pdg-4-typed object 35 cm off the line, a different object entirely - so both are delta / other.

notes: Flat-profile THRU on a deeply contained end (110 cm from every face). Range KE 453.7 MeV against MCS 1124.4 MeV (amb 0.84) is the corroboration: the track is far too straight for a 450 MeV muon. The fit end also sits just short of the drawn region's own time boundary, so there is a mundane reason the cluster stops where it does.
evidence: 194.1 cm of chain in four fitted segments, dead straight - every object in the table sits within 2.4 cm of the entry-to-stop chord - entering 0.3 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 110.2 cm from the nearest face, so this is the rubric's contained-but-not-stopping case and containment settles nothing. The dQ/dx panel at 4x, and a 9x crop of the last 25 cm, show a clean 5.5e4 MIP plateau from s=194 in to s=0 with no gradient: the core band is 4.5-6.0e4 at s=0-10, 5.5-7.3e4 at s=17-25 and 5-6e4 for the rest, exactly on the muon curve's asymptote, and the last four points sit at 3.2-3.6e4, i.e. below the plateau rather than above it. The high points near the end - 9.1-9.2e4 at s=4-5 and a tight vertical stack of 0.98-1.27e5 at s=12-15 - are delta rays, not a Bragg rise: identical stacks reaching 1.35-1.56e5 sit at s=56 and s=97, far up the body, and the s=12-15 stack is a single-position spread rather than a trend. Against the muon curve, which is at 6.0e4 by s=20 and 1.6e5 at s=0, the data fall away instead of climbing. Nothing at all is drawn past the stop: the dQ/dx negative axis is empty, the three azimuths show the point cloud simply stopping at the star with no arm, dot or speck beyond it, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The three unassigned rows are all pdg-11-typed body specks 57-180 cm back at 0.1-2.3 cm off the line - 16009 (6.1 cm, 59 cm back), 16003 (8.4 cm, 172 cm back) and 16006 (5.1 cm, 179 cm back) - so delta / other. f_meas shows measured and predicted matching, with the stop sitting about ten time slices short of the horizontal boundary that runs across all three planes at slice ~1595.

notes: Hard call, marked medium. The competing reading is THRU: the dQ/dx sawtooths five times along the track and the ramp peak at s=50 reaches 7.9e4, essentially equal to the 8.0e4 near the stop, so the terminal rise is not obviously larger than the artifact elsewhere. I went with STM_ONLY because the rubric's test is the shape over the last 10-20 cm, where the envelope climbs monotonically along the muon curve, because nothing continues past the fit end in any azimuth, because the stop is 84 cm from every face, and because MCS and range agree. A reader who weights the equal s=50 peak more heavily would call this THRU.
evidence: 112.4 cm in a single fitted chain segment, entering 1.9 cm from the z face and ending 83.8 cm from the nearest face (93.6 cm in z, 206.9 cm in y), deeply contained. This track is isochronous: entry x 256.9 and stop x 256.1, so it runs entirely in y-z at fixed drift, and f_meas shows it as a single horizontal line at time slice ~1420 in all three planes. That geometry is what the chain's lone plateau_off_mip flag is reacting to and it makes the dQ/dx level unreliable - the profile breaks into repeated ramps that fall to near zero. Reading the upper envelope of those ramps over the last 20 cm, measured off a 9x crop: ~3.2e4 at s=15, 5.6e4 at s=11, 8.0e4 at s=2.7, i.e. a ragged climb that tracks about 85-90 percent of the muon reference curve (6.4e4 at s=11, 8.7e4 at s=2.7) all the way in, with the last two points at 5.6-5.9e4, about 30 percent below the peak, which the rubric calls ordinary end scatter rather than a collapse. Note the chain did NOT raise no_bragg or shape_flat here, unlike every other item in this chunk; its only complaint is the level. Nothing at all sits past the stop: the dQ/dx negative axis is empty, the three azimuths show the point cloud ending cleanly at the star with no arm, dot or speck beyond, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. The single unassigned row 34001 is a 30 cm pdg-11-typed piece 93-98 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0 and 7.3 cm off the chord, body activity far up the track, so delta / other. Range KE 277.7 MeV and MCS 248.8 MeV agree here, unlike the through-goers in this chunk where MCS ran two to three times range.

notes: This is a disagreement with the chain, which tags the item is_stm 1. The competing reading, and the reason for medium rather than high, is that range KE 436.3, dQ/dx KE 355.0 and MCS 475.8 MeV all agree here, which is unusual among the through-goers in this chunk and is what a real stopper looks like in the energy columns. evidence: 186.1 cm of chain in eight fitted segments, entering 0.3 cm from the z face and ending 63.1 cm from the nearest (y) wall, contained. This is the one item in the chunk the chain accepts: is_stm 1, reject_names just STM. I do not see the Bragg it needs. On a 9x crop of the last 25 cm the profile is flat: the core band runs 4.5-5.2e4 from s=15 all the way in to s=0, with the last point at 5.9e4 and only two points reaching 6.5-6.9e4 at s=11-12; the muon reference curve is at 6.6e4 at s=12, 8.0e4 at s=4 and 1.6e5 at s=0, so the data leave it behind rather than following it up. Crucially the far plateau at s=57-100 carries points of exactly the same height (4.0-6.0e4, several at 5.8-6.0e4), so the near-stop band is not elevated relative to the track's own body, and the last 4 cm of a genuine 436 MeV stopper should be at 1.0-1.35e5 rather than 5-6e4. There is no peak-then-collapse either: the 6.9e4 at s=12 falls only to ~5.0e4 by s=0, a 27 percent sag rather than the sustained drop to 0.15-0.5 of MIP the overshoot signature needs. The big charge stack at s=46-48 (0.7-1.2e5) is a delta 47 cm up the body. Nothing is drawn past the stop: the three azimuths show the amber selection band running out to the star with clean space beyond it, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. The only near object is 177041, a two-point 0.8 cm speck at 12.1 cm from the stop measured on the local tangent - 10.5 cm BACKWARD and 6.0 cm off the muon line, which the chain itself calls Michel body exclusion; it is behind the stop so the gamma rule (past the stop) cannot claim it, it is outside the michel rule's 10 cm isotropic radius, and at 6 cm off a body 12 cm away it reads as body activity, so delta / other. The other five unassigned rows are pdg-11-typed pieces 96-162 cm back at 0.7-2.6 cm off the line. f_meas shows measured matching predicted, with the stop about twenty time slices short of the horizontal boundary at slice ~1595.

notes: The one hard tag is 210052. Reading it as a second capture gamma is defensible - it is 31.5 cm clear of the body, detached and compact, and the rubric says off-axis separation outranks the chain's own exclusion label - and it would not change michel_kind, which is detached dots either way. I kept it delta / other because it sits 14.6 cm behind the stop and the gamma rule asks for past the stop, and because at 7 points and 6.1e4 e/cm it is denser than a 0.7 MeV de-excitation gamma. Also noted: MCS gives 740.6 MeV against 1402.7 MeV from range, but the Bragg peak is decisive and MCS is biased on a track that is slowing down over 6 m.
evidence: 623.8 cm of chain in fourteen fitted segments, entering 0.8 cm from the x face and ending 42.2 cm from the nearest (y) wall, contained. This is the only unambiguous Bragg in the chunk. On a 12x crop of the last 12 cm the profile leaves the 5.4e4 plateau at about s=20 and climbs continuously along the muon reference curve - 6.5-7.5e4 at s=15-18, 8.2-8.8e4 at s=9-12, 9.7-1.09e5 at s=6-9, 1.05-1.14e5 at s=4-6, 1.21-1.29e5 at s=2-3 - hugging the curve the whole way and topping out at 1.29e5, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band the rubric says real stoppers reach. The two very last points, inside the final centimetre, sit at 6.2e4 and 3.7e4; that is a sharp drop but it spans well under 1 cm rather than the several-centimetre sustained collapse the overshoot signature needs, and there is nothing past the stop for the fit to have bridged to, so I left the pin at the fit's last point. Nothing is attached at the stop: the three azimuths show the point cloud ending at the star with clean space beyond, and the chain reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, so this is not a Michel item. Two compact blobs sit off in the ring. 211053 is a two-point 0.3 cm speck 28.6 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.06, i.e. 28.6 cm straight out to the side and only 1.7 cm behind the stop plane, completely clear of the muon body; f_meas shows it as an isolated brown dot 25-45 channels off the track with no charge trail back to it. That is the rubric's gamma - isolated, compact, clear of the body, within 60 cm - and the chain independently calls it a 0.74 MeV capture gamma, so michel_kind is detached dots. 210052 is a seven-point 3.7 cm piece at 34.8 cm, which decomposes to 14.6 cm BEHIND the stop and 31.5 cm off the muon line, and at 117 degrees from 211053; being behind the stop it fails the gamma rule's past-the-stop clause, so delta / other. 59023 is an 11.5 cm pdg-11-typed piece 359 cm back on the body. Caveat on the charge: f_meas shows a wide hatched dead band sitting on the track's own V channels near the stop, though the rise is far too large and too well shaped to be an artefact of it.

notes: Flat-to-falling THRU on a 28 cm stub. Range KE is only 95.1 MeV and MCS was not computed (0 segments), so the energy columns say nothing here. The whole object lives within 14 cm of the anode face with its far end on the window's first time slice, so there is an obvious mundane reason the cluster is this short; I did not call FRAG because no larger object is actually visible in any frame.
evidence: A short object: only 28.3 cm of chain in three fitted segments, entering 2.0 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 14.2 cm from that same face and 15.5 cm from the z wall, i.e. tucked into a corner. The segment means in the object table say the same thing in the same order - 65717 for the far segment 13011, 62969 for 13013, 39212 for 13001 at the stop - so the charge falls by a factor of two into the fit end while the muon reference curve climbs from 6.0e4 at s=15 to 1.6e5 at s=0. That is the opposite of a Bragg rise, and it is not the overshoot signature either: there is no peak to collapse from, the decline is monotone from the far end, and nothing sits past the stop for the fit to have bridged to. All three drawn objects are chain segments; there is no unassigned row at all, the dQ/dx negative axis is empty, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. The three azimuths show a single clean 28 cm spine with the star at one end and the entry triangle at the other and nothing beyond either. f_meas shows the object confined to time slices 0-50 with its entry end sitting at slice 0, the very start of the drawn window, and dead-channel bands well away from it in U (665, 705, 850-880), V (4655) and W (8750).

notes: Flat-to-falling THRU. The competing reading is that the 1.28e5 point at s=3 is a Bragg peak and the last 3 cm are an overshoot collapse; I rejected it because the high charge is a single-position three-point stack of the same kind that appears twice more up the body, because there is no rise leading into it over s=5-20, and because nothing sits past the stop for the fit to have bridged to. The only high charge near the end is a three-point vertical stack at s=2-4 (8.85e4, 1.14e5, 1.28e5) sitting at one arc position; that is a delta ray, and the plot carries an identical stack at s=41-46 (0.90-1.31e5) and another at s=66 (1.08e5) far up the body, so it is a recurring feature of this track rather than a terminal rise. A Bragg would be a trend over the last 10-20 cm and there is none: between the stack and the stop the charge falls, and between s=7 and s=12 there is a run of 1.0-1.9e4 points which the azimuths show as a dark violet (low-dQ/dx turbo) stretch of the point cloud about 5-14 cm back from the star, a charge gap rather than a rise.
