notes: Textbook STM_MICHEL; the only judgement was checking it is not the undershoot, and the arm's MIP-level charge over 15.5 cm settles that in the Michel's favour.
evidence: 306.5 cm of chain in two fitted segments, entering 0.3 cm from the z face and stopping 64.6 cm from the nearest (y) wall, well contained. The dQ/dx panel is the cleanest stopper in the chunk: the profile sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=300 in to about s=25, then climbs continuously and hugs the muon reference curve the whole way - 5.5-6.9e4 at s=12-20, 7.5-8.7e4 at s=3-8, 1.00-1.05e5 at s=1.5-5 and 1.11-1.13e5 at the last chain points around s=0.5-1, i.e. right in the 1.2e5 band real stoppers reach. There is no peak-then-collapse: the rise runs into the fit's last point rather than dying several centimetres short, so I left the pin alone. Past the stop there is an unmistakable second particle: 62011, a 15.5 cm 27-point arm that leaves the very vertex where the chain ends (d_min 0.0) at cos_fwd +0.80, i.e. a 44 degree kink, and all three azimuths show it as a distinct blue arm branching off the amber muon and running out about 15 cm with a slight curl. Its dQ/dx is 51228 e/cm - at MIP - and its points on the negative axis run 4.0-6.8e4 with a single 1.02e5 spike at 14 cm out. That is decisive against the undershoot case: the undershoot needs a ~2 cm tip at 0.9-1.2e5, several times MIP, and this is a 15.5 cm arm AT MIP, which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel. A muon at its own 1.13e5 Bragg peak cannot carry on at 5e4, so the arm is a second particle, and 15.5 cm and 38.8 MeV are the right scale for a Michel electron. Nothing else is drawn: no dots, no capture gamma in the ring, and the only other row 62012 is a 6.0 cm chain segment 291-296 cm back on the body. f_meas shows measured matching predicted with both the muon and the arm reproduced, and no dead-channel band at the stop in any plane. Range KE 705.6, dQ/dx KE 694.3 and MCS 673.4 MeV (amb 0.01) all agree.

notes: THRU on the shape, but marked medium because this object's charge is largely uncollected - the whole thing sits in a wide dead-channel band in W - and it is broken into six or seven fragments. The call does not rest on the absolute level: it rests on the last 10 cm being the lowest-charge stretch of the entire track, which no stopping muon produces. If the owner wants a category for objects whose imaging is too damaged to judge, this is a candidate; the rubric's instruction not to reach for UNCLEAR in place of a flat-profile THRU is what kept me on THRU.
evidence: 166.9 cm of chain in four fitted segments, but the geometry is pathological: entry z 290.2 and stop z 291.8, so the whole object lies in a 2 cm slab of z about 7 cm from the z end wall (entry d_face 8.2, stop d_face 6.6) and runs 141 cm along x, i.e. almost straight down the drift direction, and the stop is also 7.9 cm from a y seam. f_meas shows the consequence: in W the entire object sits inside a wide hatched dead-channel band at 10805-10830, and in U it hugs the edge of an even wider band at 2600-2645. The dQ/dx panel at 4x is correspondingly broken - every point on the whole 167 cm lies between 0.5e4 and 5.0e4, a tenth to a bit under a MIP, arranged in smooth humps (a 5.0e4 arc at s=60-75, a 4.3e4 hump at s=26-35, a 2.2e4 hump at s=15-20) that look like a wire-geometry artefact rather than physics. Whatever the level, the shape answers the question: the last 10 cm are the LOWEST charge anywhere on the plot, a flat 0.5-1.4e4 trough running into s=0, while the muon curve climbs to 1.6e5; there is no rise, ragged or otherwise, and no peak to collapse from, so neither fit-failure mode applies. The three azimuths show the object as six or seven separated fragments strung along one rough line - a short amber stub carrying the star, then gaps, then blue and teal pieces out to the right - consistent with a real track whose charge is mostly missing rather than with an EM blob, so I did not call MESSY. Nothing reads as decay activity: 42013 is a 7.2 cm 13-point piece at the stop but backward (cos_fwd -0.90) carrying 3150 e/cm, essentially nothing, and 181016 is a 1.5 cm four-point survey speck 46 cm forward and 26 cm off the line; on a through-goer both are delta / other by rule. Range KE 394.5 MeV against dQ/dx KE 168.1 and MCS 245.4 MeV.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit -- calling THRU on the flat profile alone, per the rubric. reject_names here is shape_flat only (no_bragg did not fire), which is the one thing that gave me pause; the picture is unambiguous.
evidence: 85.5 cm of chain, entering 0.1 cm from the anode face (|x| 339.8 of 339.9) and ending 71.7 cm from the nearest wall, 268 cm from the cathode, so the end is deep in the volume. Upscaled 4x, the dQ/dx profile is flat: the far half (s 60-86 cm) sits at 4.0-5.5e4 and the last 20 cm sits at the same 4.5e4 median with point-to-point scatter 3-7e4; the two final points at s<1 are the LOWEST of the whole run (3.1e4), the opposite of a Bragg rise, and the profile never climbs off its own plateau or follows the muon reference curve down to s=0. Segment means agree exactly (53002 terminal 45630 vs 53001 upstream 45171). A muon at its Bragg peak cannot end at MIP, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out; nothing continues past the star in any 3-D azimuth and there is no dead channel at the end in U, V or W (f_meas shows the gaps well clear of the track). The 13-point pdg-11 spray (53003) sits 18-22 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. on the body line at the 53001/53002 junction, and the 4-point survey speck 272004 is 36 cm out at cos_fwd -0.64; on a THRU both are delta / other by rule.

notes: THRU called on the flat profile alone -- no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the end. The competing reading is that the 1.3e5 pair at s~6 is the true Bragg peak and the fit overshot by 6 cm; I rejected it because the post-spike charge stays AT the plateau instead of collapsing, and because the same spike height recurs three more times along the track far from any end.
evidence: 267.5 cm chain, entering 0.5 cm from a face at the top (y 335.9) and ending 103.1 cm from the nearest wall in y, so the end is well inside. At 8x on the last 30 cm the profile is flat: s 8-30 cm sits on a 4.5-6.5e4 plateau and the last 4 cm sits at 3.4-6.2e4, i.e. the same plateau, with the final point at 6.2e4 (about 1.2x plateau) and no climb along the muon reference curve. The one thing that could be read as a peak is a two-point spike at 1.27 and 1.34e5 at s about 5.5-6 cm, but it is 2 cm wide with plateau charge on BOTH sides of it, and the same track carries identical isolated spikes at 1.03e5 (s 20), 1.04e5 (s 68) and 1.26e5 (s 81) -- a delta-ray population on a 2.7 m muon, not a Bragg peak. I also checked it against the overshoot signature and it fails: the points after the spike sit at 0.7-1.3 of the local plateau, not the 0.15-0.5 collapse the fit-bridge produces. The deep dip to 1e4 at s 40-46 is the low-charge pair 57003/57005 (mean 12390 and 37891) 40 cm back, not at the end. Nothing continues past the star in any of the three azimuths and f_meas shows the U, V and W dead bands well clear of the track, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. 57012 (9 points, pdg 11 shower) is 23-24 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the body line.

notes: Hardest item so far, hence medium. Competing reading I weighed and rejected: the profile peaks at 1.52e5 near s 30 and the thirteen points at s 20-26 sit at 5.2-9.7e4, a factor 1.6 below that branch, which could be read as the muon stopping at s about 27 with a 7 cm Michel arm leaving it at MIP -- I would then have pinned at 27.5. I rejected it because no azimuth shows a kink or any transverse offset for such an arm, the 5.2-9.7e4 spread is a factor 1.9 of scatter which the rubric calls normal, the points there are at the ordinary 0.6 cm spacing on the fitted body, and the rubric prescribes the segment junction when the fit bridges a void. Also arguable: the far blob is compact (3.3 cm) across a clean 16 cm gap, which by the attachment tiebreak reads as a capture gamma and would give STM_ONLY / detached dots.
evidence: 167 cm, entering 3.2 cm from a face and running inward to a fit end 54.9 cm from the nearest wall. The profile is a genuine Bragg branch and not a flat one: 5.0e4 beyond s 80, 5.5-6e4 at s 60, 7-8e4 at s 45, 9-10e4 at s 40, and 1.0-1.5e5 over s 27-40 with the maximum 1.52e5 near s 30, about 2.8x the track own plateau and following the muon curve shape, so this is a stopper. The fit end is not where it stopped. Below s 20 the charge collapses hard -- 4.7e4, 4.0e4, 2.3e4, 0.5e4, 0.2e4 -- and the panel is then EMPTY from s 17 down to s 4, with the last five fit points at s 0-3.3 carrying 0.9-5.6e4. All three 3-D azimuths show why: the imaged cloud ends at a flow vertex and the pin sits in free space about 16 cm further on beside a small separate blob, with nothing in between; f_meas shows the same in raw hits, the track ending near time slice 1450 in U, V and W with two or three isolated bright hits near 1400 in all three planes. So segment 60004 (10 points over 19.2 cm, mean 17892 = 0.34 of the plateau, sparse at 1.9 cm per point against 0.6 elsewhere) is the interpolated bridge the rubric describes, and the pin belongs at the 60005/60004 junction, 18.06 cm, which is where the imaged charge ends and the void begins. I tag 60004 michel as the decay-side segment; its row is split, about 14 cm of empty bridge plus a compact 3.3 cm charge blob at the far end. 60005 is 140 cm and is tagged muon; its last few centimetres before the junction sag to 5.2-9.7e4, which I read as charge degrading into the gap.

notes: THRU on the flat profile alone: no visible continuation, the end is 80 cm from any face and there is no dead-region exit. Nothing here was close.

notes: Medium, not high, for two reasons: the last 4 cm interleaves 3.4e4 points with 1.2e5 points, which took a 9x zoom to resolve into scatter rather than a collapse; and 81019 is a 10.5 cm 19-point object at MIP, which is Michel-sized, so the only thing making it a gamma rather than an electron is the 28 cm clean gap between it and the stop. notes: THRU on the flat profile alone: no visible continuation past the fit end, 48.7 cm from the nearest face and no dead-region exit there. The cluster ended where the imaging ran out.
evidence: 118.2 cm, entering 3.4 cm from the near z wall and ending 48.7 cm from it, so the fit end is inside the volume. evidence: Short object: a 47 cm chain of 137.6 MeV that enters in the corner, 0.2 cm from the z face and 2.1 cm from the anode x face, and whose fit ends 28.9 cm from the z wall. The Bragg rise is unambiguous and clean: 4.0-5.5e4 at s=40-47, 4.5-7.0e4 at s=20-35, 6.5-8.3e4 at s=10-20, 7.8-9.4e4 at s=2.5-5, and 7.6e4 and 1.01e5 at the last two fitted points, tracking the solid muon curve the whole way. The interest is what sits past the fit end. Object 39009 is five points over 2.4 cm with d_min 0.00, d_max 2.18 and cos_fwd +0.92, and on the dQ/dx panel its points include 1.03e5 and 1.115e5 about one centimetre out, the highest charge anywhere on this object and higher than the muon chain reaches at its own last point. The chain calls it the Michel core, pdg 11, with a 21 degree kink. That is the undershoot signature: a two-centimetre piece straight ahead in the 0.9-1.2e5 band cannot be an electron first centimetre, which should be at or below MIP, and the 6x zoom on c_3d_stop and e_3d_stop confirms it is essentially collinear, running on from the star to the next vertex square along the incoming direction with only a slight bend. So 39009 is the muon tip and the true stop is at its far vertex, about 2.2 cm past the fit end. Past that true stop, object 39007, ten points over 2.4 cm spanning d 2.16-4.59 at cos_fwd +0.23, turns roughly ninety degrees out of the muon line in both zoomed azimuths and its charge falls from 6.4e4 to 2.0e4, below MIP and dropping as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature. So there is decay activity past the corrected stop and this is STM_MICHEL, not STM_ONLY. f_meas has measured and predicted matching with no dead band on the stop in U or V, the nearest in W being about 15 channels beyond the end. The remaining object 39006, five points over 2.5 cm at 37-39 cm back with cos_fwd -1.00 and 0.69e4 e/cm, is body activity on the muon line: delta / other.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs about 6.5 cm past the true stop. Peak 9.1e4-1.22e5 over s=7-12, above the reference curve, then a sustained collapse to 1.8-3.4e4 across s=1.5-6.1. Pin set to 6.5; the junction is only readable to about plus or minus 1.5 cm because the chain has a single fitted segment here so there is no segment boundary to align to, and one 7.85e4 point at s=6.4 interleaves with the collapsed points. Row 51023 spans the corrected stop and is tagged muon for its 42 cm majority; its last 6.5 cm is the bridge, and the separate michel rows carry the kind so nothing is lost. 132021 is the one judgement call: forward specks at 20-27 cm are gammas on the Michel side, but 132021 at 34.9 cm and cos_fwd -0.53 points elsewhere, so delta / other.
evidence: 54.6 cm chain of 154.4 MeV, enters 0.6 cm from the y face and the fit ends 30.8 cm from the y wall. This is an overshoot with a very strong Bragg peak. Read at 5.5x, the profile climbs off a 5.5e4 plateau through 6.5-8.0e4 at s=13-20 to a seven-point peak of 9.1e4, 9.7e4, 9.75e4, 1.03e5, 1.05e5, 1.07e5, 1.12e5 and 1.22e5 spread over s=7 to s=12, which is above the solid muon reference curve there, not merely near it. It then collapses: six points at 1.8e4, 2.2e4, 2.2e4, 2.6e4, 3.2e4 and 3.4e4 across s=1.5 to 6.1, a third to six tenths of the plateau sustained over five centimetres, before three points at 4.6-5.25e4 at the fit end itself. Matching the peak heights against the reference curve puts the true stop at s of about 6.5-7.5, so I set the pin at 6.5 and the last seven centimetres of the fit are the bridge across the gap. Everything forward of the fit end is then decay charge: 51022 is a 1.8 cm stub at cos_fwd +0.94 carrying 4.6e4, below MIP so it is not the undershoot tip, then 51015 is 6.8 cm at cos_fwd +0.52, 51012 a speck at +0.37 and 51016 8.8 cm at cos_fwd +0.31, a cascade running out to 15 cm from the fit end and about 22 cm from the corrected stop, which is the right range for a Michel of a few tens of MeV. All three azimuths show that cascade leaving the stop upward and slightly forward, well off the incoming muon line, with the flow vertex squares strung along it. Note the census trap: none of 51022, 51015, 51012 or 51016 appears on the dQ/dx panel at all despite totalling 34 points, so the panel is not the census here. Further out sit four compact detached specks, 128017 at 19.9 cm, 131020 at 23.0 cm, 129018 at 24.6 cm and 130019 at 27.2 cm, all at cos_fwd between +0.22 and +0.51, that is all in the same forward direction as the Michel arm and clear of the muon body: these read as gammas, and 131020 is the one the chain itself calls a 4.90 MeV capture gamma. The remaining speck 132021, two points at 34.9 cm with cos_fwd -0.53, sits off in an unrelated direction away from the arm, so by the scattered-direction rule it is delta / other. The chain rejects this object as no_bragg and shape_flat, which the peak at 1.22e5 contradicts; the flat shape it is measuring is the seven centimetres of bridge the fit added past the real stop. f_meas shows a wide dead block in U at channels 2420-2445 but it lies on the entry side, and the stop at U 2487 has measured and predicted agreeing.

notes: Flat, low, drift-aligned profile with no terminal rise, so THRU even though the fit end is 45.5 cm from the nearest face. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). Charge quality is poor throughout because the track is nearly parallel to the drift axis and hugs a W dead channel, but the test is a relative rise and there is none. No pin move: no peak, so nothing to collapse from.
evidence: 194.7 cm chain, enters 1.7 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 45.5 cm from the z wall. The track runs almost entirely along the drift direction, from x 338 to x 161 with only 17 cm of z travel, and f_meas shows the consequence: in all three planes it is a near-vertical band covering hundreds of time ticks over about ten channels, and in W it hugs a dead channel at 10030 along its whole length. That is why every charge number here is low, with segment medians of 3.05e4, 2.45e4, 2.12e4 and 3.38e4 against a 5.4e4 reference asymptote, and why the chain quotes 455 MeV from range but only 265 MeV from dQ/dx. Even so the Bragg test is answerable, because a real peak would still show as a factor of two or three relative rise over the last 10-20 cm. There is none. The profile is a broad 0.5-4e4 scatter with periodic dips almost to zero at s=5, 50, 65 and 83, and over the last five centimetres it reads 6.4e4 and 4.1e4 right at the fit end, then 3.1e4, 2.7e4 and 0.3e4 going back, indistinguishable from the band it carries at s=20, 40 and 90. Nothing tracks the solid muon curve, which is at 1.6e5 by s=1 and 8.5e4 by s=10, and the terminal 70 cm segment averages 3.05e4 against 3.38e4 for the 87 cm behind it, that is flat or slightly falling. All three azimuths show a bare amber-banded spine that simply ends at the star with no arm, fan or dot past it, and the object table lists only the four fitted chain segments and nothing else. f_meas has measured and predicted agreeing and the charge stopping cleanly at time slice 1590, with no dead band crossing the end in U or V. Flat to the last point is enough on its own, so THRU, and all four rows are fitted chain segments and take muon.

notes: THRU on both legs: no Bragg rise, and a faint collinear trail of image points carrying about six centimetres past the fit end in all three azimuths. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). The five-point 1.0-1.14e5 cluster at s=10-12 is a hot spot, matched by two more like it further up the same track, not a terminal peak, so no pin move.
evidence: 324 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the z face and the fit ends 37.6 cm from the z wall. No Bragg rise. The bulk of the profile over the last 9 cm reads 2.55e4, 2.8e4, 3.4e4, 3.5e4, 3.6e4, 4.15e4, 4.3e4, 4.3e4, 4.45e4, 5.1e4, 5.55e4 and 5.67e4, which is at or slightly below the 5.0-5.5e4 plateau the track carries from s=40 out to s=100, so it is flat to falling into the fit end. The tempting feature is a cluster of five points at 1.00e5 to 1.14e5 around s=10-12, but that is not a Bragg peak: the identical thing happens twice more on the same track, at s=23-24 with 9.87e4 and 1.216e5 and at s=69-71 with 9.0-9.5e4, and the band between s=15 and s=22 sits back at 6-7e4 rather than collapsing. These are localized hot spots, deltas or crossings, not a terminal rise, and the bulk never leaves the plateau. That also rules out the overshoot reading, because the region between that cluster and the fit end never falls far below the plateau, only to about half of it with green points at 5.5-5.7e4 interleaved, so there is no sustained collapse to bridge and the pin stays. What does show up is a continuation. Zoomed 6x on both c_3d_stop and e_3d_stop, the thin pale halo line that runs alongside the fitted track for its whole length carries straight on past the star, collinear with the incoming direction, for roughly six centimetres before it runs out; d_3d_stop shows the same faint points above the star. Charge continuing past the fit end is itself the THRU test. f_meas has measured and predicted agreeing, and while the track crosses several dead bands in U along its body, the stop end at U 2615 has clear channels on both sides, so the fit end is not a dead-region exit. The two unassigned pdg-11 shower pieces 52004 and 52007 sit 103-120 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00 carrying 0.84e4 and 2.09e4, hugging the muon body: delta / other.

notes: Hardest item of my twelve. THRU because the last six centimetres of the fit sit on the track own MIP plateau with a dozen points at 4.9-6.75e4 and no rise, which the rubric makes the operative test. Competing reading, which the owner should look at: the seven-point 9.7e4-1.25e5 block at s=10-14 is the Bragg peak, the pin belongs at about s=10, and the three forward dots at 10.6, 18.5 and 24.4 cm are capture gammas, giving STM_ONLY with kind detached dots. I rejected it because the block has normal and low charge on both sides so it is not monotone in residual range, and because there is no charge-free gap along the fit for a bridge to cross. The dots being collinear with the extrapolated direction inside a 35 degree cone also argues continuation rather than isotropic capture gammas. Chain agrees with THRU (no_bragg, shape_flat).
evidence: 205 cm chain, enters 0.3 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 91.5 cm from the z wall, deeply contained. This is the hardest item in my chunk and I put it at medium. The plateau runs 4.5-6.0e4 from s=100 in to about s=20, and the profile at the fit end is still on that plateau: read at 5.5x, the last six centimetres carry about a dozen points at 4.9-6.75e4 with a single 8.26e4 at s=3.5 and a single 1.13e5 at s=0. Twelve points at MIP over the last six centimetres is what a through-goer looks like, and a stopping muon cannot do it, so by the operative test this is THRU and I leave the pin alone. The competing reading is a block of seven points at 9.74e4, 1.00e5, 1.02e5, 1.028e5, 1.076e5, 1.195e5 and 1.254e5 spread over s=10 to s=14, sitting above the muon curve there, with 7.4-7.8e4 just outside it at s=15-18: taken alone that has a Bragg shape and would put the true stop near s=10. I rejected it for two reasons. First, it is a four-centimetre block with ordinary or low charge on both sides, 2.3e4 at s=9.4 and 4.3e4 at s=7-8 immediately inside it, and a muon dQ/dx is monotone in residual range, so a peak that goes away again is a localized deposit, a delta or a crossing, not a Bragg peak. Second, the overshoot mechanism needs the fit past the true stop to be a low-charge bridge across a gap, and there is no gap: f_meas shows continuous amber measured charge along the fit right to its tip in U, V and W, at the same level as the rest of the body. Past the fit end there is a genuinely empty 10.6 cm with no dead channel in any plane, then three tiny detached pieces, 130004 at 10.6 cm with 2 points, 131005 at 18.5 cm with 2 points and 132006 at 24.4 cm with 3 points, at cos_fwd +0.98, +0.84 and +0.81. The chain offers 130004 as a Michel of 0.7 MeV bridged across 10.62 cm of empty space, which by the attachment rule is a detached dot and not a 35 MeV electron. Those three dots are also very nearly collinear with each other and with the extrapolated track direction in b, c and e, all inside a forward cone of about 35 degrees, which is what a sparsely imaged continuation looks like and not what isotropic muon-capture gammas look like. So they read as fragments of the continuing track. On a THRU the tag alphabet has no stop to define gamma or michel against, so all three take delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the end - the cluster simply ran out of imaging 123 cm inside the volume. Per the rubric a flat profile is enough on its own for THRU, so I did not reach for UNCLEAR. THRU tag convention applied: the 11 group=muon fitted chain segments are muon, the 6 group=unassigned rows (143031 plus fitted-but-off-chain 58013/58019/58026/58028/58030) are delta / other, kind none.
evidence: 265 cm chain, enters 6.8 cm from the y face and the fit end sits 123 cm from the nearest (z) wall, so containment is not the question here. The profile is a flat 4.5-5.5e4 MIP plateau from s=100 all the way in to s=5, never leaving it and never taking the shape of the muon reference curve, which asymptotes to 1.6e5 at s=0; the last ~4 cm then fall to 1.2-4.0e4. I considered the overshoot reading (peak then collapse) and rejected it: the only points above 1e5 are isolated singles at s~15, 26, 60 and 82, i.e. they occur all along the body, not as a sustained rise in the last 10-20 cm, so they are the factor-two point-to-point scatter the rubric warns about, not a Bragg peak. With no peak preceding it the terminal dip is just partial-charge end points. The 3-D azimuths show the spine ending abruptly with nothing attached or detached past the star, and the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The one non-body object, 143031, is 2 points / 0.8 cm at dstop 30.7 and is the grey cross at s=-30, y=5.5e4 on the dQ/dx panel - the negative s is only its 3-D distance, not a side. f_meas shows dead bands in V near 6890 and in W near 11655 but both cross the track mid-body, not at the fit end, so this is not a dead-region exit either.

notes: Competing reading weighed: the profile is flat-to-falling at the fit end, which on its own is the THRU test, and the last chain segment 63009 runs at 0.69 of the body plateau, which could be read as the overshoot (true stop at the 63001/63009 junction, 63009 the Michel). I did not move the pin because the dead-band coincidence in TWO planes over exactly that stretch is a sufficient and simpler cause for the low charge, and because there is no peak preceding the fall - the overshoot signature needs peak-then-collapse. The rubric allows STM_MICHEL with an unclear Bragg peak when the topology is there, and the attached sub-MIP transverse arm at a contained stop is that topology. Confidence medium because the Bragg evidence is destroyed by the dead channels rather than positively seen.
evidence: 199 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the anode x face, fit end 25.2 cm from the y wall and in_fv. The dQ/dx profile does not rise: the plateau upper envelope is 5.3-6.5e4 from s=100 in to s=15, then FALLS to about 4.2e4 over the last 15 cm with a scatter of 1-3e4 points and some zeros. f_meas explains that fall - in U the fit end sits right on the dead band at channel 3700-3712 and in V it runs through the wide hatched dead band at 7540-7565, so the last ~15 cm are imaged on essentially one live plane (W) and the charge there is not trustworthy. W is live at the end and shows nothing above time slice 1070, so the muon is not leaving through the dead region, it genuinely terminates. The stop zoom at all three azimuths shows the amber flow band ending and then a Y: two short arms branching transversely off the last stretch, well clear of the body line. 63006 is attached at the stop (d_min 0, out to 6.1 cm, 8.6 cm long) at 3.7e4 e/cm, sub-MIP against the body 4.8e4, which is a second particle and the right length for a ~20 MeV electron; 63007 (5.8 cm, 1.8e4) sits on the same spray at radius 5.5-6.4 cm with no charge-free gap to 63006, so it is part of the same arm and not a detached dot. 63008 (12.7 cm, cos_fwd -0.93, d 3.5-9.8) lies along the body parallel to the last chain segment 63009, so it is body activity, delta / other.

notes: Not an undershoot: the Bragg maximum is reached at the fit last point, not 1-3 cm past it. 68002 tagged muon as an unfitted tip stub.
evidence: 180 cm chain, enters 2.8 cm from a z face and the fit end sits 69.5 cm from the nearest (z) wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg on my chunk: the profile leaves the electron reference at about 6.7e4 near s=13 and climbs monotonically along the shape of the muon curve through 8e4, 9.5e4, 1.1e5 to 1.35e5 at the fit last point, a factor 2.6 above the bodys own 5.1e4 plateau. I checked the undershoot explicitly because 68002 is exactly the shape that fakes it - 4 points, 1.8 cm, 9.6e4 e/cm, straight ahead at cos_fwd 0.76 - but the diagnostic fails: the peak is AT the fit last point, not past it, and 68002 sits BELOW the peak, so it is simply the muons own unfitted last 1.7 cm and I tagged it muon (the chain calls it pdg 2212, not a Michel, so nothing is being manufactured here either way). Past the stop there are only two specks, 204003 (2 pts, 0.3 cm, 1.8e4) at 20.5 cm and 205004 (3 pts, 1.2 cm, 8.9e3) at 15.3 cm. Computing them against the local forward direction they sit 20.2 cm and 14.4 cm OFF the muon line at azimuth -142 and -143 deg, i.e. the same side of the stop as each other and nowhere near the body, so the chains gamma/Michel body-exclusion labels are wrong about the geometry and the rubrics off-axis rule outranks them. Both are detached with a clean gap and far too small to be a 35 MeV electron - 5 points between them - so they are capture-gamma dots, which does not promote the item past STM_ONLY. f_meas shows the two dots as isolated real charge in all three planes below the track end; the U plane has a dense dead-channel forest but the track and the stop are on live channels.

notes: michel_kind hangs entirely on one 2-point speck: I read 106001 as gamma because the tag tables gamma rule is met literally (isolated, past the stop, 35 cm clear of the body line, inside 60 cm) and charge is explicitly not a criterion. The live competing reading is that a lone speck 36 cm out in no particular direction, with no decay arm anywhere to define a Michel side, is unrelated charge - that would make this STM_ONLY / none. Hence medium.
evidence: 194 cm curving chain, enters 12.8 cm from the lower y face and the fit end is 72.1 cm from the nearest wall, well contained; the 3-D azimuths show a clean single spine ending at the star with nothing attached. The Bragg is unambiguous: the profile sits on a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau out at s=20-40, lifts through 6.7e4 at s=9-11, 9.5e4 at s=7, 1.06-1.13e5 at s=4-6, 1.21e5 at s=2 and 1.45e5 at s=1, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve, about 2.5 times its own plateau. Exactly two points sit at s=0 itself, at roughly 6.5e4 and 3.5e4. I considered moving the pin back 1-2 cm for those, and did not: the rubric calls a partial-charge point or two at the very end ordinary scatter and reserves the pin move for a sustained collapse over several cm, which this is not - the fall is one point wide right against the peak. The only other drawn object is 106001, a 2-point 0.4 cm survey speck the chain never offered to either stage. Against the local forward direction it lies 36.4 cm from the stop, 35.1 cm OFF the muon line and on the forward side, so it is nowhere near the body and cannot be delta by the body rule; f_meas shows it as isolated real charge in all three planes, about 67 time slices and a few channels away from the track end, with no dead band at the stop in any plane.

notes: THRU on the flat-to-falling test, plus a wide U dead band at the fit end that the track could have exited through. The item is really an over-merge: the drawn cluster is two disjoint objects glued by the chain, not one track and not a fragment of one, so neither FRAG_ nor MESSY fits cleanly - MESSY is defined as an EM blob with no coherent spine and there ARE two coherent spines here. I recorded plain THRU because the verdict-defining test (no Bragg rise at the fit end) reads the same on either piece. THRU tag convention applied: the four group=muon fitted chain segments are muon, the two unassigned are delta / other, kind none. Medium confidence because the charge at the stop is compromised by the dead band and because the assembly is wrong.
evidence: The chain is 700 cm of claimed muon with range KE 1564 MeV against MCS 406 MeV, and the pictures say why: a_proj side view and b_3d_wide both show TWO disjoint, roughly collinear track pieces separated by a ~65 cm gap - a short ~87 cm piece carrying the fit end and a much longer one beyond it - and 45004 is 434 cm of segment whose points only span 91-327 cm from the stop, so it doubles back on itself. Whatever the assembly is, the profile at the fit end settles the verdict: there is no rise of any kind. From s=35 out to s=100 the upper envelope is 4-6e4 with occasional 7-8.7e4 points, and over the last 30 cm into s=0 it FALLS to 0.5-3e4, an order of magnitude under the muon reference curve and well under the tracks own plateau - the opposite of a Bragg shape. f_meas shows why the last stretch is so faint and also why the track may simply have left: in U a wide hatched dead band sits at channel 2160-2175 right at the fit end, and V has a dead line at 5940 just past it. Nothing at all sits off the muon line here - all six drawn objects table at cos_fwd between -0.95 and -1.0, transverse offsets 0-26 cm on segments 80-430 cm long, i.e. body activity - and the chain agrees with n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The two unassigned rows 45008 (11.8 cm, 2694 e/cm) and 45010 (22.7 cm, 7444 e/cm) lie along the body at d 9-18 and 74-87 cm, so they are body/shower fragments, not decay charge.

notes: The kind call is the soft part. 227030/227031 meet every stated clause of the gamma rule (isolated, clear of the body line by 50 cm, inside the 60 cm ring, detached with a clean charge-free gap confirmed on the full azimuths), and the rubric says charge is explicitly not a criterion, so I tagged them gamma and the item is detached dots. The competing reading is the delta rules last clause, belongs to a different object entirely: 25 points over ~14 cm at MIP charge is more than a capture-gamma speck, and it sits 50 cm off-axis in no particular direction with no Michel anywhere to define a decay side. The full frames weakened that reading - the piece is a short compact arc rather than a through-going fragment - but did not kill it, so this stays medium. Under the other reading the record would be STM_ONLY / none.
evidence: 341 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the anode x face, fit end 47.1 cm from the y wall and in_fv. Textbook Bragg: the profile leaves the electron reference near 6.0-6.4e4 at s=10-12 and climbs along the shape of the muon curve through 7.6e4 at s=7, 8.2e4 at s=5, 9.4e4 at s=3, 1.04e5 at s=2, 1.17e5 at s=1 and 1.31e5 at the last point, about 2.8 times the 4.4-4.7e4 body plateau and monotone enough that no pin question arises. The three stop azimuths at full extent show the spine simply ending at the star with nothing attached and no arm, matching n_stop_arms 0. 58025 (9.6 cm, 1.6e4) and 58027 (12.1 cm, 1.7e4) sit at d 11.5-25 cm with transverse offsets of 0.1 and 3.8 cm from the muon line, i.e. they hug the body, so they are delta / other whatever the chains pdg 11 shower label says. The only thing off the body is the pair 227030 + 227031, 13 and 12 points over 7.3 and 6.6 cm at 3.9e4 and 5.3e4 e/cm: computed against the local forward direction they lie 50.5 and 54.7 cm OFF the muon line, about 14-15 cm behind the stop plane, at essentially one azimuth (125 and 129 deg), so they are one structure sitting in the 60 cm ring beside the stop. On the uncropped azimuths that structure reads as a short curved arc of a dozen or so points, separated from the spine by a wide charge-free gap in all three views - detached and compact, not a track running alongside. f_meas shows it as a clean isolated blob in all three planes, ~50 time slices from the track end, real charge and not a fit artefact. No dead band at the stop in U or W; V has a hatched band at 7540-7565 that the track skirts, but the Bragg peak is intact so it costs nothing here.

notes: THRU on both routes: no Bragg rise AND the fit end is 1.1 cm from the y wall. THRU tag convention applied - the 7 group=muon fitted chain segments are muon and all 32 unassigned rows (including the 783-point C49) are delta / other, kind none; several of those rows would otherwise have argued for gamma on distance alone, which is exactly the case the THRU convention exists to prevent.
evidence: 574 cm chain, enters 2.9 cm from a z face and the fit end sits 1.1 cm from the y wall and 3.9 cm from the z wall - a corner exit, and in_fv is 0. The side projection shows the spine running from Y=+95 straight down to Y=-330 against the bottom of the box, so this one does reach a face, but the operative test agrees independently: the profile has no rise. The plateau out at s=20-45 is 4-5e4 and over the last 20 cm it stays at 3-5e4, nowhere near the shape of the muon curve; the only excursion is a single 8.7e4 point at s=0, which is one point of the ordinary factor-two scatter and not a sustained climb, and the two neighbouring points at s=1-2 are 5.5e4 and 2.2e4. The chain rejects on all three of no_bragg, shape_flat and stop_near_boundary. There is a great deal of other charge drawn here - 32 unassigned rows including C49, 783 points over 152 cm with no PR segment - but computing them against the local forward direction they form one population at azimuth -70 to -102 deg, 30-67 cm off the muon line and 40-70 cm from the stop, i.e. a separate shower/track sitting to one side and visible as its own long ribbon of segments in the second stop azimuth. It is not decay charge from this fit end and it is not on the muon body either; it belongs to a different object. f_meas shows that population as its own cluster of blobs 50-150 time slices off the track in all three planes.

notes: Single-row item; no gamma/michel judgement needed, kind none follows.
evidence: Short, clean 76 cm muon: enters 0.8 cm from the y face and the fit end sits 29.7 cm from the nearest (z) wall, comfortably inside. The profile is the cleanest kind of Bragg on a short track - about 5-6e4 out at s=25-40, lifting through 6.5-7.5e4 at s=10-15, 8.5e4 at s=7-9, 9.5e4 at s=4-5, 1.02e5 at s=2-3 and 1.13-1.15e5 at the last centimetre, hugging the shape of the muon reference curve the whole way and finishing about 2.2 times its own plateau. Nothing to argue about on the pin: the peak is at the fit end and there is no collapse. Nothing sits past the stop either - the object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and the three stop azimuths show the spine terminating at the star with clean empty space beyond it; the only points in that space are the faint thinned context dots and the header explicitly says the 7 nearby blobs belong to another flash, not this stop. So no arm, no dot, no gamma candidate, and n_stop_arms 0 / n_dots 0 agrees. f_meas has a dense dead-channel forest in U at 2350-2450 but the track sits at 2480-2510 and the stop end is on live channels in all three planes, so the Bragg rise is measured charge and not an artefact.

notes: Ordinary STM_MICHEL, the case the rubric contrasts with the undershoot: the forward piece is at or below MIP and long, so it is the electron and not the muons last centimetres.
evidence: Short low-energy stopper: 29 cm of chain, KE 97 MeV by range, entering 1.5 cm from the z face and stopping 21.5 cm from the nearest z wall, so both ends are accounted for and this is not a fragment. The Bragg is emphatic for such a short track - the chain points climb from about 5e4 at s=25-30 through 6-7e4 at s=10-20 and 8.5-9.5e4 at s=5-8 to 1.2-1.55e5 in the last 3 cm, roughly three times the plateau and right on the shape of the muon curve. The very last point or two come back to about 1.15e5 from the 1.55e5 peak 1.5 cm earlier; that is a 25 percent dip one point wide, which the rubric calls ordinary scatter, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse that would move the pin, so I left the pin at the fit end. Past the stop there is a single arm, 46012: 13 points over 7.2 cm attached at the very vertex where the chain ends, and on the dQ/dx panel its points (plotted on the negative axis at |s| 0-7, which is only their 3-D distance and says nothing about side) run 2.4e4 to 6.6e4, i.e. straddling MIP and mostly below it. A muon at a 1.5e5 Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle, and 7 cm of sub-MIP charge leaving the stop at a 31 deg kink is exactly a ~17 MeV Michel. I checked the undershoot case and it does not apply: the tip here is 7.2 cm at MIP, not a 2 cm piece at several times MIP. No dead band anywhere near the stop in any plane; the three azimuths show the amber muon, the vertex square and the blue arm as one clean Y.

notes: LOW confidence. Revised after reading the three stop azimuths uncropped: my first reading kept 114014/117016 as an attached michel arm on the strength of the chains own particle-flow, but the full frames show a clean charge-free gap between the stop and every piece, and the rubric is explicit that a detached compact speck is a gamma however close it sits. That makes the kind detached dots and holds the verdict at STM_ONLY, since capture gammas do not promote an item to STM_MICHEL. The other live reading is THRU: the hump is only 1.3x the plateau envelope, and if it is scatter the profile is flat and this is a through-goer - the chain itself says shape_flat. I kept STM_ONLY because with the pin at 5.5 the corrected end sits at the top of the hump rather than in the empty bridge. Note MCS 74 MeV against range 1054 MeV at amb 0.94, so the momentum fit is no cross-check here.
evidence: 458 cm chain running nearly parallel to and 25 cm from the anode face; enters 0.1 cm from that face and the fit end is 25.6 cm from it, in_fv. This is the weakest call in my chunk. The profile is sparse (the chain rejects on profile_sparse) with several points per arc position: the plateau upper envelope at s=20-45 is 7.0-7.5e4, and there is a hump above it at s=6-13 reaching 8.1e4, 9.0e4, 8.7e4, 9.9e4 and 9.2e4, only about 1.3 times the envelope, which on its own is inside the factor-two scatter the rubric warns about. What decides it is what follows the hump: the charge falls 9.0e4 (s=7), 6.2e4 (s=5.5), 3.4e4 (s=5), 1.5e4 (s=4.6) and then the last ~4.5 cm of the fit are zero-charge points carrying no measured charge at all. So the fit end is demonstrably not where the charge ends, and the shape is peak-then-collapse rather than the muon curve carried into the stop: the data sits ABOVE the reference curve at s=7-12 and an order of magnitude BELOW it at s=3. I moved the pin to rr 5.5, the junction between the last real muon charge and the empty bridge. The collapse falls inside segment 48006 (d 0-24.1 cm); I tagged that row muon because 18 of its 24 cm are muon, and I record that the row is split - roughly 5.5-24 cm is muon, 0-5.5 cm is the bridge. On the three stop azimuths at full extent the space past the star is EMPTY: the four small pieces show only as isolated vertex squares floating clear of the spine with a charge-free gap to it, nothing attached and nothing bridged by visible charge. So by the rubrics attachment tiebreak all four are detached dots, not an arm: 114014 (2 pts, 0.4 cm) at 4.8 cm across the gap the chain itself describes as 4.79 cm of empty space, 117016 (4 pts, 1.6 cm) at 11.3 cm, 115015 (2 pts, 0.5 cm) at 11.4 cm and 113013 (2 pts) at 18.0 cm, with transverse offsets 4.1-16.7 cm and azimuths 45, -7, -178 and 46 deg. Ten image points in four specks is not a 35 MeV electron, so the item does not reach STM_MICHEL. 48007 (44 pts) and 48018 lie 358-394 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -0.9: body activity. Worth flagging separately: at full extent a second cyan strand of image points runs parallel to the fitted spine for its whole visible length and converges on it near the stop, with no object row of its own, so the local point cloud here is doubled.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test with no visible continuation, no face and no clean dead-region exit at the end - the cluster ended 30 cm inside the volume where the imaging ran out, which the rubric says is enough on its own; I did not use UNCLEAR. Competing reading, and why this is medium not high: the last 2-3 cm do reach 1.0e5 against a 6.5-7.0e4 plateau, and if that pair is read as a genuine weak Bragg the item becomes STM_ONLY / none. I rejected it because the same size excursion appears at s=19-20 and a much bigger one at s=38, and because there is no rise over the preceding 10-20 cm. Note the track runs nearly along the drift, so it spans only ~25 channels over 145 time slices and its dQ/dx is poorly sampled in any case.
evidence: 109 cm track running almost along the drift direction: enters 12.7 cm from a z face and the fit end is 30.0 cm from the nearest z wall, in_fv, and the 3-D azimuths show it simply terminating at the star with nothing attached or detached beyond it (only two rows in the table, both muon chain segments, and n_stop_arms 0 / n_dots 0). The profile does not rise. Its upper envelope is about 6.5-7.0e4 from s=100 all the way in to s=5, and the excursions above that are not localised at the end: 8.4-9.3e4 at s=19-20, 9.9-10.2e4 at s=0-3, and a spike of 1.09-1.41e5 at s=37-39, which is 39 cm back from the fit end and can only be a delta ray or an overlap. That last one is the useful control - it shows this track produces 1.4e5 points mid-body, so the 1.0e5 pair in the last 3 cm is the same population, not a Bragg peak. There is also no gradient over the last 10-20 cm, which is the interval the test is defined on: s=20, 15, 10 and 5 all sit at 6.5-7.0e4 with sub-MIP points down to 3.1e4 mixed in. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) and its momentum fit is internally inconsistent - MCS 481 MeV against 272 MeV by range with amb 0.76, i.e. the track is straighter than a 272 MeV muon should be. f_meas shows the U plane is a dead-channel forest here, with bands at 1440-1450 and 1470-1490 flanking the track at 1445-1470, which is a plausible reason for the cluster to end where it does.

notes: Medium, not high, and this is the row I would most like the owner to look at. If the fiducial boundary were not there the evidence would read as a stopper: there is a 1.02e5 bump 3-4 cm before the fit end, a fall over the last 3 cm, and a 5.5 cm sub-MIP arm attached at the very stop vertex - i.e. the overshoot pattern plus a Michel, which would have given STM_MICHEL / attached with the pin near rr 3. I did not record it that way because d_face 2.0 cm and in_fv 0 fail the ends inside the volume clause that both STM verdicts open with, and because even with the pin moved back the corrected stop would still be only ~5 cm from the wall. THRU tag convention applied: only the fitted chain segment 30010 is muon; 30011 and 103012 are delta / other and the kind is none, since gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop this item does not have.
evidence: 81 cm track that crosses from one face to another: it enters 0.9 cm from the y face and the fit end sits 2.0 cm from the z wall, with in_fv 0, and the side projection shows exactly that - the spine runs from Y=+340 at the top of the box down to Z=2.8 at the left edge. Both STM verdicts require the track to end inside the volume and this one does not, so the verdict is forced before the profile is even read. The profile does not rescue it either: the plateau is 5.0-6.5e4 with occasional 7.0-7.8e4 points along the whole body, and the only excursion near the end is two points at 9.4e4 and 1.02e5 at s=3-4, after which the last 3 cm fall back to 7.5e4 (s=2) and 3.5e4 (s=1). That is a 1.6x bump two points wide, not a rise following the muon curve over the last 10-20 cm. The chain rejects on no_bragg, shape_flat and stop_near_boundary, and its momentum fit is incoherent - MCS 39.9 MeV against 210.7 MeV by range at amb 0.96. The chain does offer an arm, 30011, 10 points over 5.5 cm at 1.8e4 e/cm attached at the stop vertex at a 142 deg kink (its points are the large blue markers at |s| 0-3.5 on the dQ/dx panel, on the negative axis only because it is off-chain). Under the THRU convention that row is delta / other, as is 103012, a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 51.9 cm out and 50.4 cm off the muon line. f_meas shows a dead-channel forest in U at 1400-1460 alongside the track, but V and W are clean and the track is imaged to its end.

notes: 1.52e5 terminal point is above the rubric's stated 1.2-1.35e5 band for real stoppers here and essentially touches the muon reference curve; judged on shape as the rubric directs. No undershoot, no overshoot.
evidence: A 555 cm cosmic muon (chain KE 1259 MeV) entering 0.5 cm from the anode x face and stopping 72.1 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1, so containment is a comfortable numbers call. Upscaled 4x, g_dqdx sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 MIP plateau for 100 cm and then climbs smoothly along the shape of the muon reference curve over the last ~10 cm, 6e4 at s=10, 8e4 at s=5, 1.05e5 at s=2 and a terminal 1.52e5 at s=0 - the cleanest possible Bragg, and it peaks AT the fit's last point with no peak-then-collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. The blue near-zero points at s=45-47 are mid-track fit points with no measured charge, not a terminal collapse. Nothing sits forward of the stop at all: every drawn row has negative cos_fwd and the nearest non-body object is 47.6 cm away, so the undershoot signature (a high-charge 1e5 tip a couple of cm straight ahead) cannot apply here either. 75005/75009/75012/75013 are the four fitted chain segments running 0-526 cm back up the body, transverse offsets 0-39 cm on a 555 cm chord, all muon. 75011 is a 3 cm 6-point pdg-11 shower speck 210 cm back at cos_fwd -0.97 and 10 cm off the body line: body activity, delta / other. The call I had to weigh is the three 2-point survey specks 189014/190015/192016 at 47.6/49.8/52.4 cm, dqdx 1.8-5.7e4: they are well clear of the muon line (transverse 30/43/49 cm) which pulls towards gamma, but projecting them onto the muon axis puts all three 19-37 cm BEHIND the plane through the stop, so they are not past the stop and the gamma rule does not reach them; they are also three isolated blips with 11 and 23 cm charge-free gaps between them, not a radial trail from the stop, and with no Michel there is no decay side for the faint-far-speck rule to key on. Called delta / other, hence kind none. f_meas shows the track terminating cleanly at time slice ~930 in all three planes with the hatched dead bands (U 1320-1340, V 5130, W 9280) alongside but not at the end, so this is not a dead-region exit.

notes: Flat profile is the operative test and it is met, so THRU even though the fit end is 87.9 cm from every face with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit - the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. No undershoot (no forward object exists at all), no overshoot (no peak-then-collapse; the last 2 cm sit above, not below, the plateau).
evidence: 326 cm, enters 0.6 cm from the z face at (-293,-172,1.4) and the fit ends at (-58,-126,210), 87.9 cm from the nearest wall and in_fv 1 - so this is not a face exit, and f_meas shows the track terminating cleanly at time slice ~1595 in U, V and W with the hatched dead bands well to the side in every plane, so it is not a dead-region exit either. The verdict rests entirely on the shape. Upscaled 4x and again 9x on the last 20 cm, the profile is flat: the last 2 cm sit at 6.5-7.7e4, the 2-5 cm bin at 6.6-9.6e4 and the 5-10 cm bin at 6.4-8.2e4, against a body that runs 6-8e4 the whole way out to 100 cm with routine excursions to 1.05-1.37e5 at s=16, 25, 37 and 50. The terminal band is therefore inside this track's own ordinary scatter - the median of the last 2 cm is actually BELOW the median at 30-40 cm - and nothing follows the shape of the muon reference curve, which would have to reach 1.2-1.6e5 in the last 2 cm. There is one point at 9.6e4 at s=3.5 that briefly touches the muon curve, and that single point is the whole case for a weak ragged Bragg, which is why this is medium and not high; but a lone excursion the same size as four others further up the body is not a rise off the plateau. The three azimuths show a clean, slightly curved amber track ending at the star with absolutely nothing past it - no arm, no dot, no continuation - and the object table has only three rows: 23001 (the 288 cm muon chain) and 23002 (a 38 cm pdg-13 chain segment 281-318 cm back) are the fitted chain, tagged muon; 23003 is a 2.7 cm 5-point pdg-11 shower speck 281 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00 and 3.6 cm off the body line, plain body activity, delta / other. Per the rubric a through-goer has no stop, so kind is none.

notes: No undershoot, no overshoot. Dead bands sit ~15 U channels past the stop and the body crosses V/W dead bands mid-track, but a dead-region exit cannot produce a 3x Bragg peak, so containment stands.
evidence: 146 cm, enters 0.4 cm from the z face and the fit ends at (276,-220,76), 63.9 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1. The Bragg is unambiguous: measuring the small chain markers off the 4x/9x crop, the body runs 4-6e4 from s=20 out to s=100 and the last few centimetres go 7.3e4 at s=5.4, 8.3e4 at 4.8, 9.5e4 at 4.2, 9.2e4 at 2.4, 1.05e5 at 1.8, 1.39e5 at 1.15 and 1.12e5 at 0.66 - a factor three off this track's own plateau, following the muon curve's shape, and the peak sits at the fit's last centimetre rather than several cm before it, so there is no peak-then-collapse and the pin stays put. There is a real mid-track dip, s=7-13 falling to 1.1-1.6e4 and recovering by s=15, but it is 7-13 cm BACK from the stop, on the wrong side to be the bridged-gap signature, and f_meas shows the V and W dead bands the body crosses in that stretch. Past the end sits 46007, the chain's Michel: 4 points over 1.8 cm attached at the shared stop vertex, cos_fwd +0.31 with a 68 deg kink, 0.7 cm off the muon line, and its three drawn points carry 8.1e4, 6.2e4 and 2.5e4 - at or below this track's own MIP, and falling as it goes out. A muon at a 1.39e5 Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle and the ordinary attached-Michel case, not the undershoot (that needs a forward tip at several times MIP; 6.2e4 is 1.4x plateau and the angle is 68 deg off forward). It is a small Michel - 4.6 MeV, 1.8 cm - which is what keeps this at medium rather than high. 46012 is a 12.8 cm 22-point pdg-11 shower running 6.8-15.5 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 and only 2.1 cm off the body line, visible in c_3d and e_3d as a thin green trail hugging the amber band: it hugs the muon body, so delta / other whatever the chain's shower label says. 46008 and 46013 are the two fitted chain segments, muon.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs 1.8 cm past the muon's true stop; pin set to rr 1.8, segment 63006 (chain-typed muon) retagged michel. Stretch: the rubric asks for a collapse 'sustained over several cm' and this one is 1.8 cm / 4 points - I took it because it is a whole named segment at 0.24 MIP rather than a single low point, and because the rubric also says the depth is not a threshold and the collapse is the diagnostic. The 183005 gamma-vs-michel call does not change the kind: 182004 is a gamma on its own, so both either way.
evidence: 334 cm, enters 0.1 cm from the anode x face at (340,248,158) and the fit ends at (38.5,194,252), 46.1 cm from the nearest wall (z) and 35.5 cm from the cathode, in_fv 1. The chain rejects this as no_bragg + shape_flat and it is wrong: measured off the 9x crop, the body climbs monotonically along the muon reference curve - 5.2e4 from s=100 down to s=30, 7.0e4 at 20-30, 7.8e4 at 10-15, 8.5e4 at 5-10 and 1.0e5 at 2-5, sitting on the black curve the whole way - and then the last two chain points, at s=1.3 and s=0.8, drop to 2.9e4 and 1.8e4. Those points are segment 63006, a named 4-point 1.8 cm chain row carrying dqdx 12635, which is 0.24 of this track's own MIP plateau. That is the bridged-gap signature, not scatter: a muon whose profile has just reached 1.9x MIP cannot finish at a quarter of MIP over four consecutive points. So the muon's real stop is the junction between 63002 and 63006, pin moved to rr 1.8, and 63006 is tagged michel although the chain calls it muon. Past that junction the three azimuths show a diffuse electron-like cloud of image points about 10 cm across leaving the end: 63007 (the chain's Michel core, 12 points over 6.8 cm out to d 4.8, cos_fwd +0.19, kink 74 deg, dqdx 13977) and 63001 (a 10-point 5.4 cm pdg-11 shower at d 0.8-3.0, dqdx 24835) - both at or below MIP and both inside 5 cm of the stop, where the rubric says direction does not discriminate, so both michel. 183005 is a 2-point 0.6 cm speck at d 12.0, forward (cos_fwd +0.48) and 12 cm off the muon chord, separated from the Michel core's last charge at 4.8 cm by a clean ~7 cm gap - the rubric's own worked example (a 2-point speck across a gap is not a 35 MeV electron), so gamma. 182004 is a 4-point 1.8 cm survey speck at d 42.6, forward and 42 cm off the body line, isolated and inside the 60 cm ring and on the same side as the decay: gamma. C26 is not a speck at all - 49 points, size 179.3 cm, no PR segment, nearest approach 55.9 cm and 52 cm off the axis: a different object entirely, delta / other. 63002 is the fitted 333 cm body, muon.

notes: No undershoot, no overshoot. The michel_kind hinges entirely on 185005: gamma gives detached dots, delta / other would give none. Competing reading stated in the evidence.
evidence: 96 cm, enters 0.8 cm from the upper y wall at (307,336,236) and the fit ends at (221,318,210), 17.9 cm from that same y wall - shallow but inside, in_fv 1, and the shape settles it anyway. On the 9x crop the last centimetres sit exactly on the muon reference curve: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=40 out to s=100 and from s=10 to s=40, then 6.4e4 at s=5-10, 8.0e4 at 2-5, 9.6e4 at 1-2 and a terminal 1.09e5 at s=0.75 - a factor 2.2 rise following the curve's shape, peaking at the fit's own last point with no collapse behind it, so the pin stays. Nothing is attached at the stop in any of the three azimuths: the amber track simply ends at the star and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The only other drawn object is 185005, a 2-point 0.4 cm speck at 17.3 cm whose two points are drawn on the dQ/dx panel as grey crosses at s=-17 carrying 7.5e4 and 1.1e4. Geometrically it sits 15.7 cm off the muon's line and 7.5 cm behind the plane through the stop (cos_fwd -0.43, and my chord-derived cosine reproduces it, so the track is not curved here and the number is honest). I called it gamma: it is isolated with a wide clean gap in d_3d and f_meas, compact, well inside the 60 cm ring, and 15.7 cm clear of the body line, which the rubric says outranks both the cos_fwd number and the chain's own 'gamma body exclusion' label. At 17.3 cm it is inside the 20-60 cm band that the faint-far-speck paragraph governs, so that paragraph's 'no decay side, therefore delta' fallback does not reach it. What made this hard is the 25 degrees of backward tilt: the strict along-axis test says it is not past the stop, and reading it that way would make the row delta / other and the kind none. f_meas shows the end clean in U and W; a V dead band runs alongside the last centimetres, but a dead-region exit cannot produce this Bragg peak.

notes: Competing reading: the rubric's operative THRU test (no Bragg rise at the fit end) is met, so THRU is defensible and would tag 33006/33008/33016/33017 muon. I went MESSY because the fitted chain bridges a ~33 cm charge-free gap and its centre segment sits at 0.15 MIP, so there is no single track to call a through-goer. Kind is none either way. No undershoot, no overshoot. CONSISTENCY NOTE: 039349_37/52 is the neighbouring cluster in this same event, its stop 18.6 cm from this one, and it has the same 0.1-0.5 MIP mid-chain pathology but I graded it THRU, not MESSY. The discriminator I used is empty versus continuous-but-suppressed: here f_meas shows two disconnected charge clumps with a bare fit line and no measured charge across ~33 cm, whereas 37/52's suppressed stretch is a dense continuous band of points and that object also has a genuine near-MIP region at s=48-62 that its terminal charge sits level with. If a reviewer rejects that distinction, both items should read the same way.
evidence: The chain claims a 96 cm muon ending at (95,127,40), 39.0 cm from the z wall, and rejects it as shape_flat + profile_sparse. It is not one track. Three independent things say so. First the charge: the whole object lives between 0.5e4 and 4.3e4 e/cm, i.e. 0.1 to 0.8 of MIP, and the 88 cm centre segment 33016 carries a segment-level dqdx of 7579 - a fifth of MIP over 88 cm, which no muon does. Nothing on the panel comes within a factor of two of the muon reference curve at any arc length. Second the gap: the dQ/dx panel has chain points at s=0-12 and again at s=45-100 and absolutely nothing between, and f_meas confirms it is a real hole rather than the panel's usual incompleteness - U-measured and V-measured show two disconnected clumps, a small amber one at time slice ~1045 and a dark near-zero-charge band at ~1120-1130, joined only by a thin straight fit line with no measured charge under it. The fit bridges roughly 33 cm of nothing. Third the kinematics: range gives 332 MeV/c while dQ/dx gives 119 and MCS 111, ambiguity 0.92. So the piece that owns the 'stop' is an 8 cm stub, and there is no coherent spine to hang a stopping point on. At the fit end the profile is flat and noisy (2.9e4 at s=0, 2.4e4 at 2.4, 1.5e4 at 5.2, 2.4e4 at 5.8, 4.3e4 at 7.0) with no rise of any kind, so this is certainly not an STM whichever way the object is carved. The three azimuths show the amber stub sitting alone, a diffuse cloud of image points 30-60 cm away with its own scattered vertex squares, and the long low-charge piece well separated. Six 2-point survey specks sit at 38-60 cm at cos_fwd from -0.75 to +0.17 and 29-57 cm off the chord - scattered in unrelated directions around the ring, the rubric's delta case. Per the MESSY convention every row is tagged delta / other, including the chain's own 0.79 MeV capture-gamma candidate 205012 at 30.5 cm, because the tag alphabet presupposes an identified stop and this item has none.

notes: No undershoot, no overshoot. A U dead band at channel 2110-2115 sits under the last centimetres, but a dead-region exit cannot make a 1.55e5 terminal point.
evidence: 261 cm, enters 0.1 cm from the anode x face at (340,-134,105) and stops at (137,-210,26), 24.7 cm from the z wall, in_fv 1. The Bragg is as clean as they come: a 4.5-5e4 plateau from s=40 to s=100, 6.4e4 at 20-30, 7.0e4 at 10-15, 7.8e4 at 2-5 and then 1.21e5 at s=0.95 and 1.55e5 at the fit's own last point at s=0.44, sitting on the muon reference curve for the last 3 cm - a factor three off plateau, rising monotonically into the last point, so no peak-then-collapse and the pin stays where it is. Nothing forward of the end carries several times MIP either, so this is not the undershoot case. Past the stop d_3d and e_3d show a short blue-teal arm leaving the star almost perpendicular to the muon and running about 8 cm: that arm is three contiguous rows - 320064 (11 points, 5.8 cm, d 0.4-5.3, the chain's 29.5 MeV Michel bridged across 0.40 cm), 320063 (6 points, d 5.3-7.0) and 320061 (7 points, d 6.5-8.4) - carrying 0.5e4 to 4.5e4, at or below MIP and falling outward. The chain body-excluded the outer two, and this is exactly the collision the rubric works through: cos_fwd -0.36 and -0.39, a few cm behind the stop but 6.2 and 7.5 cm out to the side. Off-axis separation and attachment decide it - they are clear of the muon body and form an unbroken chain from d 0.4 to d 8.4 - so all three are michel. 140048 is different: 9 points over 4.7 cm at 1.76e4, 40.6-43.8 cm away, 31 cm PAST the plane through the stop, forward at cos_fwd +0.58 and 28.5 cm off the muon chord, and both d_3d and e_3d show it as a completely isolated pair of markers with a wide charge-free gap - isolated, past the stop, clear of the body line, inside 60 cm, so gamma. The rest is body activity: 137046, 318050, 319058, 319059 and 39034 are a low-charge (0.8-1.8e4) knot of about 110 points sitting 33-48 cm BACK along the body at cos_fwd -0.95 to -0.99, visible in d_3d as pink and orange trails hanging off the muon line, and 39031 and 39040 are pdg-11 shower specks 99 cm and 187 cm back, also on the line - all delta / other. The twelve fitted chain segments are muon.

notes: No undershoot, no overshoot - the pin question does not arise on a THRU. Competing reading I weighed: taking 1.2e4 as the plateau makes the last 6 cm a 4x rise and the item STM_ONLY. I rejected it because the object has a genuine near-MIP region at s=48-62 and the terminal points sit level with it, and because the last 4 cm are flat rather than still climbing.
evidence: The chain claims a 67 cm muon ending at (112,133,32), 30.8 cm from the z wall, and rejects it as plateau_off_mip. Reading the profile off the 4x crop, the object has three regions: the last 6 cm rising 1.26e4 at s=6.4 to 2.1e4, 2.9e4, 3.6e4 and then flat at 4.1-5.2e4 over s=0.3 to 4.0; a 40 cm stretch from s=7 to s=47 sitting in a dense wavy band between 0.4e4 and 2.4e4, i.e. 0.1-0.5 of MIP; and a normal region at s=48-62 carrying 4-8e4. That last region is this track's own MIP plateau, and the terminal 4.1-5.2e4 is not above it - it is level with it. So what looked at first like a 4x Bragg rise is the track climbing back out of the anomalously suppressed 40 cm stretch, and the actual last four centimetres are flat on the MIP plateau, which a stopping muon cannot do. Nothing follows the muon reference curve anywhere: at s=2 the curve is at 1.05e5 and the data is at 4.1e4. The chain agrees there is nothing at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0), and the three azimuths show the amber piece simply ending at the star with clear space beyond it. Supporting evidence that the calorimetry here is not to be trusted at face value: range gives 267 MeV/c, dQ/dx 143 and MCS 101, ambiguity 1.04, and the neighbouring cluster in this same event (stop 18.6 cm away) shows the same 0.15-0.25 MIP pathology. evidence: 190.7 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the x face at (339.4,235.3,65.7) and stopping at (206.1,131.1,120.8), 120.0 cm from the nearest wall and 203 cm off the cathode - deeply contained. evidence: A short one: only 19.3 cm of chain, entering 1.7 cm from the x (anode) face at (338.2,-319.7,76.1) and stopping at (324.1,-311.3,67.3), 15.9 cm in from that same anode face and 25 cm from the y wall - a low-energy muon (73 MeV range KE) that came in through the anode and stopped just inside the corner, not a fragment: the wide view shows nothing else anywhere near it.
