notes: Flat-profile THRU on a deeply contained (75 cm) fit end with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit; called on the profile alone per the rubric.
evidence: 300.3 cm chain entering 0.4 cm from the x (anode) face at (339.5,106.8,219.3) and ending at (97.5,261.4,177.7), 74.9 cm from the y wall, 94.5 cm off the cathode and 120.7 cm from the z wall, so the fit end is well inside and containment cannot decide it. The profile is flat from end to end: on the 9x crop the chain scatters between 4.5e4 and 6.5e4 from s=100 all the way in to s=5, and the last three points read about 4.5e4, 4.0e4 and 3.8e4 - level with, or a shade under, its own plateau, with no hint of a climb in the last 10-20 cm and nothing anywhere near the muon reference curve, which asymptotes to 1.6e5. The only points above 8e4 are a pair at 1.0e5 about 19 cm back and a cluster at 1.0-1.15e5 some 85-90 cm back, both isolated excursions on the body rather than a terminal rise. A stopping muon cannot arrive at its final point at MIP, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ended where the imaging ran out; the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0), and the MCS estimate of 1317 MeV against a 691 MeV range KE (ambiguity 0.48) leans the same way. All three azimuths show one long, clean, straight spine that terminates abruptly at the star with nothing past it - no arm, no dots, no specks anywhere in the ring (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). Every one of the seven drawn objects lies at cos_fwd -1.00 back along the body: the four muon-group rows are the chain segments, and the three unassigned rows are all 264-291 cm away at the far end near the entry (65003 a 9.5 cm pdg 11 shower piece, 65009 a 2.7 cm one, 65010 a 0.6 cm two-point piece typed pdg 2212), i.e. entry-end activity that has nothing to do with this fit end; on a THRU they are delta / other. In f_meas the fit end is live in all three planes - the nearest dead structure is a wide V block at channels 7540-7555, about 25 channels beyond the track, plus single dead lines in U at 3705 and W at 11995.

notes: Flat-at-plateau ending; the 9e4-1.5e5 patch 3-6 cm back is non-monotone and only a few points wide, so read as a delta/crossing rather than a Bragg peak - pin left alone. Medium for that reason, and because V is dead beside the track at the stop and W shows no charge along the track there.
evidence: 190.7 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the z face at (92.5,256.4,0.9) and ending at (-55.8,168.1,49.2), 48.4 cm from the z wall and 52.8 cm off the cathode, so it is inside but not deeply so, and the profile decides. The last centimetres do not rise: on the 9x crop the chain plateau is 5.5-6.5e4 and the points nearest the fit end read 6.7e4 at s=0, 5.6e4 at s=0.4, then 3.5e4 and 1.9e4 at s=1.7-2.3 and 6.5e4 at s=2.5 - level with the plateau and scattered, not climbing, and nothing approaches the muon reference curve. What made this one take a second look is a localised high-charge patch 3-6 cm back: single points at 9.2e4 (s=3.6), 9.9e4 (s=4.7), 1.04e5 (s=6.0) and one at 1.53e5 near s=5, sitting right next to other chain points at 6.0-6.3e4 at the same arc length. I read that as a delta or a crossing piece rather than a Bragg approach, for three reasons: it is non-monotone (9.2e4 at s=3.6 is LOWER than 1.04e5 at s=6.0, whereas a Bragg peak climbs steadily toward the end), it is only a few points wide where a real Bragg builds over 10-20 cm, and the charge afterwards recovers to 6.7e4 at the fit end rather than collapsing, so the overshoot signature (peak then sustained collapse) is not present and I left the pin alone. The 3-D azimuths support it: there is a small piece lying across the muon body a few centimetres before the star, and past the star there is nothing at all (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no gamma ring). The chain rejects on no_bragg (and, unusually for this chunk, not on shape_flat), and the MCS estimate of 1283 MeV against a 446 MeV range KE, ambiguity 0.88, is consistent with a track that did not stop. The three unassigned rows are 27, 40 and 50 cm out (198011 a 1.4 cm gamma-body-exclusion piece, 197010 a 0.7 cm speck, 172009 a 2.2 cm two-point speck) and on a THRU all three are delta / other. Caveat for the audit: at the fit end V has a dead line at channel ~4980 running right beside the track, and the W panel shows no collection-plane charge along the track at all in the stop region, so the terminal charge here rests mostly on U - another reason the numeric depth of individual points should not be over-read, though no reading of them produces a rise.

notes: Flat/declining profile to the last point with nothing past the end; called THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs, not on containment (stop is 31.6 cm from the nearest face). The last two points at 2.3-2.9e4 are a terminal dip, not the overshoot signature: there is no peak above plateau to collapse from and no object past the end to bridge to, so the pin was left alone.
evidence: 60.4 cm chain, enters 1.3 cm from the z face and ends 31.6 cm from the nearest wall, well inside the FV, so containment is not what decides this. On the 4x-upscaled profile the data sit on a ~5e4 MIP plateau for the whole 60 cm; going into the fit end the points reach 6.5-7.5e4 around s=6-10 cm and then FALL, to 4.0-4.4e4 over the last 4 cm and 2.9e4 / 2.3e4 at the final two points. That is a decline, not a rise: nothing approaches the muon reference curve, which asymptotes at 1.6e5 at s=0, and real stoppers in this set top out at 1.2-1.35e5 whereas this tops out at 0.75e5, only ~1.4x its own plateau. The brief bump is far too small and too early to be a Bragg peak, and there is no peak-then-sustained-collapse either, because there is nothing past the end for the fit to bridge to: the object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring. f_meas shows measured and predicted agreeing along the whole track with no charge continuing past the last point in V or W; U does have a dead-channel band a few channels beyond the end, so a dead-region exit cannot be excluded, but by the operative test that does not matter -- a flat-to-declining profile at the fit end is a through-goer whether or not I can see where it went. Range KE 167 MeV against MCS 405 MeV (amb 0.88) points the same way. Single row tagged muon, kind none.

notes: Hard item, medium. Competing reading: the chain carries 1.2-1.45e5 at s=14-28 cm and then falls to 4.5e4 at the fit end, which has the SHAPE of a peak-then-collapse overshoot with the true stop ~20 cm back and the last 20 cm a Michel. I rejected it on three grounds: (1) the collapse only reaches ~0.8 of the tracks own plateau, where the rubrics bridged segments run 0.15-0.5 of MIP; (2) an equally high 1.0-1.6e5 cluster sits at s=80-90 cm, so high-charge blobs are a body feature of this track and not a stop signature; (3) both high-charge regions coincide with the drawn pdg-11 shower blobs (26041/26027/26030 at d 21-33, and 26021/26033/26044/26045/26050/26051 at d 83-93), so the charge is shared with overlapping shower, not a Bragg peak. Pin left alone. Also flagging that the range/MCS agreement (519.6 vs 558.3, amb 0.17) is the kind of consistency a genuine stopper shows, and it is the reason this is medium and not high.
evidence: 224 cm chain in 13 fitted segments, enters 0.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends 93.6 cm from the nearest wall, so this is decided on the profile, not on containment. The 3-D azimuths show one clean straight spine with a dense spray of small pdg-11 shower blobs hugging it, so it is one object, not MESSY. On the 4x profile the plateau is ~5.5e4; the last 12 cm before the fit end run 5.5-6.5e4 falling to 4.2-4.7e4 at the final three points, i.e. at or slightly below its own plateau, with no climb toward the muon reference curve (which asymptotes at 1.6e5). No Bragg rise at the fit end, and the flow block confirms n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring, so there is nothing past the end either. The two survey specks are at dstop 37.9 (cos_fwd -0.99) and 41.2 (cos_fwd -0.91), both BACK along the body on a spine that the azimuths show is straight, so cos_fwd is trustworthy here and both are body activity; the sixteen pdg-11 shower rows all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 between 21 and 154 cm along the body, which is hugging the body line and delta / other by the off-axis rule whatever the chain calls them. f_meas: measured and predicted agree along the whole track and nothing continues past the end in U or W; the end does sit a few channels from a V dead band, so a dead-region exit cannot be excluded, but that is a THRU either way. Range KE 519.6 MeV vs MCS 558.3 MeV (amb 0.17) is the one number pulling the other way.

notes: Overshoot direction (fit runs PAST the stop), pin moved back 4.3 cm; not the UNDERSHOOT case. Medium, for two reasons. (1) The FRAG call and the C51=muon tag stand or fall together: C51 is collinear with the backward extension in every view and the fit entry is 121.9 cm from any face so the 24 cm chain cannot be a whole cosmic, but there is an 11 cm reconstruction gap between the fit start and C51 d_min, so a parallel unrelated cosmic is not excluded. If C51 is unrelated the verdict is plain STM_MICHEL and C51 is delta / other; the STM_MICHEL core is unaffected either way. (2) 126005 vs michel: it is the chains own Michel and moving the pin back leaves it ~16 cm from the corrected stop, but the gap is explicitly empty and the piece is 0.1 cm of 2 points, so I took gamma on the attachment rule; if it were called michel the kind would still be attached-plus, i.e. the record would read attached rather than both.
evidence: Only 24.1 cm of fitted chain, and both its ends are deep: entry 121.9 cm from the nearest face, fit end 131.3 cm, so nothing here is a wall effect. On the 4x profile the data climb monotonically from 7.4e4 at s=24 cm to 1.63e5 at s=4.9 cm, reaching the muon reference curve (which asymptotes 1.6e5) -- an unambiguous Bragg peak -- and then COLLAPSE over the last 4.2 cm to 5.4-6.3e4, 3.7e4 and 3.1e4, i.e. 0.2-0.4 of the peak, sustained over several cm rather than one low last point. That is the overshoot signature exactly: the true stop is at s = 4.3 cm and the fit ran on past it, so I set --pin-rr 4.3. A muon at 1.6e5 cannot continue at 0.3 of that, so the bridged tail is a second particle: segment 28003 (d 0-2.39 cm) lies wholly inside the collapse and is tagged michel; the collapse also swallows the last ~1.8 cm of 28001, so THAT ROW IS SPLIT -- 20 cm of it is muon and I tagged it muon, but its first 1.8 cm past the corrected stop is Michel too. 126005 is the chain Michel object but it is a 2-point, 0.1 cm dot at 1.1e5 e/cm sitting 14.9 cm out at cos_fwd 0.06, i.e. ~86 deg off the muon axis and well clear of the body line, and the flow block itself says the parentage was assigned across 14.90 cm of EMPTY SPACE by proximity, not a graph edge -- a clean charge-free gap, so by the attachment tiebreak it is a detached dot, gamma, not the electron. The two survey specks 127006 (36.8 cm, cos_fwd -0.25) and 125004 (55.0 cm, cos_fwd -0.41) are faint 2.4-2.6e4 pairs in unrelated directions around the ring: delta / other. C51 is the reason for the FRAG prefix -- 167 points at cos_fwd -1.0, d 35.3-59.8, and in all three azimuths plus the Z-vs-X top view it lies collinear with the fitted track extended backward (top-view slope dx/dz 2.36 against the fits 2.2), so it is this muons own upstream body, unfitted and split off by the clustering, and I tagged it muon rather than delta / other for that reason.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point profile over 100 cm; THRU on the profile alone, and here I can also see the exit -- a dead band immediately downstream in U, V and W at the fit end. The 8 cm 9.1e4 dot the chain calls the Michel is retagged delta / other under the THRU tag convention.
evidence: 102.9 cm straight chain in two segments, enters 0.1 cm from the z face and the fit ends 36.3 cm from the nearest wall. The 4x profile is dead flat: a ~5.2e4 plateau with the usual factor-two scatter runs the whole 100 cm and is still 4.5-5.5e4 at s = 1-12 cm, with no hint of a climb toward the muon reference curve; the only sub-plateau points are the last two, 3.9e4 and 1.9e4 at s = 0-1, which is the ordinary terminal-scatter case the rubric tells me to leave alone, not a sustained collapse off a peak -- there is no peak above plateau anywhere to collapse from. That is the operative THRU test and it settles the item. f_meas explains where it went: at the fit end (time slice ~1595) the track sits a few channels from a dead band in ALL THREE planes -- U 3450 with the band at 3425-3435, V 7205 with the band at 7195, W 11915 with the band at 11890 -- and the track is running toward decreasing channel in every plane, so it walks straight into dead material. The chain Michel object 164007 is a 2-point 0.9 cm dot at 9.1e4 e/cm sitting 8.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.08, bridged by the chain across 7.99 cm of empty space by proximity alone, and 53004 is a 5 cm pdg-11 shower blob at cos_fwd -1.0 hugging the body 18-21 cm back; 163006 is a faint 1.5e4 pair 50.5 cm out. On a through-goer none of these can be michel or gamma -- those tags need a stop -- so all three are delta / other and the kind is none. Range KE 257.6 MeV against MCS 524.9 MeV (amb 0.77) also says this muon is more energetic than its visible range.

notes: Awkward item, medium. The fit overshoots the charge by ~45 cm through a near-empty region, so the terminal collapse is a fit artefact, not the rubrics peak-then-collapse: there is no peak above plateau anywhere to collapse FROM, so I did not move the pin -- and moving it would not help, because at the real end of the charge (s ~ 45) the profile is still flat plateau with no Bragg. Competing reading is UNCLEAR, on the grounds that the last 45 cm of fit is not measuring anything; I rejected it because the 215 cm of real track that IS measured answers the question on its own. W has a dead band right at the pin channel (11765-11775), U and V do not, so a clean three-plane dead exit is not what ended this.
evidence: 260 cm chain in 12 fitted segments, enters 0.4 cm from the z face and the fit ends 133.8 cm from the nearest wall. From s = 100 cm down to s = 45 cm the profile is an ordinary 5.5-7e4 MIP plateau with no trend. Below s = 45 cm it does not rise -- it falls, smoothly and over 45 cm, into a low arch that tops out at 2.5e4 near s = 18 and sits at 0.5-1.5e4 (effectively zero-charge fit points) at s = 0-8 and s = 28-40. The 3-D azimuths say what that is: the dense spine ends in a knot of vertices about 45 cm short of the pin and the fit then runs on as a thin, almost charge-free dotted trail to the star, which is exactly the chains own profile_sparse rejection. So the real end of the charge is at s ~ 45, and THERE the profile is flat on its own plateau at 5.5e4 with no climb toward the muon reference curve -- no Bragg rise at either candidate end, which is the operative through-goer test. Nothing here can be a Michel: 45 cm of tail is twice the range of the most energetic Michel possible, and the chains own Michel object 222048 is a 2-point 0.4 cm dot at 8.5e4 sitting 13.1 cm out, bridged across 13.07 cm of empty space by proximity. Under the THRU tag convention all twelve fitted segments are muon and every other row -- 222048, the gamma-body-exclusion speck 223049 at 17.9 cm cos_fwd -0.98, the survey specks 224050 (42.4 cm) and 225051 (35.6 cm), and the six pdg-11 shower blobs at cos_fwd -0.98 to -1.0 hugging the body between 26 and 108 cm -- is delta / other, kind none. Range KE 600.4 MeV against MCS 457.4 MeV.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit; called THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs. Checked the undershoot explicitly: 244004 is forward-ish (cos_fwd 0.03) but at 0.18 of MIP and 10.9 cm out, i.e. the opposite of the several-times-MIP 2 cm tip that signature needs.
evidence: 72.9 cm chain in two segments, enters at the x (anode) face with d_face 0.0 and the fit ends 48.1 cm from that face, so containment is not the issue. On the 4x profile the data are a flat ~5e4 MIP plateau with ordinary factor-two scatter over the whole 73 cm, and the last 5 cm before the fit end are 7.2e4, 7.0e4, 5.5e4, 5.2e4, 3.7e4, 3.7e4 and one 2.35e4 point -- indistinguishable from the plateau 40 cm back, with no climb toward the muon reference curve at all. A stopping muon cannot do that, so this is a through-goer by the operative test. The one striking feature is a vertical stack of points at s = 39-40 cm reaching 1.10e5, 1.41e5 and 1.50e5: that is a localised delta blob 40 cm back on the body, not a terminal Bragg peak, and it has no counterpart at the end. What the chain offers as the Michel, 244004, is 3 points over 1.3 cm at 9.2e3 e/cm -- about 0.18 of MIP -- sitting 10.9 cm out at cos_fwd 0.03, bridged by proximity across 10.89 cm of empty space; 68003 is a 13 cm pdg-11 shower blob at cos_fwd -0.98 hugging the body 18-24 cm back. On a through-goer neither can be michel or gamma, so both are delta / other and the kind is none. f_meas shows measured and predicted agreeing and no dead band immediately downstream of the fit end in any plane -- the nearest is V at 7300-7310, about 50 channels away -- so this one just runs out of cluster; the rubric says that is still THRU. Range KE 193.7 MeV against MCS 528.6 MeV (amb 0.83) agrees.

notes: Medium, and the reason is worth recording: this items last 39 cm is not measured, not flat -- the fit interpolates 12 points across it at 0.2 MIP and there is a 29 cm stretch with literally no plotted point. I still called THRU rather than UNCLEAR because the measured part answers the question: at the last place charge exists (s ~ 39) the profile is already at or below its own plateau and only falls, and a stopping muon cannot hide a Bragg peak in two dead planes and show a fall in the third. If the owner wants a category for fits that run through dead material, this and 039349_44/66 are the two in my chunk. Pin not moved: there is no peak to collapse from.
evidence: 102.9 cm chain but only 88 chain points, and both ends are deep -- entry 40.4 cm and fit end 43.4 cm from the nearest z face -- so nothing about a wall is doing any work here. The 4x profile is charge-starved rather than flat: a real 4-6e4 plateau exists only for s = 60-103 cm, there is a thin scatter at s = 37-40 (4.2e4, 4.4e4, 1.9e4, 0.7e4), then a completely EMPTY stretch from s = 37 down to s = 8 with no points at all, and finally seven or eight points at s = 0-7 carrying 0.6-1.6e4, about 0.2 of MIP. The terminal chain segment 72001 says the same thing numerically: 12 points spread over 39.0 cm at mean 9192 e/cm. f_meas explains it -- the measured charge is three small isolated blobs, and in V the track sits at channel 7420-7430 which IS a dead band, and in W at 12200-12210 which is also a dead band, so most of this track lands in dead material in two of three planes. The three 3-D azimuths show the same object: three separated clumps lying roughly along one line with large empty gaps between them, i.e. one track with its middle unimaged, not an EM blob, so it is not MESSY. The decisive point is that nowhere in the measured part does the profile rise: it is at or below its own plateau at s = 37-40 and it only falls from there to the fit end, so there is no Bragg anywhere and no stop to hang a Michel or a gamma on. All five survey specks (dstop 30.5 to 59.0, cos_fwd -0.13 to -0.92, including the gamma-body-exclusion speck 270017) and the 8.7 cm pdg-11 shower blob 72013 at cos_fwd -0.99 on the body are therefore delta / other, kind none. Range KE 257.5 MeV against a dQ/dx KE of only 114.2 MeV is the missing-charge signature, and MCS could not be computed at all.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence on its own; the medium is for michel_kind. All three near specks are detached compact pieces 33-42 cm out and 15-36 cm off the muon line, clustered within ~50 deg of each other on one side of the ring, which is the rubrics gamma reading; if the owner instead reads three specks 30 cm apart from each other as scattered, or lets 282052s cos_fwd -0.9 keep it on the body line, the kind falls back to none while the verdict does not move. No undershoot and no overshoot here: the Bragg peak is AT the fit end.
evidence: 772 cm cosmic, enters 0.1 cm from the x (anode) face at [339.8, 158.0, 230.5] and stops at [-307.7, -103.8, 76.3], 32.2 cm from the anode face and comfortably inside. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the profile sits on a 5.5-7e4 plateau out beyond s = 20 cm, lifts to 7-8e4 at s = 15-20, 8-9.7e4 at s = 8-14, 1.00-1.08e5 at s = 3-6 and 1.03e5, 1.17e5, 1.23e5, 1.35e5 over the last 2 cm, hugging the shape of the muon reference curve the whole way in and topping out at exactly the 1.2-1.35e5 the rubric says real stoppers reach. It is monotone, not ragged, and there is no terminal collapse and no forward high-charge tip past the fit end, so neither fit-failure mode applies and I left the pin alone. Nothing is attached at the stop -- n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 -- so there is no Michel and the verdict is STM_ONLY. What IS there are three faint specks: 278050 (3 points, 1.1 cm, 1.2e4 e/cm) at 33.4 cm, 282052 (4 points, 1.7 cm, 3.5e4) at 35.3 cm and 281051 (2 points, 0.1 cm, 2.9e4) at 41.6 cm. Their transverse offsets from the muon line are 32, 15 and 36 cm, so all three are well clear of the body, and in all three 3-D azimuths they sit in open space below and to one side of the track with the star clean above them. Their unit vectors from the stop lie within 42-51 degrees of one another -- one side of the ring, not scattered in unrelated directions -- so by the faint-far-speck rule they are gammas, not deltas, and charge is explicitly not a criterion for that. The chain labels two of them gamma body exclusion, which the rubric tells me the off-axis judgement outranks; 282052 is the one that tests it, since its cos_fwd -0.9 formally trips the on-the-body clause while it actually sits 15 cm off the line. Three capture gammas past the stop and no michel piece give michel_kind detached dots without promoting the verdict. The four pdg-11 shower blobs 75034, 75040, 75043 and 75049 are 4.7-5.7 METRES back along the body at cos_fwd -0.97: delta / other. Range KE 1715.0 MeV against MCS 1613.4 MeV with amb 0.00 -- a consistent stopper.

notes: Undershoot candidate CHECKED AND REJECTED on the charge clause: 2.4 cm forward stub at cos_fwd 0.98 but only 0.65 MIP, so it is a stub carrying on past a non-stop, not a muon tip. Flat-then-sagging profile to the last point, dead band immediately downstream in U.
evidence: 263 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from the x face and the fit ends 33.1 cm from the nearest z wall. The 4x profile is a flat 5.5e4 plateau from s = 260 cm all the way in; over the last 20 cm it does not climb but sags -- 6.5-7.5e4 at s = 10-20, 4.5-5.6e4 at s = 3-9, and 3.1-3.5e4 over the last 2 cm, about 0.6 of its own plateau. Nothing anywhere approaches the muon reference curve. Two isolated points at s = 6 reach 1.03e5 and 1.10e5, but they are a 2-point delta spike on the body with 4.5-5.5e4 points either side of them, not a Bragg peak, and there is no sustained collapse off them. I checked the undershoot explicitly because this item has exactly the geometry for it: 16017 is a 2.4 cm fitted stub at d 0-2.11 with cos_fwd +0.98, dead ahead of the fit end. But its charge is 35843 e/cm, about 0.65 of MIP, where that signature requires 0.9-1.2e5, four to six times MIP. A partial match is not a match, so this is not a muon tip and the real stop is not past the fit end. What it IS, on a track whose profile never rises, is charge carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop -- which the rubric makes both a THRU indicator and a muon tag. f_meas agrees: in U the track runs toward increasing channel and its last point at ~1520 sits right against a dead band at 1525-1535, so it walks out through dead material. All five fitted segments are muon; 16014, a 5 cm pdg-11 shower blob at cos_fwd -1.0 hugging the body 80 cm back, is delta / other, kind none. Range KE 606.9 MeV, dQ/dx 649.9 MeV and MCS 625.3 MeV (amb 0.09) all agree, which on a track with no Bragg means a muon that kept going.

notes: My hardest item; medium, and the competing reading deserves the owners eye. I first wrote this as FRAG_STM_MICHEL with 25003 tagged michel, on the rubrics clause that a Michel topology is sufficient when the Bragg is unclear plus the shared-vertex attachment, and on the kinematic argument that a 27 MeV knock-on delta from a several-hundred-MeV muon is emitted within ~20 deg FORWARD, so nothing can put a real delta at this arms 169 deg kink. I reversed it because the rubric does not invite that kinematic override and does explicitly say to resolve michel-vs-delta on off-axis distance -- and my OWN measurement, not cos_fwd, puts the arm 0.3 cm off the muon line. Note what that leaves unexplained: a 27 MeV, 8.4 cm object attached at the stop vertex, running backward at 169 deg, ~2 cm off the body, which is neither a plausible delta nor, under the rule as written, a Michel. If the owner reads it as a backward Michel the item becomes FRAG_STM_MICHEL / attached; if as a mis-split piece of the muons own end it is FRAG_STM_ONLY with 25003 tagged muon; both readings need the arms 1.1-1.35e5 vertex points to stand in for a Bragg the chain itself does not have. FRAG: forced by the deep 59.2 cm entry. C61 is a poor collinear match in projection -- centroid exactly on the backward axis, but a side-view slope of dY/dZ ~ -0.63 against a chain that is nearly pure Y, i.e. a 20-25 deg kink -- so it may be an unrelated track that merely ends here, in which case the FRAG rests on the deep entry alone. Pin not moved: no peak-then-collapse and no forward several-times-MIP tip.
evidence: Only 47.4 cm of fitted chain and BOTH ends are deep -- entry 59.2 cm and fit end 58.0 cm from the nearest z face -- so a muon cannot have begun where this chain begins, which is why this carries the FRAG prefix. The chain runs at 69070 and 74233 e/cm, about 1.3 of MIP, which is what the last half-metre of a long muon should look like, and on the 4x profile it lifts from ~6.8e4 at s = 20-48 to 8-9e4 at s = 6-12 and then scatters between 3.2e4 and 8.6e4 over the last 5 cm. That is not a Bragg rise: the two fitted segment means differ by only 7 percent, the last centimetres FALL rather than climb, and the chain never gets within a third of the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches here. Every point in this item above 9e4 -- and it goes to 1.345e5 -- belongs to 25003, not to the chain. 25003 is the chains own Michel candidate, 15 points over 8.4 cm carrying 27.2 MeV, leaving the shared stop vertex 25000 itself rather than bridged across empty space. But I recomputed its geometry from the coordinates instead of trusting cos_fwd, because trap 5 warns that number lies on curved tracks, and it does not help it here: centroid 3.2 cm from the stop, unit vector (0.91, 0.375, -0.22) against the muons local backward unit (0.93, 0.37, -0.05), dot 0.996, so the arm runs back along the incoming line at about 0.3 cm off-axis at its centroid and no more than ~2 cm along its length -- the 3-D azimuths show it as a second strand lying just under the amber band, parallel to it. The governing collision paragraph says off-axis separation decides and that hugging the muon body is delta / other at any distance whatever the chain says, and 0.3 cm is as tightly hugging as a piece can be. With 25003 off the michel side of the ledger there is no decay activity clear of the body and no Bragg rise, so the item is a through-goer whose fit simply ran out of cluster 58 cm from the nearest wall. C61 is the presumed parent body -- 70 drawn points of a 312 cm cluster whose centroid sits at cos_fwd -1.000 (I checked: exactly antiparallel) 57.5 cm back, terminating right where this chain begins -- but the THRU tag convention admits only fitted chain segments as muon, so it goes to delta / other with 25003. Range KE 138.5 MeV against MCS 224.0 MeV (amb 0.88) is the usual through-goer mismatch.

notes: Flat and slightly sagging to the last point; THRU on the profile. Undershoot candidate CHECKED AND REJECTED: 133018 is forward at cos_fwd 0.97 but 10.6 cm out, detached across 9.69 cm of empty space, and at 0.9 MIP rather than several times MIP.

notes: Cleanest item in my chunk: monotone Bragg on the reference curve, no object of any kind past the stop, no dead band downstream. Pin unmoved; neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies.
evidence: 80.2 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from the z face at [254.3, 179.2, 297.9] and stops at [208.9, 184.3, 234.6], 63.9 cm from the nearest wall and well inside the volume. notes: Flat profile to the last point with no visible continuation to a face or dead region -- THRU on the profile test alone, per the rubric. evidence: 294 cm chain, enters 0.6 cm from the x (anode) face and the fit ends 58.6 cm from the nearest wall, so containment alone would suggest a stopper. The dQ/dx panel says otherwise. notes: The only judgement call was the two survey-only clusters: 20-26 cm off the chord would make them gammas if they were past the stop, but they are 40-51 cm back up the muon and on the far side from the Michel arm, so delta / other and kind stays attached rather than both.
evidence: 98 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the z face and the fit ends 15.9 cm from the anode face, deep enough to be a real stop. notes: Chain also calls it STM with no daughter; I reached STM_ONLY from the profile and the empty negative axis before reading that. notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead region -- the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. The 98 cm containment is the only thing arguing the other way and the rubric explicitly says the profile test governs.
evidence: 156 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the z face, and the fit ends 98.2 cm from the nearest wall and 26 cm from the cathode -- about as deeply contained as an end can be, which is why I looked hard at the profile before calling this. notes: Confidence medium for the kind, not the verdict: STM_ONLY is solid, but 208004 sits 13.7 cm past the stop and 48 cm off the body and would be a gamma by the letter of the gamma rule, which would make this detached dots. evidence: 112 cm chain, enters 0.1 cm from the x face and the fit ends 71.8 cm from the nearest wall, well inside. notes: Judged end is a 0.3 cm wall exit with in_fv 0 and a flat profile, so THRU is not in doubt. The drawn cluster is the x<0 half of a cathode-split cosmic; I record that in the evidence rather than as FRAG_THRU because the continuation is at the far end, not the end being judged.
evidence: 235 cm drawn cluster running almost horizontally along the floor of the detector, and the fit end sits 0.3 cm from the y wall with in_fv 0 -- it leaves through the bottom face. The profile confirms it independently: a flat 4.5-5.5e4 band from s=3 out to s=100 with the usual scatter, no lift off the plateau anywhere in the last 10-20 cm, and the five centimetres just before the end actually sag to 3.0-4.0e4. There are two high points sitting exactly at s=0 (9.9e4 and 7.6e4), which is the only thing that could be read as a Bragg tip, but identical excursions to 1.0-1.12e5 recur at s=22-26, s=43-48 and s=84-89 along the flat part of the same track, so they are this track s ordinary scatter and not a rise -- a Bragg is a sustained climb over 10-20 cm and there is none. The far end of the drawn cluster is a separate matter: it sits at x = -3.1, on the cathode plane, and the 3-D wide frame zoomed 4x shows a faint thinned trail continuing from the orange entry marker in nearly the same direction for about the same length again, with the end view showing it running on along the floor to x = +240. So the object is very likely one cosmic split at the cathode. I did not use a FRAG verdict for that, because the end I am judging -- the fit end at the y wall -- is a genuine exit and is not misdescribed by the plain verdict, and on a cathode-centred detector every crossing cosmic splits this way. Non-chain rows: 112026 is the grey cross at s = -27 on the panel, a 2-point 0.4 cm speck 20 cm back along the muon and 17.9 cm off the entry-stop chord, which the chain itself labels gamma body exclusion; 14014, 14017, 14020 and 14023 are pdg-11 shower pieces 87 to 210 cm back, all within 6.2 cm of the chord, i.e. body activity. notes: Hardest item in my chunk. Competing reading: overshoot, pin at rr 19.8 with 21003/21005/21018 retagged michel, giving STM_MICHEL / attached. I rejected it because the charge at the junction is MIP rather than several times MIP and the only high points are a 1.2 cm three-point spike matched elsewhere on the same track. Deep containment (131.9 cm) is the argument on the other side and is why this is medium, not high.
evidence: 225 cm chain entering 2.7 cm from the x face, and the fit end is 131.9 cm from the nearest wall, so this one had to be decided on the profile alone. It is the strangest panel in my chunk. From s=0 to s=17 the fit carries a dense chain of points at 0.4e4 to 1.8e4, i.e. 0.1 to 0.4 of this track s 4.3-5.5e4 MIP; it then climbs steeply through 2.1, 2.7, 3.3e4 at s=17.7-18.8 and joins the plateau at 4.3e4 by s=19.5. The object table explains the shape: rows 21003, 21005 and 21018 have sizes 8.0, 3.9 and 7.9 cm, 19.8 cm of arc in total, yet every one of their points lies within 4.3 cm of the pin in 3-D -- the fit is coiled into a small ball. The 8x crop of frames d and e shows exactly that: the amber selection band is a tight coil of about ten overlapping markers hanging off the junction at an angle to the spine, with only faint scattered image points around it, and f_meas confirms near-zero measured charge over that whole window. I took the overshoot reading seriously, because peak-then-collapse is what this looks like at first sight, and read the s=15-40 window at 12x to test it. It fails: approaching the junction from s=40 the profile is flat at 4.3-5.5e4 with two narrow spikes -- 6.8-8.2e4 across s=28.7-29.8 and 6.2, 9.0, 10.2, 11.3e4 across s=22.0-24.0 -- and the spike is only about 1.2 cm wide, dropping straight back to 6.2e4 at s=22.0 and 4.3e4 through s=19.5-22. A Bragg is a sustained climb over 10-20 cm, not a three-point spike, and comparable isolated excursions to 1.02e5 and 1.23e5 sit at s=90 on the same track. Decisively, the charge at the junction itself, where the muon would have to be at three to five times MIP if it stopped there, is 4.3e4 -- exactly MIP. So the muon does not stop; its charge simply ends at MIP around s=19 and the remaining 19.8 cm of fit is a tangle through near-empty space. Every row is a fitted chain segment, all tagged muon, and with no stop there is no gamma or michel to define, so kind none.

notes: LOW, and my only outright disagreement with the chain (it says no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0 and reports no daughter). Two independent doubts: the 1.37e5 tip sits inside a coiled segment so its dQ/dx denominator is unreliable, and 54010 could be a hard delta ray thrown 4.7 cm before the stop rather than the Michel -- cos_fwd cannot separate them because the local tangent at the stop is inside the coil. The competing verdicts are STM_ONLY / none if 54010 is a delta, or THRU if the coil is a fit end that is not a stop. I went with STM_MICHEL on off-chord separation plus attachment, per the rubric tie-break, but this row deserves the owner eye more than any other in my chunk.
evidence: 129 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode face, fit end 61.8 cm from the nearest wall. Read at 9x the profile is ragged: the plateau from s=20 out is 4.5-6e4, a compact ten-point arc sits at 8.5-9.3e4 across s=11.7-17.5, the band drops back to 4.8-5.4e4 at s=8-11 and then to a real hole of 1.5-3.3e4 across s=2.3-7, and the last centimetre and a half comes back up through 4.9e4 and 7.6e4 to 1.12e5 and 1.37e5 sitting on the origin. I originally leaned on that 1.37e5 as the Bragg peak, and I no longer trust it, which is why this is low. Rows 54006 (10.5 cm of arc) and 54003 (7.0 cm) both lie entirely within 4.7 cm of the pin -- the fit is coiled -- and the 10x crops of frames d and e show it plainly: an amber lambda-shaped band plus a small blue hook, all inside a few centimetres of the star. The origin sits inside 54006, i.e. inside the coil, so its dQ/dx denominator is the fit step length, which is wrong in both directions where a fit doubles back: too long where it runs on, giving the 1.5-3.3e4 hole at s=2-7, and too short where it folds, which can inflate a point to 1.37e5. I am therefore treating both the hole and the peak as unreliable and resting the verdict on geometry instead. What survives is row 54010: 24 points, 13.7 cm, 4.33e4 e/cm, the pink dotted arm running up and away in frames d and e with its own image points following it, branching off the junction at d = 4.7 cm from the pin. I measured it at 8.6 cm off the entry-stop chord, so it is well clear of the muon body line, it is attached at the junction, and its d_min of 4.7 cm puts it inside the radius where the rubric says direction does not discriminate. 13.7 cm at MIP is the right range for a roughly 30 MeV electron, and the rubric allows STM_MICHEL on a Michel topology alone even when the Bragg peak is unclear, which is exactly the situation. The overshoot does not apply on the ordering: its signature is peak, then sustained collapse, then the fit end, and here the hole is at s=2-7 with the high points AT the last point, so the pin stays. The remaining rows are body or bystander: 54009 is a 6-point 2.6 cm pdg-11 speck 98 cm back and 3.2 cm off the chord, and 211011 is a 2-point survey speck 48.7 cm out but 21.5 cm BACK along the muon and 43.7 cm off the chord, in an unrelated direction -- both delta / other, so the kind is attached rather than both.

notes: The W plane has dead-channel bands adjacent to the track in f_meas but the U and V measured panels carry the stop cleanly, so the Bragg is not a dead-region artefact. Chain agrees (is_stm 1) but calls 222018 the Michel object; I disagree on that one row -- across a 9 cm empty gap it is a detached dot.
evidence: 265 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.3e4 plateau beyond s=40 climbing smoothly along the solid muon curve through 6.0e4 at s=20, 6.7-7.5e4 at s=10-18, 8.7-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.5-1.02e5 at s=3-4, 1.14-1.22e5 at s=1.5-2.5 and 1.39e5 at s=0.5, with the row mean for the last segment 58015 quoted at 1.05e5 over its 7.8 cm. Past the stop there is exactly one thing: 222018, two points spanning 0.3 cm, 9.3 cm from the stop, 7.3 cm past it and 5.7 cm off the entry-stop chord, carrying 2.0e4 e/cm and 0.5 MeV, and the chain itself records that it was bridged to the stop vertex across 9.11 cm of EMPTY space rather than by a graph edge. f_meas confirms the gap: in all three planes the speck is a single isolated brown dot at time slice 1058 with a clean charge-free break below it before the track s own hits resume at 1040. Two gammas and no michel gives detached dots.

notes: UNDERSHOOT-SHAPED but below the rubric threshold: 63027 is a 1.6 cm forward tip past the fit end that the chain types pdg 11, which is the undershoot geometry exactly, but its 9.18e4 is 1.67x this track MIP rather than the several-times-MIP the rubric requires before invoking it. I tagged it muon anyway because it sits 0.5 cm off the muon axis and is above MIP, so it cannot be an electron first centimetres -- I am NOT counting this as a clean undershoot. Competing reading for the whole item is THRU on the grounds that the rise only reaches 1.5x plateau and single points elsewhere on the track go higher.
evidence: 330 cm chain, enters 6.2 cm from the z face and the fit ends 142.6 cm from the nearest wall -- the most deeply contained end in my chunk. The rise is real but modest, which is why this is medium. Read at 9x the top envelope goes 5.5e4 at s=100, 6.0e4 at s=60, 6.5e4 at s=30, 6.9-7.4e4 at s=6-10 and 7.4-8.1e4 at s=1-2, a monotone climb of about 1.5x over the last 30 cm that follows the shape of the solid muon curve without ever approaching it; the plateau band itself sits at 5.4-6.5e4 with a low branch down to 2.4e4 at s=13-30. Against that, isolated excursions to 1.0e5 at s=43-48 and 1.28e5 at s=35 are higher than anything near the stop, so I would not call this rise strong -- but it is monotone over 30 cm, which a delta spike is not. Row 63027 is the interesting one: 4 points, 1.6 cm, 9.18e4 e/cm mean, centroid 0.4 cm PAST the fit end and only 0.5 cm off the entry-stop chord, i.e. carrying straight on along the muon axis, and the chain types it pdg 11. It plots as the green marker just left of the origin at 7.1e4. An electron s first centimetres are at or below MIP and this is 1.67x this track s MIP, so it is not an electron; it is the muon s own last centimetres and the true stop is about 1.6 cm beyond the fit s last point. Tagged muon under the stub-carrying-straight-on rule. Past the stop the ring holds three compact specks, all well clear of the body: 226023 (2 points, 0.3 cm) 17.0 cm out, 2.8 cm past the stop and 16.7 cm off the chord, which the chain itself calls a capture gamma at 2.03 MeV; 225022 (3 points, 1.2 cm) 20.7 cm out and 20.5 cm off; and 227024 (2 points, 0.2 cm) 11.9 cm out and 11.4 cm off. I measured them 37, 41 and 78 degrees apart as seen from the stop, i.e. a coherent cone on one side rather than scattered round the ring, and all three are detached compact dots, so gamma for all three. 231025 is the opposite case -- 4 points 17.2 cm BACK along the muon at cos_fwd -1.00 and only 2.1 cm off the chord, hugging the body: delta / other. Three gammas and no michel gives detached dots, and capture gammas do not promote STM_ONLY.

notes: Flat to the last point. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) but the call came from the plot. Not a fragment: only 1 thinned context point in the whole event and no continuation past either end.
evidence: 298 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode face; the fit end is 28.9 cm from the z wall, close enough to a face to be an exit and far enough that the profile still had to decide it. The profile is flat: read at 9x the band sits at 5.4-6.5e4 from s=0 continuously out to s=100, lying on the solid muon curve s asymptote the whole way, with no lift off it anywhere in the last 10-20 cm. The only thing at the origin is a single yellow point at about 8.9e4, and that cannot be a Bragg -- the same track throws isolated excursions to 1.0e5 at s=22 and s=78, 1.09-1.10e5 at s=36, 40 and 56, 1.17e5 at s=46 and 1.20e5 at s=35, i.e. half a dozen points further back that are HIGHER than the one at the stop. A Bragg is a sustained climb over 10-20 cm and there is nothing of the kind; the last ten centimetres before the origin (5.4-6.5e4) are indistinguishable from the plateau a metre away.
