Only three rows: two fitted chain segments, tagged muon, and 48004, a 7-point 3.5 cm pdg-11 shower speck 170 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1.00 and 1.1 cm off the entry-stop chord, which is body activity. On a through-goer there is no stop, so delta / other and kind none. The orange entry marker sits mid-track in the projections here rather than at an end, which is the known display trap and not evidence about either end.

notes: Nothing borderline here. The only judgement was gamma versus michel for 137001, and the 60-slice charge-free gap in f_meas plus its two-point zero-extent size settles it as a detached dot.
evidence: 143 cm single-segment chain entering 17.0 cm from the z face and ending 72.9 cm from the nearest wall, well inside. The dQ/dx panel is the best-behaved in my chunk: the data do not merely rise, they sit ON the solid muon curve for the last 20 cm. Plateau 5.2-5.5e4 beyond s=50, then 6.0e4 at s=15, 6.5-7.0e4 at s=10-12, 7.2-8.0e4 at s=8-10, 8.4-8.7e4 at s=3-4, 9.3-9.8e4 at s=6-7, 1.04e5 at s=2, 1.23e5 at s=1 and 1.44e5 and 1.49e5 at the origin. That is a factor of 2.8 over the track s own MIP, monotone, and the two highest points sit exactly where the curve puts them, so the pin does not move; there is no sustained collapse anywhere in the last 20 cm and nothing forward of the fit end at all, so neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies. The only other row is 137001, a two-point object of zero extent carrying 0.30 MeV in total, sitting 29.8 cm from the stop, 18.8 cm PAST it and 23.2 cm off the entry-stop chord -- isolated, compact, well clear of the muon body line and inside the 60 cm ring, which is the gamma rule exactly. f_meas shows it as a single brown dot at time slice 468 in all three planes with the track s own hits stopping at 410, a clean charge-free break of nearly 60 time slices, so it is detached rather than attached and cannot be the Michel; its 1.58e5 e/cm is not a counter-argument since charge is explicitly not a criterion for this tag. The chain agrees and books it as a capture gamma. One gamma and no michel gives detached dots, and a capture gamma does not promote STM_ONLY to STM_MICHEL. Frames c, d and e show a clean uniform amber band ending at the star with empty space beyond and no arm of any kind.

notes: THRU on a flat/scattered profile alone: no continuation is visible past the fit end, but the last points sit inside the entry islands own charge spread and the profile falls into the fit end rather than rising. The 50 cm charge hole makes the plateau poorly defined, which is what keeps this at medium rather than high; the competing reading is STM_ONLY on the s~6 excursion to 9.9e4 being a real ragged Bragg peak with an overshooting fit, but that would need a sustained collapse after it and the last points are ABOVE the plateau, not below.
evidence: 74.1 cm of fit from an entry 1.4 cm off the x (anode) face to a fit end only 3.2 cm from the y wall, in_fv 0. The charge is in two islands with a ~50 cm hole between them (chain reject profile_sparse is right): points at s=62-75 near the entry and points at s=0-10 near the fit end, nothing in the middle, and f_meas confirms only one short blob of real charge with the fit line bridging the rest. The entry island itself scatters from 1.2e4 to 8.6e4 with its bright points at 4.8-8.6e4, so the tracks own plateau is broad. The last two points before the fit end are 6.9e4 and 7.2e4 - inside that same island spread, not above it - and the profile shape is wrong for a Bragg: it peaks at s~6 (9.9e4, 9.4e4) and comes DOWN into the stop, whereas the muon reference curve climbs monotonically as s goes to 0. Points at the same s range straddle 1.2e4 to 9.9e4, so the excursion at s~6 is scatter, not a rise off a plateau. Flat-to-scattered to the last point plus a fit end sitting on the y wall reads as a through-goer that left through the wall. Not the overshoot case (the last points are above, not below, the plateau, so no sustained collapse to bridge) and not the undershoot case (no short forward piece at several times MIP). Past the fit end there is one 0.1 cm two-point speck 14.6 cm out, 6.6 cm forward and 13.0 cm off the muon line (my own cen-minus-stop projection reproduces its cos_fwd 0.45 exactly, so the track is not curved here and cos_fwd is trustworthy); on a stopper that would read as a detached gamma, but on a THRU there is no stop to define gamma or michel, so it is delta / other. The three survey specks 36-50 cm out at cos_fwd -0.75 to -0.95 hug the muon body line, and the 6 cm pdg-211 stub at the far entry end is a different object.

notes: OVERSHOOT: fit runs about 4.3 cm past the real muon stop into the Michel; pin moved to rr 4.31. The collapse actually starts around s=6, so the last ~1.7 cm of segment 54031 is also bridge charge - that row is split and is tagged muon for what most of its 212 cm is. Confidence medium is about the pin position, not the verdict: the STM_MICHEL topology (contained end, attached 9.8 cm kinked MIP arm) is clear. The chain rejects no_bragg / shape_flat and is_stm 0, i.e. the reconstruction misses this one; the rise to 1.6x plateau is modest but it is a rise, and the collapse after it is what the chain read as flat.
evidence: 321 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the z face and ending 61.6 cm from the nearest face, in_fv 1 - deeply contained, so containment is not the question. The plateau from s=20 out to s=100 sits on the muon curve at about 5.5e4. Coming in toward the fit end the profile lifts off it - 6.3e4 at s=20, a bump to 8.0e4 at s=14, and a pair at 8.5e4 at s=7.2-7.8, about 1.6x plateau - and then falls monotonically and without recovery over the last 7 cm: 6.8e4 at s=6.1, 5.3/4.9e4 at s=5.6, 4.3e4 at s=4.4, 3.5e4 at s=3.9, 2.7e4 at s=3.3, 2.1e4 at s=2.9 and 1.1e4 down to 0.4e4 inside the last 3 cm. That is the peak-then-sustained-collapse signature, not one low last point: the last chain segment 54029 carries dqdx 24957, 0.47 of the plateau, exactly the band the rubric describes for a fit bridging a gap between the muon stop and the electron. The three 3-D azimuths show it directly - the green high-charge spine runs up to a vertex, and the fit star sits a short way along a separate low-charge arm that leaves that vertex at a large angle and carries on past the star. So the pin goes back to the 54031/54029 junction at rr 4.31 and 54029 is Michel charge, not muon. Past the corrected stop, 54030 is a 9.8 cm 17-point arm attached at the shared stop vertex, kink 59 deg, dqdx 46368 which is at MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so it is a second particle, and 9.8 cm and 21.8 MeV are right for a Michel. 158033 is a 0.3 cm two-point speck 27.6 cm out; my own decomposition puts it 4.0 cm behind the stop but 27.9 cm off the muon line, with a transverse direction cos +0.99 to the Michel arms own offset - it is on the Michel side, detached across a clean gap well past the arms 9 cm end, so gamma rather than michel. 157032 sits 31 cm back and 24.7 cm off with its transverse direction cos -0.91 to the arm, i.e. the opposite side and an unrelated direction: delta / other despite its 1.5e5 charge. The 6 cm pdg-11 shower 205 cm back hugs the body (perp 2.5 cm) and is body activity. A dead V-channel band clips the stop region but U and W cover it and measured-minus-predicted is clean there.

notes: The four michel rows are absent from g_dqdx entirely (77 points and 16 cm of charge missing from the panel), so the michel evidence is the object table plus the three azimuths, not the dQ/dx plot. The chain typed 64011 pdg 13 and grouped it muon, but it starts at the stop, runs forward and carries 0.26 of MIP, so it is the head of the electron, not muon body.
evidence: 423 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and stopping 35.0 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1; the projections show one clean spine with no companion, so containment is not in doubt. The profile is a textbook rise: flat on the muon curve at about 5.4e4 from s=100 in to s=40, then 6.2e4 at s=30, 6.5e4 at s=20, 7.5e4 at s=10, 8.0e4 at s=5 and 8.2-8.6e4 at the last two points. That is a smooth 1.6x climb off the plateau over the last 30 cm following the shape of the muon reference curve, and it runs all the way to the fit end with no terminal collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. The chain reject shape_flat is wrong here. Past the stop the display draws four forward pieces that my own decomposition places 1.4 to 7.9 cm ahead of the stop and only 1.9-7.1 cm off the muon line: 64011 (10 pts, 5.2 cm, dqdx 13979, attached at d_min 0), then 64008 (14 pts, 8.0 cm, 27935), 64004 (26 pts, 14.9 cm, 11007) and 64003 (27 pts, 15.7 cm, 18041), all starting 4.0-4.7 cm out and reaching 15-16 cm. All four sit at 0.2-0.5 of MIP, and the three 3-D azimuths show them as a diffuse fan of points that opens out from the very last muon point rather than a second track - an EM shower attached at the stop. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at a quarter of MIP, so this is the decay electron and its shower; 67 points over 16 cm is right for a Michel. This is not the undershoot case: the forward pieces are at or below MIP, not the several-times-MIP tip that would mean the fit stopped short. All four are contiguous with the stop through 64011, so they are one attached arm, tagged michel, and there is no detached dot anywhere in the 60 cm ring. None of these four appear in the dQ/dx panel at all - the panel shows nothing on the negative axis - which is the known census trap, so the object table carried this call. No dead channel touches the stop in U, V or W and measured minus predicted is clean there.

notes: The three michel rows and all three specks are absent from g_dqdx, so the attribution rests on the object table plus the azimuths. The soft call is 213015/215017: their transverse direction is about 65 deg from the Michel arm, so they are on the decay side of the stop but not along the arm - I read them as capture gammas in the ring rather than deltas because they sit 46 cm off the muon body and nothing hugs the body here. This does not move michel_kind: 214016 alone already makes it both.
evidence: A short 34.2 cm 58-point chain, entering 1.0 cm from the z face and ending 23.7 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1 - a low-energy muon (109 MeV KE) that came in through the boundary and stopped well inside. The profile is the cleanest rise I have seen so far: 4.9-5.5e4 at s=34, 6.3-7.0e4 at s=30, a scattered 6-8.5e4 band from s=25 down to s=5, then 9.3e4, 10.2e4 and 10.4e4 at the last three points - a factor 1.9 climb off the plateau that follows the muon reference curve and runs right into the fit end, with no terminal collapse, so the pin stays. Three high outliers at 1.1-1.7e5 sitting 28-34 cm back are delta activity on the body, not the end. Past the stop the display draws a connected forward structure that the panel does not show at all (nothing on the negative axis - the census trap): 65019, 6 points over 4.7 cm attached at d_min 0 and lying straight ahead at perp 0.4 cm carrying 30973 e/cm, then 65014, 15 points over 8.2 cm at 3.8 cm forward and 2.9 cm off carrying 56013, then 65009, 13 points over 18.0 cm fanning out to 16.3 cm off the line at only 7618 e/cm. In the three azimuths this is a diffuse spray opening out from the last muon point, not a track carrying on. A muon that has just reached 1.04e5 at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at half MIP and then at a seventh of MIP, so this is the decay electron and its shower - about 30 cm and 34 points, right for a Michel. Not the undershoot case: the forward tip is at 0.5 MIP, not the several-times-MIP piece that would mean the fit stopped short. Three detached specks sit further out: 214016 (4 pts, 1.6 cm, 38.4 cm away) lies 38.9 cm off the muon line with its transverse direction cos +0.91 to the Michel arms own offset - squarely on the Michel side and far clear of the body, so gamma; 213015 and 215017 (2 pts each, 53-57 cm away) are a coherent pair 46 cm off the line and 27-35 cm forward of the stop, i.e. in the decay hemisphere rather than on the body, so gamma as well. The V plane has a dead band right where the track ends, but U and W both cover the stop and measured minus predicted is clean.

notes: THRU on a flat profile alone, as the rubric allows: there is no visible continuation past the fit end, no face within 53 cm, and no dead-region exit at the star itself - the cluster just ends. The strongest evidence is the peel-away from the muon curve over the last 15 cm; the chain reached the same reading (no_bragg, shape_flat).
evidence: A short, straight, isolated 64.2 cm cluster with both ends floating inside the volume - the far end 14.6 cm from the z face, the fit end 53.5 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1 - so containment cannot decide this one and the profile has to. The dQ/dx band sits on the muon curve at 5.5-7.0e4 all the way in from s=64 and then simply stays there: 5.8-6.5e4 at s=40, 6.0-6.5e4 at s=20, 6.3e4 at s=5 and 6.0-6.4e4 at the last two points, with a single 8.45e4 outlier at s=0. The muon reference curve over that same stretch climbs from 6.5e4 at s=20 to 8e4 at s=8 and 1.6e5 at s=0, so the data peels away from the curve over the last 15 cm instead of following it. That is no Bragg rise at the fit end, which is the operative test, and a stopping muon cannot end at plateau. The three 3-D azimuths show a plain straight segment with nothing at all past the star - no arm, no dots, no fanning - and the object table agrees: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the only companion is 15003, an 8-point 4.5 cm shower piece 15.5 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1.0 and 1.2 cm off the line, i.e. body activity, so delta / other. In f_meas the cluster is bracketed by dead U channel bands at roughly 1400-1440 and 1495-1525 and its charge stops right at the lower band, which is the ordinary way a through-going cosmic fragment ends: the imaging ran out. The high-charge outliers at 1.1-1.5e5 scattered 10-56 cm back are deltas on the body, not an end effect. Nothing here is close to the overshoot signature (no peak and no terminal collapse) or the undershoot signature (no forward high-charge tip). The orange entry circle sits mid-track rather than at the far end, which is the known display trap and does not mark a start.

notes: Medium, not high: the competing reading is a very ragged STM_ONLY built on the 1.03e5 point at s=0.7 and the 8.4e4 at s=4. I rejected it because the other five points in the same last 5 cm are at or below plateau and because the same event shows an unmistakable delta population at 1.1-1.6e5 further back, so a lone high point near the end is not distinguishable from one of those. 17001 sits past the far end and would be a carrying-on stub under the muon rule, but on a THRU the regime is fitted chain segments muon and everything else delta / other, so it is tagged delta / other.
evidence: 84.3 cm chain running almost parallel to the z wall, entering 0.5 cm from it and ending 9.2 cm from the same z face and 13.9 cm from the anode face - a corner stop, so the geometry already argues for an exit, and in_fv 1 only just. The profile never develops a coherent Bragg. The band sits at 4-6.5e4 from s=84 in to s=60 and at 5-8e4 from s=60 to s=10, tracking the muon curve while the curve is still flat. Over the last 5 cm, where 141 points at 0.6 cm spacing give about eight samples, the values are 1.03e5 at s=0.7, 8.4e4 at s=4, then 5.0e4, 4.85e4 and 4.7e4 at s=1-3 and 3.65e4 and 2.95e4 at the last two points - a median of about 4.9e4, i.e. still at plateau, while the muon reference curve over that same stretch demands 8.3e4 at s=4 and 1.3e5 at s=1. So the profile falls below the curve at the end instead of climbing above it, which is the operative THRU test. The single 1.03e5 point at s=0.7 and the 1.16e5 at s=8 sit in a population of clear delta rays (five more points at 1.1-1.6e5 scattered 35-60 cm back along the body), so I do not read them as the Bragg. The three azimuths show a plain slightly-curved track that stops dead at the star with nothing past it - no arm, no dots, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 in the object table too - and in f_meas the charge ends right against a solid channel boundary at U 1672 with the V and W ends similarly close to boundaries, which is how a track that leaves the imaged region ends. Not the overshoot case: the two low last points span under 1 cm, which is ordinary terminal scatter rather than a sustained collapse, and there is no Michel anywhere for a bridge to run to, so the pin stays. The only companion object is 17001, a 3.6 cm seven-point pdg-211 stub sitting past the FAR end at cos_fwd -1.0 and 0.3 cm off the body line - a different object on the body, not decay charge.

notes: Not counted as an overshoot. The profile has the peak (1.40e5 at s=3.7) and a five-point collapse over the last 2.5 cm, but the rubric signature is a sustained collapse INTO something the fit then bridges, and here there is no daughter at all - so I left the pin alone rather than assert a bridge with no far end. Medium confidence is about exactly that decision; the verdict STM_ONLY and kind detached dots hold either way, since moving the stop back 3 cm would only push the two gammas from 18.9/29.5 cm to about 22/32 cm and change no tag.
evidence: 261.5 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the x face and ending 115.9 cm from every face - about as deeply contained as this set gets, and a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show one clean curved spine with no larger parent, so the profile is the only question. It answers clearly: the band sits on the muon curve at 5.4e4 from s=100 in to s=25, lifts to 6.5e4 at s=18, 7.6-8.2e4 over s=6-11, then 9.4e4 at s=4.9, 1.15e5 at s=4.2, 1.40e5 at s=3.7 and 1.15e5 at s=3.0 - a 2.6x rise following the shape of the muon curve, and the highest charge anywhere on the 261 cm track. The last five points, s=2.5 down to s=0.15, then run 5.5e4, 4.8e4, 4.8e4, 3.3e4, 2.9e4, a monotone decline over 2.5 cm to half plateau. I checked that against the overshoot signature and it fails the third clause: there is nothing past the fit end for the fit to have bridged into. n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and all three azimuths show the spine ending at the star with no attached charge of any kind, the nearest object being a detached piece 18.9 cm away. A collapse with no far end is a terminal dip, not a bridge, so the pin stays at the fit last point and the 2.5 cm decline is recorded here rather than acted on. Past the stop the display draws two detached green pieces and nothing else: 137021, 9 points over 4.8 cm, 16.8 cm forward of the stop and 11.0 cm off the muon line, and 141023, 4 points over 1.7 cm, 26.8 cm forward and 12.9 cm off. Both are separated from the stop by a clean charge-free gap - attachment is what decides between michel and gamma - so they are detached dots, and compact 4.8 cm and 1.7 cm pieces at 3.8e4 and 1.0e4 are far too small and too far out to be a 35 MeV electron. Capture gammas do not promote this to STM_MICHEL, so STM_ONLY with kind detached dots. The last object, 140022, is a 2-point speck 54.6 cm away and 55.7 cm off the muon line, so nowhere near the body, but its transverse direction is cos -0.95 against both gammas - the opposite side of the 60 cm ring, an unrelated direction - so delta / other. No dead channel touches the stop in U, V or W.

notes: Medium: the competing reading is STM_ONLY with the pin moved back to about rr 8, taking the 1.28e5 cluster as the Bragg peak. I rejected it on the coexistence argument (normal-charge points interleaved with the high ones at the same s) and on the geometry (perfectly straight through, no kink, nothing past the star). Note also that the last 8 cm sits AT MIP, not at the 0.15-0.5 of MIP that the rubric describes for a bridged over-run, so even under that reading it would not be the overshoot signature - and there is no daughter for a bridge to end on.
evidence: 216 cm chain entering 1.5 cm from the y face and ending 33.3 cm from the same y wall, in_fv 1; a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show one gently curved spine with no parent object, so this is not a fragment. The plateau from s=20 out to s=100 sits at 4.0-5.5e4 with a median near 4.5e4. Over the last 8 cm the values are 5.02e4, 4.87e4, 4.72e4, 4.57e4, 4.47e4, 4.37e4, 4.27e4, 3.63e4, 3.38e4, 3.08e4 - that is the same plateau, not a rise, while the muon reference curve over that stretch demands 8e4 at s=5 and 1.6e5 at s=0. No Bragg rise at the fit end is the operative THRU test and it fails cleanly here. There IS a striking cluster of six points at 9.1e4 to 1.28e5 between s=8.4 and s=12.5, and I weighed reading that as the real Bragg peak with the fit over-running by 8 cm. Two things rule it out. First, the elevated points COEXIST with ordinary ones at the same arc length - 6.9e4 at s=9.6 and 6.3e4 at s=7.6 and s=10.1 sit right among the 1e5 points - and a Bragg peak lifts every point in its range whereas a delta ray lifts only the points it overlaps. Second, all three azimuths show the track running dead straight through that region and on to the star with no kink, no fan and no second arm, and e_3d_stop shows a small protrusion hanging off the body right about there, which is what a knock-on electron looks like. So the cluster is a delta on the body, the muon is at plateau to its last point, and the fit end is not a stop. Nothing at all lies past the star: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring, and the only two companions are 46005 (6 pts, 3.1 cm) and 46008 (8 pts, 4.1 cm), both 172-182 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1.0 and 1.7-3.1 cm off the line, i.e. body activity. On a THRU there is no stop to define gamma or michel, so those two are delta / other and the kind is none. In f_meas the charge ends at time slice 1590 in all three planes with no dead band at that end; the cluster simply stops being imaged.

notes: High confidence: this is not a marginal flat profile, it actually DECLINES into the fit end, so both the STM_ONLY and the pin-move readings fail at the first step. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). Nothing here resembles the overshoot signature (no peak to collapse from) or the undershoot signature (the forward piece 58012 is at MIP, not several times MIP).
evidence: A short 32.5 cm 56-point cluster entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 15.1 cm from that same z wall; a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show a small isolated object with no larger parent, so it is not a fragment, but it is also too short to carry much information other than the profile. The profile settles it, and it goes the wrong way: the highest chain charges are in the MIDDLE, 6.3-6.7e4 at s=15-20 and 5.9-6.4e4 at s=25-30, while the last 5 cm reads 5.55e4, 5.5e4, 5.3e4, 5.1e4, 4.7e4 and 4.0e4. So the profile falls from about 6.5e4 to about 5.0e4 going into the fit end, whereas the muon reference curve over that stretch climbs from 6.4e4 at s=15 to 8.3e4 at s=5 and 1.6e5 at s=0. The data peels away from the curve over the last 15 cm and there is no rise of any kind at the end - not ragged, not partial - which is the operative THRU test. The mean dQ/dx of the two chain rows makes the same point: 49940 for the body 11-31 cm back and 49667 for the last 10.9 cm, i.e. identical. All three azimuths show a plain slightly-curved track running to the star with nothing past it but a couple of faint dots. The two low-charge families visible in the panel are 58007, an 11-point 5.7 cm pdg-11 shower piece 9 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0 and 0.4 cm off the line (it is the orange group at s = -8 to -11, plotted at minus its distance), and 58012, a 0.7 cm two-point piece sitting essentially ON the stop, 0.3 cm forward and 0.0 cm off the line at 48330 e/cm - charge continuing straight past the fit end at MIP, which is itself a THRU indication rather than a Michel: a 2-point 0.7 cm speck is not a 35 MeV electron and there is no arm behind it. The remaining object 209010 is a 2-point speck 58.8 cm out and 52 cm off the muon line. On a THRU there is no stop to define gamma or michel, so all three non-chain rows are delta / other and the kind is none. In f_meas the V-plane end of the track abuts a channel boundary at about V 6855; U and W show no dead band at the end.

notes: High: the profile does not merely fail to rise, it falls into the fit end, so neither STM_ONLY nor a pin move is on the table. Note C15 is a 118-point 51.5 cm unfitted cluster, big enough to be tempting, but it sits 44 cm BEHIND the stop and 32 cm off the line - a neighbouring object, not decay charge, and it never appears on the dQ/dx panel (it is past the -40 cm axis limit), which is the census trap again.
evidence: 71.3 cm chain entering 7.0 cm from the y face and ending 41.6 cm from the anode face, in_fv 1, so it is neither wall-adjacent nor deeply buried and the profile has to decide. It is as flat as anything in this chunk: the band runs 4.5-6.0e4 from s=70 all the way in to s=2, sitting on the muon curve while the curve is flat and then staying put once the curve turns up. The last six points read 5.15e4, 5.1e4, 3.95e4, 3.8e4, 2.45e4 and 1.05e4 - if anything a decline - against a reference curve that demands 8.3e4 at s=5 and 1.6e5 at s=0. The two chain rows carry the same message: 48232 for the 3.5 cm stub at the far end and 51340 for the 67.7 cm main segment. No Bragg rise at the fit end is the operative test and it fails outright. The four high points (1.41e5 at s=15, 1.28e5 and 9.8e4 and 8.85e4 around s=34, 8.85e4 at s=19) are scattered deltas on the body, nowhere near the end. All three azimuths show a dead-straight track running to the star with nothing past it - no arm, no dots, no fan - and the object table agrees: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring. The two companions are both well behind and well off to the side: 232003, a 4-point 1.8 cm speck 45 cm away, 28.9 cm behind the stop and 35.3 cm off the muon line, and C15, an unfitted 118-point 51.5 cm cluster 47.9-60 cm away, 43.6 cm behind and 32.1 cm off. Their transverse directions are identical to each other (cos +1.00), so they are two pieces of one separate object lying beside the muon, which b_3d_wide and c_3d_stop show plainly as a distinct elongated cloud with its own vertex marker. That object belongs to something else entirely, and in any case on a THRU there is no stop to define gamma or michel, so both are delta / other and the kind is none. In f_meas the track crosses a dead U band at about channel 515-555 mid-way but ends clear of it at channel 575, with time slices still available well below the end, so this is not a readout edge - the cluster simply stops being imaged.

notes: High confidence and nothing marginal about it: one object, a flat profile that declines rather than rises into the fit end, and no candidate decay charge anywhere. The orange entry circle is drawn right at the fit end rather than at the far end here, which is the known display trap - I read the ends from ends.entry / ends.stop, not from the circle.
evidence: The simplest item in my chunk: a single drawn object, one 61.3 cm chain of 103 points, entering 0.4 cm from the z face and ending 44.5 cm from that same z wall, in_fv 1. a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show a short isolated straight track with no companion and no parent, so it is not a fragment and there is nothing to attribute. The profile is flat from end to end: the band sits at 4.3-6.0e4 for the whole 60 cm, straddling the muon curve while the curve is flat, and the last few points read 6.75e4 at s=2, 5.95e4 at s=3, then 4.5e4, 4.4e4 and 2.55e4 at s=0-0.5. The reference curve over that same stretch climbs to 8.3e4 at s=5 and 1.6e5 at s=0, so the data peels away from it rather than following it up, and the segment mean of 52422 e/cm is the plateau value. No Bragg rise at the fit end, which is the operative test, so this is a through-goer regardless of the 44.5 cm of clearance to the nearest wall - the rubric is explicit that a flat profile alone is enough and that deep containment does not rescue it. The four high points (1.41e5 at s=20, 1.31e5 at s=41, 9.6e4 and 9.3e4 near s=29) are isolated deltas 20-40 cm back on the body, not an end effect, and they are exactly the kind of spike I would need to see at s=0-3 instead. All three azimuths show a dead-straight track ending at the star with only three or four faint unassociated image points just beyond it - no arm, no dots, no fan - and the object table has literally one row: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring. That single row is the fitted chain, tagged muon, and with no stop there is no gamma or michel to assign, so the kind is none. In f_meas the charge runs from time slice 285 down to 158 and stops there, about ten slices above a horizontal region boundary at time 148 that also truncates the dead-channel bands, so the cluster ends where the imaged region does.

notes: Not counted as an overshoot, but the fit does over-run: the profile peaks about 8 cm inside the fit end and the muon almost certainly stopped near rr 7.5. I left the pin alone because the charge between rr 2.5 and rr 7.5 is at full MIP rather than the 0.15-0.5 of MIP the rubric describes for a bridged over-run, and because there is no daughter past the fit end for a bridge to reach - the same test that kept the pin on 039349_50/45. The hardest part of this item was telling the s=7-13 lift from a delta cluster; the rubric gives no test for that, so I used point-by-point coherence (every point lifted, monotone over 6 cm) plus a predicted-versus-observed comparison against the reference curve under the two stop hypotheses. Medium: if the owner reads the lift as a long delta, this becomes THRU / none with every non-chain row delta / other; if the owner reads the MIP stretch as a short Michel, it becomes STM_MICHEL / both with the pin at 7.5 and 21009 tagged michel.
evidence: 92.4 cm curved chain entering 2.1 cm from the z face and ending 22.4 cm from that same z wall, in_fv 1; a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show one isolated spine, so not a fragment. Plateau is 5.4e4 out at s=40-90. Coming in, the whole band lifts coherently: 7.2e4 at s=18, 7.3e4 at s=14.3, 8.1e4 at s=13.6, 9.5e4 at s=13, 1.02e5 at s=12.6, 9.9e4-1.01e5 at s=10-11, 1.04e5 at s=9.7, 1.21e5 at s=9.2 and 1.15e5/1.13e5 at s=8.1 - a smooth monotone 2.2x climb over six centimetres in which EVERY point is lifted, with no ordinary-charge points interleaved. That coherence is what makes it a Bragg peak rather than a delta cluster: on the neighbouring item 039349_50/46 I rejected a very similar 1.28e5 spike precisely because normal 6.3e4 points sat among the 1e5 ones at the same arc length, and here they do not. So this track really does stop. The fit then over-runs it: s=2.7 to 7.1 reads 6.26, 6.2, 6.0, 5.9, 5.6e4 - flat at MIP, not below it - and only the last 2.7 cm, 3.07, 2.79, 1.68 and 2.79e4 at s=0-2.5, drops under plateau. Testing the two stop hypotheses against the reference curve shows how far the over-run goes: with the stop at the fit end the curve wants 8.3e4 at s=5, 1.0e5 at s=2.5 and 1.6e5 at s=0 against observed 5.9e4, 2.8e4 and 3.1e4, hopeless; with the stop near s=7.5 it wants 7.8e4 at rr 6.8, 8.1e4 at rr 5.5, 1.0e5 at rr 2.5 and 1.15e5 at rr 1.7 against observed 7.3e4, 9.5e4, 1.01e5 and 1.21e5, a match at every point. I did NOT move the pin even so. The rubric bridge is low-charge interpolation across a gap into a daughter, and 5.6-6.3e4 against a 5.4e4 plateau is full MIP, not a bridge; the genuinely sub-plateau stretch is only the last 2.7 cm, and past the fit end there is nothing at all for a bridge to end on - n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the zoomed azimuths show the thin continuation running to a vertex square and then only three or four stray points to the star, no arm, no fan, no kink. So this is recorded as an over-running fit with the pin left where the chain put it, the same way I handled 039349_50/45. With no electron anywhere, the verdict is STM_ONLY. Past the stop, 85010 is a 5-point 2.1 cm piece 29 cm forward at cos_fwd 0.96 and only 7.0 cm off the muon line, detached across a clean charge-free gap and far too faint at 9370 e/cm to be a 35 MeV electron - a capture gamma, which does not promote the verdict, so the kind is detached dots. 86011 is a 2-point speck 34.7 cm out and 34.6 cm off the line, with its transverse direction cos -1.00 against the gamma, i.e. the exact opposite side of the ring in an unrelated direction: delta / other. The 4.2 cm 8-point stub 84-88 cm back at 13982 e/cm is body activity on the muon side.

281 cm chain, enters 129 cm from the nearest face and stops deeply contained, d_face 70.9 cm (nearest x/anode). At 4x the profile sits on a 5.4-6.0e4 plateau out at s = 40-100 cm and climbs through 7-8.5e4 over s = 10-4 to 1.00-1.02e5 at s = 2-3, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve (which asymptotes to 5.4e4 and never gets crossed); the two final points at s < 1 fall back to 6.3-7.5e4, but that is one-to-two points at the very end, not a sustained collapse over several cm, so the pin stays at the fit end. The chain rejects this as shape_flat with is_stm 0; I disagree, the rise off the plateau is there and ragged-but-real. Past the stop a 10.2 cm 18-point segment 24003 leaves the vertex at 88 deg carrying 4.1e4 e/cm and is continued by the 1.6 cm 4-point 24001 at 1.8e4 out to 7.8 cm - at or below the muon plateau and falling as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature and not the undershoot case (that needs a couple-of-cm tip at 0.9-1.2e5). Four unassigned specks lie past the stop essentially along the arm direction (the arm points +z): 94011 at 24 cm, 8 points, cos 0.97 to the arm and detached across a ~16 cm charge-free gap; 95012 at 46 cm and 92006 at 51 cm both at cos 0.97/0.82; 93007 at 30 cm forward - detached dots on the Michel side, so gamma. 97013 (2 points, 54 cm, up in +y) is the arguable one, kept gamma as it is past the stop and on the decay side; it cannot change the kind since 94011 already does. 91005 (3 points, 44 cm, cos_fwd -0.83) is on the backward/muon side of the stop, so it fails the gamma rules requirement to be past the stop - delta / other, not because it hugs the body line (its transverse offset is 25-30 cm). A W-plane dead band sits at channel ~9390-9400 with the stop at ~9405; U and V are clear there and the measured-minus-predicted residual at the stop is small, so the Bragg rise is not a dead-channel artefact.

54.9 cm chain, enters 12.3 cm from the z face and stops well inside, d_face 48.6 cm to the nearest wall (z), in_fv. This is the textbook Bragg of the twelve: at 4x the profile leaves a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau at s = 45-55, climbs to 7e4 by s = 25, 8-9e4 by s = 8-12, 1.05e5 at s = 5-7, and then 1.14 / 1.29 / 1.44 / 1.56e5 at s = 3.5, 2.5, 1.8, 1.0, riding the muon reference curve the whole way up. The two points at s < 0.5 fall back to 8.8-9.5e4; that is still 1.6x the plateau, nothing like the 0.15-0.5-of-MIP sustained collapse that would mean the fit bridged a gap, so it is last-point scatter and the pin stays at the fit end. Nothing leaves the stop: n_stop_arms 0, and the three azimuths show a bare track end with only the usual thin image-point halo. The one other drawn object, 99007, is a 2-point speck 21.4 cm away at cos_fwd 0.20, which puts it forward of the stop with a 21 cm transverse offset from the muon line - isolated, past the stop, clear of the body, well inside 60 cm, and separated from the end by a completely charge-free gap: gamma, so detached dots, and per the rubric an isolated capture-gamma-like piece does not promote this to STM_MICHEL. Worth flagging for a re-auditor: the U plane has dead bands and the stop end sits at U channel ~1145 next to a dashed dead line at ~1140, but V and W image the end cleanly and a muon leaving through a dead region could not produce a 1.56e5 peak first, so the containment call stands.

notes: Competing reading, and why I did not take it: the chain rejects this as no_bragg + shape_flat, and one can read the whole thing as flat-to-the-end THRU with the terminal fall being the imaging losing the track. I went the other way because a THRU needs the plateau to hold TO the last point and here nine consecutive points fall steadily from 6.8e4 to 1.7e4 below it, and because the 7-14 cm window really is elevated above the plateau on every one of its seven points, not on one outlier. The peak height rests on a 2-point 1.22-1.27e5 excursion though, and this track shows single 1.2e5 points elsewhere, so medium confidence. Verdict STM_MICHEL with kind detached dots is not a contradiction: the Michel charge is inside the fitted row, which the tag alphabet cannot split, so the only gamma/michel tags left to derive the kind from are the three detached pieces.
evidence: OVERSHOOT item. 73.8 cm chain entering 1.8 cm from the z wall and ending 52.2 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not the question - the profile is. At 4x the body sits on a 6.5-6.7e4 plateau from s = 20 out to s = 70 (with this tracks usual +/- 2e4 scatter and a couple of 1.0-1.2e5 single-point excursions at s = 47 and 52). Between s = 14 and s = 7.5 every point is above that plateau - 9.1, 9.8, 10.8, 12.2, 12.7, 10.2, 9.5 e4 - peaking at 1.27e5 around s = 9. Then over the last 7-8 cm the profile collapses: 6.8, 6.2, 6.2, 5.8, 4.5, 3.7, 3.5, 2.9, 1.7 e4 (plus four genuinely zero-charge fit points at s = 4-6 which I ignore), i.e. from the plateau down to 0.25 of it, monotonically outward, while the muon reference curve over those same 8 cm climbs from 7e4 to 1.6e5. That is the fit-bridges-a-gap signature exactly: a muon at 1.27e5 cannot continue at or below MIP, so the last ~9 cm of the fit is a second particle and the real stop is 9 cm back - pin set there. The U and V measured panels corroborate it independently: the drawn track is orange (~2e4 ADC) for its body and turns dark over the final stretch, in measured AND predicted, and there is no dead band at that end (the U hatching is at 1490-1530 with the end at 1620, and the W dashed lines are crossed mid-track at slice 140-165, not at slice 55). Nothing continues past the fit end in any plane. Because the collapse falls inside the single fitted row 29006, that row is split: the first ~65 cm is the muon, the last ~9 cm is the electron, and I tag the row muon for the majority as the schema has no way to say so. The other three drawn objects are a coherent detached group 35-49 cm past the stop and 30 cm clear of the muon line - 107008 (9 points, 4.8 cm, up to 1.4e5, the chains 18.5 MeV capture gamma, cos_fwd 0.52), 108009 (2 points, 44 cm, cos_fwd 0.23) and 106007 (2 points, 49 cm, cos_fwd 0.79) - all forward of the stop and clustered together rather than scattered round the ring, so gamma for all three.

notes: Two readings weighed. The competing one is OVERSHOOT: peak at s = 11-13 then an 11 cm collapse to 0.4-0.55 of MIP, which would make this STM_MICHEL with the pin 11.5 cm back. I did not take it because (a) the s = 11-13 excursion is not unique on this track - two other 2x excursions sit at s = 44-46 and 53-56, and (b) the rubrics overshoot mechanism is a fit bridging a GAP with low-charge interpolated points, and here the cloud is continuous with no gap and no zero-charge points, and the decline is smooth rather than a collapse. What I cannot explain under THRU is why a through-going muons dQ/dx would fall 2.6x over its last 11 cm; attenuation cannot do it (the drift distance changes by only 10 cm there), so I am attributing it to terminal charge attribution on a drift-parallel track. Hence medium, not high. If the owner reads that terminal ramp as a real Michel, the verdict flips to STM_MICHEL with pin_rr 11.5.
evidence: 148.8 cm, essentially straight, entering 0.4 cm through the anode face and running 19 deg off the drift axis to an end 74.4 cm from the nearest wall, so this is a profile call and not a containment call. The tracks own plateau is low, 4-5e4, below the muon curves 5.4e4 asymptote, over the whole span s = 20-100. There is no Bragg rise at the fit end: over the last 11 cm the profile does the opposite, an unusually smooth monotone DECLINE through 6.6, 6.5, 6.4, 6.3, 6.1, 5.9, 5.8, 5.5, 5.2, 4.8, 4.3, 4.1, 3.8, 3.5, 3.3, 3.1 to 2.55e4 at the last point, ending at 0.55 of the plateau while the muon reference curve over those same centimetres climbs from 6.5e4 to 1.6e5. Five points at s = 10.6-13.4 sit at 7.3-9.4e4, about 2x the plateau, and I considered reading them as a Bragg peak with the fit overshooting by 11 cm - but this track shows the same 2x excursions twice more where nothing special is happening (6.5-8.8e4 at s = 44-46 and 6.1-8.35e4 at s = 53-56), and, decisively, there is no gap: the point cloud in all three azimuths runs continuously to the star with no charge-free break and no zero-charge fit points, so the fit is not bridging anything. Nothing continues past the fit end in any projection, and the end is not in a dead region (U hatching at 2870/2900/3040 with the track at 2995-3010, V at 6770-6790 and 6890 with the track at 6815-6830, W at 11400 with the track at 11235-11270). Under the operative test - no Bragg rise at the fit end - this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out, most likely helped by the near-drift-parallel geometry that squeezes 148 cm onto ten U channels and makes the terminal dQ/dx unreliable. Tagging by the THRU convention: all seven fitted chain rows muon, and the two unassigned pdg-11 shower pieces (44021, 44024) sit 77-85 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, i.e. right on the muon body far from either end, so delta / other; kind none.

311.2 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the z wall and ending 46.9 cm from the nearest wall - contained by the numbers, and irrelevant, because the profile settles it. At 4x the dQ/dx is flat on a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s = 100 all the way in to the last point: the points inside s = 10 read 7.5, 6.5, 6.4, 6.2, 5.9, 5.1, 4.9, 4.85, 4.1, 2.5, 2.4 e4, i.e. the same band as the body with a little low-side scatter, while the muon reference curve over that same stretch climbs from 6.5e4 at s = 10 to 1.15e5 at s = 2. There is no rise off the plateau in any shape, ragged or otherwise. Two isolated single points at 1.18e5 (s = 6) and 1.41e5 (s = 8.5) are the only high values anywhere near the end; single points with the neighbours on either side back at 6e4 are delta-ray hits, not a Bragg shape, and a stopping muon cannot show 1.4e5 at s = 8.5 and then 2.4e4 at s = 2. The three azimuths show a straight uniform spine running into the star with nothing attached, nothing past it, and no widening. Per the rubric a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out; worth noting for the record that it may not even be a mystery, since in f_meas the V plane has a hatched dead band at channels ~6810-6825 and the fit end sits at V ~6812 right inside it, while U (2965, bands at 2850/2870/2900/3040) and W (11210, band at 11070) are clear there. THRU tagging convention applied: the four fitted chain rows 59006, 59001, 59003, 59005 are muon and the one unassigned pdg-11 shower piece 59007 sits 195-199 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, dead on the muon body, so delta / other; kind none because gamma and michel are only defined relative to a stop.

notes: Medium, not high, for one reason: the michel side of this is small - a 4.2 cm fitted tail plus a 2.4 cm unfitted piece, all at 0.25-0.5 of MIP, and the very last fit points measure essentially zero charge in U. The competing reading is STM_ONLY with the pin still moved to 6.5: that the fit simply ran on into nothing past the muon stop and 36013 is a stray fragment rather than an electron. I went with STM_MICHEL because 36013 is real reconstructed charge attached at the stop, forward, off the body line, which the tag alphabet calls michel, and because the collapsed tail carries 2.5-5e4 over five centimetres, too much to be nothing.
evidence: OVERSHOOT item. 201.3 cm, whole object (the wide view shows one curved spine from the anode to the star, the only other charge in the frame being faint thinned context points from other tracks), entering 0.2 cm through the anode face and ending 49.1 cm from the nearest wall. Undershoot screen first: the only forward piece at the stop is 36013 at 2.4 cm and 2.4e4 e/cm, i.e. a third of MIP, nowhere near the 0.9-1.2e5 tip that would mean the fit stopped short - so not that case. The profile at 4x rises off a 5.5e4 plateau in a clean curve-shaped run, not a single-point excursion: 7.6e4 at s = 15, 7.9, 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6 through s = 14 to 10, then 9.2, 9.3, 9.1 e4 at s = 9-8 and 1.00e5 at s = 7, sitting just above the muon reference curve the whole way. That run of ten consecutive elevated points is quite distinct from this tracks ordinary scatter, whose isolated highs elsewhere (9.5e4 at s = 19, 8.8e4 at s = 51, 8.2e4 at s = 38) are single points with 5-6e4 neighbours on both sides. From s = 6 the profile then collapses and stays collapsed: 5.1, 4.6, 4.5, 4.4, 3.85, 3.4, 3.0, 2.55, 1.7 e4 and finally three points under 1e4 which I discount as no-measured-charge. Falling to a quarter of MIP over five to six centimetres where a muon at its own Bragg peak would be far above it is the fit-bridges-a-gap signature, so the real stop is about 6.5 cm back and the pin goes there. The chains own segmentation agrees: it broke the chain at 3.84 cm, and that whole terminal row 36014 (4.2 cm, 2.79e4) lies inside the collapsed region, so it gets tagged michel; 36010 keeps muon because 195 of its 198 cm are muon, with the last ~2.7 cm belonging to the electron and no row to say so. Also at the stop is 36013, an unfitted 5-point 2.4 cm cluster the chain types pdg 11 at 2.4e4 and then declines to accept (n_stop_arms 1 but no daughter) - attached, forward, well off the body line, so michel. The three azimuths back this: the orange high-charge chain markers stop several cm short of the star and the last stretch to it is drawn in low-dQ/dx teal with a small kink, and in f_meas the U plane, which is live there (its dead band is at 2170-2180, the end at 2205), shows a bright orange body ending in near-black points at the vertex, so the terminal collapse is measured, not a V-plane artefact - though I note the V plane does have a hatched band at ~6040-6055 right where the track ends. Two more objects, 96011 (2 points, 20.0 cm) and 98012 (5 points, 36.4 cm), lie in almost exactly the same direction from the stop (their unit vectors agree to 0.996), forward and well clear of the muon line: a collinear pair of detached dots on the decay side, so gamma for both.

Short one, 38.9 cm, and a whole object - the wide and stop views show a single continuous spine from the entry circle to the star with no companion cluster and nothing that reads as a broken-off piece. It enters 0.4 cm through the anode face and stops 34.5 cm from that same anode face, contained by the numbers. Undershoot screen: no forward piece at the stop at all (n_stop_arms 0), so that failure mode is not in play. The profile is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau at s = 25-38, then 6.5-7.5e4 at s = 10-15, 8.4e4 at s = 8, 9.3-9.8e4 at s = 5-6, 1.15-1.20e5 at s = 3-4, 1.27e5 at s = 2 and 1.42e5 at s = 0.8, riding the muon reference curve point for point. The single last point at s = 0.1 sits at 1.08e5, a quarter below the peak - one terminal point low is ordinary scatter, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse that would mean the fit bridged a gap, so the pin stays where it is. Nothing is attached at or leaves the stop in any of the three azimuths: the star sits on a bare track end. Two drawn specks remain, both 2-point and 0.6 cm, and both roughly perpendicular to the muon at the stop. 164001 is 30.5 cm out at cos_fwd 0.04, isolated, compact, entirely clear of the muon body line, with a clean charge-free gap back to the stop, and it is what the chain calls its 3.3 MeV capture gamma - detached dot past the stop, so gamma, which makes the kind detached dots (per the rubric an isolated capture-gamma piece does not promote the verdict to STM_MICHEL). 165002 is 50.3 cm out at cos_fwd -0.01, and I computed the two specks directions from the stop: they point almost opposite ways (their unit vectors dot to -0.49), so this one is not part of any coherent decay-side family, it is a lone survey speck in an unrelated direction at the outer edge of the ring, which the rubrics faint-far-speck rule sends to delta / other. That is the one judgement call here and it does not change the kind either way. No dead band at the stop in any plane (U bands at 3360 and 3425 with the end at 3460, V at 7200/7290/7315 with the end at 7265, W at 11720/11780/11895 with the end at 11850).

120.5 cm, entering 0.5 cm through the anode face and stopping 77.1 cm from the nearest wall. The drawn muon is a whole object - one continuous spine from the entry circle to the star - although it shares the frame with C54, a 622-point 164 cm unfitted cloud whose diffuse blue points spray across and alongside the muon body; C54 has d_min 50 cm and lies at cos_fwd -0.99, i.e. back along the body, so it is a different object crossing the scene and not a continuation of this one. Undershoot screen: nothing sits 1-3 cm ahead of the stop at all (n_stop_arms 0), so that mode is out. The profile is a clean Bragg: a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s = 30 to 100, 6.0-6.5e4 at s = 10-15, 7.5-8.5e4 at s = 6-9, 9.3-9.6e4 at s = 4-5, 1.02e5 at s = 3 and 1.15e5 at s = 1.8, tracking the reference curve; the two final points at s < 0.5 fall to 8.7e4 and 7.4e4, still 1.4x the plateau, which is terminal scatter rather than the several-centimetre collapse to a fraction of MIP that would move the pin, so the pin stays. The three azimuths show a bare end: no arm, no widening, nothing bridging out of the star. Object attribution. 177014 is the chains 0.88 MeV capture gamma, 2 points 28.9 cm out at cos_fwd 0.56, isolated and clear of the body across a charge-free gap - gamma, which sets the kind to detached dots without promoting the verdict. Three more faint pieces sit in the same forward cone and I checked their directions from the stop rather than trusting cos_fwd on this slightly curved track: 174011 (4 points, 46.4 cm, straight ahead at 0.93), 176013 (2 points, 50.0 cm, 0.48) and 175012 (2 points, 57.4 cm, 0.71), the last two pointing within 35 deg of each other - a coherent forward family inside the 60 cm ring, so gamma rather than random deltas. The odd one out is 173010, 21 cm away perpendicular to the muon in +y, which is the direction C54 occupies and the one piece the chain itself body-excluded; a lone speck in a direction unrelated to the forward family, so delta / other, as is C54 itself. U has a dead line at channel ~3640 right where the track ends and V a hatched band at 7420, but the Bragg peak is measured before that and W is clear there, so the stop is not a dead-region exit.

notes: The end is abrupt: uniform orange charge to the last point in all three measured planes, live channels either side, 45 cm from the nearest wall, and nothing drawn beyond it. That is the rubrics no-continuation-no-face-no-dead-region case, which it says is still THRU on a flat profile.
evidence: 131.2 cm, dead straight, entering 0.1 cm through the anode face and ending 45.3 cm from the nearest wall (z). Undershoot screen: nothing at all sits ahead of the fit end (n_stop_arms 0, no michel-group row), so that mode is out. The profile is flat on its 5.5-6.0e4 plateau right through to the last point - the points inside s = 7 read 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9, 5.4, 5.5 e4 with two low strays at 3.7 and 4.2e4 - while the muon reference curve over the same stretch climbs from 7e4 at s = 7 to 1.15e5 at s = 2. There is no rise of any shape at the fit end. That is a delta-ray or hard-interaction burst in the middle of the track, not a Bragg peak: it is 62-76 cm from the fit end rather than several cm, the charge after it does not collapse into a bridged gap but declines smoothly for 60 cm, and no muon carries 60 cm of range past its own Bragg peak. Nothing sits past the fit end at all - flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma - and the only rows away from the body are 209030 and 210031, 2- and 7-point survey specks 52-55 cm out at cos_fwd about -0.05, i.e. sideways, not forward. The other unassigned rows (66020, 66023, 66026) all sit at cos_fwd -0.99 or -1.0, on the muon body. Under the THRU convention the six fitted chain segments are muon and everything else is delta / other.

notes: The chain gets this one wrong: it rejects on shape_flat and sets is_stm 0, yet the terminal rise to over 1.65e5 is the most convincing Bragg peak in my chunk. evidence: 312.6 cm of chain entering 0.4 cm from the anode x face and running diagonally across the detector to an end 125.1 cm from the nearest z wall, 227.6 cm from the anode and 321.3 cm from the y wall - about as deeply contained as an end can be here. notes: Flat to the last point with a stub continuing straight on and a face 13.7 cm ahead, so the muon most likely left through the top y wall just past where the imaging ended. The undershoot was checked and fails on the charge clause.
evidence: 198.5 cm of chain entering 1.0 cm from the anode x face and running across to a fit end 13.7 cm below the top y face, 170.6 cm from the anode and 136 cm from the z wall. From s = 100 in to s = 25 the band sits at 4.5-6e4; the final four centimetres read 8.3e4 at s = 4, then 6.6e4, 6.9e4, 7.0e4 and a last point of 5.8e4 at s = 0 - falling, not rising, and well under the muon reference curve which is already 8e4 at s = 4 and 1.15e5 at s = 1. The only forward object is 31020: 2 points over 0.6 cm at 63976 e/cm sitting exactly at the fit end with cos_fwd 1.0, which is 1.2 times this tracks MIP, nowhere near the several-times-MIP the undershoot rule requires, and far too small to be an electron - it is a stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop, so it takes the muon tag under that clause. notes: Clean, simple case - flat MIP profile to the end and no drawn object of any kind past the stop, so no attribution to weigh. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). evidence: 222.9 cm of chain in three segments, entering 1.0 cm from the anode x face at x = 338.9 and running almost straight across the drift to a fit end at x = 132.4 that is 20.5 cm from the nearest z wall, 124.6 cm from the y wall and 129.4 cm from the cathode. notes: The chain rejects only on plateau_off_mip here (it does not raise no_bragg or shape_flat), which is why I checked the terminal 1.15e5 excursion carefully; I read it as a delta because the same track shows an identical spike cluster at s = 41-46 and the charge afterwards returns to plateau rather than collapsing. notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation, no face within 137.6 cm and no dead-region exit at the stop: the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Chain agrees (reject no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). Neither undershoot nor overshoot applies.

notes: No Michel arm anywhere (n_stop_arms 0), so this is STM_ONLY with capture-gamma dots => detached dots, not none. Neither undershoot nor overshoot: nothing lies forward of the stop, and the profile's maximum is the last point itself with no post-peak collapse. Bragg evidence is a one-point terminal spike over a flat plateau; a reader who required a multi-centimetre rise could call this THRU, which is the competing reading.
evidence: 102.2 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends 52.1 cm from the nearest wall, comfortably contained. Range KE 256.1 against dQ/dx KE 206.6 agrees to 20 percent, consistent with a stopper; MCS 377.5 with amb 0.88 is uninformative. Nothing at all past the stop in c/d/e - the spine simply ends at the star with empty space beyond in all three azimuths - and f_meas confirms the V and W planes are live either side of the stop, so it is not a dead-region exit even though a U dead band runs close to the stop channel. 28009 (6 points, 3.0 cm, pdg 11 by the chain) sits 5.8-8.7 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 and in the e azimuth it lies directly on the spine between two flow vertices, hugging the body, so off-axis separation makes it delta / other rather than an isotropic Michel piece despite being inside the 10 cm radius; 28005 is the same case at 41-46 cm, cos_fwd -1.0. The three survey specks are all well clear of the body: 115011 is 32.9 cm out and 23 cm off the muon line and 116012 is 51.1 cm out and 34 cm off it, and the two lie along one common ray from the stop, so I read them as one capture gamma's deposits and tagged both gamma; f_meas shows both as real measured charge 25 and 115 time slices past the stop, not fit artefacts. 114010 is 39.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.06, i.e. perpendicular and in a direction unrelated to that ray, so by the scattered-in-unrelated-directions rule it goes delta / other; it is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck and I am not confident in it either way.

notes: Flat-profile THRU: no continuation visible, both ends 22-29 cm from any face, no dead-region exit at the fit end (V and W are live either side of it) - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. FRAG_THRU is also arguable given the dead-channel environment, but no larger object is visibly drawn. Neither the undershoot nor the overshoot signature applies as the rubric defines them.
evidence: A short isolated 23.7 cm chain (40 points), contained at both ends: entry 28.6 cm from the z face, fit end 22.5 cm from the z wall, nothing else drawn in the bundle. Reading the profile off the upscaled panel, the last two points are 7.7e4 and 6.9e4 over a 4.6-5.7e4 stretch that runs flat from s=1.7 out to s=11, i.e. a 1.35x two-point uptick against a muon reference curve that is at 1.4e5 at s=0.1 and 8.5e4 at s=2.6 - the data sits 30-40 percent under the curve the whole way and never takes its shape, so I read no Bragg rise at the fit end. The one thing that gave me pause is a 5 cm bump at s=12-17 reaching 0.8-1.07e5 with the charge falling away beyond it (5.1e4 at 19.3, 2.9e4 at 21, 1.4e4 at 23); read as a Bragg peak that would put the true stop at s=14.5 and make the last 14 cm a Michel, which is why this is medium and not high. I did not move the pin, for three reasons: past the bump the charge sits at full MIP (4.6-7.7e4) rather than collapsing far below the plateau, which is the actual diagnostic; the charge over that stretch RISES toward s=0 instead of falling as an outgoing electron's would; and the sub-MIP values at the far end (1.4-4.6e4, well under any muon's plateau) look like charge loss, since f_meas shows dead-channel bands crowding the track in both U (1455-1465, 1500-1520) and W (9600-9610, 9628-9635), so the apparent rise from s=23 to s=15 is as easily recovery of lost charge as a real profile. The only other row, 118001, is a 4-point 1.8 cm speck 31.6 cm from the stop and about 30 cm off the muon line; on a THRU there is no stop to define a gamma so it takes delta / other.

notes: OVERSHOOT of the ordinary kind: the fit ran about 1.5-2 cm past the muon's Bragg peak into the base of the Michel, pin moved to rr 1.5. Row 36003 is split - d 1.5-7.25 muon, d 0-1.5 bridge/Michel - and the tag alphabet cannot express that, so it is tagged for the majority. Separately: a 9 cm near-zero-charge patch in the chain 7-16 cm back from the stop, which I read as lost charge, not as a second stop.
evidence: 218.4 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the anode x face and ending 87.0 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained; range 507.2, dQ/dx 524.9 and MCS 476.8 MeV all agree (amb 0.02), which is what a clean stopper looks like. Off the upscaled panel the profile holds a 6-8.5e4 plateau from s=39 back to s=17, crosses a 9 cm stretch at s=7-16 where the charge falls to 3e3-2e4 (a charge-less patch I discount as the rubric says to discount zero-charge fit points), and then climbs monotonically 5.8e4, 9.1e4, 9.9e4, 1.04e5, 1.17e5, 1.32e5 over s=6.3 down to 2.7 - a textbook Bragg rise topping out right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band, above the reference curve rather than merely approaching it. Past that peak the last two fit points collapse to 2.5e4 and 3.1e4, about 0.4 of the muon's own plateau and a fifth of the peak, exactly where a muon at its Bragg peak would be far above the plateau; that is the overshoot signature, so I moved the pin to rr 1.5 cm, the junction between the last elevated muon point at s=2.0 and the collapsed pair. The collapse falls inside chain segment 36003 (d 0-7.25), which has no separate row to retag, so 36003 is tagged muon for the 5.7 cm of it that is muon and the evidence records that its last 1.5 cm is the bridge. 36001 is the Michel: 18 points, 10.2 cm, cos_fwd +0.61 (a 49 deg kink), median 4.5e4 which is at MIP, and all three azimuths show it leaving the star as a distinct blue arm with a visible kink and running clear of the muon body to a vertex 10 cm out - a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so it is a second particle, and 10 cm and 32.7 MeV are right for a Michel. This is NOT the undershoot case: that needs a 2 cm tip at 0.9-1.2e5 with cos_fwd above 0.85, and 36001 is 10 cm at 4.5e4 with cos_fwd 0.61. C48 is a 657-point 345 cm object 33-60 cm away, visible in the wide 3-D view as a separate diffuse track and in the projections as an unrelated diagonal, so it is a different object entirely: delta / other. No capture-gamma dots anywhere in the ring, so the kind is attached, not both.

notes: STM_ONLY with an empty ring: no michel piece and no gamma dot, so kind none. Neither the undershoot nor the overshoot signature is present. Chain agrees (is_stm 1).
evidence: 360.7 cm of chain (448 points), entering 0.2 cm from the anode x face and ending 138.3 cm from the nearest wall - about as deeply contained as a stop gets in this detector. The dQ/dx panel is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.4-6.7e4 plateau from s=45 back to s=20, then a smooth monotone climb through 7.0e4 at s=10.7, 7.8e4 at 7.5, 8.3e4 at 6.9, 9.1e4 at 5.7, 1.02e5 at 4.4 and 1.10e5 at 3.4-1.4, and over that whole stretch the points sit right on top of the overlaid muon reference curve rather than merely approaching it. notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation and no face within 85 cm: the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). Neither undershoot nor overshoot: nothing is forward of the fit end, and the profile has no peak-then-collapse near it.
evidence: 156.6 cm chain, enters 0.3 cm from the y face and the fit ends 85.0 cm from the nearest wall. notes: Flat-profile THRU: no visible continuation, nearest face 27.7 cm away, no dead-region exit - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). Neither undershoot nor overshoot: nothing is forward of the fit end and there is no peak-then-collapse.

evidence: 181.6 cm of chain with BOTH ends deep inside the volume - entry 116.8 cm from the z face, fit end 129.5 cm from the z wall - which was the first sign that the drawn cluster is not a whole object. Zooming the side and top projections settles it: a faint grey context track continues from the drawn cluster's entry end on the same line and the same curvature and runs off to the detector edge in both views, so this is a fragment of a longer through-goer. There is no Bragg rise anywhere. The plateau runs 5-9e4 from s=100 in to s=25 with heavy scatter, and the single 1.55e5 point at s=24.6 has 9.8e4 at s=24.0 and 7.7-9.3e4 at s=26 on either side of it, which is an isolated spike with plateau on both sides - a delta or a crossing, by exactly the test I applied to the s=42-46 spike on 039349_56/47 and the s=12-17 bump on 039349_56/30. Past that the profile FALLS into the fit end: 4.3-9.2e4 for 10 cm, then 3.6e4, 2.5e4, 1.5e4, 0.6e4 over 2 cm, then an 8 cm hole with no points, then 1.0-2.5e4 for the last 1.4 cm. A stopping muon cannot do that. What clinches it is 92006, the 8-point 4.4 cm piece the chain offers as a capture gamma: taking its centroid against the entry-to-stop chord it lies at cos 0.966, i.e. 20.8 cm straight ahead of the fit end and only 5.4 cm off the track's own line, carrying 4.7e4 which is MIP - that is charge continuing past the fit end on the track's line, which the rubric makes THRU by itself. I first read the thick-to-thin transition at the 26001/26002 boundary as a muon ending and a Michel leaving, and moved the pin 21.7 cm; that was the amber selection band ending, which display trap 2 warns about, not a change in the object, and the charge argument does not support it either. Verdict revised. On a through-goer there is no stop, so both fitted chain segments are muon and 92006 takes delta / other; the chain's own rejection, shape_flat plus profile_sparse, says the same thing about the fit end.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs ~3 cm past the true stop. Collapse floor 2.4e4 is 0.53 of the 4.5e4 plateau, at the shallow edge of the 0.15-0.5 band quoted in the rubric; the competing reading is ordinary terminal scatter, which would make this STM_ONLY with no pin. evidence: 41.2 cm chain, enters 0.3 cm from the z face and the fit ends 14.0 cm from the nearest active face (in_fv 1), so containment is fine. Over the last ~3 cm the profile then collapses to 4.4e4, 4.2e4, 3.6e4, 2.4e4, 2.4e4 while the muon curve is at 1.2-1.6e5 there: a sustained collapse over several cm, the overshoot signature, so the true stop is at the junction at s~3 and the last 3 cm of row 69004 is the Michel. The label schema has only one chain row, so 69004 is tagged muon for what most of it is; the row is split, s>3 muon and s<3 michel. Past the stop sit seven compact specks 16.6-27.8 cm out (0.2-2.9 cm, 2-6 points, 1.4-6.1e4) spread over cos_fwd 0.17-0.99 on the forward side, which read as capture gammas. The 621-point 64.6 cm cluster C71 at d_min 25.5 is not a continuation: for a continuation d_max would be near 25.5+64.6=90, but d_max is 45.8, so the cloud lies across the line of flight, and it is far too large for Michel or gamma - a different object, delta/other. Two specks at 22-41 cm (152006, 156007) and the zero-charge pair 163014 go the same way. No dead channels at the stop in U, V or W.

notes: The only soft call is the lone 46.9 cm speck 165012: it decides attached vs both on its own. Taken as gamma on the rubric's faint-far-speck rule because its direction from the stop is essentially the Michel arm's direction (cos 0.99 with 246016), not a random point on the 60 cm ring. Its 1.05e5 e/cm over 2 points is not used as a criterion. No pin move; the terminal ease-off from 9.2e4 to 5.6e4 over 5 cm is neither an undershoot nor an overshoot signature.
evidence: 129.9 cm chain in two fitted rows, enters right on the x face (d_face 0.0) and the fit ends 45.8 cm from the nearest active face, well contained. The profile sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau all the way out to s=100 and climbs from about 7e4 at s=12 onto the muon reference curve, peaking at 9.0-9.2e4 at s=5-6; over the last 5 cm it eases back to 7.3e4, 6.4e4 and 5.6e4 at the fit's last point. That terminal easing ends at about 1.15 of the plateau, nowhere near the far-below-plateau collapse that would say the fit overshot, so the pin stays where the fit put it and I read the ease-off as the last centimetres already sharing charge with the electron that starts 1 cm away. Three michel-group pieces sit at d_min 1.05, 2.12 and 8.77 cm carrying 1.6-3.6e4 e/cm, i.e. at or below MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so these are the second particle - and the three azimuths show them as one curled hook about 10 cm long leaving the stop and folding back, the textbook Michel shape; all three are michel. One 2-point 0.1 cm speck (165012) sits 46.9 cm out; its direction from the stop is cos 0.99 with the michel piece 246016 and 0.76-0.86 with the other two, so it lies squarely along the Michel arm's own line rather than scattered in an unrelated direction, and there is a clean charge-free gap between it and the stop, which by the attachment tie-break makes it a detached dot: gamma, hence kind both. The V plane has dense dead-channel bands running through this region but U and W show the stop and the hook cleanly and the measured-minus-predicted panels are flat there.

notes: Called THRU on the flat-to-falling last 7 cm, but this is the hardest kind of call: the competing reading is that the s=8-9 maximum is a real Bragg peak and the last 7-8 cm are an overshoot, which would make it STM_ONLY with pin-rr about 8. I rejected that because the rubric's overshoot signature needs the terminal segment to fall FAR BELOW the muon's own plateau, and here it lands at 5.3-6.2e4, i.e. at or slightly above the level the same track carries at s=10-14. Neither undershoot nor overshoot counted. Dead channels cover the track in U and V, so every dQ/dx number on this item is suspect; medium confidence for that reason too.
evidence: A short, lonely, smoothly curved 24.9 cm chain of 42 points and absolutely nothing else drawn - one object row, no arms, no dots, no gamma ring. It enters 6.2 cm from the z face and the fit ends 23.1 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not the issue; the profile is. Read from the far end inwards the dQ/dx climbs steadily from 1.1-2.1e4 at s=22-25, through 1.9-2.8e4 at s=19-22, 3.3-3.9e4 at s=17-19, 4.3-5.0e4 at s=15-17 and 5.4-6.1e4 at s=10-14, to a four-point maximum of 8.0-8.3e4 at s=8-9 - and then it comes back down and sits flat at 5.3-6.2e4 for the whole last 7 cm to the fit's last point. There is no rise at the fit end, which is the operative test, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Two things say the same: the maximum of 8.3e4 is only about 1.5 times the local level and nowhere near the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches, and the far end's 1.1e4 is a fifth of MIP, far too low for muon body charge, so the profile's overall slope is an artefact of the reconstruction rather than a Bragg curve. f_meas shows why: hatched dead-channel bands cover essentially the whole track in V and clip it in U, with only W clean, so the charge on this object is under-measured over its length. Nothing at all lies past the fit end in any of the three azimuths, so there is no decay activity to judge and kind is none.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 0, reject no_bragg + shape_flat) but the call is made on the picture: 88 cm of unbroken MIP plateau. Note that under a stopping reading 103006 and 102005 would have been a gamma pair (they are 26.7 and 36.5 cm out and cos 0.98 with each other, i.e. one line of dots), which would have made kind detached dots; the THRU convention forbids that, so they are recorded delta / other. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 87.7 cm straight chain in two fitted rows, entering 1.5 cm from the z face and ending 72.1 cm from the nearest active face - deeply contained, and containment is exactly the trap here, because the profile is flat. dQ/dx sits on a 5.0-6.5e4 band from s=88 all the way in to s=3 with no upward trend whatsoever; the scattered 1.0-1.4e5 points are spread over s=13, 19, 33, 40, 57, 67, 72 and 80, i.e. delta activity along the whole body, not a terminal rise. A stopping muon cannot hold MIP to its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ended where the imaging ran out; f_meas shows the dead-channel bands sitting clear of the track in all three planes, so it is not a dead-region exit either - it simply ends. Because there is no stop, everything else is delta / other by the THRU convention: 25003 (8 points, 4.2 cm, chain-typed pdg 11 shower) is 15.2-16.0 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 and its direction from the fit end is cos 0.99 with the muon body, so it hugs the body line; 105007 likewise at 42 cm, cos_fwd -0.94, cos 0.95 with the body; 103006 and 102005 sit 26.7 and 36.5 cm out roughly transverse to the body (cos 0.98 with each other) and 99004 is 59 cm out in an unrelated direction. kind none, as the THRU rule requires.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation and no face - exactly the case the rubric says to call THRU rather than UNCLEAR. notes: Textbook flat-profile THRU 120 cm from any face and with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit - the exact configuration the rubric tells scanners not to hedge into UNCLEAR. evidence: A 374.2 cm ruler-straight chain in four fitted rows, 623 points, entering exactly on the x face (d_face 0.0, the anode) and ending 120.0 cm from the nearest z wall and 65.5 cm from the cathode - as deeply contained as anything in this set, which is precisely the case the rubric warns about. All four rows muon, kind none.

notes: The chain calls this an STM (is_stm 1, reject STM) and I am overruling it on the flat profile. The pieces that made the call take a moment are 160011/160012: cos_fwd -0.84 is just outside the rubric's -0.85 body-line threshold and their 17 cm transverse offset at 30 cm would read as well clear of the body - but they are BACKWARD of the fit end, not past it, so the gamma rule does not reach them either, and on a THRU the convention settles it. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 295.8 cm of chain in three fitted rows, 496 points, entering 0.1 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 58.1 cm from the nearest z wall - contained, but the profile decides and the profile never rises. dQ/dx holds a 3.5-6.5e4 band the whole 296 cm; over the last 15 cm the values run 6.0-7.9e4 on the upper branch and 4.0-5.5e4 on the lower, and the fit's own last points are 7.6e4, 6.2e4, 4.5e4, 4.4e4 and 4.0e4. Compared with the far body at s=60-100, where the same two branches sit at 5.5-6.5e4 and 4.5-5.5e4, the last 15 cm are perhaps 10-15 per cent higher - nothing like the factor of two to three the muon reference curve demands, and the curve itself is at 1.6e5 at s=0, three to four times above the data. There is no peak-then-collapse anywhere in the last 40 cm either, so this is not an overshoot with a mislaid pin; it is a flat MIP profile to the last point, which a stopping muon cannot produce, and at 681 MeV range-equivalent that is what one expects. The three azimuths show the star bare with a clean gap in every direction: the nearest drawn objects are the pair 158009/159010 about 19-22 cm out (cos 0.99 with each other, 66 degrees off the body) and the pair 160011/160012 at 29-33 cm sitting about 17 cm off the body line on the backward side, with 157008 a lone 2-point speck 53 cm out. Under the THRU convention all five, plus the two chain-typed pdg 11 showers 62003 and 62007 that lie on the body at cos_fwd -1.00, are delta / other and kind is none.

notes: f_meas is worth recording: the fit end lands at time slice ~0, the very start of the drawn readout window, which is a plausible mechanism for where the rest of the track went, though the rubric does not require one. The competing reading is an overshoot with pin-rr about 3 (peak 8.0e4 at s=3, collapse to 1.95e4 = 0.39 of MIP, inside the quoted 0.15-0.5 band) - rejected because the 8e4 pair is indistinguishable from the delta outliers scattered along the whole body. Counted as neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 244.6 cm chain in six fitted rows, 414 points, entering 4.8 cm from the y face and ending 39.9 cm from the anode x face - contained on the numbers. The profile is a flat 4.5-5.5e4 MIP band from s=245 in to s=5, decorated all along its length by 8-12.5e4 delta points at s=24, 28, 50-52, 58, 73-75, 80-82 and 88-95, and it never turns up towards the muon reference curve, which sits at 1.6e5 at s=0 while the data end below 6e4. Over the last 5 cm the values are 6.0-6.3e4 at s=5-10, a two-point excursion to 7.5-8.0e4 at s=2-4, and then 5.6e4, 4.2e4, 2.7e4 and 1.95e4 at the fit's own last centimetre. I looked hard at that as a possible overshoot - a peak followed by a collapse to 0.4 of MIP is the right shape - but the peak is two points at 1.6 times the plateau in a track that carries a dozen larger excursions along its body, with no sustained rise leading into it, so there is no Bragg peak for the pin to be moved back to. Flat to the last point means through-goer. The three azimuths back this up completely: the star is bare, and the only large neighbour, C55, is a 350-point 299.6 cm cluster whose d_min 40.9 and d_max 59.9 span just 19 cm - a 300 cm object seen almost edge-on across the line of flight, and the wide 3-D views show it plainly as a second, roughly parallel cosmic track well below this one. The chain-typed pdg 11 shower 75014 sits on the body at 81-84 cm, cos_fwd -1.00. All chain rows muon, the other two delta / other, kind none.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs about 6 cm past the true stop; pin-rr 6.1 at the 40001/40002 junction. Called medium because the terminal segment sits at 6.5e4, i.e. 1.3 times the 5e4 body plateau, whereas the rubric's overshoot examples run 0.15-0.5 of MIP - it is far below what a post-Bragg muon would carry but NOT below the track's own plateau, which is how the rubric words the test. Competing readings: (a) STM_ONLY with the pin left alone, which I rejected because the profile is falling, not rising, at the fit's last point, so there is no Bragg rise there to justify a stop; (b) THRU, rejected because the factor-two rise over s=6-20 is real and a through-goer cannot produce it. Also note the 1.28-1.30e5 pair at s=7.5-7.8 sits ABOVE the muon reference curve, which the rubric says never happens for real Bragg charge, so I treated those two as delta points and read the trend from the medians instead.
evidence: 328.9 cm chain, 549 points, entering 0.2 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 141.2 cm from the nearest z wall - as contained as it gets. The body plateau is 4.5-5.5e4 out to s=100 and beyond, and from about s=20 the profile lifts off it: median 7e4 at s=15-20, 8.3e4 at s=11-14, and 9.6e4 over s=6-13 (individual points 7.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.25, 8.7, 9.5, 9.6, 9.65, 9.7, 10.3, 12.8, 13.0 e4). That is a genuine ragged Bragg rise of about a factor two over the last 15 cm, and a through-goer cannot make it. Then over the fit's last 6.8 cm the ten points read 3.96, 4.0, 5.42, 5.46, 6.06, 6.4, 6.4, 7.3, 9.36 and 10.78 e4, mean 6.5e4 - a 32 per cent drop from the segment in front of it, at a place where a muon carrying on from a Bragg peak would be at 1.2-1.6e5. So the muon's true stop is at the junction and the terminal piece is the decay electron. The chain has already broken the track exactly there: 40002 is its own row, d_min 0.00 to d_max 6.13 cm, 12 points, mean dQ/dx 63336 against 49588 for the 322 cm body row, and the three azimuths show a vertex square at that junction with the last stretch drawn out of the amber selection band, bending about 18 degrees off the body centroid direction. 6.8 cm at roughly 1.3 times MIP is the right size and the right charge for a ~15 MeV Michel, and within 10 cm of the stop direction does not discriminate, so 40002 is michel and the pin goes to 6.1 cm. The only other drawn object, 80003, is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 56 cm out whose direction from the stop is 97 degrees from the Michel arm and 106 degrees from the body - an isolated speck in an unrelated direction, so delta / other and kind stays attached. f_meas shows the track curving steadily over its last 30 cm in all three planes, which is what a muon losing momentum does, and no dead channels at the end.

notes: MESSY rather than THRU or UNCLEAR: the failure is specific and I can name it, so UNCLEAR would understate what the picture shows, and THRU would assert a single through-going track that the empty ~100 cm middle rules out. notes: THRU on no rise at the fit end; the last 10 cm sags to 0.15-0.45 MIP, explained by charge attribution splitting between the chain points (1-3e4) and the co-located unassigned cluster 66009 (4.5e4).
