Strongest overshoot CANDIDATE in this chunk and worth the owner reviewing: a real 5e4 to 1.0e5 climb from s=30 to s=16 then a sustained collapse. Rejected because the peak is 16-17 cm back rather than several, it reaches only 1.0e5, and the sole thing past the fit end is 66009 at cos_fwd -1.0, on the body line, so there is nothing to bridge to. Pin left on the fit last point. No undershoot.
evidence: 252.8 cm chain entering right at the z face (0.4 cm) and ending 146.5 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained - and containment does not decide, the profile does. At the fit end there is no rise: the last 10 cm sit at 1-3e4, a fifth to a half of the 6.7e4 MIP line, against a reference curve that is at 8e4 by s=5 and 1.6e5 at s=0. No Bragg rise at the fit end is the operative test, so THRU, and the chain reaches the same verdict independently (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) on a track whose MCS momentum of 1012 MeV/c fights its 681 by range at ambiguity 0.47. The sag has a mundane explanation that does not need the pin moved: charge attribution is split over exactly that stretch. The chain points carry 1-3e4 across the last 5 cm while an unassigned cluster, 66009, carries 4.5e4 over 6.2 cm across the same 5 cm, so the two together are about MIP and the fit is simply drawing the thinner half. f_meas confirms the last 8 cm is genuinely dark in U, V and W with no dead band on the track, i.e. the charge really is low on the fitted points. I considered and rejected the overshoot reading. The profile does climb from 5e4 at s=30 to 8.5e4 at s=19 and 1.0e5 at s=16-17 before the collapse, which is the strongest peak-then-collapse shape I saw in this chunk, and the collapsed segment lands squarely in the 0.15-0.5 of MIP band the rubric quotes. But the peak is 16-17 cm back, not the several cm the signature describes, it tops at 1.0e5 rather than the 1.2-1.35e5 real stoppers here reach, and above all the mechanism needs something past the stop for the fit to bridge to - and there is nothing. The only candidate, 66009, sits at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. on the muon body line, which the tag table and the collision paragraph both make delta / other at any distance whatever the chain types it. Geometry is still worth recording: 66006 is 210.9 cm long over a 206 cm radial span and straight, while 66011 is 38.6 cm over a 31 cm span and visibly hooks in all three azimuths. On a THRU item the three fitted chain segments are muon and 66009 is delta / other, kind none.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation, no face contact (31.4 cm) and no clear dead-region exit - the cluster simply ends where the imaging runs out. Recorded per the rubric's flat-profile clause rather than reaching for UNCLEAR. MCS 391 MeV against range 223 MeV is what a truncated track looks like.
evidence: A single clean 87 cm spine, 145 chain points, entering 0.8 cm from the z face and ending 31.4 cm from the nearest face; the drawn rows sum to 147 points against 145 chain points, so this is the whole object and not a fragment. At 4.6x zoom on the stop band the profile is flat to the very last point: the muon points oscillate between about 2.5e4 and 5.3e4 from s=40 all the way in, and the last three points at s=0-3 sit at 3.6e4, 4.2e4 and 5.3e4, dead on the same MIP plateau, with no climb of any shape toward the black muon reference curve over the last 10-20 cm. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot end at MIP, so this end is not a stop. The three fitted segments 70005, 70007 and 70008 all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 running back up the body from the stop, and the one unassigned 3.7 cm 7-point piece 70006 also sits at cos_fwd -1.0, 75-79 cm back along the body at the far entry end, so it is body activity there and not decay charge at this end. No arm, dot or speck anywhere past the fit end in any of the three 3-D azimuths. In f_meas U and V are clear of dead channels at the stop; W has dead bands within a few channels of the last hits, but with two clean planes there and a flat profile the call does not rest on them.

notes: No Bragg rise anywhere on this track - on charge alone THRU is defensible. I called STM_MICHEL on topology: contained end at 43 cm, no continuation in live W channels beyond the fit end, tightening curvature, MCS consistent with range, and a 46 MeV branched electron object 10-27 cm forward. The 10.13 cm charge-free gap between the stop and the nearest Michel piece is the one fact that argues the other way and I could not explain it away - W is live and empty across it. Medium, not high, for exactly that reason: if the gap is real and unbridgeable, this is a THRU with unrelated EM activity nearby.
evidence: 84 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the anode x face and ending 43 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained, with visible curvature that tightens over the last 20 cm - the arc in all three azimuths is what a slowing muon looks like, and the track's own MCS 175 MeV against range 217 MeV is consistent rather than the MCS-far-above-range signature of a truncated track. The profile does NOT show a Bragg rise: at high zoom it falls smoothly from about 7.1e4 at s=13 through 4.3e4 at s=10 and 3.0e4 at s=5 to 1.8e4 at the last point, roughly a third of its own 5.5e4 plateau. f_meas gives a partial account of that: the U dead band at channel 3040 sits exactly on the fit's last points, so the terminal charge is measured through one dead plane. It does not explain the 10.13 cm hole past the stop - W is live right across that gap, channels 11320-11348, and shows no charge there - so I do not claim the gap is a dead-plane artefact; it looks real. Past the end, 10-27 cm forward at cos_fwd 0.39-0.88, sits a five-to-nine-piece branched EM complex the chain calls a 46 MeV electron: 6 to 14 cm segments of 12-24 points each, well clear of the muon body line, which runs the other way at cos_fwd -0.94. That is an electron-sized, electron-shaped object on the forward side of a contained track end, and it is far more than the compact speck the gap tie-break was written for, so I take it as the Michel; the rubric lets a Michel topology carry STM_MICHEL even with the Bragg unclear. A separate three-piece clump 32-37 cm out at cos_fwd -0.17 to +0.13, perpendicular to the muon and nowhere near its body line, is isolated and past the stop on the same side as the decay: gamma. The hard part is that 10.13 cm charge-free gap; the competing reading is that the fit overshot the true stop near s=13 and the last 13 cm are low-charge bridge points, which would put the electron more than 20 cm from the real stop and argue the complex is unrelated EM. I did not move the pin: the decline is smooth rather than a collapse off a peak, and 7.1e4 at s=13 is only 1.3x the plateau where a real Bragg peak is over 2x.

notes: Flat 0.4-MIP plateau to the last measured points, with a plausible dead-region exit (wide U dead band at ch 2168-2182 and the V dead pair at 6050-6060 both under the fit's last points). Medium, not high, for two reasons: the whole object's charge scale is off MIP so I am reading shape on a track whose normalisation is wrong, and about 50 cm of the fitted chain is a near-zero-charge bridge, which means the fit is demonstrably unreliable on this object. The competing reading is STM_ONLY on the strength of the single 1.57e5 terminal point; I rejected it because a Bragg peak is a shape over 10-20 cm, not one point, and 8x the local plateau is too high rather than too low.
evidence: A 120 cm kinked chain entering 0.4 cm from the z face and ending 29.6 cm from the x face. The charge scale is untrustworthy on this object: the chain's own plateau sits at about 2e4 e/cm, roughly 0.4 of the 5e4 MIP seen on clean tracks in this set, and one segment, 47013, carries 106 points over 63.6 cm at a mean 2634 e/cm, so about half the fitted length is a near-charge-free bridge between the piece at the stop and a normal 4.2e4 piece 77-86 cm out. Over the region that is measured the profile is flat: 1.8-3.5e4 from s=3 all the way to s=25, no climb of the muon reference curve's shape anywhere in the last 10-20 cm. The only terminal feature is a three-point spike in the last 1.5 cm - 4.4e4, 7.2e4, then a single point at 1.57e5 - which is 8x the track's own plateau where a real Bragg peak is about 2.2x MIP, so it reads as end-of-track charge pile-up, not a Bragg curve. f_meas gives the exit: in U the fit's last points sit inside a wide dead band at channels 2168-2182, and in V the same points sit on the dead pair at 6050-6060, so the track most plausibly left through a dead region in two planes. Past the fit end there is nothing that reads as an electron - 47012, a 6.7 cm 12-point piece the chain calls pdg 11 shower, sits at cos_fwd -0.88 only 8-11 cm out, hugging the muon body where the chain itself still runs, so it is body activity; 47009 is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck at cos_fwd -0.98 on the same body line; and 115014 is a 2-point survey-only speck 47 cm out that neither stage was offered. On a through-goer there is no stop to define gamma or michel against, so all three take delta / other.

notes: Nothing at all past the stop: the two survey specks at 55-58 cm are the only other drawn rows and I read them as unrelated activity, not capture gammas, because there is no decay side on this item for a gamma to sit on. High confidence on both the verdict and the kind.
evidence: A textbook stopper: one 113 cm chain of 188 points, entering 0.3 cm from the anode x face and ending 92.5 cm from the nearest face, as deeply contained as anything in this chunk. At high zoom the Bragg rise is unmistakable and it tracks the black muon reference curve's shape over the last 15 cm rather than jumping: a 5.5e4 plateau out at s=40-100, 6.5e4 by s=15, 7-8e4 through s=8-12, 9-9.5e4 at s=5-7, 1.05-1.10e5 at s=2-3, and the last two points at 1.20e5 and 1.315e5, which is exactly the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers top out in, sitting just under the curve without crossing it. The three momentum estimates from the track itself agree (range 368, dQ/dx 382, MCS 349 MeV/c, MCS ambiguity 0.04), which is what a fully contained stopping track looks like. The three azimuths show a clean single spine with only a thin sheath of image points and absolutely nothing attached at the stop - no arm, no bridged piece, no charge leaving the end in any direction, so there is no Michel and no decay side. The only other drawn objects are two survey specks, 2 points and 0.3 cm at 55.2 cm and 2 points and 0.8 cm at 57.8 cm, at cos_fwd -0.04 and -0.17, perpendicular to a body line that runs at cos_fwd -1.0. Two 2-point specks of that size, at the outer edge of the 60 cm ring and in unrelated directions on an item with no arm to define a Michel side, are the scattered-speck case rather than the on-the-Michel-side case, so they are delta / other and the kind is none. No dead channels anywhere near the stop in U, V or W.

notes: The Bragg is absent, not merely unclear: the last 20 cm sit below the track's own plateau. I called STM_MICHEL on the Michel topology alone, which the rubric allows, with the deep containment and the absence of any continuation supporting it. Medium because the arm is only 3.9 cm and 3.3 MeV at a 142 degree kink, and because I chose not to move the pin to the s=7.5 spike on the strength of a comparable spike 85 cm up the track - if that spike is the real Bragg peak instead, the stop is 7 cm back and the last 7 cm of segment 55001 are the Michel's first part.
evidence: A 181 cm chain of 303 points entering 0.4 cm from the z face and ending 102 cm from the nearest face - one of the deepest stops in this chunk, and no continuation past the fit end in any of the three azimuths. The dQ/dx is a mess rather than a Bragg curve: the plateau is 4.5-5.5e4, the last 20 cm run mostly BELOW it at 1.7-4.6e4, and the terminal points measure 4.6e4 at s=2.5, 7.6-7.9e4 at s=1.6-2.1 and 3.9e4 at s=0.8, so there is no climb of the reference curve's shape into the stop. There is a four-point spike to 0.90, 1.04, 1.20 and 1.27e5 at s=6.7-8.6, which is tempting to read as the real Bragg peak with a 7 cm overshoot, but a near-identical excursion to 1.14-1.17e5 sits at s=85-87, 85 cm up the same track where no stop can be, so excursions of that size are a property of this noisy track rather than a peak - on that control I left the pin at the fit's last point. What carries the verdict is the arm: 55004, 7 points over 3.9 cm at 2.1e4 e/cm, attached at the shared stop vertex with a 142 degree kink, which the chain reconstructs as a 3.3 MeV electron. That is 0.4 of MIP where a muon at its own Bragg peak would be several times MIP, and a muon with only a few MeV left cannot kick out a 3.3 MeV delta, so the arm is a second particle emitted at the stop, not the muon continuing and not a delta. Within 3.4 cm of the stop direction does not discriminate, so the 142 degree kink does not demote it. Everything else drawn sits at cos_fwd -0.92 to -0.99 squarely on the muon body line - two survey specks at 53-55 cm, one 0.1 cm speck at 25.8 cm, and a 9.8 cm near-zero-charge shower piece 128 cm out at the entry end - so all four are delta / other.

notes: The only judgement call is the 2-point survey speck 213030 at 60.5 cm, cos_fwd -0.83: it is about 33 cm off the body line, which is clear of the body, but it lies in the backward hemisphere rather than past the stop and is not along the Michel arm, so I read it as delta / other. Calling it gamma would make the kind both without touching the verdict.
evidence: A 697 cm cosmic crossing the whole detector, 1147 chain points, entering 0.8 cm from one x face and ending 47.4 cm from the other, so the stop is comfortably inside. The Bragg rise is textbook and follows the black muon curve's shape over the last 15-20 cm rather than jumping: a 4.5e4 plateau beyond s=40, 5.5e4 by s=15-20, 6.5-7.5e4 through s=5-10, 8.5-9.5e4 at s=3-5, 1.05-1.10e5 at s=1.5-2, and the last two points at 1.20e5 and 1.27e5, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band and just under the curve without crossing it. Range 1658, dQ/dx 1719 and MCS 1592 MeV/c all agree with ambiguity 0.00. Attached at the very stop vertex is 67013: 24 points over 13.9 cm at a mean 4.9e4 e/cm, a 40 MeV electron leaving at a 144 degree kink, and the d and e azimuths show it unmistakably as a separate teal arm branching off the yellow muon spine at the star with its own transverse spread. A muon at 1.27e5 cannot continue at MIP, and 14 cm is the right range for a 40 MeV electron, so the arm is the Michel; within 12.5 cm of the stop the backward direction does not demote it. The remaining rows are all body activity at cos_fwd -0.97: two pdg 11 shower pieces 280 cm and 625 cm back along the chain, and the fitted chain segments themselves. One 2-point 0.2 cm survey speck sits 60.5 cm out at cos_fwd -0.83, backward rather than past the stop and not along the Michel arm's direction in either 3-D azimuth, so it is delta / other and does not raise the kind to both. No dead channels at the stop in U, V or W.

notes: The chain scores this shape_flat with no daughter, but the Bragg peak is there at 1.375e5 and there is a 14.4 cm MIP arm attached at the stop that the chain left unassigned - worth the owner's eye as a missed Michel. Medium rather than high only because michel_kind rests on the 2-point speck 86004 at 51 cm: it satisfies the gamma rule literally (isolated, past the stop, clear of the body, inside 60 cm) but it sits in the opposite hemisphere from the Michel arm, and read as an unrelated speck the kind would be attached.
evidence: 188 cm, 316 chain points, ending 45.4 cm from the nearest face; the other end stops 32 cm short of the z wall with only faint thinned context charge beyond it, so the object is essentially complete and the stop end is untouched by that. The Bragg rise is clean and follows the black muon curve over the last 15 cm: 5.4e4 plateau beyond s=40, 6.5-8.7e4 through s=10-17, 8.5-9.5e4 at s=3-6, then 1.375e5 at s=2, which is the terminal segment 24002 - 5 points over 2.5 cm at a mean 1.38e5. One partial-charge point at 4.8e4 sits at s=0.2 after that peak; a single low point at the very end is ordinary scatter rather than a sustained collapse over several cm, so I left the pin alone. The decisive feature is 24003, which the chain leaves unassigned and reports as no daughter with n_stop_arms 0: 25 points over 14.4 cm at a mean 5.2e4 e/cm, and the zoomed d and e azimuths show it unmistakably as a green arm leaving the stop vertex and curving away, with its own vertex square at its far end, plainly off the amber muon spine rather than lying along it. A muon whose last 2.5 cm are at 1.38e5 cannot continue at MIP, and a muon with a few MeV left cannot kick out a 30 MeV delta, so that arm is a second particle emitted at the stop; at d_min 2.46 cm direction does not discriminate, so cos_fwd -0.83 does not demote it. This is a Michel the chain missed. A 2-point 0.1 cm speck sits 51.2 cm out at cos_fwd +0.94, isolated, forward of the stop and clear of a body line that runs at cos_fwd -1.00, so gamma. The two survey pieces at 40-47 cm, cos_fwd -0.74 and -0.76, are in the backward hemisphere rather than past the stop and read as unrelated activity: delta / other.

notes: Busy and bent; the hard part is that the Michel cloud branches from a junction about 5 cm short of the fit's last point rather than from the star itself. I did not move the pin because the profile RISES into the fit's last point instead of collapsing away from a peak, which is the opposite of the overshoot signature. Medium: the Bragg tops out at only 1.01e5 against a 6-7e4 plateau, and cos_fwd is unreliable here because the track is visibly curved, so both the michel and gamma assignments lean on the 3-D azimuths rather than the numbers.
evidence: A short one, 51.6 cm of chain in 87 points, entering 0.3 cm from the anode x face and ending 31.0 cm from the nearest face, so the stop is inside. The three azimuths show a coherent 38 cm spine (52023 plus 52013, both at cos_fwd -1.00) running into a junction about 5-6 cm from the fit's last point, a short fitted piece carrying on from that junction to the star, and a diffuse multi-piece cloud leaving the same junction in a third direction - so this is a Y, not a single line, and the object is not MESSY because the spine is unmistakable. This track is visibly bent, so I treated cos_fwd as advisory and read the geometry off the azimuths, as the curvature trap says. Charge: the plateau is 6-7e4 and the profile dips to 1-4e4 through the junction region at s=6-12, then climbs over the last 5 cm - 5.0e4 at s=4-5, 6.0-6.7e4 at s=1.6-3.8, 8.4e4 at s=0.8 and 1.01e5 at the last point. That is a factor-two rise off the plateau and it holds a constant 0.55-0.63 fraction of the black muon curve all the way in, so the shape matches even though it never reaches the 1.2e5 band. The cloud past the junction - 52016 through 52020, five pieces of 5.8 to 10.8 cm carrying 2.4e3 to 2.6e4 e/cm, which the chain types pdg 11 shower and then leaves unassigned with no daughter - totals roughly 20 MeV of diffuse EM sitting 5.5 to 17.6 cm from the stop. A muon with a few MeV left cannot make a 20 MeV shower, so it is not brem or a delta off the dying muon; at that distance direction does not discriminate, so I read it as the Michel. Three compact pieces of 0.6 to 1.9 cm and 2 to 4 points sit 25 to 32 cm out at cos_fwd -0.19 to -0.59, well clear of a body line at cos_fwd -1.00 and roughly along the shower's own ray, so gamma. 52014, a 3.5 cm piece at cos_fwd -0.99 sitting 27-30 cm back squarely on the body, is delta / other despite its pdg 11 label.

notes: Flat-profile THRU. The end is 28 cm short of the z face with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit in any plane, which the rubric's flat-profile clause covers explicitly: the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. MCS far above range corroborates a truncated track.
evidence: A dead-straight 212 cm line, 352 chain points, entering exactly on the anode x face (d_face 0.0) and ending 28.0 cm from the z face; all three azimuths and all three projections show one rod with no kink, no branch and no arm anywhere. The profile is flat to the last point: the segment means are 5.2e4 over both chain segments, and at high zoom the points from s=0 to s=20 sit at 3.6-5.8e4 with the very last point at 3.6e4 - if anything slightly below the track's own plateau, and nowhere near a climb of the muon curve's shape. The nearest thing to a feature is a pair at 1.10e5 at s=17 and a pair at 8.7-9.0e4 at s=11-12, well back from the end and of the size this track scatters by anyway. A stopping muon cannot end at MIP, so this end is not a stop. The track's own MCS momentum, 1773 MeV/c against 589 from range with ambiguity 0.90, is the signature of a track much longer than the piece that was fitted. Nothing sits off the muon body: the only other rows are a 0.1 cm 2-point speck 12.6 cm out at cos_fwd -0.85, a 0.6 cm 2-point speck 26.9 cm out at cos_fwd -0.94, and a 5.7 cm pdg 11 shower piece 33-38 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00, all three squarely on the body line, and on a through-goer there is no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so all three are delta / other. f_meas shows the fit's last points clear of dead channels in all three planes - the U end at 3475 and the W end at 11940 are both between dead bands, not on one.

notes: The verdict is solid; the kind is the judgement. I split the outer rows on the body-line test (cos_fwd -0.85 or beyond goes to delta / other) and read the inner shell of seven few-MeV specks at 14-37 cm as capture gammas rather than unrelated activity, because they cluster in a shell around the stop rather than sitting singly at the edge of the 60 cm ring - which is how I read the two lone 55-58 cm specks on 039349_63/52 and called that one none. If the owner treats a scattered shell as unrelated too, this becomes STM_ONLY / none. The chain's own Michel object is a 2-point speck across a 14 cm gap and I demoted it to gamma.
evidence: A 291 cm cosmic, 488 chain points, entering exactly on the anode x face and ending 24.8 cm from the nearest face. The Bragg rise is as good as any in this chunk and follows the black curve's shape over the last 15-20 cm: a 5.4e4 plateau beyond s=25, 6.5-7.2e4 through s=5-15, 7.8-8.1e4 at s=2-4, then 1.37e5, 1.44e5 and 1.65e5 in the last 1.5 cm, with the segment means climbing 4.2e4 to 4.4e4 to 6.0e4 to 7.3e4 as you walk in. The last point actually sits a touch above the reference curve, which is hotter than the usual 1.2-1.35e5 ceiling, but the shape is unambiguous. Range 768, dQ/dx 663 and MCS 623 MeV/c agree with ambiguity 0.02. Nothing is attached at the stop: the object the chain offers as the Michel, 200022, is 2 points over 0.5 cm carrying 3.2 MeV and bridged across 14.26 cm of empty space, and a 0.5 cm two-point speck across a 14 cm gap is not a 35 MeV electron - it is a detached dot, so this is not STM_MICHEL. What is there instead is a shell of seven compact specks 14 to 37 cm from the stop, 0.0 to 1.5 cm and 2 to 3 points each, totalling only about 8 MeV between them, lying in many different directions around the stop and clear of the body line by cos_fwd -0.69 to +0.84. Seven small blobs in a tight shell around a contained stopping-muon end at a few MeV apiece is what muon capture looks like, so I read them as gammas and the kind as detached dots. The four rows at cos_fwd -0.86 to -0.93 - a 0.5 cm speck at 53 cm, a 3.7 cm piece at 55-58 cm, the 6.4 cm unfitted cluster C293 at 51-54 cm and the pdg 211 piece 262 cm back at the entry end - all sit on the muon body line and are delta / other.

notes: Low confidence, genuinely three-way. The competing readings are (a) UNDERSHOOT: 65003 is the muon's own last 3.8 cm, the true stop is 3.8 cm further out and this is STM_ONLY - I rejected it only because 6.9e4 is at MIP rather than several times it; and (b) THRU, because the profile is scattered rather than shaped and charge continues collinearly past the fit end at the same level. I went STM_MICHEL because the object clearly terminates in open volume with a range consistent with its KE, and because the rubric puts a forward piece at or below MIP in the ordinary Michel case. The stop is only 6.9 cm from the anode face, the track runs nearly parallel to that face, and the whole track's charge sits at about half the panel's MIP line, so every charge judgement here is on shaky footing.
evidence: A short one: 38.5 cm of chain in 65 points that enters exactly on the anode x face and runs almost parallel to it, so the fit's last point is only 6.9 cm from that face even though the track has travelled 38 cm in y and z. The object genuinely terminates rather than heading for a wall - the direction is mostly in y and z, where the nearest wall is far away, and range KE 118.6 MeV matches the roughly 42 cm of total charge, so a stopping particle is the right reading. The charge scale is depressed: the chain segments average 3.6-3.9e4 where the panel's own MIP reference sits at 6.7e4, which is what a track skimming the anode plane looks like. Against that plateau the last 5 cm do lift - 4.4e4, 6.0e4, 7.0e4 and two points at 7.8e4 - but it is a factor of two at best and it is not monotone, and there is a comparable pair at 7.8e4 and 8.95e4 at s=14-16 where no stop can be, so I would not call this a convincing Bragg on its own. What sits past the fit end is 65003: 7 points over 3.8 cm at 6.9e4, dstop 0.00, cos_fwd +0.99, typed pdg 11 by the chain, which also flags n_stop_arms 1. I checked this against the undershoot signature and it does not meet it - the load-bearing clause there is charge several times MIP at 0.9-1.2e5, and 6.9e4 is essentially at the panel's own MIP line, which the rubric says is the ordinary Michel case rather than a muon tip. So I left the pin alone and tagged it michel. The remaining two rows sit on the body at cos_fwd -0.99: a 4.1 cm piece at 17-20 cm, and 65010, a 20 cm 34-point trail at 6363 e/cm that the azimuths show running parallel to and offset from the amber chain - a near-charge-free companion trail, not decay charge - so both are delta / other.

notes: Flat-then-zero THRU. The end is 53 cm from every face, no visible continuation and no dead-region exit, which the rubric's flat-profile clause covers: the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. The last few centimetres are zero-charge fit points rather than a real collapse, so I did not read them as an overshoot. MCS far above range corroborates.
evidence: A single straight 108 cm rod of 182 points, entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 53.1 cm from the nearest face, with nothing else drawn anywhere near it - the object table has only the two fitted chain segments, and the three azimuths show a bare spine with a thin sheath of image points and no arm, branch, dot or speck at either end. The profile never rises: the plateau is about 5e4 out to s=100, it is still 4.5-5.5e4 at s=8-12, and then it only falls - 3.1-3.7e4 at s=5-8, 1.4-2.4e4 at s=2-5, and 0.3-2.8e4 over the last 2 cm, where the terminal points are the near-zero fit points the rubric says to ignore. Discounting those, the last measured charge is at or below the track's own plateau, so there is no climb of the muon curve's shape anywhere in the last 10-20 cm and a stopping muon cannot end that way. I checked this against the overshoot signature and it does not qualify: there is no peak above the plateau anywhere before the fall, and there is no second object for a collapsing segment to be bridging to, so I left the pin at the fit's last point. The track's own MCS momentum of 628 MeV/c against 359 from range, ambiguity 0.77, is the truncated-track signature. Both drawn rows are fitted chain segments and take muon; with no stop there is no gamma or michel to assign, so the kind is none. f_meas shows the fit's last points clear of dead channels in all three planes - U at 3225, V at 7030 and W at 11560 are each between dead bands, not on one.

notes: No overshoot, no undershoot: the last point IS the peak at 1.35e5. Confidence medium only because michel_kind hinges entirely on one survey-only 2-point speck at 50.2 cm; the competing reading tags it delta / other and makes the kind none.
evidence: 293 cm curved chain entering 0.4 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 123.7 cm from the nearest active face, so contained by the numbers even though the chain rejects it as stop_near_boundary - that rejection is a seam call, the stop sitting 5.0 cm from a y seam, not a wall. The profile is a 4-5e4 plateau far out, lifts to 5.5-6.5e4 over the last 20 cm, reaches 7-8e4 at s=0.3-4 and the fit last point itself sits at 1.35e5, right at the top of the 1.2-1.35e5 band the rubric gives for real stoppers here. Nothing collapses after that peak and nothing continues past it, so the pin stays where the fit put it. The body has two mid-track gaps visible in the 3-D azimuths (seam or dead-region drops well upstream of the stop) but the last 30 cm is continuous, and f_meas shows the track ending cleanly at the pin time slice in U, V and W with the dead-channel bands beside the track rather than on it. There is no arm and no dot at the stop - n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - so this is not a Michel item. The one other drawn object, 66006, is a 2-point 0.7 cm speck carrying 1.5e4, 50.2 cm from the stop at cos_fwd +0.67, i.e. forward and well off the muon body line, which the muon runs away from in the opposite sense; the projections put it at z 139 / x 35 while the body heads to z 227 / x 340. Isolated, past the stop, clear of the body and inside 60 cm makes it a gamma by the table, and charge is explicitly not a criterion, so the kind is detached dots. That single speck is the only reason the kind is not none, and it is a survey-only 2-point object, which is what the medium confidence is for; the STM_ONLY verdict itself is unambiguous.

notes: THRU on a flat profile; the fit end coincides with a dead-channel band in V and W, so the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: 139.5 cm single-segment chain entering exactly at the z face (d_face 0.0) and ending in the corner region 36.5 cm from the y wall and 41.8 cm from the z wall. The profile is the whole story: it sits flat between 4.5e4 and 6.5e4 from s=100 all the way in to the last point, with the last 20 cm indistinguishable from the plateau at 50 cm - no lift off the plateau, nothing following the muon reference curve, and the fit last point itself at about 5.5e4, below the 6.7e4 MIP line rather than above it. The scattered 1.0-1.6e5 points at s=8, 18, 22-25, 60-70 and 85-95 are spread the length of the track, not concentrated at the end, so they are body deltas, not a Bragg rise. A stopping muon cannot be at MIP on its last point, so this is a through-goer, and the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). f_meas says where it went: in V and W the last measured points sit right on a narrow dead-channel band at V 5127 and W 9160, so the cluster ends where the imaging does. The three azimuths show a straight unbroken body with nothing at all past the star. The only other drawn object, 123001, is a 6-point 3.2 cm survey-only piece 50.4 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, i.e. lying on the muon body line, which is delta / other by the body-line rule and in any case would be delta / other on a THRU item since gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop that does not exist here. No undershoot candidate and no peak to overshoot.

notes: THRU on a flat MIP profile over the only 43 cm of the chain that has charge; the other 115 cm of the fit is a chargeless phantom line (dqdx 2207). Competing reading MESSY. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: A degenerate fit. The chain claims 261.1 cm but only about 43 cm of it carries charge: segment 33003 is 115 cm long with a mean dQ/dx of 2207 e/cm, and in b, d and e the object is a solid amber point-cloud track from the star to a sharp kink, after which a bare blue-grey fit line runs off in a different direction with no cloud on it at all. f_meas shows the same thing - the amber track descends from time slice 1590 to 1495 in U, V and W, and past that the fit is a horizontal constant-drift-time line with only two or three isolated charge patches on it, not a continuous track. The KE estimates say it too: 602 MeV by range against 129 by dQ/dx and 119 by MCS, ambiguity 0.89. Judging only the real 43 cm: the profile is flat between 4e4 and 6e4 from s=43 all the way in, and the fit last point sits at about 6.3e4, below the 6.7e4 MIP line and nowhere near the reference curve, which is at 1.6e5 there. No lift off the plateau over the last 10-20 cm at all, so no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). The stop is 16.3 cm from the z wall with no dead band on the last points in any plane - the charge simply stays at MIP and stops, which is the flat-profile THRU the rubric describes. The three other drawn objects are 2-point gamma-body-exclusion specks all at the same spot 32.6-33.0 cm away at cos_fwd -0.2 to -0.3, well off to the side; on a THRU item they are delta / other by rule, and one of them carries an implausible 1.4e5 over 0.2 cm, which is a 2-point artefact rather than a physical gamma. The competing reading is MESSY, given how broken the fit is, but there is a coherent 43 cm spine here, not an EM blob, so I kept THRU.

notes: THRU: flat-to-sagging profile with the fit end sitting on a V dead-channel band. The five aligned unassigned pieces are a separate track 24 cm away, not decay activity. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: 81.8 cm chain entering right at the y face (0.2 cm) and ending 38.5 cm from the same y wall. The profile never rises: it sits at 4-5.5e4 from s=80 in to s=20, and over the last 15 cm it actually sags to 3-4e4, below its own plateau and far below the 6.7e4 MIP line, with the fit last points down at 1-3e4. There is no peak anywhere to collapse from, so this is not the overshoot case - it is simply a track that is still at or under MIP where a stopper would be two to three times above it. f_meas says why it ends where it does: the last measured points sit inside a hatched dead-channel band at V 7540-7555, with further dead bands immediately beside the end in U (3700-3705) and W (12070), so the cluster ends in a dead region rather than at a Bragg peak. The chain reaches the same verdict independently (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) and its KE estimates are incoherent, 213 MeV by range against 802 by MCS at ambiguity 0.90. The five unassigned pieces 229010, 230011, 231012, 232013 and 233014 are not decay products: their centroids march in a straight line from (260.7, 275.6, 198.0) to (283.2, 275.6, 207.2) at constant y about 22 cm below the stop, which the d and e azimuths show as a separate 25 cm track running its own direction with a clean gap to the muon, and 81009 is a 7 cm shower-typed piece 44-50 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. on the muon body. On a THRU item all of them are delta / other by rule anyway, since gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop this track does not have.

notes: Clean stopper, pin unmoved. No overshoot (the terminal 20-40 per cent dip is one-to-two-point scatter still above MIP with nothing past the stop to bridge to) and no undershoot.
evidence: 197 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the x (anode) face and stopping deep, 110.2 cm from the nearest active face. Textbook Bragg: the plateau sits at 5.5e4 out beyond s=20, lifts to 6-7e4 by s=12-15, 8-9e4 at s=6-9, 1.1-1.22e5 at s=2.8-4.4 and a top point at 1.37e5 at s=5, tracking the muon reference curve the whole way in, and the last-segment mean in the object table agrees at 1.08e5 over the final 5 cm. The very last 1.5 cm scatters between 6.9e4 and 1.09e5, which is 20-40 per cent below the peak, but that is ordinary end scatter, not the overshoot signature: it is one or two points over about 1.5 cm rather than a sustained collapse over several cm, it never gets near the 0.15-0.5 of MIP band those collapsed segments occupy (it is still at or above MIP), and above all there is nothing on the far side for the fit to bridge to - the object table has no row past the stop, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters and no capture gamma in the ring. So the pin stays on the fit last point. The three azimuths show a straight unbroken body with the stop clean and empty, and f_meas confirms the last measured points are the brightest ones in U, V and W with nothing beyond and the dead-channel bands standing off the track. The only non-chain object, 37011, is a 27-point 15.9 cm shower-typed piece 157-166 cm back up the body at cos_fwd -1.0, so body activity: delta / other. Nothing past the stop reads as an electron or a gamma, hence STM_ONLY with kind none.

notes: THRU on a flat profile despite a 89.7 cm d_face - the rubric case where containment does not decide. No visible continuation past the end; no overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: 231 cm straight chain entering 0.4 cm from the z face and ending 89.7 cm from the nearest wall, so deeply contained by the numbers - and that is exactly the case the rubric says containment does not settle. The profile is flat: 5-6.5e4 from s=100 all the way in, and over the last 15 cm the points sit between 4.5e4 and 6.9e4, i.e. at or just below the 6.7e4 MIP line and far under the muon reference curve, which is at 8e4 by s=5 and 1e5 by s=2. There is no lift off the plateau at any scale. The scattered 1.0-1.6e5 points are spread over s=3, 20-30, 40 and 60-85, the whole length of the body, so they are deltas, not an end-of-range rise; the single 1.23e5 point at s=3.5 is one of that family and has no neighbours climbing with it. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot be sitting at MIP on its last point, so this is a through-goer, which is also the chain verdict (no_bragg, shape_flat) and matches its MCS momentum of 2.3 GeV against 632 MeV by range, ambiguity 0.87 - the scattering says it never slowed down. The three azimuths show a straight unbroken body ending abruptly at the star with nothing past it and no visible continuation, and f_meas shows the last measured points at ordinary charge with a dead band running alongside the track in U. The cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out. The other three objects are all on the muon body line and hence delta / other: 41011 and 41014 are shower-typed pieces at cos_fwd -1.0, 215 cm and 51 cm back respectively, and C136 is a 14-point unfitted cluster 58.5 cm back at cos_fwd -0.98. On a THRU item they would be delta / other in any case.

notes: THRU on a flat sub-MIP profile. The apparent continuation past the star in the Z-Y projection is a different object - it is at X -100 to -320 in the top view. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: 218 cm chain entering 0.4 cm from the z face and ending 127.3 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained. The profile is flat and low the whole way: 4.5-5.5e4 from s=100 in to s=5, never touching the 6.7e4 MIP line, let alone rising above it, and the muon reference curve at s=5 is 8e4 and at s=2 is 1e5, so the data is a factor of two under the curve exactly where a stopper would be climbing. Over the last 4 cm it goes the wrong way - a small bump to 5.5e4 around s=3-5 and then two points down at 3.3-3.8e4 at s<1.5. That two-point end dip is not the overshoot signature: there is no peak to collapse from (5.5e4 is the plateau, not a peak), the drop lasts about 1.5 cm, and the object table has nothing past the stop for the fit to bridge to. So: no Bragg rise at the fit end, hence THRU, which the chain also concludes (no_bragg, shape_flat) and which its MCS momentum of 916 MeV/c against 604 by range supports. I checked the continuation question carefully. In the Z-Y side projection a faint context trail appears to carry straight on past the star for another metre, but in the Z-X top projection that trail is at X between -100 and -320 while the star is at X +52, so it is a different object that only lines up in one projection - and the three 3-D azimuths and b_3d_wide all show the point cloud ending cleanly at the star with nothing beyond. The cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out. Both drawn objects are fitted chain segments, so both are muon: 64001 the 217 cm body and 64002 a 3-point 1.1 cm stub at the far entry end.

notes: Undershoot checked and rejected on charge: the offered Michel is 5.1 cm at 0.65 MIP with cos_fwd 0.70, not a 1-3 cm stub at 0.9-1.2e5, and the muon already peaks at 1.4e5 on its own last point. Pin unmoved; no overshoot. michel_kind both rests on two 2-point specks at 29 and 49 cm that lie within 24 and 48 degrees of the arm direction.
evidence: 154 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and stopping 21.0 cm from the x (anode) face, inside the volume. The Bragg rise is clean and follows the reference curve the whole way: 5.5-6.5e4 plateau beyond s=15, 7-8e4 at s=8-11, 8.7-9.5e4 at s=4-6, 1.1-1.15e5 at s=2-3 and a top pair at 1.37-1.40e5 within the last 1.5 cm, and the range, dQ/dx and MCS momenta agree at 461/466/444 MeV/c with ambiguity 0.32. I ran the undershoot check explicitly, because the chain does offer a forward piece as the Michel: 75001, 9 points over 5.1 cm at a 45 degree kink from the stop vertex. It fails the undershoot on the load-bearing clause, which is charge - its mean is 43491 e/cm, below the 6.7e4 MIP line, and on the panel its points scatter between 1.9e4 and 1.03e5 with most of them at 2-3.5e4, whereas the undershoot piece is a 1-3 cm stub at 0.9-1.2e5 sitting straight ahead at cos_fwd above 0.85. Here cos_fwd is 0.70 and the piece is 5 cm long. Decisive on top of that, the muon already has its Bragg peak at 1.4e5 on its own last point and a muon cannot have two of those, so an arm leaving that peak at or below MIP is a second particle - the ordinary STM_MICHEL case. Five centimetres and 13.9 MeV is the right scale for a Michel, and the c, d and e azimuths all show it as a distinct blue arm breaking off the star at a visible angle. Past the stop there are also two detached 2-point specks: 214006 at 29.1 cm, cos_fwd 0.41, and 213005 at 48.5 cm, cos_fwd -0.05, both well clear of the muon body and both detached across a clean charge-free gap. Taking their 3-D directions from the stop, they sit 24 and 48 degrees off the Michel arm direction and only 29 degrees from each other, so they are clustered on the decay side rather than scattered around the ring, which the rubric makes gammas - charge is not a criterion for them. Michel plus gammas gives kind both.

notes: THRU on a flat profile. The 1.1-1.2e5 pair at s=3.5-4.5 is one of a family of isolated delta spikes along the whole body, not a Bragg peak - no climb into it and the following charge stays at 0.7-0.8 MIP. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: Short 75.6 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 40.3 cm from the z wall. The profile is flat at 4.5-5.5e4 over essentially its whole length, sitting on and just under the 6.7e4 MIP line, and the last 2-3 cm into the fit end are at 4.5-5.5e4 with one point at 3.8e4 - no lift at all, against a reference curve that is at 8e4 by s=5 and 1e5 by s=2. Two orange points do appear at s=3.5 and s=4.5 carrying 1.19e5 and 1.09e5, and I looked hard at whether they are a peak the fit then overshoots. They are not: there is no progressive climb into them (s=5 to s=20 is back at 4.5-6.5e4), an identical isolated pair or single appears at s=20, 30, 35, 47 and 55 all along the body, so they belong to that delta family, and the charge after them stays at 0.67-0.82 of MIP, well above the 0.15-0.5 band a bridged collapse occupies, with nothing past the stop for a fit to bridge to (n_dots 0, no unfitted clusters). So the pin stays and the verdict is driven by the flat end: THRU. The chain independently rejects it as no_bragg / shape_flat, and its MCS momentum of 765 MeV/c against 286 by range, ambiguity 0.87, says the track never slowed. The three azimuths show a straight body ending abruptly at the star with nothing beyond, and f_meas shows the last measured points at ordinary charge with dead bands crossing the body in W and standing beside it in V. Both drawn chain objects are muon - 76005 the 75.6 cm body and 76006 the 2.3 cm terminal segment at 4.8e4, which is a fitted pdg 13 stub and not offered as a Michel, so no undershoot candidate. 218004 is a 7-point 3.8 cm shower-excluded piece hanging off the body 26 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, visible in all three azimuths as a small spur on the track: delta / other, which is also what a THRU item requires.

notes: Clean short stopper, pin unmoved. Peak 1.0e5, a little below the usual band, and the upstream end is at 0.4 MIP - both consistent with the drift-parallel topology degrading the dQ/dx scale; the shape of the rise is not in doubt. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: Short isolated 44.3 cm chain, nothing else in the event at all - 303 image points and zero thinned context points - running almost purely along the drift axis, from x -202.8 to -245.3 with z fixed at 287-288 and only 7 cm of y. Both ends stand off the z wall, the entry by 10.2 cm and the stop by 11.2 cm, so neither end is at a face. The profile rises monotonically the whole way in and follows the muon reference curve: 2-3.5e4 at s=35-44, 4-5e4 at s=20-30, 5.5-6.5e4 at s=10-18, 7-8e4 at s=4-8, 8.4-9.2e4 at s=1-3 and 9.7e4-1.02e5 on the last points. That is a factor of four rise into the fit end with no collapse after it, so the pin stays where the fit put it and the chain agrees, accepting it as an STM. The peak tops out at 1.0e5 rather than the 1.2-1.35e5 usual for stoppers here and the far end sits at 0.4 of MIP, which is lower than a 44 cm-range muon should be that early - I read both as a scale effect of the drift-parallel geometry, where the charge lands on one or two wires and the path-length assignment is poor, rather than as evidence against the stop, since the rubric asks for shape off the plateau and not an absolute number and the shape is unambiguous. The three azimuths show a clean single track with the star at one end, the green entry triangle at the other and absolutely nothing past the stop; f_meas shows a near-vertical track in time at fixed channel in U, V and W with the dead bands standing clear of it and no charge beyond the end. The object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters and no capture gamma in the ring, so there is no decay activity to attribute: STM_ONLY with kind none.

notes: THRU on a flat-then-collapsing profile with no visible continuation past the fit end; the mechanism is a dead-channel exit in U and W (see f_meas), not a face crossing. Undershoot signature checked and EXCLUDED: the terminal segment 28001 carries 1.1e4 e/cm (0.17 MIP) at cos_fwd -0.46, nowhere near the 0.9-1.2e5 / cos_fwd >= +0.85 tip that manufactures a false STM_MICHEL. Overshoot/pin-move also excluded: that signature needs a peak several cm before the last point, and this profile never rises above its own plateau, so no --pin-rr. Residual risk: dead U/W wires in the last few cm could mask a real Bragg peak; the inward FALL from s=12 to s=5, outside the dead bands, is what argues against it.
evidence: 204.6 cm chain, enters 37.5 cm from the nearest (x) face at z=150 and the fit ends at z=276.5, 22 cm from the z wall and well inside the FV, so containment is not what decides this one. The dQ/dx profile is the whole story: it sits on its own 6.5-6.7e4 plateau all the way in, and over the last 12 cm it FALLS rather than rises - about 6.4e4 at s=12, 5.4e4 at s=5 - passing under the muon reference curve exactly where that curve is climbing through 7-9e4, and then the final 5 cm collapse through 3e4, 1.9e4, 1.4e4, 0.9e4 to a knot of points near 0.4-0.5e4 at s<1.5. There is no rise above the plateau anywhere, ragged or otherwise, so the operative Bragg test fails. f_meas shows why the tail dies: the fit end sits on a dead-channel band in U (bands at global rank ~1487-1497 and 1505-1525, track ending near 1495) and on another in W (~9605-9615, track ending near 9610); V is clean there. So the cluster ended where the imaging ran out, not at a stop. The three stop azimuths show nothing leaving the end - the amber blob at the end is the particle-flow selection band, not charge - and the flow block itself reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The two 2-5 point specks the chain calls capture gammas sit 26.7-27.7 cm out at cos_fwd -0.09/-0.12, and the eight survey specks are scattered 32-53 cm out in unrelated directions; with no stop they are body and ambient activity, tagged delta / other per the THRU rule. What made this hard is that the dead wires could in principle also hide a genuine Bragg peak, which is why this is medium and not high - but the decline starts 12 cm out, before the dead bands bite, and a stopping muon cannot fall inward there.

notes: THRU on a flat-to-falling profile with no Bragg rise; deeply contained fit end (113 cm from the nearest face) with no visible continuation, which the rubric explicitly allows - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Dead-region confound checked and excluded: V and W are both live at the stop in f_meas. Undershoot signature EXCLUDED - no short high-charge forward tip; the only forward object, 102017, is 20-28 cm out at 0.63 MIP, not a couple of cm at 1e5. Overshoot/pin-move EXCLUDED - no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 242.7 cm chain entering 0.4 cm from the anode x face at z=82 and ending deep inside the volume at z=114, 113 cm from the nearest face and 115 cm from the cathode, so this is a containment-irrelevant case and the profile has to decide it. It decides it flatly: the far body sits around 5.2e4 with the track plateau line drawn at 6.7e4, and over the last 20 cm the points scatter 3.0-7.1e4 with no organised climb - the closest points run 6.05e4, 5.5e4, 5.2e4, 4.6e4, 3.7e4, 3.0e4 at s under 3 cm, and the local plateau reference actually dips to 5.2e4 near the origin, i.e. the profile is if anything falling inward while the muon reference curve is climbing through 8e4 to 1.6e5. Nothing resembling a Bragg rise, ragged or otherwise, and the chain agrees twice over with reject flags no_bragg and shape_flat; the range/MCS split (561 MeV by range against 1488 MeV by MCS, ambiguity 0.75) is the same story from the kinematics side. f_meas shows only the U plane partly dead at the fit end, with V and W both clean there, so the missing Bragg is not a dead-wire artefact - this is the flat-profile through-goer whose cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Past the fit end there is one real object, 102017: 17 points, 9.9 cm, 4.2e4 e/cm, 19.8-28.1 cm out at cos_fwd +0.25, which the three azimuths show sitting well off the muon line and separately oriented rather than collinear with it - a distinct object, and on a through-goer there is no stop to be gamma or michel relative to, so it takes delta / other along with the two small pdg-11 shower pieces on the body at 31-33 and 124-127 cm.

notes: THRU on a profile that bumps to 8.6e4 at s=5-11 cm and then falls back to MIP over the last 4 cm instead of continuing up the muon curve. Competing reading: a ragged Bragg whose tip is lost - rejected because all three planes are live at the stop in f_meas. Pin NOT moved: the terminal fall is to 0.9 of the plateau, not the far-below-plateau sustained collapse the pin rule requires (0.15-0.5 MIP), and there is no Michel past the end for the fit to have bridged to. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing at all past the fit end in any azimuth, so no short high-charge forward tip.
evidence: 341.6 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode x face at y=179, z=198 and ending at (-70, 17, 262), 36 cm from the z wall and 67 cm from the cathode, so containment does not settle it. The profile runs on a 6.0-6.5e4 body with the plateau line at 6.7e4, and the interesting feature is a modest bump at s = 5-11 cm reaching 7.4-8.6e4, which does sit on the muon reference curve where that curve passes 8-8.5e4. But it does not continue: over the last 4 cm the points fall back to 5.7-6.2e4 with a single 7.1e4 at s = 0.5, exactly where the reference curve is climbing through 1.0-1.6e5 and where a real stopper here should be reading 1.2-1.35e5. So the profile turns away from the curve at the steepest part of the Bragg, and the chain flags it twice, no_bragg and shape_flat. I checked the obvious alibi and it is not available: f_meas puts the stop end (time slice 1595) at U 1470, V 5325 and W 9585, all of them between dead bands rather than inside one, so the missing last centimetres of charge are not a dead-wire artefact. All three stop azimuths show a completely bare end - the amber is the particle-flow selection band, not charge - and the flow block confirms n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no gamma in the ring. All eleven unassigned pieces are pdg-11 shower fragments strung along the body at cos_fwd -1.0 between 101 and 205 cm back, i.e. body activity around the two kinks, not stop activity. The hard part is that 8.6e4 bump: read generously it is the start of a ragged Bragg that then loses its last few centimetres, which is why this is medium and not high - but the fall-back to MIP over the final 4 cm with all three planes live is what a through-goer looks like and not what a stopper looks like.

notes: THRU on a flat MIP profile to the last point. No continuation visible and the fit end is 139 cm from every face; per the rubric that is still THRU, the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Stop is live in all three planes in f_meas so no dead-region alibi. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing past the fit end at all. Overshoot/pin-move EXCLUDED: no peak and no collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 331 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the anode x face at y=-260, z=200 and ending at (59, -115, 159) - 139 cm from the nearest wall, 56 cm from the cathode, about as deeply contained as a fit end gets, so the picture cannot help and the profile has to decide. The profile is flat: the body sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 band the whole way and the last 15 cm are indistinguishable from the rest, running 4.9e4, 5.0e4, 5.3e4, 4.3e4 with a single 8.4e4 outlier and a single 3.8e4 at s under 1 cm. The muon reference curve climbs from 5.4e4 at s=40 through 6.6e4 at s=13 to 1.6e5 at the origin, and the data simply do not follow it up - there is no rise off the plateau, ragged or otherwise, and the chain flags no_bragg and shape_flat. The MCS/range split points the same way (762 MeV by range against 1090 by MCS, ambiguity 0.44). f_meas puts the stop at U 2635, V 6528, W 10845, all in live wire regions with the dead bands 60-100 channels away in every plane, so nothing is hiding the last centimetres. All three stop azimuths show a completely bare end with no arm, no dot, no speck - the amber is the flow selection band, not charge - and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no gamma in the ring. The only non-chain object is 49009, a 18 cm 31-point pdg-11 shower fragment at 4.3e3 e/cm lying on the muon body at cos_fwd -1.0, 234-241 cm back at the kink between the second and third chain segments: body activity, delta / other. This is the rubric case of a flat profile with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out.

notes: Close call between STM_MICHEL and THRU and the reason is in the evidence: the Bragg is ragged and gives up its last 4 cm, and the chain rejects with no_bragg + shape_flat, but the rubric makes a Michel topology sufficient on its own and the forward pieces are sub-MIP (0.6-0.7 of this track own ~5e4 plateau) and terminate after 2.8 cm, which is the ordinary-Michel case rather than a MIP stub carrying straight on. UNDERSHOOT EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: 63008/63002 carry 3.2e4 and 3.9e4 e/cm, an order of magnitude short of the 0.9-1.2e5 forward tip that manufactures a false STM_MICHEL. Pin NOT moved: the terminal fall is to about 4.8e4 against a ~5e4 plateau, not the sustained fall far below plateau the pin rule needs, so no --pin-rr. MCS/range disagree (391 vs 256 MeV, ambiguity 0.74), which is the strongest single argument for the THRU reading.
evidence: 102 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the anode x face at (340, -274, 235) and ending at (259, -222, 213), 81 cm from the nearest face and 256 cm from the cathode, so the end is genuinely inside the volume. This track is mostly along the drift and its own body plateau sits near 5e4, well under the fixed 6.7e4 MIP reference line the plot draws, so I read the last centimetres against 5e4 and not against that line. On that basis there is a rise: the far body runs 4.5-5.5e4, s = 12-25 cm sits at 6.0-7.0e4 and s = 5-10 cm reaches 6.5-8.0e4, following the shape of the muon curve, before the last 4 cm fall back to 4.1-5.5e4. Two isolated points at 1.08e5 and 1.18e5 sit at s = 9-10 cm, exactly at the vertex where the faint 63003 branch leaves the chain, so I read those two as a delta at that vertex rather than as the Bragg tip; the rise does not depend on them and it is ragged and loses its last few centimetres, which is why the chain flags no_bragg and shape_flat and why this is medium. What decides it is the topology past the end. Two fitted pieces, 63008 (3 pts, 1.3 cm, 3.2e4 e/cm, 0-1.2 cm out, cos_fwd +0.95) and 63002 (4 pts, 1.8 cm, 3.9e4, 1.2-2.8 cm out, cos_fwd +0.87), leave the stop vertex forward at an 18 deg kink and stop after 2.8 cm; f_meas shows them as real measured charge in all three planes, not a fit artefact. At 0.6-0.7 of this track own plateau they are at or below MIP, which is the rubric ordinary-Michel case and the opposite of the undershoot tip, and a stub simply carrying the muon straight on would be at MIP or above rather than sub-MIP and terminating after 2.8 cm. 6.9 MeV is a low Michel but it is a Michel shape. Beyond them, 209006 is a 2-point 0.4 cm speck 16.2-16.5 cm out at cos_fwd +0.95, detached across a clean gap and lying on the same side as the arm: a capture gamma by the isolation-plus-side rule, so the kind is both. The remaining chain piece 63003 is odd - 28 points over 16.5 cm at only 4.1e3 e/cm, branching off the body at the vertex 10 cm back - but it is on the muon side and the chain types it pdg 13, so it takes muon; its faintness is noted, not used to drive a tag.

notes: STM_ONLY. Stop is only 7.8 cm from the anode face, but the track is moving away from that face at the fit end (x 338 -> 332), so I read it as a contained stop rather than an exit; this is the least comfortable part of the call. The dQ/dx is compromised by the track running nearly parallel to the U wires (30 U channels for 68 cm of track), which is why most points read near zero and why the range/dQ-dx KE estimates disagree so violently (182 vs 55 MeV). Competing reading: the terminal 1.3e5 bunch is instrumental, the profile is simply unmeasured, and the item is UNCLEAR - I did not take it because the four-point monotone rise has the muon curve shape and the chain accepted the item as STM. Undershoot EXCLUDED and overshoot EXCLUDED: there is no object of any kind past the fit end, and no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 67.6 cm chain that skims the anode: it enters 1.9 cm from the x face at (338, 83, 51) and ends at (332, 82, 104), 7.8 cm from that same anode face, 103 cm from the z wall and 329 cm from the cathode, so the whole track sits 2-8 cm under the anode plane at essentially zero drift. Direction matters here - x runs 338 to 332 along the track, so at the fit end the muon is moving away from the anode, not into it, and the end is a stop rather than a face crossing even at 7.8 cm. The profile is the hard part and it is badly sparse: most of the 120 chain points read under 1.5e4 e/cm, with charge concentrated in three bunches at s = 0-2, 20-26 and 50-54 cm, and f_meas shows why - in U the whole 68 cm track occupies only channels 3010-3040, i.e. it runs nearly along the U wire direction, while V spans 6780-6865 and W 11230-11320. Ignoring the near-zero fit points as the rubric requires, the terminal bunch is a clean four-point monotone rise into the last point: 3.9e4 at s=2, 7.2e4 at s=1, 1.05e5 at s=0.3 and 1.30e5 at s=0, which is both the shape of the muon reference curve and exactly the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach here, and it is roughly twice the height of the other two bunches (6.5e4 and 5.5e4). The chain agrees, accepting this as STM with no reject flags. All three stop azimuths show a bare end with nothing past it - no arm, no dot, no speck - and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring, so there is no decay activity to promote this past STM_ONLY. The only other drawn object is 65014, a 13.7 cm 24-point pdg-11 shower fragment at 1.9e4 e/cm sitting on the body 55-62 cm back at cos_fwd -0.98, which is the visible kink in the 3-D frames: body activity, delta / other. What keeps this at medium rather than high is that the charge bunching is roughly periodic along the track, so the terminal peak could in principle be the same instrumental effect landing at the end rather than a Bragg peak; the monotone two-centimetre decay away from the last point and the factor-two height over the other bunches are what argue it is real.

notes: MESSY rather than STM_ONLY or THRU. The competing reading is STM_ONLY on the strength of the six-point terminal rise to 7.65e4, and that is why this is medium rather than high - but the rise comes off a near-zero floor rather than a MIP plateau, the object bends 59 cm of path into 33 cm of displacement, and every segment sits at 5-30 percent of MIP, so I do not believe there is a muon here. Not FRAG: the event has 0 thinned context points near it, so there is no larger object it is a fragment of. Undershoot and overshoot both EXCLUDED - there is no forward tip past the fit end and no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: A small, faint, badly broken object rather than a track. The chain claims 59 cm over 75 points between (207, 190, 278) and (238, 198, 274) - but that is only 33 cm end to end, so the thing wanders by nearly a factor of two, and the four chain segments have cos_fwd running -1.0, -1.0, -0.78, -0.55, i.e. it bends continuously. Every piece is far under MIP: 71023 at 3.2e3 e/cm over 19 cm, 71025 at 5.5e3 over 9 cm, 71011 at 1.9e4 over 24 cm, 71030 at 2.1e4 over 7 cm, with two pdg-11 shower fragments (71029 at 2.3e4 over 16 cm, 71026 at 4.8e4 over 3 cm) and a 2-point gamma-body-exclusion speck. The chain rejects on plateau_off_mip and its own kinematics do not close - 164 MeV by range against 46 MeV by dQ/dx and 38 MeV by MCS at ambiguity 1.00. A muon in the last 59 cm of its range would be at or above MIP everywhere, and this is at 5-30 percent of it. The dQ/dx panel is almost all floor: the points sit under 1.5e4 from s = 5 to 17 and again over most of s = 18-58, with only a handful of green points at 5-6.5e4 scattered at s = 30, 40-43 and 57-59. There is a terminal rise - 1.7e4 at s=4, 2.5e4 at s=3, 3.6e4 at s=2, 5.0e4 at s=1, 6.5e4 at s=0.7, 7.65e4 at s=0.3 - but it climbs off a floor that is not a MIP plateau, so it is the end of a faint fragment, not a Bragg peak off a muon body. Geometrically the object is a scatter of short amber pieces with vertex squares between them: the d azimuth can be read as a broken line, but the c and e azimuths show the pieces spread across a two-dimensional patch rather than along any one line, and a real line projects to a line in every view. f_meas confirms the whole thing occupies only U 3610-3650, V 7355-7395 and W 12210-12260 over time slices 1195-1345 - a compact, drift-aligned patch with a W dead band at 12213-12220 right beside it. With no coherent spine and no identified stop, the tag vocabulary does not apply and every row takes delta / other per the MESSY convention.

notes: THRU on a flat profile that never leaves its own 6.5e4 plateau in the last 15 cm. The two 1.0-1.2e5 singletons near the stop are the only thing that could be read as a Bragg tip; I read them as deltas because they are isolated points with plateau-level neighbours on both sides and the same pattern recurs at s=27, 32, 86 along the body. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing sits past the fit end except a 3-point speck 39 cm out at cos_fwd -0.62, i.e. backward, not a forward high-charge tip. Overshoot EXCLUDED: no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 330 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode x face at (-340, -281, 95) and ending at (-79, -266, 271), 28 cm from the z wall and 76 cm from the cathode, so the end is inside the volume and the profile decides it. The body runs on a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau and the last 15 cm do not leave it: reading the near-stop points off a 4x crop they run 8.1e4 at s=0.3, 6.7e4, 6.8e4, 6.6e4, 7.5e4 and 5.3e4 within the first 3 cm, then 7.0e4, 5.2e4, 5.1e4, 4.9e4 out to s=7, and 7.9e4, 7.3e4, 6.7e4, 6.0e4 from s=9 to 12 - a scatter centred on the same 6.5e4 the rest of the track sits at, while the muon reference curve over that stretch climbs from 7e4 at s=10 through 1.1e5 at s=2 to 1.6e5 at the origin. Two isolated orange points at 1.17e5 (s=4) and 1.03-1.09e5 (s=8-9) stand well clear of their neighbours and read as deltas on the body, not as a Bragg tip; there are matching orange singletons at s=27, 32 and 86 along the plateau, which is what deltas look like on this plot. So no rise off plateau, and the chain agrees with no_bragg and shape_flat; the range and MCS momenta (860 against 1062 MeV/c, ambiguity 0.53) do not close either. f_meas puts the stop at U 580, V 4440 and W 8435, with the U dead bank ending near 555 and the V bank near 4370, so the last centimetres are measured, not lost - only a thin W line sits close, and one plane cannot erase a Bragg the other two would show. All three azimuths show a bare end with nothing leaving it and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. The four unassigned pdg-11 pieces sit on the body at cos_fwd -1.0 between 114 and 179 cm back, clustered at the two chain kinks, and 72017 is a 3-point 1.0 cm survey speck 39 cm out at cos_fwd -0.62, backward and clear of any stop - all body and ambient activity, delta / other under the THRU rule.

notes: STM_MICHEL. The Bragg is unambiguous; the judgement is whether 56006 is the Michel or a delta. I took Michel on physics: the muon has ~13 MeV KE at the vertex where the arm attaches, whose kinematic delta maximum is a few hundred keV, so a 13.6 cm arm cannot be body activity from that muon, and cos_fwd -0.81 does not reach the -0.85 body-line threshold. The competing reading is STM_ONLY / detached dots with 56006 as delta-other, which the ~5 cm gap between the stop and the arm attachment would support. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing forward of the fit end except a 2-point speck 25 cm out; the terminal high charge is on the chain itself, not in a separate tip. Overshoot EXCLUDED: the profile rises monotonically to the last point with no collapse, so no --pin-rr. Note also that dead bands sit across the stop in all three planes, which may be why the arm reconstructs sparse (13.6 cm carrying only ~7 MeV of visible charge).
evidence: 113.8 cm chain entering 2.2 cm from the anode x face at (338, 80, 145) and ending at (234, 83, 158), 106 cm from the nearest face and 231 cm from the cathode - a deeply contained end. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the body sits at 2-4e4 far out, climbs through 5-6e4 over s = 6-12 cm, reaches 6.8e4 at s = 4-6, then 8.15e4, 8.5e4, 9.4e4, 1.02e5, 1.065e5, 1.07e5 and 1.13e5 at the last point, tracking the muon reference curve the whole way up and topping out squarely in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach here. The chain accepts it as STM with no reject flags. It is worth noting that f_meas shows dead bands straddling the stop in all three planes (U 3415-3435, V 7310-7325, W 11695-11705 and 11720-11730), which can only remove charge, so the measured Bragg is if anything an underestimate. What makes the item interesting is 56006: 21 points, 13.6 cm, 1.35e4 e/cm, d_min 4.7 to d_max 12.5 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.81, which the chain types pdg 11 shower but leaves unassigned (flow says no daughter, n_stop_arms 0). Zooming the c and d azimuths shows it leaving the brown vertex square at the far end of the 6.3 cm terminal Bragg segment and curving away from the muon line, clearly clear of the body rather than hugging it. It cannot be a delta: at that vertex the muon has 6.3 cm of range left, i.e. about 13 MeV of kinetic energy, whose maximum delta is a few hundred keV with a sub-millimetre range, so a 13.6 cm electron-like arm there is physically impossible as body activity. Within the michel rule ten-centimetre radius direction does not discriminate, and the only physical source of a 13 cm electron beside a demonstrated muon stop is the decay, so 56006 is the Michel. Past the stop, 161015 is a 2-point 0.1 cm speck 25.2 cm out at cos_fwd +0.58, isolated, compact and clear of the body, which the chain itself considered as a capture-gamma candidate and rejected only on its energy window: gamma by the plain rule, so the kind is both. What keeps this medium is the roughly 5 cm offset between the stop and the arm attachment point - a Michel should leave the stop itself, and this one leaves the vertex just before it.

notes: OVERSHOOT (the pin-move case), pin moved back to rr 5.9 cm. Peak 1.36e5 at s=9, collapse to 0.7-1.9e4 (0.12-0.32 MIP) sustained over the last 6 cm, then a diffuse EM cloud the fit bridged to. The pin position carries about 3 cm of uncertainty because the profile declines from the peak at s=9 to plateau at s=6.1 before collapsing, so the true stop could be argued anywhere in 6-9 cm; I put it at the collapse boundary. Row split recorded: 4008 spans 2.59-200 cm and its innermost ~3 cm lie on the Michel side of the moved pin, but the tag alphabet cannot split a row so it stays muon. Undershoot EXCLUDED: this is the opposite failure. Competing reading is THRU, supported by the range/MCS split (487 against 1128 MeV, ambiguity 0.81) and the chain rejects shape_flat + profile_sparse - which is why this is medium.
evidence: 209 cm chain entering 0.8 cm from the z face at (-96, -319, 2) and ending at (-208, -177, 93), 92 cm from the nearest wall and 205 cm from the cathode, so the end is well inside the volume. This is the overshoot case in its textbook form. The body runs at 5.5-6.5e4; measured off a 9x crop the profile climbs from 5.7e4 at s=15 through 6.8e4 at s=11.4 and 8.3e4 at s=10.3 to a peak of 1.28-1.36e5 at s=8.5-9.8, falls back through 9.8e4 at s=7.3, 7.5e4 at s=6.8 and 5.6e4 at s=6.1, and then COLLAPSES: every point below s=5.6 sits between 0.67e4 and 1.91e4, i.e. 0.12-0.32 of the plateau, over the last six centimetres. That is the peak-several-cm-before-the-fit-end-then-collapse signature, and it is sustained over 6 cm rather than being one low last point. The zoomed c azimuth shows the same thing in colour: the turbo track runs green, then orange, then RED at the peak, then a couple of plateau points, then blue, and then a diffuse pink and yellow cloud of flow segments spreading out to the star - the fit bridged the muon own stop to that cloud. f_meas puts the stop end at U 215, V 4045 and W 7795, all live with the dead banks 50-150 channels away, and its measured-minus-predicted panels show a real brown residual blob at time slices 550-580, i.e. measured charge at the end that the muon fit does not account for. So I moved the pin to rr 5.9 cm, the junction between the last real muon charge (5.6e4 at s=6.1) and the collapsed stretch. The collapse falls inside chain segment 4008, which has no separate row for its last 3 cm, so 4008 keeps the muon tag for what most of its 206 cm is and the split is recorded here. Past the moved stop, 4011 (6 points, 2.8 cm, 1.03e4 e/cm, the collapsed terminal chain segment) and the two unassigned pdg-11 shower pieces 4009 (15 points, 8.5 cm, 1.34e4) and 4010 (15 points, 8.6 cm, 2.2e4) all lie inside the bridged 0-6.8 cm stretch and together form that diffuse sub-MIP cloud: they are the Michel, and their cos_fwd of -0.93 to -0.95 is measured from the fit last point rather than from the true stop, so it does not read as body activity once the stop moves. 4006, a 6.1 cm pdg-11 shower fragment 200-203 cm back at the entry end, is body activity: delta / other. No gamma anywhere in the ring, so the kind is attached.

notes: THRU on a flat profile whose last two centimetres are zero-charge fit points. Medium because the three-point 12.5e4 bump at s=3.4 is a real competing Bragg reading; I rejected it because identical isolated 1.1-1.3e5 bumps recur at s=41-43, 48, 62, 67-68 and 96 along the same plateau, so it is this track own delta signature. Mechanism named: the fit end is 17.6 cm from the cathode with the track heading into it, i.e. maximum drift and worst S/N, which is where a cluster fades out; f_meas rules out a dead-wire exit. Undershoot EXCLUDED: the only thing past the fit end is a 1.1 cm 3-point speck at 3.2e4 across an 8.5 cm gap, not a 2 cm tip at 1e5. Pin NOT moved: the collapse is only ~2 cm of near-zero fit points, which the rubric tells me to ignore rather than to bridge from, and there is nothing at the fit end for the fit to have bridged to.
evidence: 383 cm chain entering 8.9 cm from the anode x face at (-331, 230, 192) and ending at (-21, 102, 57), 56 cm from the z wall but only 17.6 cm from the cathode - and it is travelling toward the cathode, x running -331 to -21, so the fit end sits at maximum drift where the imaging signal-to-noise is worst. The profile is flat: the body holds 5.5-6.5e4 the whole way and s = 4 to 20 cm is indistinguishable from s = 40 to 100. Reading the last centimetres off a 10x crop gives 6.0e4 at s=4.3, 8.5e4 at s=4.1, 12.5e4 at s=3.4, 7.4e4 at s=2.7, 3.4e4 at s=2.05, then 1.9e4, 0.9e4 and 0.1e4 at s below 1.3. The last three are effectively zero-charge fit points and the rubric says to ignore them, and once they go the only feature left is a three-point bump centred at s=3.4. I do not read that bump as a Bragg tip, because this track carries exactly that pattern all along its body: isolated 1.07-1.31e5 clusters sit at s = 41-43, 48, 62, 67-68 and 96 on the same plateau, so a 1.25e5 excursion at s=3.4 is the same delta signature landing near the end. A real Bragg has to be a rise following the reference curve over the last 10-20 cm, and over that stretch this profile does not move off 6e4 while the curve climbs from 6.6e4 to 1.6e5. The chain agrees with no_bragg and shape_flat, and the kinematics do not close either - 884 MeV by range against 1713 by MCS, ambiguity 0.57, i.e. the track is straighter than a stopper of that range. f_meas shows the stop end live in all three planes (U 1130, V 4910, W 8895) with the dead banks 30-150 channels away, so the fade is not a dead-wire effect - it is the cluster running out of signal 17.6 cm short of the cathode. All three azimuths show a bare end. The chain does offer a Michel: 115010, 3 points, 1.1 cm, 3.2e4 e/cm, 2.7 MeV, sitting 8.5-9.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.19 - but it says itself that it bridged that across 8.54 cm of empty space by proximity rather than by a graph edge, and a 1.1 cm three-point speck across a 9 cm charge-free gap is the rubric own example of a detached dot, not a 35 MeV electron. With no stop it cannot be gamma either, so it and the two survey specks 52-58 cm out take delta / other under the THRU rule.

notes: THRU, and the clearest one in my chunk - the profile is flat on its own 5.2e4 plateau to the last point with no rise of any kind, on a fit end 90 cm from the nearest face and 89 cm from the cathode. No visible continuation; per the rubric that is still THRU and I say so rather than reaching for UNCLEAR. Dead-region exit EXCLUDED by f_meas in all three planes. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing forward of the fit end at all, only a 2-point speck 15.8 cm out at cos_fwd -0.55. Overshoot EXCLUDED: no peak and no collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 252.8 cm chain entering 0.6 cm from the z face at (314, 32, 1) and ending at (92, 33, 91), 90 cm from the z wall and 89 cm from the cathode, so the end is comfortably inside the volume and the profile has to decide it. It decides it flatly and without ambiguity: the body sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 band from s = 100 all the way in, and the last 20 cm are indistinguishable from the rest - 6.2e4, 5.1e4, 5.3e4, 4.8e4, 4.7e4, 3.95e4, 4.2e4, 5.5e4, 5.2e4 scattered between s = 0 and s = 10, with the local plateau reference sitting at 5.2e4 right up to the origin. Meanwhile the muon reference curve climbs from 5.5e4 at s = 40 through 6.6e4 at s = 13 to 1.6e5 at the origin, and the data never follow it up by so much as one point: there is not even a ragged rise to argue about, and the highest points anywhere near the stop (8.4e4 at s = 11, 8.55e4 at s = 17) are the same isolated excursions this track shows at s = 36, 38, 40 and 48. The chain flags no_bragg and shape_flat, and the kinematics agree - 584 MeV by range against 1064 by MCS, ambiguity 0.79. f_meas puts the stop at U 2945, V 6745 and W 11295, with the nearest dead channels 30-100 away in every plane, so nothing is masking the last centimetres. All three stop azimuths show a completely bare end with no arm, no dot and no continuation, and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. The one other drawn object is 182014, a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 15.8 cm out at cos_fwd -0.55 that the chain itself labels a gamma body exclusion; on a through-goer there is no stop for it to be a gamma relative to, so it takes delta / other. This is the rubric plain case - a flat MIP profile to the last point, no face, no dead-region exit and no visible continuation, i.e. the cluster ended where the imaging ran out.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation, no face (36.4 cm) and no dead-region exit at the end - the rubric's explicit "the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out" case. The competing reading was an overshoot with the pin at rr~14, made attractive by the 1.0-1.32e5 patch 15-30 cm back and by a 6.5 cm branch attaching at exactly that junction; rejected because MIP points are interleaved through that same window and because the post-patch 14 cm sits at ~1.0 MIP rather than the 0.15-0.5 MIP the bridged-gap signature calls for. This item is the concrete case where the rubric's two overshoot tests disagree; marked medium for that reason. No undershoot: no row carries dstop of a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 with chain pdg 11 - the closest piece, 185030, is 4.3 cm out at 6.6e4, about 1.3x MIP, which the rubric says is a real Michel signature and not the undershoot.
evidence: 98.3 cm chain, enters 6.3 cm from the z face and the fit ends 36.4 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not the issue. Upscaled 5x on the terminal region, the profile over the last 10-20 cm does not rise: the last two fit points sit at 2.9e4 and 3.4e4, below the track's own ~5e4 plateau, and from s = 0 to 14 the points scatter between 3e4 and 5.7e4 with a handful of greens at 7.5-8.3e4, far under the muon reference curve which runs from 6e4 at s = 14 to 1.6e5 at s = 0. There is a real cluster of eight points at 1.0-1.32e5 fifteen to thirty cm back, and I nearly read it as a Bragg peak with a 14 cm overshoot. What rules that out is the interleaving: inside that same 15-30 cm window there are roughly fifteen cyan points at 4-6e4 and three blue ones near 2.5-3.5e4 sitting between the high ones. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot have MIP points scattered through the same 20 cm of track, so that patch is localised delta deposits on an otherwise-MIP stretch, not a terminal rise, and there is nothing behind the fit end for a pin to move to.
