The orange and salmon stretch in the d and e azimuths that first suggested a peak is the amber particle-flow band, not turbo charge (trap 2). Nothing past the fit end reads as an electron: the only close pieces are 185030 (4 pts, 1.6 cm, 6.6e4) and 184029 (3 pts, 1.2 cm, 3.5e4) at 4.3-5.6 cm, both backward at cos_fwd -0.6 and -0.76 and, projecting them onto the body direction myself, only 3.0-3.9 cm off the muon line - body activity beside the end, not a 10-20 cm decay arm, and the chain itself body-excludes 184029. The 6.5 cm MIP piece 57015 branches at 12-14 cm back with its centroid 2.8 cm off the body line, visible as the short orange spur in the d and e azimuths, so it is a delta or small shower on the body. f_meas shows a V-plane dead band straddling the track over part of its extent, a plausible source of the very low points 35-60 cm back, but U and W are clean at the end. Flat to the last point with no continuation drawn and no face reached: through-goer whose cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out.

notes: No undershoot candidate: the only non-chain row is 23.5 cm away at the entry end, and no row sits at dstop 1-3 cm forward at ~1e5. No overshoot: the peak is at the last point, not several cm before it. Pin left at the fit's last point.
evidence: Short 23.9 cm single-segment chain, 84.4 MeV by range, entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 13.9 cm from the nearest (y) face, in_fv 1, so it stops inside the volume. Upscaled 6x on the terminal region the profile is unambiguous: a flat ~4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s = 24 in to s = 3, then three points at 1.06-1.09e5 over the last ~1.5 cm sitting exactly on the muon reference curve where it turns up, i.e. a factor 2.1 rise off the track's own plateau with the right shape. One green point at 6.9e4 sits at s = 0 itself; that is the ordinary single partial-charge last point the rubric tells you to leave alone, not a sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit's last point. Two mid-track points at 7.5e4 and 9.8e4 near s = 8-10 are scatter above the plateau and do not change the shape. Past the stop there is nothing at all: the flow reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0, and all three azimuths show clean white space beyond the star with no speck, arm or bridged piece. The only other drawn object is 237001, a 4-point 1.5 cm speck at 23.5-24.8 cm from the stop, i.e. down at the entry end, at cos_fwd -0.93 on the muon body line and carrying only 8372 e/cm, so it is body activity beside the entry, delta / other. f_meas shows the track solidly imaged in all three planes with dead bands 18 wires away in V and about 10 wires beyond the end in W but U and V clean past the end, so it is not a track leaving through a dead region. Nothing that reads as an electron anywhere, so STM_ONLY with kind none; the chain's shape_flat rejection is the disagreement, and I think it is wrong because the rise is only 1.5 cm long on a 24 cm track and a flatness statistic over the whole segment will wash it out.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence on its own; the medium is entirely about detached dots vs none. If the owner reads the three perpendicular specks (34-56 cm transverse, no decay arm to define a Michel side) as belonging to a different object, the kind flips to none and no tag but theirs changes. 240005 has size 0.0 and no dqdx value at all - a degenerate survey speck - and I tagged it with the other two only because the rubric forbids charge as a criterion. No undershoot: no row sits at dstop 1-3 cm forward at ~1e5. No overshoot: the peak is the last point.
evidence: 118.6 cm single-segment chain, 289.8 MeV by range, entering 4.0 cm from the z face and ending 51.7 cm from the nearest face, deeply contained. The terminal profile is a textbook rise and it is the cleanest thing on this item: a 4.0-5.0e4 plateau over most of the track, climbing through 5.7-6.0e4 at s = 5-8, 6.9-7.5e4 at s = 2-4, 8.4e4 at s = 0.7 and a final point at 1.31e5 that sits exactly on the muon reference curve where it turns up. That is a factor ~3 rise off the track's own plateau over the last 8 cm with the muon curve's shape, so the chain's plateau_off_mip rejection is about the absolute level of the plateau (median 42771, under MIP) and not about the shape; it does not make this a through-goer. The dense near-zero points at s = 19-28 and 53-60 are the zero-charge fit points the rubric says to ignore. Nothing is attached at the stop in any of the three azimuths and the flow confirms n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, so there is no electron: STM_ONLY, not STM_MICHEL. The three remaining objects are faint far specks: 239004 (2 pts, 0.3 cm, 26491) at 34.7 cm, 241006 (3 pts, 1.0 cm, 13114) at 50.3 cm and 240005 (2 pts, 0.0 cm, no measured charge) at 56.7 cm. Projecting each onto the muon direction they are 34.6, 49.1 and 56.4 cm transverse, i.e. essentially perpendicular and nowhere near the body line, so the delta rule's on-the-body clause cannot claim them; and their unit vectors from the stop have mutual cosines 0.83-0.99, so they are collimated on one side of the stop rather than scattered in unrelated directions around the 60 cm ring. By the rubric's faint-far-speck rule that makes them gamma, and charge is explicitly not a criterion, so I kept 240005 in the same population even though it carries no measured charge at all. Kind is therefore detached dots, which is what makes this call medium rather than high - the gamma-versus-delta reading of three perpendicular specks with no decay arm to define a Michel side is the hard part here, and if they were delta the kind would be none.

notes: Flat-to-declining profile THRU at 109.9 cm from every face with no continuation drawn. The verdict itself is not in doubt - the rubric's operative test is the profile and the profile falls into the fit end - but the mechanism is unaccounted for: no face, no dead-region exit in U, and no charge past the star, so where the muon went is not visible in these frames. That is the rubric's stated 'the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out' case, not a reason to weaken the call. No undershoot: no row carries dstop of a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 with chain pdg 11; the only forward-ish rows are C15 and 93014 at 39-50 cm and 41-43 cm off-axis. No overshoot: no terminal peak to collapse from, so the pin stays put.
evidence: 139.7 cm chain in five fitted segments, entering 0.6 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 109.9 cm from the nearest face, so this is a deeply contained fit end and containment cannot decide it. The profile is the operative test and it says through-goer: the plateau sits at 5.0-6.0e4 for the whole 140 cm, and over the last 4 cm the points fall to 4.0e4, 3.6e4, 3.5e4, 2.9e4 and 2.3e4 with two near-zero fit points mixed in, i.e. the charge goes down into the fit end rather than up, and it never approaches the muon reference curve which is at 9e4 to 1.6e5 over that same span. The five chain segments carry medians 54318, 57303, 55145, 58213 and 41951 from the stop backwards - the terminal segment is indistinguishable from the rest, so there is no rise anywhere near the end. I checked for the overshoot and it is not there: a peak-then-collapse needs a peak several cm before the last point, and the only high points (1.25e5 at s = 15, and others at s = 57, 80, 85, 95) are isolated delta spikes scattered along the whole track, not a terminal maximum. All three azimuths show clean white space past the star with no arm, speck or bridged piece, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. f_meas shows the track cleanly imaged in all three planes; the U projection is near vertical at channel ~1750 with the nearest dead band 50-78 channels away, so a continuation would have been seen in U and this is not a dead-region exit. The large object C15 (298 pts, 62.9 cm, no PR segment) and the speck 93014 sit 41-43 cm off the muon line at 44-50 cm and are visibly a separate diffuse streak in every azimuth, so they belong to a different object; 20009 and 20012 are pdg-11 shower pieces at cos_fwd -1.0 sitting 3.0-3.4 cm off the body at 59 and 126 cm back, i.e. deltas on the body. Deep containment with no visible continuation is the uncomfortable part, but the rubric is explicit that a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own.

notes: THRU on the flat profile alone; the U+V dead bands immediately past the fit end give it a mechanism as well, so this is not the rubric's "ended where the imaging ran out" case but an ordinary dead-region exit. No undershoot and no overshoot: the muon chain is the only drawn object, so there is no forward piece to mistake for a Michel, and the profile has no terminal peak.
evidence: 69.9 cm single-object chain, 187.3 MeV by range, entering 0.5 cm from the y face and ending 30.9 cm from that same nearest face; it is the only object drawn, so there is nothing to attribute except the muon itself. The profile is flat to the last point: a 4.3-5.5e4 plateau all the way in, with the final points at 5.2e4, 5.1e4, 5.3e4 and a single 7.05e4 at s = 0, against a muon reference curve that is at 8e4 by s = 5 and 1.6e5 at s = 0 - the data never approaches it and never turns up. The only excursions are a bump of 7.4-9.9e4 at s = 6-11 and two isolated spikes at 1.32e5 and 1.49e5 at s = 49, all of them delta-ray scatter well away from the end, and the segment median is 51766 for the whole 70 cm. So there is no Bragg rise, no terminal peak to collapse from, and no reason to move the pin. All three azimuths show a single clean isolated track with nothing whatsoever past the star - no arm, no dot, no second object anywhere in the frame - and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, so STM_MICHEL is not on the table either. f_meas adds the mechanism: the fit end sits at U channel 3710, V 7548, W 12108, and the track's own direction carries it to lower channel in U and V, where U has a dead line at ~3705 and V's end is already inside a hatched dead band at 7540-7558; only W is clean there, and one live plane cannot make 3-D points, so a continuation past the end would simply not be imaged. MCS 604.8 MeV against 187.3 MeV by range (amb 0.82) points the same way - the track is far stiffer than a muon with 70 cm left to live. Through-goer leaving through a two-plane dead region.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence; the medium is about detached dots vs none. The three pieces at 41-56 cm are at the outer edge of the gamma rule's ~60 cm and the chain never offered them to either stage (survey only), so if the owner reads them as belonging to a different object the kind flips to none. No undershoot: no row at dstop 1-3 cm forward at ~1e5. No overshoot: the peak is the last point, pin left alone.
evidence: 391.4 cm chain in six fitted segments, 903 MeV by range with MCS 821.7 MeV at amb 0.00, entering 0.5 cm from the x face and ending 97.8 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained. The Bragg is the best I have seen in this chunk: the data tracks the muon reference curve point for point from the plateau inwards, 5.2e4 out at s = 40-90, 6.5e4 at s = 12-20, 7.0-7.5e4 at s = 6-11, 8.5-8.7e4 at s = 2-5, 1.10e5 at s = 1.5 and a final point at 1.475e5 at s = 0, which is the 1.2-1.35e5 top-out band and above. The chain agrees, is_stm 1. No pin move: the peak is the last point, there is no collapse behind it, and the only high outliers (1.0-1.17e5 at s = 24, 53-56, 70) are delta spikes far from the end. Nothing is attached at the stop - all three azimuths show the star capping a clean track end with no arm and no bridged piece, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - so this is not STM_MICHEL. Past the stop there are three detached pieces, 144024 (7 pts, 3.7 cm, 72372) at 40.9 cm, 145025 (2 pts, 0.1 cm, 56106) at 43.1 cm and 146026 (10 pts, 5.1 cm, 61303) at 56.4 cm, all at cos_fwd +0.17 to +0.41, i.e. on the forward side of the stop and not back along the body, and all visibly clear of the track in every azimuth. They are not one object: 145025 sits 9.6 cm from 144024 in the same direction from the stop (cos 0.98) but 146026 is about 45 deg away and its offset from 144024 is nearly perpendicular to the 144024-145025 axis, so they are three separate compact deposits rather than a broken second track. Isolated, past the stop, clear of the body and inside 60 cm is the gamma rule, and they are not scattered in unrelated directions around the ring, so I tagged all three gamma and the kind is detached dots - which by the rubric does not promote the verdict. The chord-based transverse offsets I computed (40-55 cm) are unreliable here because the track makes almost a right-angle bend near the end, so I judged the separation from the three azimuths instead, as trap 5 requires. f_meas shows dead bands close to the fit end in U (3040 against the end at 3070) and V (6815-6825 against the end at 6825), which would matter for a flat profile, but a track exiting through a dead region does not first climb to 1.475e5.

notes: This is the STM_MICHEL-versus-THRU collision in its sharpest form: the THRU test (no Bragg rise at the fit end) is satisfied and so is the STM_MICHEL carve-out (decay activity past the end, holds even when the Bragg is unclear). I went STM_MICHEL because the charge past the end is a 41 deg arm at 0.4-0.9 MIP with falling charge, not a collinear continuation at MIP; if the owner reads 61001 as a delta ray at the last point of a through-goer, the verdict is THRU, 61001 becomes delta / other and the kind becomes none. Marked medium for that. The arm is only 4.1 cm and 5.9 MeV, small for a Michel, which is the other thing that made it hard. No undershoot: 61001 is 0.6 MIP, the explicit opposite of the several-times-MIP tip. No overshoot: the s = 8-15 high points are interleaved with MIP points, so no pin move.
evidence: 279.5 cm chain, 644 MeV by range, entering 0.1 cm from the x face and ending 38.3 cm from the nearest face, so it ends inside the volume. The muon's own profile gives no help: a 4.2-5.0e4 plateau all the way in and 3.7-4.5e4 over the last 8 cm, i.e. flat at or just under its own plateau against a reference curve that is at 7e4 by s = 10 and 1.6e5 at s = 0. There is a scatter of five or six points at 7.5-9.9e4 between s = 8 and 15, and I tested it as an overshoot peak, but MIP points at 4-5.5e4 are interleaved through that same window, which a muon at its Bragg peak cannot do, so it is delta scatter and I left the pin at the fit's last point. What decides the item is the topology past the end. 61001 is attached at the shared stop vertex 61002, 8 points over 4.1 cm leaving at a 41 deg kink, and its points appear on the negative axis at magnitudes 0.3 to 4.5 cm carrying 4.0e4 down to 1.7e4 - at and below MIP, and falling as it goes out. That is the rubric's own description of the ordinary Michel and the explicit counter-case to the undershoot, whose load-bearing clause is charge several times MIP; 3.0e4 is 0.6 MIP, so this is not a mis-cut muon tip. The delta clauses cannot claim it either: it is forward at cos_fwd +0.77, attached at d_min 0.0, and not body-excluded by the chain. In the d and e azimuths the arm leaves the star at a large angle to the muon line, not as a collinear continuation, which is what separates decay activity from a through-goer here. f_meas shows the arm as real measured charge - the dark navy low-charge points at the top of the track are present in the measured panels, not only the predicted - so it is not a fit artefact. The uncomfortable part is that a muon that stops must have a Bragg peak and this one has none at all, which is exactly what the chain rejected on (no_bragg, shape_flat); I am calling it STM_MICHEL because the rubric says a Michel topology is sufficient on its own even when the Bragg is unclear, and an attached sub-MIP arm at 41 deg with falling charge is that topology.

notes: FRAG_THRU rather than plain THRU because the drawn cluster is visibly broken - a 25 cm piece, 22 cm of nothing, then the two-point blob the pin sits on - and the main piece is clipped at time slice 0, the readout-window edge, so more of the object exists outside what is drawn. MESSY was the other reading I weighed and rejected: there is a coherent straight spine, it is just short and under-charged, not an EM blob in many pieces. Marked medium because with 41 image points and a heavily dead U plane there is very little to go on, and because FRAG versus plain THRU turns on reading time slice 0 as a truncation. Deliberately did not tag 135001 gamma even though the chain names it one - the rubric forbids gamma on a THRU. No undershoot and no overshoot: there is no terminal peak and no forward high-charge tip, only a bridged gap.
evidence: This is a broken, boundary-clipped cluster rather than a track with a stop. The chain is quoted as 41.0 cm over 30 points but the whole event has only 41 image points at full density, and the 3-D frames show why: there is a single coherent amber piece about 25 cm long, then roughly 22 cm of completely empty space, then an isolated two-point blob which is where the pin sits. The dQ/dx panel shows the same hole - chain points at s = 25-41 and at s = 0-2 and nothing at all between s = 3 and s = 24 - so the fit bridged two disconnected pieces and its last point is essentially fictitious. Both ends hug the same wall: the entry is 1.3 cm from the y face and the fit end 0.8 cm from it, in_fv 0, so the object runs along the top y boundary about a centimetre inside it for its whole visible length. There is no Bragg anywhere: the five points at s = 0-2 carry 1.5-2.9e4, the main piece is mostly 0.4-1.5e4 with a handful up to 7.8e4, and the segment value is 13916, about 0.28 of MIP - far under the plateau, let alone the reference curve which is at 1.6e5 at s = 0. f_meas explains the missing charge: the U plane is heavily hatched with dead bands right across this channel range, and the main piece runs down into time slice 0, the edge of the readout window, so the object is cut there rather than ending there. That is what makes me call it a fragment: the drawn cluster is one broken piece of something that continues out of the imaged window, and whatever the full object is, it is not a stopping muon - no rise, no plateau even, and both ends on the boundary. The only other row is 135001, two points at 0.2 cm and 22177 which the chain offers as a capture gamma 29.3 cm out at cos_fwd +0.67; on a THRU-family item gamma is not available because it would assert decay charge past a stop that does not exist, so it is delta / other.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with a deeply contained fit end (68 cm), no continuation drawn and no dead band immediately past the end. No undershoot: no row carries dstop of a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 with chain pdg 11 - the nearest object of any kind is 38 cm away and 38 cm off-axis. No overshoot: no terminal peak. Note that the five perpendicular survey specks at 38-60 cm are exactly the population I called gamma on 039349_7/65 and 039349_70/56; here the THRU verdict forecloses that tag, which is the rubric working as intended but does mean the same physical configuration gets different tags depending on the verdict.
evidence: 264.8 cm chain in three fitted segments, 610.9 MeV by range, entering 0.2 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 68.0 cm from the nearest face, so the fit end is well inside and containment cannot decide it. The profile is flat to the last point: the plateau sits at 5.0-6.0e4 for the whole 265 cm and the last few centimetres carry 5.5-6.3e4, which is a couple of thousand electrons above the plateau and nowhere near the muon reference curve, which is at 8e4 by s = 5 and 1.6e5 at s = 0. The terminal segment's own value is 55776 against 56006 and 40744 for the two behind it, so the end is indistinguishable from the body. A small group of 6.6-7.2e4 points sits at s = 11-16 and single spikes of 1.16e5 and 9.2e4 at s = 24-26 and 9.9e4 at s = 94, but those are delta scatter mid-track, not a terminal maximum, so there is no peak for a collapse to follow and the pin stays at the fit's last point. All three azimuths show the star capping a clean, straight, continuous track with nothing attached and nothing drawn past it, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The five remaining rows are all survey-only pieces the chain never offered to either stage, sitting 38-60 cm out with transverse offsets of 38-57 cm, i.e. essentially perpendicular to the muon and scattered in several different directions in the azimuths rather than collimated on one side; the largest, 137009, is 23 points over 13.2 cm at 50442 e/cm, which is a small track segment of its own rather than a compact dot. On a through-goer none of them can be gamma anyway - gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop - so they are all delta / other. f_meas shows the fit end 20-22 channels clear of the nearest dead bands in U and V, so this is not a dead-region exit either; the cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out, which the rubric says is still THRU.

notes: OVERSHOOT: pin moved from the fit's last point to rr 6.5 cm. Real stop is 6.5 cm back along the fit from the drawn star; the last 6.5 cm of segment 37001 is the collapsed stretch plus the Michel, and 37001's tag describes only its outer 116 cm. michel_kind is forced to none because the Michel has no row of its own - schema limitation, not an assertion that there is no decay charge. The competing reading is plain THRU with no pin move, treating the six 7.9-9.9e4 points as a delta ray on an under-charged track and the s = 3-6 clump as the track's own lower band; I rejected it because those six are the only 8-10e4 points on 197 cm, they sit on the muon curve, and the upper band vanishes entirely between s = 3 and s = 6 rather than continuing alongside. Medium, and specifically: f_meas shows uniform measured charge to the last time slice with no hole, so the pin move rests on the 3-D dQ/dx alone; and this track's median is 0.6 MIP throughout with two segments carrying almost no charge, so its charge reconstruction is not trustworthy in detail. If the owner discounts the pin move, the item is THRU / none with the same tags. No undershoot: no row sits a couple of cm forward of the fit end at 0.9-1.2e5.
evidence: 197.4 cm chain in seven fitted segments, entering 2.3 cm from the z face and the fit ending 44.9 cm from the nearest face, in_fv 1, so it ends inside. The whole track is under-charged - the terminal segment's value is 31912 and two mid-track segments carry 2483 and 5006 - and the profile is visibly two-banded everywhere, roughly 4-5.5e4 upper and 2-3.5e4 lower, so I read the upper band. Zoomed 6x the last 15 cm are neither flat nor a simple decline. Coming inwards the upper band sits at 4.8-5.8e4 at s = 12-15, then six points at 7.85e4, 7.9e4, 8.0e4, 8.75e4, 9.0e4 and 9.9e4 fill s = 7-11 sitting on the muon reference curve - and these are the only points anywhere on 197 cm that reach 8-10e4, so this is not the track's ordinary scatter. Immediately inside that, s = 3-6 collapses to a tight clump of about eight points at 1.7-2.3e4, which is 0.4-0.5 of this track's own plateau and squarely in the band the rubric quotes for the bridged gap; what makes it a collapse rather than the lower band showing through is that the upper band is absent there - there is not a single 4-5.5e4 point between s = 3 and s = 6 - and then the last 3 cm come back up to 2.9-3.9e4. Peak, sustained collapse over several cm with the upper band gone, then charge again is the overshoot signature, so I have set the pin at 6.5 cm, the junction between the last real muon point at s = 7 and the collapsed clump. I checked this against f_meas and it is the weak point of the call: the measured charge in all three planes runs down to the last time slice at uniform brightness, with no visible hole over the stretch the dQ/dx says collapsed, so the 2-D projections neither confirm nor refute a physical gap and I would not claim one. The collapse falls inside segment 37001, which spans the whole 123 cm from the fit end, so there is no separate row to retag: I tagged 37001 muon because that is what most of it is, and the row is split - its outer 116 cm is muon and its last 6.5 cm is the collapsed stretch plus the Michel. That also forces michel_kind to none even though the verdict is STM_MICHEL, which is the schema limitation the rubric names. Nothing else is attached at the corrected stop; 37009, 37012 and 37015 are pdg-11 shower pieces at cos_fwd -1.0 sitting 0.8-2.1 cm off the body 130-165 cm back, and C61 is a 377-point 226 cm unfitted cluster running roughly parallel about 35 cm away, plainly a different object in every azimuth.

notes: The hard call is 43003: 7.2 cm and chain-typed pdg 11 is Michel-scale, but it is 1.3 cm off the muon line, backward, and at 0.2 of MIP, so both the hugging-the-body clause and the close-backward-body-excluded clause send it to delta / other. If that piece is really the Michel the item becomes STM_MICHEL / both, which is why the confidence is medium.
evidence: 101 cm of chain, enters 2.7 cm from the anode x face and stops 55.2 cm from the nearest wall (z), so containment is not in question. The profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to about s=20, then climbs steadily through 7e4-9e4 over the last 15 cm and finishes at 1.22e5 and 1.63e5 on the final two points, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve; the rise is ragged with several 6e4 points mixed in but it is a genuine rise off the plateau and there is no terminal collapse, so the pin stays on the fit last point. The one piece at the stop, segment 43003, is 13 points over 7.2 cm at only 1.18e4 e/cm, sitting 1.9-4.4 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.95; projecting its centroid onto the entry-to-stop line puts it 1.3 cm off that line and 2.7 cm back along it, and all three azimuths show it as a small blob lying alongside the amber last-segment band rather than an arm leaving the stop, so it is hugging the muon body and goes delta / other even though the chain types it pdg 11 shower, which is also what the chain itself did by reporting n_stop_arms 0. Past the stop there is one isolated 4-point 1.7 cm speck, 149007, at 25.2 cm and 25 cm clear of the body line with cos_fwd 0.25, drawn with a clean charge-free gap to the track end in all three measured planes: a detached capture gamma, which does not promote the item. The 2-point survey speck 148006 at 47.8 cm projects 35 cm back along the muon axis, so it is behind the stop rather than past it and is delta / other. No dead channels touch the stop in U, V or W.

notes: Low confidence and the owner should look at this one. Three readings are live. (1) THRU as recorded: no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the rubric says a flat or non-rising profile is enough on its own even with no visible continuation and no face. (2) MESSY: plateau at 0.4 of MIP, six pdg 11 shower segments interleaved along the body, a four-way fan at the fit end, 26 drawn objects in a 60 cm box, and chain KE of 236 MeV by range against 114 by dQ/dx and 123 by MCS with amb 0.66 all say this is not one muon; I did not use MESSY only because a coherent spine is visible end to end in all three azimuths, which the MESSY definition excludes. (3) STM_ONLY with an overshooting fit, pin near rr 2.5, reading the three points at s = 2-3 as a real Bragg peak that the fit then bridges for its last 2 cm; I rejected it because the points immediately before the spike (s = 3-5) are also low, so there is no rise leading into the peak, and the same spike height recurs three times near the entry. Dead-channel bands crossing the track in U and V mean the profile itself is partly untrustworthy, which is the main reason I did not go higher than low.
evidence: 93 cm of chain over a 61 cm chord, entering 3.5 cm from the z face and ending 42.9 cm from the nearest wall, so the fit end is nowhere near a face. The profile never establishes a MIP plateau: after ignoring four multi-centimetre runs sitting at 3e3-6e3 (s = 20-30, 41-47, 58-63, 80-84, which line up with grey dead-channel bands crossing the track at U 3040 and V 6890 in f_meas) the surviving points oscillate between 1.2e4 and 5e4, i.e. around half of the 5.5e4 that a clean muon plateau reads on comparable items, which is also the chain own rejection, plateau_off_mip. Over the last 20 cm there is no climb: s = 20 to 5 wanders 5.2e4, 2.5e4, 4.0e4, 1.6e4, 1.9e4, and the final two centimetres sit at 2.4-2.9e4, no higher than the body. The only elevated points anywhere near the end are three at s = 2-3 (8.0e4, 8.2e4, 1.06e5) with low points on both sides of them, so they read as a spike rather than a Bragg peak, and identical spikes to 1.05e5, 1.01e5 and 9.6e4 occur at s = 65-92 near the entry end where the charge is highest. Charge highest at the entry and lowest at the fit end is the wrong way round for a stopper. The stop itself sits at the tip of a short segment past a vertex from which three further segments fan out in the c, d and e azimuths, and six of the fitted segments along the body are typed pdg 11 shower; twelve of the eighteen unassigned rows are 2-4 point survey specks scattered 7-56 cm off the body line in unrelated directions, including the four-point 178031 that the chain offers as a capture gamma 21.9 cm past the stop. With no rise at the fit end the object is a through-goer or is not a single muon at all, and either way there is no stop to hang a michel or gamma on, so every non-chain row is delta / other.

notes: THRU called off a flat-to-the-last-point profile with no visible continuation and no face contact at 19.9 cm; per the rubric a flat profile is sufficient on its own. Likely continuation is through the dead-channel bands sitting just past the end in W and V. No pin move: there is no Bragg peak to collapse from.
evidence: 228 cm straight chain, enters 0.3 cm from the y face and the fit ends 19.9 cm from the nearest z wall, so containment numbers alone would allow a stopper. The dQ/dx panel kills it: the profile sits on a ragged 2-5e4 plateau all the way from s=100 down to s=12, tops out at 4.8e4 around s=10-12 which is exactly the same level the same track shows at s=70-100, and then falls to 2.9e4, 2.0e4 and 1.1e4 over the last centimetre. There is no rise above the plateau and nothing following the shape of the muon reference curve, which asymptotes at 5.4e4 and is never approached; the local maximum at s=10 is plateau, not a Bragg peak, so the overshoot collapse-after-peak signature does not apply and the three low end points span only about 1 cm, which is ordinary end scatter. A muon cannot run flat at MIP to its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any of the three 3-D azimuths - the track is a clean single spine that simply terminates at the star. The one non-chain object, 213021, is a 2.2 cm five-point speck 35 cm from the end at cos_fwd -0.17, sitting well off the track line in the d and e azimuths and typed by the chain as gamma body exclusion; on a through-goer there is no stop to hang a gamma on, so it is delta / other. The measured panels show dead-channel bands immediately past the end in W (around channel 12250-12262) and in V (around 7540-7550), which is a plausible place for the track to have left the image.

notes: THRU called off a flat-core profile to the last point with no visible continuation, no face contact at 128.5 cm and no dead region at the stop; per the rubric a flat profile is sufficient on its own. I explicitly checked the undershoot case and it does not apply - the undershoot needs a two-centimetre tip at 0.9-1.2e5, four to six times MIP, whereas this piece is long and sits at MIP, which the rubric names as the ordinary STM_MICHEL case. notes: Low confidence. notes: The verdict is a confident STM_MICHEL. The kind rests on the two detached specks: 146007 at 27 cm and 145006 at 57 cm are 31 and 15 degrees from the Michel arm direction and 95-104 degrees from the muon body, so I judged them isolated dots on the decay side and tagged both gamma, giving both rather than attached. If a reader takes 145006 at 57 cm as a random speck in an unrelated direction, the kind becomes both anyway on 146007 alone, so only tagging BOTH of them delta would move it to attached. The other thing I weighed is the 1.49e5 and 1.31e5 on the two Michel points nearest the stop; I read those as blob overlap with the muon own Bragg peak 0.3-0.8 cm away, since the rest of the arm falls to 6.7e4.
evidence: 106 cm of chain over a 102 cm chord, entering 0.4 cm from the z face at z 1.3 and stopping at (144.7, 149.9, 79.5), 78.7 cm from the nearest wall, 195 cm from the anode and 145 cm from the cathode plane, so the stop is deeply contained. The Michel is 54005, six points over 2.9 cm leaving from 0.6 to 2.6 cm past the stop; recomputing its direction against the entry-to-stop chord puts it 116 degrees from the muon body, i.e. a 64 degree kink from forward, which matches the 78 degree kink the chain quotes, and a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot turn 70 degrees and carry on, so the arm is a second particle. Its charge falls outward, 1.49e5 and 1.31e5 on the two points nearest the stop where the blobs overlap the muon own peak, then 9.1e4, 7.8e4, 7.0e4, 6.7e4 going out, mean 8.5e4, which is 1.5 times this track plateau. That is not the undershoot case: the undershoot needs the piece to be the only Bragg peak, lying straight ahead at cos_fwd above 0.85 and several times MIP, whereas here the muon already peaks at 1.65e5 at its own last point, the piece kinks 70 degrees, and its charge is 1.5 times the plateau and falling as it goes out, which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel case. The chain agrees, is_stm 1, arm attached at the shared stop vertex 54003, pdg 11, 19.3 MeV over a 6.5 cm core range. Two further pieces sit past the stop, both detached with a clean charge-free gap visible in all three measured planes in f_meas: 146007, six points over 3.2 cm at 27.0 cm from the stop and 95 degrees off the muon body, and 145006, a 2-point 0.2 cm speck at 56.7 cm and 104 degrees off the body. Both lie on the Michel side, 31 and 15 degrees from the arm direction in 3-D, both are inside the 60 cm ring and both are well clear of the body line, so both are gamma rather than delta / other, which makes the kind both. No dead channels touch the stop in U or W, and the nearest V band at 6890 sits beside the very end without truncating the rise.

notes: Medium, not high, for two reasons. First, the whole track sits inside a wide V-plane dead band, so the dQ/dx is degraded along its entire length and a genuine Bragg could in principle be suppressed; against that, the profile does not merely fail to rise, it falls monotonically over the last 15 cm into the fit end, which no stopper does. Second, a 35 cm piece dying into low charge at BOTH ends with no face at either is a natural candidate for FRAG_THRU, a fragment of a longer track broken by that dead region. I recorded plain THRU because the rubric asks for the larger object to be VISIBLY there and nothing else is drawn in any frame, but a reader with the full event may want to promote this to FRAG_THRU.

The terminal 55 cm segment 21015 means 56039 against 57441 for 21010 and 50720 for the 138 cm segment 21013 - the last segment is not the hottest, there is no lift. The few 1.2-1.43e5 points sit at s=54-56 and s=86, far up the body, so they are scatter. Nothing whatever sits near the stop: the closest non-muon row is 21017 at 53.9-55.0 cm back on the body line (cos_fwd -1.0), then 21014 at 66.5 cm and 21011 at 190 cm, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. c/d/e_3d_stop show a clean single spine with no arm, dot or blob past the star in any azimuth. f_meas has the track ending together in U, V and W at time slice ~1450 with no continuation; dead bars sit at U 190/355, V 4000/4098 and W 8030/8080 and the track runs between them rather than into one. Flat on the plateau to the last point is exactly what a stopping muon cannot do, so this is a through-goer.

notes: Pin moved back 6.0 cm to the junction between the last real muon charge (peak 7.2e4 at s=6.5-8) and the collapsed stub. SCHEMA LIMITATION: the collapse falls INSIDE row 25002, so there is no separate row to tag michel - 25002 is tagged muon because 26 of its 32 cm are muon, and michel_kind therefore comes out none even though the verdict is STM_MICHEL. To be explicit: 25002s outer 26 cm is muon, its last ~6 cm is the Michel. Medium and not high because the pre-collapse peak reaches only 7.2e4, about 1.6x this tracks unusually low plateau, and there is no separately clustered Michel object to corroborate it.
evidence: 84 cm chain, enters 9.7 cm from a y face, fit end 25.0 cm from the nearest y wall, so contained though not deeply. At 10x the profile shows the overshoot signature cleanly: the track sits on its own low plateau of 4.0-5.5e4 from s=80 in to s=15, climbs raggedly to 6.4-7.2e4 between s=15 and s=6.5 - a 1.6x rise off its own plateau following the shape of the muon curve, even though it never approaches the curves absolute 1.6e5 - and then collapses over the last 6 cm to 1.2-3.0e4, i.e. 0.2-0.45 of the MIP line at 6.7e4, held down over five or six consecutive points rather than dipping at one. The segment means agree: the terminal 32 cm segment 25002 means 53726 against 41927 for the 52 cm behind it, so the rise is real and the collapse is confined to the very end. In the d_3d_stop and c_3d_stop zooms the last ~5 fit points are a dark-blue, visibly KINKED stub that leaves the straight teal muon body and runs to the star, with only a thin sparse image cloud around it - a different structure from the body, not the muons own last centimetres. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at a fifth of MIP, so the stub past the peak is the decay electron and the true stop is about 6 cm back along the fit, where I have put the pin. The only other row, 25003 (11 pts, 6.1 cm, 40551 e/cm, pdg 11 shower), sits 31-34 cm back at the 25001/25002 junction right on the body line at cos_fwd -1.0 and is body activity, so delta / other. f_meas shows the track in all three planes with no dead band under the terminal stub.

notes: Undershoot screened and rejected: 41004 has the undershoot GEOMETRY (cos_fwd 0.86, dstop 0.0, ~1 cm forward tip typed pdg 11) but fails the load-bearing charge clause - median 41987 is 0.63 of MIP, not several times it - and the muons own Bragg peak at 1.45-1.63e5 is already inside the fit, so the fit did not stop short. Competing reading: 41004 is the muons own final centimetre split off by the clustering, which would make this STM_ONLY / none; rejected because two of its three points are sub-MIP.
evidence: Short one-segment track, 37.6 cm, enters 4.7 cm from a z face and ends 22.7 cm from the nearest z wall, contained though not deeply; range KE 116.6 MeV matches a 38 cm muon. The Bragg evidence is the cleanest in my chunk: at 4x the profile sits at 4.4-6.5e4 from s=37 in to s=12, lifts through 6.0-6.7e4 at s=3-6 and then climbs hard over the last 2 cm to 8.85e4 at s=2, 1.455e5 at s=1 and 1.63e5 at s=0, the only points in this chunk that actually reach the muon reference curve. The chain rejects it only on shape_flat, which the picture contradicts. Past the fit end sits 41004, the chains own Michel object: 3 points over 1.2 cm at d_min 0.0, cos_fwd 0.86, leaving the tip with a 28 deg kink, and its three points plot on the negative axis as 1.145e5, 4.2e4 and 3.5e4 (median 41987). The two sub-MIP points are the load-bearing ones - a muon that has just passed 1.6e5 has no range left and cannot deposit another centimetre at 0.5-0.6 of MIP, so this is a second particle attached at the stop, i.e. the decay electron, and by the michel rule direction does not discriminate inside 10 cm anyway. In the 12x c/e_3d_stop crops the amber muon runs into the brown stop vertex and only a green sliver of a few points pokes past it - the Michel is barely resolved in 3-D, which is why this is medium and not high. No other object is drawn, no dots and no capture gamma in the ring, and f_meas shows the track well clear of the dead bars in all three planes with the charge visibly piling up at the last few time slices.

notes: OVERSHOOT: pin moved back to 7.53 cm, the 44007/44001 junction, and 44001 is tagged michel although the chain types it as the muon chain, per the rubrics rule that the segment past the peak is the Michel. Medium not high because the collapsed segment sits at 0.64 of MIP, shallower than the 0.15-0.5 the rubric quotes for this signature, and because a competing reading exists: the dense 2-point blob 147004 sits on the body at 12 cm and could be inflating the fits dQ/dx there rather than the muon genuinely peaking. Both readings still put the muon at rest near s=8-12, which is why the verdict is STM either way.
evidence: 154 cm chain, enters 0.2 cm from an x face, fit end 59.1 cm from the nearest face. This is the overshoot case. At 10x the long segment 44007 sits on a 5.0-6.0e4 plateau from s=145 down to s=25, lifts through 8-9.5e4 at s=15-22 and then spikes to three consecutive points at 1.26e5, 1.46e5 and 1.50e5 at s=10-12, the highest charge anywhere on the track and above the muon reference curve there. Immediately below that, at s=7.53, is the 44007/44001 junction, and the last 8.8 cm (44001, 16 pts) runs at a mean of 42918, about 0.64 of the MIP line and below the tracks own plateau, all the way to the pin. A muon that has just deposited 1.5e5 has a centimetre or two of range left and cannot then travel 9 cm at two thirds of MIP, so the true stop is at the junction and I have put the pin there. The 9x c_3d_stop and d_3d_stop crops make the same point geometrically: the muon spine arrives colour-coded with a dark-red high-charge patch right below the brown vertex square, and above the square the fit continues as a fat amber chain of 16 points that visibly S-bends twice before reaching the star - a curving, sub-MIP, 9 cm terminal piece is an electron, not a muons last centimetres, and a faint arc of unfitted image points curls away from it to the side as well. Of the remaining rows, 147004 (2 pts, 0.9 cm, 1.33-1.60e5, 12.0 cm out, cos_fwd -0.84, chain-labelled Michel body exclusion) lies on the muon body line right where the spike is and is body charge, so delta / other; 146003 (42.1 cm, cos_fwd -0.31), 149005 (56.8 cm, cos_fwd -0.44) and 198006 (56.5 cm, cos_fwd +0.27) are three faint specks scattered in unrelated directions around the 40-60 cm ring rather than lying along the arm, so they are delta / other rather than gammas; 44008 sits 146 cm back at the entry end. f_meas shows the charge concentrated in a compact knot at time 1560-1600 in all three planes with no dead bar under it.

notes: MESSY convention applied: all 35 rows delta / other and kind none, per the rubric rule that a MESSY item has no stop and therefore no michel/gamma. Note this is the item where the fitted spine is essentially fabricated - 24 points over 71.5 cm at a tenth of MIP with a 33 cm charge hole - so nothing here is a stopping-muon measurement.
evidence: This is not one track. 35 drawn objects in a compact region roughly 65 cm in z by 100 cm in x: 13 muon-group fragments of 1.8-10.4 cm each, 21 unassigned pieces of which 17 are typed pdg 11, shower, and a 2-point 0.3 cm michel seed. The nominal spine 45001 is 24 fit points spread over 71.5 cm - one point every 3 cm - at 7190 e/cm, about a tenth of MIP. At 4x the dQ/dx panel confirms there is no muon anywhere: every chain point from s=0 to s=20 lies between 0.3e4 and 2.7e4, there is a complete 33 cm hole with no points at all between s=20 and s=53, and the only points that reach 3.5-6.7e4 sit at s=85-100, i.e. at the far end inside the shower clump, not at the stop. a_proj_full draws no track line at all, just a knot of brown vertex squares and orange circles; c_3d_stop and d_3d_stop show a handful of disconnected amber blobs and vertex squares floating in empty space with no spine between them; e_3d_stop shows the pin sitting alone at the left with the entire dense, ragged, many-vertex clump 70-100 cm away to the right. f_meas has about ten isolated measured points per plane and no continuous trajectory in U, V or W, although the dead bars (U 2530/2725, V 6390-6440 and the wide 6565-6580 band, W 10820/11025) do not sit under the pieces. The chains own numbers agree: range KE 302.9 MeV against dQ/dx 87.5 MeV and MCS 40.4 MeV at ambiguity 1.41, and it rejects on profile_sparse as well as shape_flat. With no identified stop the tag vocabulary does not apply, so every row is delta / other by the MESSY convention.

notes: THRU on the operative test - flat MIP profile to the last point - and I did not reach for UNCLEAR, per the rubric. The competing reading is STM_MICHEL on the clause that a Michel topology is sufficient even when the Bragg is unclear: the 9-14 cm cluster is genuinely electron-like and well off the body, and if it is this muons decay the verdict flips and 201017/201019/201020/199012 all become michel. I went the other way on two grounds - the Bragg here is not unclear but absent and flat to the last point, and the 9.21 cm charge-free gap the chain itself reports means the electron does not start at the pin. Medium confidence; this is the item in my chunk most likely to be wrong.
evidence: 72 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from an x face, fit end 57.3 cm from the nearest face. At 12x the profile is flat to the very last point: every chain point from s=25 in to s=0 lies between 4.0e4 and 7.0e4, with the final point at 6.5e4, sitting on the tracks own MIP band while the muon reference curve has already climbed to 7e4 by s=10 and 1.6e5 at s=0. The segment means say the same: the terminal 40 cm segment 51008 means 51323 against 54947 for 51007 and 49352 for 51004, so the last segment is not even the hottest. The only high points on the whole track (1.0-1.63e5) sit at s=44-52, far up the body. The hard part of this item is what sits beside the fit end: a real electron-like structure of about 27 points - 201017 (9 pts, 4.8 cm, 26954), 201019 (11 pts, 5.8 cm, 31491) and 201020 (7 pts, 3.6 cm, 45555), all sub-MIP, plus the 3-point seed 199012 at 12.1 cm - lying 9.2 to 14.3 cm out at cos_fwd -0.33 to -0.56, i.e. a few cm behind the stop plane and about 9 cm off the body line, drawn in the c/d/e zooms as a short kinked amber-and-blue arm running to its own vertex with a faint arc of image points curling away from it. The chain builds a 12.9 MeV Michel out of it, and it is well clear of the body so it is not a delta hugging the muon. What stops me calling it the Michel is that the chain itself describes the parentage as bridged across 9.21 cm of EMPTY SPACE: a Michel electron starts at the muons stop with no gap, and here there is no charge at all between the pin and the cluster. Combined with a profile that is flat on the plateau to its last point - which a stopping muon cannot produce - I read the muon as passing through and the off-axis cluster as a separate small object rather than this muons decay. 202021 (20.2 cm) and 203022 (19.3 cm) lie on the body line at cos_fwd -0.93/-0.94, 51006 and 51009 are body pieces 34-48 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, and 197010/198011 are faint 2-point specks 55-58 cm back. f_meas shows the track squeezed between two U dead bars at 3375 and 3420 but clear in V and W, with no continuation past the last time slice in any plane.

notes: Undershoot screened and rejected: 25002 has the geometry (1.8 cm forward tip, cos_fwd 0.90, dstop 0.0) but carries 3364 e/cm, a twentieth of MIP - the opposite of the several-times-MIP charge clause. Pin left alone: the terminal dip is a couple of zero-charge fit points over under 2 cm, not the sustained several-cm collapse. Medium not high because the Bragg rise is only about 1.4x the plateau and this tracks other hot spots (9.7e4-1.33e5 at s=20-22) are higher; the competing reading is THRU on scatter.
evidence: 99.6 cm chain, enters right at a z face (d_face 0.0) and ends 39.7 cm from the nearest z wall, deep enough to be contained; range KE 250.4 MeV matches a 1 m muon. At 13x the profile does lift at the end, modestly but in the right place: the plateau runs 4.5-6.0e4 from s=100 in to s=10, and then six points between s=2.3 and s=6 sit at 6.7, 7.05, 7.1, 7.15, 7.2 and 7.65e4, i.e. about 1.35-1.4x the tracks own mean of 53847 and above the MIP line at 6.7e4, which is exactly where a Bragg rise should be. It is a ragged rise - 5.3e4 and 4.3e4 points at s=6.4 and 7.4 sit inside the same window - and it never approaches the reference curve, which is 9e4 at s=4 and 1.6e5 at s=0, but it is a rise off the plateau confined to the last 6 cm and not a sag, which is what separates this from the flat items in this chunk. The very last 1.7 cm is the 4-point arm 25002 at 3364 e/cm, plotted as three points at 0.85e4, 1.4e4 and 2.9e4: at a twelfth of MIP these are fit points with no measured charge, which the rubric says to ignore, not a 2 cm collapse to be pinned out. Nothing else is drawn at all - only two rows in the whole table, no dots, no capture gamma ring, n_stop_arms 1 and no daughter - and c/d/e_3d_stop show a clean single spine ending at the star with nothing beyond it in any azimuth. f_meas has the track ending together in U, V and W at time slice ~1430 with dense dead banding at U 420-500 and V 4220-4260 well clear of the track channels. Nothing past the end reads as an electron, so STM_ONLY.

notes: Cleanest STM in the chunk and the only item where the chain itself accepts it (is_stm 1, reject STM). No undershoot candidate exists - the nearest object past the end is 52.8 cm away. STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL because nothing whatever sits within 50 cm of the stop.
evidence: 213 cm chain, enters 1.8 cm from an x face and ends 61.2 cm from the nearest face, well contained; range KE 494.7 MeV and MCS 454.9 MeV agree to 8 percent at ambiguity 0.02, which is the best-behaved fit in my chunk. The Bragg is unambiguous and it is the shape rather than any single number that says so: at 4x the profile sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s=200 in to s=30, lifts to 6-8e4 through s=30-15, reaches 8.0-9.4e4 over s=5-9, 8.7-9.5e4 at s=2-4 and finishes at 1.02e5 and 1.10e5 at s=1.5 and s=0.5, tracking the muon reference curve point for point over the last 20 cm. The segment means agree: the terminal 11.8 cm 41001 means 80490 against 53687 for the 107 cm behind it and 42-43k further back. A cluster of eight fit points at 2.0-2.6e4 sits at s=8-12 alongside points of 8-9e4 at the same arc length, so it is a second row of low-charge fit points rather than a dip in the profile. Nothing at all sits near the stop: the closest drawn object is 52.8 cm away, the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring, and c/d/e_3d_stop show the amber terminal segment running into the star with clean empty space beyond it in all three azimuths. The five unassigned rows all sit on a 52.8-59.1 cm shell but point in every direction - 115007 at cos_fwd -0.90 and 116008 at -0.91 lie on the muon body line, while 118009 (-0.05), 120014 (-0.25) and 119013 (+0.90) fan out sideways and forward - and 119013 is a 14-point, 7.6 cm track fragment rather than a speck, with the three of them roughly collinear in b_3d_wide. Objects scattered in unrelated directions on a 60 cm ring, one of them a track fragment, read as a neighbouring object rather than a decay ring, so they are delta / other and the kind stays none. f_meas shows the track ending in U, V and W together with the charge visibly piling up over the last time slices and no dead bar under the end.

notes: No pin move: the rise is monotonic to the fit last point with no sustained collapse. Undershoot explicitly checked and rejected (forward 2.1 cm tip is at MIP, not 1e5).
evidence: 255 cm chain, enters 0.2 cm from an x face and stops with d_face 128.6 cm (nearest z) — deeply contained, so containment is not in question. On the 4x-upscaled dQ/dx panel the chain sits on a 5e4 MIP plateau out to s=60-100 cm, is already 6.5-8e4 by s=10-15, and climbs monotonically 8-9e4 (s=4) -> 1.03-1.05e5 (s=2) -> 1.13e5 -> 1.19e5 at the last point, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve (which asymptotes near 1.6e5 and is never crossed, as expected). There is no peak-then-collapse before the last point, so the pin stays on the fit end. Past the stop, the d and e azimuths show a thick two-piece arm (48034 2.1 cm then 48009 8.4 cm, ~10.5 cm total, kink 20 deg) attached at the stop vertex and bending away from the muon line; it carries 4.9e4 and 5.6e4 e/cm, i.e. MIP, and a muon that has just reached 1.19e5 at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so the arm is a second particle and 10 cm is the right range for a ~28 MeV electron: michel. Undershoot check made explicitly and it fails: the forward tip 48034 is 2.1 cm at cos_fwd 0.92, the right geometry, but 4.9e4 is at MIP, not the several-times-MIP 0.9-1.2e5 the undershoot signature requires, so this is the ordinary Michel case, not a mis-typed muon tip. Two speck groups sit past the stop and I judged them separately: 156029 and 158031 (4 and 2 points, 17.6-18.6 cm, cos_fwd 0.17-0.19) lie up-left of the stop in the e view, roughly transverse to the muon and about 8 cm off its body line, isolated and compact — detached dots on the far side from the arm, so gamma by the primary rule (isolated, past the stop, clear of the body, inside 60 cm; charge is not a criterion), not because they are on the Michel side, which they are not; 154028, 157030 and 159032 (2-4 points, 0.1-1.6 cm, 21-34 cm, cos_fwd 0.51-0.82) lie down/down-right, i.e. along the Michel arm side, detached across a >10 cm charge-free gap, so gamma on both the primary rule and the Michel-side speck rule — the chain calls them gamma-body-exclusion but they are nowhere near the body line in any of the three azimuths, and off-axis separation outranks the chain label. 48014 and 48026 (10 and 13 points, pdg 11 shower) sit 229-235 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00, on the muon body line: delta / other. In f_meas the W plane has dead bands at global rank ~11700-11720 right where the last points sit, which is the one thing that could fake a stop, but U and V both end cleanly at the same time slice ~1185-1195 with measured-minus-predicted flat along the track, the profile rises instead of staying on the plateau, and the decay charge is reconstructed in 3D past the stop — a dead-region exit does not produce a Bragg rise, so it does not move the call.

notes: Confidence medium only because the kind hinges on one 5-point survey speck (175008) that the chain itself never adjudicated ('survey only -- neither stage was offered it'); the verdict STM_MICHEL is itself solid. Chain says is_stm 0, reject shape_flat, and reports 'no daughter / nothing at the stop' while the display draws a 27.5 cm pdg-11 arm attached at the stop - I disagree with the chain on both counts. V plane dead across the stop.
evidence: Short object in the top anode corner: the chain is only 11.8 cm (21 points, KE 51.3 MeV by range), entering 0.2 cm from the anode face and stopping 8.6 cm from it, in_fv 1. The dQ/dx profile is short but it is a rise, not a plateau: 6.7-7.0e4 at s = 10-11 cm climbing to 9.0-9.2e4 in the last 1-2 cm, tracking the overlaid muon curve almost point for point (curve 6.9e4 at s=11, ~1.0e5 at s=1) rather than the flat 6.8e4 electron dashed line. The single 7.6e4 point at s~0 is one low terminal point, ordinary scatter, so the pin stays on the fit's last point. Past the stop the object rows tile with no gap: 54003 [0, 3.61], 54005 [3.61, 24.29], 54007 [24.29, 27.51] - one continuous 27.5 cm arm leaving the stop nearly perpendicular to the muon (computed perpendicular offset from the muon line 10.3 cm at R=10.7 and 25.6 cm at R=25.9, so it is well clear of the body line, and the kink is obvious in d_3d_stop). Its charge is 4.5e4 / 3.8e4 / 5.0e4, at or below the muon's own 5.4-6.7e4 plateau; a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle and 27 cm is the right range for a high-end Michel: michel on all three. The undershoot screen does not fire - 54003 is short, forward (cos_fwd 0.66) and typed pdg 11, but at 4.5e4 it is at/below plateau, not the several-times-MIP tip the undershoot requires. 175008 is a 2.0 cm five-point speck at 44.97-45.48 cm, i.e. across a 17.5 cm charge-free gap past the arm's end, and it lies along the arm's own direction (cos 0.98 with the stop->54007 line): detached and on the Michel's side, so gamma, which is what carries the kind from attached to both. Caveat recorded in f_meas: a wide dead-channel band covers V 7540-7557 and the muon and the stop sit inside it, so the stop is imaged on U and W only - both of those are live at the stop with a flat measured-minus-predicted residual, and the far Michel pieces reappear in V beyond channel 7553.

notes: Declined overshoot candidate, and this is the hard call. The profile does reach its maximum at s = 7.6 rather than at the fit end and the last 3.4 cm are low, which is the shape the rubric describes. I did not move the pin because the collapse fails the rubric's own depth clause - it returns to this track's plateau (top-of-band 6.1e4 against a 5.4e4 plateau) rather than falling far below it - because the same track shows dips of the same depth every 15-25 cm along its whole length, and above all because the rubric's mechanism is the fit bridging the muon's stop to a Michel, and here there is no arm, no dot and no object of any kind at the stop for it to bridge to. If a reviewer disagrees, the pin belongs at rr ~3.4; verdict, kind and all six tags are unchanged either way. Chain rejects with no_bragg and shape_flat; I disagree - there is a clear 15 cm rise to 1.05e5, it just does not carry through the last three centimetres, which is exactly what would make an automatic shape test on the terminal points read flat.
evidence: A 451.5 cm cosmic that enters 0.4 cm from the z = 0 face at (203, 242, 1) and runs down across the cathode to a fit end at (-130, -20, 72), 70.6 cm from the nearest wall - deeply contained, so containment is not what decides this one. The profile is on a 5.5-6.5e4 MIP plateau for hundreds of centimetres and then lifts clearly off it over the last 15 cm, tracking the muon reference curve: top-of-band 6.5e4 at s = 15, 7.5-8.2e4 at s = 12-13, 8.8-9.5e4 at s = 8-12.6, a 1.02-1.05e5 pair at s = 7.6, and 8.25-8.78e4 across s = 3.4-7.7 with no low points at all in that stretch. A through-goer cannot do that - it would sit flat to its last point - so this is a stopper, and the chain's own kinematics agree with a genuine stop: range gives 1040.8 MeV and MCS 977.6 MeV over the same track, within six per cent of each other. The last 3.4 cm are the awkward part and I looked hard at them: fourteen points scattered from 6.13e4 down to 1.50e4, median about 3.2e4. I considered the overshoot and decided against moving the pin, for three reasons given in the notes - briefly, the depth is wrong (top-of-band 6.1e4 is still at this track's own plateau, and the median 3.2e4 is 0.6 of MIP where the rubric's overshoot segments run 0.15-0.5), this track carries recurring 5-10 cm dips of the same depth at s = 15-20, 30, 40 and 65-70 where its median is also about 4e4, and there is nothing for the fit to have bridged to. On that last point: the object census has no arm, no dot and no unfitted cluster near the stop (chain: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0), the U, V and W measured panels are all live at the stop end (the dead stripes at U 432-437 and beyond sit 40-60 cm back up the body, not at the tip), the W tip terminates cleanly with nothing above it, and the faint points just past the star in c_3d_stop are the ordinary low-charge cap that both ends of this track carry. So: a Bragg rise, a contained end, and nothing past it that reads as an electron - STM_ONLY, kind none. The one off-chain object, 60015, is 301-307 cm back up the body at cos_fwd -0.99 and a computed 8.4 cm perpendicular offset - hugging the muon line, so delta / other whatever its pdg 11 label says.

notes: No visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the fit end - the cluster simply ran out of imaging 58 cm from the nearest wall - but the profile is flat on the MIP plateau to the last point, which the rubric makes sufficient on its own, so THRU rather than UNCLEAR. Chain agrees it is not an STM (is_stm 0, no_bragg + shape_flat); where I differ from the chain is that it still hands back a Michel core (23001, kink 47 deg), which I read as a 2-point speck with no stop to belong to.
evidence: 210.7 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z = 0 face at (-20, -258, 1) and ending at (-213, -236, 59), 57.9 cm from the nearest wall - so this is decided on the profile, not on reaching a face. The profile is flat: top-of-band 6.0-6.5e4 from s = 100 all the way in to s = 3, with the usual delta spikes to 0.9-1.15e5 scattered uniformly along the whole 200 cm (they are at s = 20, 35, 50, 60, 70, 75, 90 - nowhere near the end), and there is no lift off the plateau anywhere in the last 10-20 cm; the muon reference curve pulls up to 1.6e5 while the data stay pinned at 6e4. The last two centimetres actually fall - 3.2e4, 2.4e4, 1.7e4, 1.2e4 - which is a fit end, not a Bragg peak. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot be at MIP for its last 20 cm, so this is a through-goer. What sits at the end: the chain offers 23001 as the Michel, but it is a 2-point 0.8 cm speck at 2.8e4 (1.7 MeV) sitting 0.4 cm off the last fit point - the two oversized blue markers at s ~ 0 on the panel - and with no stop there is nothing for it to be the decay of; delta / other. c_3d_stop looks at first as though a faint track continues straight on up-right from the star, which would have been the other route to THRU, but d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop both show clean white space past the star along the muon direction, and the zoom shows the c-view feature is a broad diffuse swath, not a collinear stub - a depth coincidence in one azimuth, so I did not use it. evidence: The cleanest item in my chunk. 130.7 cm entering 0.1 cm from the z face at (221, 256, 298) and stopping at (125, 229, 220), 78.5 cm from the nearest wall - deeply contained, so containment is not in question. I checked the undershoot explicitly and it does not fire: 55002 is short and forward (cos_fwd 0.84) and typed pdg 11, which is three quarters of the pattern, but the charge is the load-bearing clause and 7.3e4 is 1.35x MIP, not several times it, and the charge FALLS as the arm goes out (7.3e4, 5.8e4, 6.2e4, 1.9e4, 0.76e4) which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel case rather than a muon tip. Both lie along the arm's own outward direction - cos 0.91 and 0.85 with 157005, and cos 0.99 with each other - so they are dots on the Michel's side rather than specks scattered in unrelated directions: gamma both, whatever 159007's 'gamma body exclusion' label says, since off-axis separation outranks the chain's exclusion. f_meas confirms the arm is real measured charge past the muon's end in all three planes with a flat measured-minus-predicted residual, and no dead stripe sits on the stop.
